trait.name: Retribution of Ragnarok
entries: When Bolgrim dies, runes engraved on his chest explode. {@actSave dex} {@dc 12} Each creature in a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from Bolgrim. {@actSaveFail} 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Necrotic damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Bolgrim casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 12}, {@hit 4} to hit with spell attacks):

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Bolgrim makes three attacks, using Longsword, Handaxe, or Necrotic Ray in any combination.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Slashing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Slashing damage if the target is marked.

action.name: Handaxe
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., or range 20/60 ft., one target. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Slashing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Slashing damage if the target is marked.

action.name: Necrotic Ray
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 4} to hit, range 120 ft., one target. {@h}8 ({@damage 1d12 +2}) Necrotic damage. If the target is a creature, it is spiritually marked with a necrotic rune until the end of its next turn.

reaction.name: Parry
entries: {@actTrigger} Bolgrim is hit by a melee attack roll while holding a weapon. {@actResponse} Bolgrim adds 2 to his {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

trait.name: Icewalker
entries: Ylsa can move across and climb icy surfaces without needing to make an Ability Check. Additionally, {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} composed of ice or snow doesn't cost her extra movement.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If Ylsa fails a saving throw, she can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Retribution of Ragnarok
entries: When Ylsa dies, runes engraved on her chest explode. {@actSave dex} {@dc 15} Each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from Ylsa. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Cold damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Ylsa makes two attacks, using Battleaxe or Ice-Eye in any combination.

action.name: Battleaxe
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 2d10 + 5}) Slashing damage, plus 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Cold damage if the target is {@condition Prone|XPHB}, it takes an additional 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Slashing damage.

action.name: Ice-Eye
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 6} to hit, range 120 ft., one target. {@h}18 ({@damage 4d8}) Cold damage and the target's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by 10 feet until the start of Ylsa's next turn.

action.name: Ice Wall Orb (once only)
entries: Ylsa crushes this small sphere of ice in her hand and can cast {@spell Wall of Ice|XPHB} using Charisma as her spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 16}). The wall created by this item requires no {@status Concentration|XPHB} and lasts 1 minute.

bonus.name: Overpower
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, Ylsa can shove an adjacent creature standing on {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. The creature must make a {@dc 16} Strength saving throw, gaining the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition on a failure.

reaction.name: Glamsyni Shield {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actTrigger} Ylsa is hit by an attack or affected by a spell while holding this shield. {@actResponse} She teleports up to 10 feet, causing the attack or spell to miss her if she is no longer within range or within the spell's area of effect.

legendary.name: Axe or Eye
entries: Ylsa makes one Battleaxe or Ice-Eye attack.

legendary.name: Ice Slick
entries: Ylsa conjures slippery ice in a 15-foot radius centered on a point within 60 feet. The ice counts as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. Each creature within this area or that starts their turn there is targeted by the following effect. {@actSave dex} {@dc 16}. {@actSaveFail} Target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} The ice remains until Ylsa uses this action again or she has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition; she can't take this action again until the start of her next turn.

legendary.name: Skate
entries: Ylsa moves up to her {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. If she begins this movement while standing on ice or snow, she doesn't provoke {@action Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}.

trait.name: Heated Body
entries: The heat Krusgr exudes from his body is so intense it provides him with {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Cold damage. In addition, any creature within 5 feet of him that strikes his heated body with a melee attack takes 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Fire damage.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Krusgr makes two attacks, using Flame Sword or Hammer Throw in any combination.

action.name: Flame Sword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 12}, reach 10 ft. {@h}21 ({@damage 4d6 + 8}) Slashing damage plus 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Fire damage.

action.name: Hammer Throw
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 12}, range 60/240 ft. {@h}23 ({@damage 3d10 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage plus 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Fire damage, and the target is pushed up to 15 feet straight away from Krusgr and has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the next attack roll it makes before the end of its next turn.

action.name: Angrboda's Tears {@recharge 5}.
entries: Krusgr can expel a stream of boiling iron from his eyes. {@actSave dex} {@dc 18}, each creature in a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. {@actSaveFail} 27 ({@damage 6d8}) Fire damage, and the creature suffers 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level from the hot metal. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage and negates any further effect.

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: Thyrin has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Thyrin casts one of the following spells, using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 17}):

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Thyrin makes three attacks, using Crushing Mace or Eye of Fimbulwinter in any combination. He can replace two of these attacks with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Crushing Mace
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}13 ({@damage 2d8 + 5}) Bludgeoning damage plus 18 ({@damage 4d8}) Force damage.

action.name: Eye of Fimbulwinter
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 9} to hit, range 30/120 ft., one target. {@h}21 ({@damage 6d6}) Cold damage and the target is frozen in place ({@condition Restrained|XPHB}) by ice until the end of its next turn.

bonus.name: Curse of Ragnarok
entries: Thyrin pronounces a curse against an enemy he can see within 30 feet of him. {@actSave wis} {@dc 19}. {@actSaveFail} The target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on all attack rolls and saving throws until the end of its next turn. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is unaffected.

reaction.name: Healing Reprisal (3/day)
entries: {@actTrigger} When Thyrin takes damage from a melee or ranged attack or becomes affected by a condition. {@actResponse} Thyrin heals 23 ({@damage 4d8 + 5}) {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and ends a single condition affecting him.

items.name: Rock
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 12}  range 60/240 ft., one target. {@h}24 ({@damage 3d10 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target is pushed up to 15 feet straight away from the giant.

trait.name: Divine Vitality
entries: Skymir's ability scores and HP maximum can't be reduced except by means of a {@spell Wish|XPHB} spell.

trait.name: Icy Weapons
entries: Skymir's weapon attacks are magical. When he hits with any weapon, the weapon deals an extra 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Cold damage (included in the attack).

trait.name: Magic Resistance
entries: Skymir has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against spells and other magical effects.

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If Skymir fails a saving throw, he can choose to succeed instead.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Skymir casts one of the following spells, requiring no material components and using Wisdom as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 19}):

spellcasting.name: Frightful Presence
headerEntries: Skymir uses Spellcasting to cast {@spell Command|XPHB} or {@spell Fear|XPHB}. Skymir can't take this action again until the start of his next turn.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Skymir makes two attacks using Runesword or Arcane Sphere in any combination. He can replace one attack with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Runesword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 12} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}15 ({@damage 2d8 + 6}) Bludgeoning damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Cold damage; the target is Marked with a glowing spectral rune until the end of Skymir's next turn.

action.name: Arcane Sphere
entries: {@atkr r} {@hit 12} to hit, range 120 ft., one target. {@h}25 ({@damage 3d12 + 6}) Force damage, and the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls until the end of Skymir's next turn.

action.name: Icy Sweep {@recharge 5}
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 16} Each creature in a 20-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on Skymir. {@actSaveFail} 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Slashing damage, 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Cold damage, and the target is pushed up to 15 feet away from Skymir and gains the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage and not pushed or knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}.

bonus.name: Translocative Word
entries: Skymir speaks a word of power, and up to two creatures Marked by Skymir's Runesword are teleported to unoccupied spaces on the ground within 60 feet that he can see. The Mark on those targets then fades.

reaction.name: Protective Word
entries: {@actTrigger} Skymir is hit by an attack roll. {@actResponse} Skymir utters a word of power, adding 6 to his AC against that attack, possibly causing it to miss.

legendary.name: Attack
entries: Skymir makes a Runesword or Arcane Sphere attack. He can't take this action again until the start of his next turn.

legendary.name: Life-Draining Word
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 16} Skymir utters a word of power, targeting up to three creatures of his choice within 60 feet. {@actSaveFail} 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage, and Skymir regains {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage taken from each target. {@actSaveSuccessOrFail} Skymir can't take this action again until the start of his next turn.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Tetra casts one of the following spells, using Intelligence as the spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}):

spellcasting.name: Misty Step (3/Day)
headerEntries: Tetra casts {@spell Misty Step|XPHB}, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

spellcasting.name: Protective Magic (3/Day)
headerEntries: Tetra casts {@spell Counterspell|XPHB} or {@spell Shield|XPHB} in response to the spell's trigger, using the same spellcasting ability as Spellcasting.

items.name: Frost Spear
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 9}, reach 15 ft. {@h}19 ({@damage 2d12 + 6}) Slashing damage plus 9 ({@damage 2d8}) Cold damage.

items.name: Bitterfrost Cyclone (1/Day)
entries: Galnafur whips up a bone-chilling cyclone that swirls around her for up to 10 minutes. The cyclone generates and repositions up to 3 feet of snow in a 15-foot radius that moves with her, creating {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for Large and smaller creatures. Additionally, the cyclone protects Galnafur from projectiles. All but the heaviest Ranged weapon attacks targeting her are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. If she takes damage, she makes a {@status Concentration|XPHB} check to maintain the cyclone. Otherwise, the cyclone lasts for the duration, until Galnafur is {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} or spends a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to end the effect.

spellcasting.name: Spellcasting
headerEntries: Keldar casts one of the following spells, using Charisma as her spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 14}, {@hit 5} to hit with spell attacks):

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Keldar makes two attacks using Longsword or Handaxe in any combination. She can replace one of her attacks with a use of Spellcasting.

action.name: Longsword
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}7 ({@damage 1d8 + 3}) Slashing damage plus 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Thunder damage.

action.name: Handaxe
entries: {@atkr m,r} {@hit 5} to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft. {@h}6 ({@damage 1d6 + 3}) Slashing damage plus 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Thunder damage. Creatures within 5 feet of the target take 1 Thunder damage.

bonus.name: Percussive Shove
entries: Kelda's drum emits a blast of percussive force. {@actSave dex} {@dc 13} Each creature in a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. {@actSaveFail} Target is pushed away from Kelda to the end of the line.

reaction.name: Thunderous Rebuke
entries: {@actTrigger} A creature Keldar can see makes an attack roll against her. {@actResponse} {@actSave dex} {@dc 13} The triggering creature. {@actSaveFail} Triggering creature takes {@damage 1d6} Thunder damage and is pushed 10 feet away from Keldar.

items.name: Rend
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 4}, reach 5 ft. {@h}14 ({@damage 2d8 + 2}) Slashing damage.

items.name: Chain Whip
entries: {@atkr m} {@hit 7}, reach 5 ft. {@h}11 ({@damage 3d4 + 5}) Slashing damage.

monsterFluff.name: Bolgrim Boar-Scar
entries: Bolgrim first appears in {@adventure Down the Wolf Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1} and leads the {@adventure Assault on Hvalfell|NorthlandsSagas|4}. Ylsa succeeds him as the characters' main foil with the cult in Wotan's Gauntlet and Attack on Birgkrona.

monsterFluff.name: Finulf One-hand
entries: Early thirties. Blue eyes. Long blond hair, full mustache, and short beard. Blade scar on right cheek. Wears patched leather armor over green tunic, black pants. A cloak with a white fur trim. Sword and dagger on his belt. Missing left hand capped with metal cuff.
{@b Found Initially In:} Down the Wolf's Barrow. Also appears in Attack on Birgkrona.
{@b Background:} Leader of the Fangs of Vanagandr, a mercenary company.
{@b Personality Traits:} Direct, never gives up, has a hundred stories that start "This reminds me of the time . . ."
{@b Bonds:} Members of the Fangs. Fighting the good fight.
{@b Flaws:} Is a bit "glass-half-empty," cheerfully points out problems in gory detail.
{@b Wants:} When they first meet, to keep the stolen Uror's Shears from the hands of the Cult of Ragnarok. Later, to defeat the cult once and for all.

monsterFluff.name: Hekja No-Curl
entries: Lanky sailor with a surprising bald head. Yellow eyes and lupine features. Always scowling. Hide armor. Handaxe and seax dagger on her belt.
{@b Found Initially In:} Ogre's Run. Also appears in The Redspear Trail.
{@b Background:} First mate on Sly Raven; later second in command of the longship Stokkvari.
{@b Personality Traits:} Grim and brooding, dark sense of humor.
{@b Bonds:} Owes a life-bond to Kosktup for saving her life.
{@b Flaws:} She is a descriptive pessimist, providing "helpful" worst-case-possibilities.
{@b Wants:} To save her captain and support him in his crazy adventures.

monsterFluff.name: Kosktup Farleap
entries: Small squirrelfolk. Red-brown fur. Eyes the color of acorns. Cocky grin. Plain but serviceable leather armor over a teal shirt. Gold earrings in one tufted ear. Matching rapier and dagger hanging from his belt.
{@b Found Initially In:} Ogre's Run. Also appears in Among the Norns, The Redspear Trail, and others.
{@b Background:} Courageous swashbuckler, longship captain, squirrelfolk.
{@b Personality Traits:} Daring, cocky, and charming in equal measure.
{@b Bonds:} This longship dream—oh, and stopping the Cult of Ragnarok.
{@b Flaws:} Hides his idealism and dedication behind vanity and playful indifference.

{@b Wants:} To fulfill his dream of building and owning the greatest longship in the North, but when they first meet him, he'd settle for getting away from the ogres and perhaps a nice bath. Ultimately, he wants to keep his ship and crew alive and whole, which means stopping the end of the world.

monsterFluff.name: Skrolmuk
entries: Great ogre in command of giantkin

monsterFluff.name: Henrika Langerkvist
entries: Headwoman of Hvalfell

monsterFluff.name: Gretl Gunrsdottir
entries: Master shipbuilder

monsterFluff.name: Eirik Ellefsen
entries: Bard and leader of Skaldholm

monsterFluff.name: Uffi Toothless
entries: Trollkin jarl of Trollheim

monsterFluff.name: Ylsa Ice-Eye
entries: Bearfolk agent of the Cult of Ragnarok

monsterFluff.name: Sanngrior
entries: Valkyrie from the Isle of Swords

monsterFluff.name: Azala Stormsinger
entries: Blue-white skin. Serious and focused expression. Thoughtful blue eyes. Long golden hair tied into a single thick braid. White robes and a belt of golden disks. Ceremonial scepter. Diadem of silver and diamonds on her brow.
{@b Background:} Considers cloud giants superior to all others.
{@b Personality Traits:} Determined, strong, and unyielding.
{@b Bonds:} Truly cares for her people.
{@b Flaws:} Fears she will make the wrong decision and lead her people to ruin.
{@b Wants:} To keep her people safe from Ragnarok.

monsterFluff.name: Lagertha Giantblooded
entries: Gray-blue skin. Ice eyes. White, braided hair. Old battle scars on her face.
{@b Background:} A member of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin.
{@b Personality Traits:} Appears smug and confident. Well-hidden ruthlessness and cruelty.
{@b Bonds:} Fanatically loyal to Thyrin the Black and his cause.
{@b Flaws:} Can't resist being scornful.
{@b Wants:} To fool the giants into turning against the characters and to murder any disloyal to the Blood Reckoning.
{@b Other Notes:} Disguised as a paladin of Thor, Deception +5
{@b Talking to Lagertha:} Among other details, the giantkin "false paladin" gives the following evidence for her accusation:

items: The characters aided the known criminal Finulf One-Hand, even though they knew he was a thief who'd stolen an important relic from a temple of Wotan in Wolfheim (in {@i Down the Wolf Barrow}).
After slaughtering a remote outpost, the characters freed a heretical ratatosk, leaving a trail of destruction across the Haamu Hills (in {@i Ogre's Run}).
Aided by a disreputable ratatosk, the characters consorted with fell entities near the lair of Nidhogg, the creature gnawing at the roots of Yggdrasil (in {@i Among the Norns}).
The characters prevented the villagers of Hvalfell from fleeing a force of ogres and trolls because they needed time to finish building a longship (in {@i Assault on Hvalfell}).

While participating in a bardic competition in Skaldholm, the characters organized the murder of a prominent bard to gain influence over the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles} (in {@i Trials of the Lost Skald}).

monsterFluff.name: Gorm Rotholfsson
entries: Disciple of Chernobog

monsterFluff.name: Katlaug
entries: Prim and proper. Caretaker and majordomo.
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 6.
{@b Background:} Has served as hallwarden for several moots and takes great pride in performing her duties to the letter.
{@b Personality Traits:} Dignified, proud, expects a level of respect.
{@b Bonds:} Protective of Helgihond.
{@b Flaws:} Dismissive of "smaller" species.
{@b Wants:} To ensure that no one questions the hospitality of Helgihond.
{@b Talking to Katlaug:} The thursir freely relates information about Helgihond's amenities. She neither knows nor cares about the hall's history. She focuses on the here and now.

monsterFluff.name: Sigkva Runigsdottir
entries: Light blue complexion. Short-cropped golden hair. Formally attired.
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 10.
{@b Background:} Enjoys good relations with other cloud giant clans; frequently interacts with storm and lightning giant tribes.
{@b Personality Traits:} Attentive, kind, humble.
{@b Bonds:} Her family and the cloud giants in her charge.
{@b Flaws:} She naively assumes the best intentions in everyone with whom she interacts.
{@b Wants:} A successful moot with no hard feelings among the attendees, as well as assent from the assembled giants to help fight the Cult of Ragnarok.
{@b Talking to Sigkva:} She freely relates the following (in order):

items: She trusts Katlaug implicitly. The hallwarden understands the PCs' reasons for attending, and Sigkva tells them the thursir will attend to their needs while at the moot.
She hasn't met Izhova or Beli previously but knows Izhova's reputation as an accomplished diplomat.

She must resolve the dispute between the stone giants and jotuns before she can turn to the PCs' discussion. She figures smoothing things over between Sinmara and Glytta will entice them to pay attention to the party.

monsterFluff.name: Queen Sinmara
entries: Towering woman, even for a giant. Gleaming, golden eyes. Crimson garments bedecked with melted and reformed gold concealing a suit of crimson plate armor. Smells of sandalwood.
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 8.
{@b Background:} As wife of the dreaded Surtr, she has become accustomed to his wanderings across the globe and takes personally her leadership responsibility.
{@b Personality Traits:} Decisive, driven, imperious.
{@b Bonds:} Her husband, Surtr; her land, Reykurbrand; and her people, the jotuns, in that order.
{@b Flaws:} Underestimates non-giants.
{@b Wants:} The appearance of peacefully resolving her territorial dispute with the stone giants.

{@b Talking to Sinmara:} The PCs first must convince the reduced-size jotun to deign to talk with them with a {@dc 14} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check or {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check. Afterward, the queen freely relates the following (in order):

items: She expects Glytta Weggesdottir, the stone giant, to give in to her demands eventually.
She's heard about so many doomsday cults that come to naught, she has no interest in discussing another one.

monsterFluff.name: Izhova
entries: Dark red coloration. Close-cropped hair. Angular features. Adorned in simple yet elegant shift. Smells faintly of spices.
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 4.
{@b Background:} A skilled diplomat from Sengajordensblod, the giant capital; feels humbled to be here, as he is not a leader like many other delegates.
{@b Personality Traits:} Fastidious, soft-spoken, coercive.
{@b Bonds:} His chieftain, who sent him to the moot.
{@b Flaws:} Relies on diplomacy, bordering on intimidation.
{@b Wants:} A smooth negotiation between Queen Sinmara and Glytta Weggesdottir, and a chance for the PCs to speak their piece.
{@b Talking to Izhova:} The fire giant freely relates the following (in order):

items: He expresses dismay at the PCs' treatment by some giants and attempts to provide insight into the giant perspective.

Sigkva's death has shaken him. He didn't know her except by reputation, which he describes as positive among most giants. He gets right to the heart of the matter by suggesting the Cult of Ragnarok's involvement.
He went to the kitchen yesterday to ask about the ingredients of the entrees (he has culinary interests).
If asked whether he noticed anything amiss the night of the murder, he reports that he fell asleep quickly after the feast and slept through to the morning.

monsterFluff.name: Glytta Weggesdottir
entries: Granite skin. Bald. Bittersweet perfume. Decorative yet functional chainmail.
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 9.

{@b Background:} Frustrated over her clan's lower status due to a stone giant transgression so long ago as to be meaningless. She won't discuss this offense other than to say her chieftain, Karn, is working to address it.
{@b Personality Traits:} Belligerent, devious, muddled.
{@b Bonds:} Her community of Brotdalr.
{@b Flaws:} Hates being patronized when she is wrong.
{@b Wants:} A "victory" over Sinmara in the negotiations.
{@b Talking to Glytta:} The stone giant freely relates the following (in order):

items: She feels frustrated at the treatment her fellow stone giants receive from other giants. Glytta hopes to return her people to equal status with other giants.

If the PCs help her get leverage over Sinmara, she will happily entertain their proposal, up to a promise of stone giant fighters to help in the assault. She won't remember this unless the PCs get it in writing, a delicate task requiring a successful {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check or {@dc 17} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check.

monsterFluff.name: Beli Groundshaker
entries: Stout. Somewhat paunchy. Simple clothing. Coarse voice.
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 5.

{@b Background:} A longtime member of the Blood Reckoning, Beli discovered the primordial mi-go and devised this plot. He spent enough time in Thursrike to gain the trust of frost giant king Haakon Drakechoker and met Glytta there.
{@b Personality Traits:} Amiable, blunt, insightful. (After being uncovered as the murderer: arrogant, calculating, cruel.)
{@b Bonds:} The Cult of Ragnarok, provided it continues supplying Beli with items to create mayhem.
{@b Flaws:} Murderous.
{@b Wants:} To sow chaos at the moot, while learning about the PCs' and the giants' plans.

{@b Unique Powers.} Beli has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks against other giants. He can cast the {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} spell at will and the {@spell Shapechange|XPHB} spell twice per day.

{@b Talking to Beli:} At first, Beli speaks of himself in the third person. Once he drops his simplistic guise, he refuses to divulge information. Until that time, the thursir freely relates the following (in order):

items: Beli hasn't heard about the hill giant's death and is saddened to learn about it. He recalls that a hill giant was supposed to attend the moot.
Being invited to the moot surprised Beli. He confides that thursir rarely get the opportunity to attend.
He shows interest in allying with the giants and PCs in the assault on Birgkrona and hopes to hear more about their plans.
Regarding Sigkva's murder, he expresses his regrets and offers to help in any way he can. He also (truthfully) suggests the murderer has framed Glytta Weggesdottir.

monsterFluff.name: Eyvora Fiddercall
entries: Sleek feathers. Large amber eyes. Thick protective goggles.
{@b Background:} Her family has served the cloud giants for generations, and she is the latest in a long line of royal messengers.
{@b Personality Traits:} Chatty and curious, birdlike mannerisms.
{@b Bonds:} Loves her "flock" of eagles.
{@b Flaws:} She is a trifle flighty. Doesn't pay much heed to future problems.
{@b Wants:} To do a good job for her queen.
{@b Talking to Eyvora:} The ravenfolk messenger freely relates her background (above) plus the following:

items: Sunreach is a palace of wonders. It stays at a comfortable temperature no matter the altitude, kept afloat by magic (which Eyvora doesn't really understand).
Though strong-willed and serious the queen always has been kind to Evyora and her family. (She can chat endlessly about the wonders of Bjarmia and the beneficence of the queen.)

{@b Personality Traits:} Demanding, professional, untiring.
{@b Bonds:} Her kitchen and kitchen staff.
{@b Flaws:} Expects other humanoids to follow her orders without question.

{@b Talking to Vorbis:} The giantkin has little time to indulge in conversation. Vorbis keeps the kitchen open as much as possible to accommodate the giants' appetites. Her underlings deliver food to the banquet (Area 1) and to individual rooms upon request.

{@b Personality Traits:} Direct, greedy, "predator-or-prey" mentality.
{@b Bonds:} Avoids or submits to any creature bigger than himself.

{@b Wants:} Territory all to himself, with no cult and no giants to compete with.
{@b Talking to Odri'vetr:} If the PCs speak to the allied armies and guarantee Odri'vetr rulership of Birgkrona, the dragon agrees to stop fighting on behalf of the cult.

items: {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check: A PC convinces Odri'vetr to abandon Birgkrona, at which point the dragon grabs its treasure urn and flies into the wilds to the north. The PCs can gain a +5 bonus on the check by offering a Rare magic item or treasure worth at least 1,000 GP as "tribute."

{@dc 20} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB} or {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check: A PC makes a separate check to convince Odri'vetr to assist in one battle in the Upper Keep. All the PCs need do is call out his name, and he will arrive to help.

vehicle.name: Stokkvari
action: On its turn, Stokkvari can take two actions, choosing from the options below (it can take the same action multiple times). It can take only one action if it has fewer than 40 crew. It can't move or take actions if it has fewer than 3 crew.

items.name: Fire Ballista
items.entry: {@atk rw} {@hit 8} to hit, range 120/480 ft., one target. {@h}24 ({@damage 3d10 + 8}) Piercing damage.

items.name: Shield Wall
items.entry: Order the rowers to raise their shields in defense. This grants creatures in the ship a +5 bonus to their Armor Class and Dexterity saving throws, but the ship's current {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced by half until the end of the next round.

items.name: Volley
items.entry: Archers release a volley of arrows at a point within 600 feet. Creatures within 30 feet of that point must make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw, taking 13 ({@damage 3d8}) Piercing damage on a failure, or half as much on a success. Creatures that fail the saving throw by 5 or more have their {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduced by 10 feet until the start of Stokkvari's next turn.

other.name: Dragon's Head
entries: The magic drakahofud figurehead on the prow of the ship can be used as a ritual to transport the ship and anyone on board as if using the {@spell Plane Shift} spell. After using this relic twice, you must finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before you can use it again.

other.name: Sails and Rowing
entries: While in {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, Stokkvari's listed {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is its Sailing Speed. Reduce this by half when sailing against the wind, unless the crew is rowing.

other.name: Initiative
entries: Stokkvari has an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} modifier of +4.

vehicleFluff.name: Stokkvari
entries: Kosktup Farleap's longship, Stokkvari, is an impressive specimen of its type. Its stat block appears below. See "Ships and Sea Combat" in Northlands Worldbook, Chapter 7: Running a Northlands Campaign for ship rules.

item.name: Mother's Comb
entries: This bone comb is sized to assist with the weaving of cloth on a loom. It appears quite plain and unadorned. Using the {@spell Identify|XPHB} spell on the comb reveals its name but no other features.
When someone views the comb using {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB}, it radiates extraordinarily powerful Divination magic.
The comb first appears in {@adventure Among the Norns|SagasAdventure|3} and returns in {@adventure The Redspear Trail|NorthlandsSagas|7}.

item.name: Uror's Shears
entries: Legends tell of the three Norns, entities of power who weave the threads of fate and destiny. Of the trio, Uror appears as a crone. She crafted these shears to cut the threads of mortals when they die.

This pair of scissors seems forged from crude iron, rough and pitted—but they are impossibly sharp. They first appear in {@adventure Down the Wolf Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1} and return in {@adventure Among the Norns|SagasAdventure|3} and {@adventure Storming the Den of Fenris|NorthlandsSagas|10}.

entries.name: Fated Edge
entries: While wielding the shears, you can use an Action to cut through any single object, regardless of the material or nature of the object. A single action allows you to cut through {@b 5 feet} of material, and you can use your Action on subsequent rounds to continue cutting. On your turn, you can change the direction of your cuts, as long as the shears continue to touch the object and don't stop cutting. The GM has the final determination as to what counts as a single object.

If used on a living creature, the shears are a magic weapon that grants a +1 bonus to attack. On a hit, the shears deal 1 Force damage. A creature that takes damage from the shears must make a {@dc 18} Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, the thread of the creature's fate is cut, and it vanishes forever; on a success, it takes {@damage 10d10} Force damage.

entries.name: One Use Only
entries: When you successfully hit a living creature or have cut through one object (or cut though a number of {@b 5-foot} squares equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}), the shears immediately vanish. Stories suggest the shears return to the hands of the Norns, but this remains unconfirmed.

item.name: Tyr's Blade
entries: This magic weapon deals an extra {@damage 2d6} damage to any creature it hits. This extra damage is of the same type as the weapon's normal damage.

entries.name: Extraordinary Quality
entries: A flute of extraordinary quality that grants +2 to {@skill Performance|XPHB} checks.

item.name: Birdcage of Innocuousness
entries: This silver birdcage, sized for giants, features figures of songbirds giving the impression they fly around its exterior.

When a creature with a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} enters the birdcage, it must make a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw, becoming docile on a failure until it leaves the cage (on a success it can open the cage from the inside and escape). A creature outside the cage can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to open or close it. A creature outside the cage also can use an action to speak a command word to either create an illusion of a harmless songbird in place of the creature inside or revert the illusion to the caged creature's true appearance. When a creature exits the birdcage, it returns to its true appearance.

item.name: Glamsyni Shield
entries: This round metal shield is emblazoned with the glamsyni rune. While wielding it, you can use a reaction to teleport up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. This property can't be used again until the next dawn.

item.name: Ice Wall Orb
entries: You can cast {@spell Wall of Ice|XPHB} using Charisma as her spellcasting ability (spell save {@dc 16}). The wall created by this item requires no {@status Concentration|XPHB} and lasts 1 minute.

table.name: Ship Encounters
rows: When the PCs sail within 100 feet of the coast, 4 {@creature Hill Giant|XMM|Hill Giants} emerge from some brush to hurl abuse and trash at the ship. If they sail on, {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} endures 4 rounds of bombardment before moving out of range. Engaging the giants means leaving the longship. (The giants each carry 50 SP in hacksilver; one uses a {@item Javelin of Lightning|XDMG} as a hair pin.)

While Kosktup navigates through heavy fog, {@dice 2d4} {@creature Will-o'-Wisp|XMM|Will-o'-Wisps} emerge from the mist to pick off sailors, killing one each unless the PCs intervene. The creatures flee once half are destroyed.

The PCs see a pitched battle between a sailing ship from Stannasgard (crew of 15 {@creature Pirate|NorthlandsWorldbook|Pirates} and a {@creature Merchant|NorthlandsWorldbook} in command) and a raider longship from Wolfheim (20 {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook|Vikings} and a {@creature Pirate Captain|NorthlandsWorldbook}). If they don't help, the sailing ship is captured within minutes. If the PCs capture (rather than sink) one or both ships, they collect bags of grain, casks of wine, 155 GP worth of hacksilver, and a {@item Potion of Water Breathing|XDMG}.

Roll on the {@table Unusual Weather|NorthlandsWorldbook|Unusual Weather} table in the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 7: Running a Northlands Campaign|NorthlandsWorldbook|7}.

2 {@creature Lindwurm|ToB1-2023|Lindwurms} emerge from the ocean to attack, focusing their attention on the PCs. They aren't up for a serious fight; once one dies or both are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, they flee.

table.name: Isle of Loki Encounters
rows: {@dice 1d2} {@creature Frost Giant|XMM|Frost Giants} hunt for walruses along the coast. If they spot the PCs, they attack. The giants know of Loki's Hall but have never been inside the glacier and are not allied with the cultists there.
{@dice 1d3} {@creature Lindwurm|ToB1-2023|Lindwurms} skate across the frozen plains looking for prey. They are keen to add some humanoid flesh to their diet.
{@dice 2d4} hungry {@creature Winter Wolf|XMM|Winter Wolves} stalk a wounded {@creature Mammoth|XMM} (hobbling on HP 65) across the tundra. The wolves happily attack any PCs who get in the way.

An earth tremor causes a nearby snowdrift to collapse on the party (use the crumbling monument hazard in {@i ToV Game Master's Guide} or {@hazard Rockslide|XDMG} hazard in {@i D&D Dungeon Master's Guide}). The snowdrift deals 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Bludgeoning damage and 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Cold damage.
A {@creature Young White Dragon|XMM} flies over the PCs' heads. It attacks but retreats quickly if they prove formidable targets.
A {@creature Rime Worm|ToB1-2023} erupts from the snow and attempts to drag a character back into its hole to devour.

table.name: Asgard Random Encounters
rows: 1 {@creature Frost Giant|XMM} and 3 {@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thursirs} smash into a nearby longhouse looking for treasure.
2 {@creature Stone Giant|XMM|Stone Giants} hurl stones toward a distant position of einherjar, while 2 {@creature Ogre|XMM|Ogres} haul more ammunition from a nearby ruined structure.
A {@creature Fire Giant|XMM} works to train his pet {@creature Salamander|XMM} how to burn a nearby great hall.
A {@creature Thrudgelmir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thrudgelmir} argues with an {@creature Ettin|XMM} over a locked chest.
A wandering patrol of 4 {@creature Troll|XMM|Trolls} marches into view hunting for foes to fight.
An intoxicated {@creature Storm Giant|XMM} wanders alone through the street, swigging from a barrel of mead.

table.name: Asgard Noncombat Encounters
rows: A Valkyrie's body rests on top of a pile of trolls, surrounded by her slain einherjar patrol.

A strange portal flickers into view. PCs who try it must make a {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. {@actSaveSuccess} It teleports them to their next destination. {@actSaveFail} It teleports them to a random location in Asgard.
A {@creature Valkyrie|ToB1-2023} and 3 {@creature Einherjar|ToB1-2023} move through the streets looking for giants to battle.

Choking smoke requires a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw of all creatures within a 20-foot {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere}. {@actSaveFail} Target gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level and has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 10 minutes.
A group of 4 mortal servants of the gods flee through the ruined streets, searching for shelter.

Flaming debris requires a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw of all creatures within a 20-foot {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere}. {@actSaveFail} 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Fire damage. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage.

table.name: Asgard Discoveries
rows: A torn Asgardian banner soaked in ash and blood.
A cache containing 3 {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing (Greater)}.
Five bottles divine wine (each worth 250 GP).
A chipped, blood-flecked tooth the size of a human fist.
Magic item in a trapped coffer. Choose one: {@item Stone of Good Luck|XDMG}, {@item Horn of Valhalla, Bronze|XDMG|Bronze Horn of Valhalla}, or a card from the {@deck Mysterious Deck|XDMG}.
A collection of gem-studded artwork and fine silk fabrics. It weighs 50 pounds but is worth 4,500 GP.

data.name: Introduction
entries: Heed Loki's call! The Northlands need you to help stop Ragnarok!

{@i Northlands Sagas} is a connected storyline formed of twelve adventures that span the length and breadth of the Northlands and pit the player characters against cultists, giants, and even gods in an epic quest. If the player characters (PCs) complete the adventure path successfully, they will reach 13th level and will have preserved the gods of Asgard—and the rest of the world—from the ruin of Ragnarok.

This adventure path, designed for use with either the Tales of the Valiant® or Dungeons & Dragons 2024 games, is optimized for four to five player characters, the heroes of this epic saga. Much of the lore about the regions, nonplayer characters (NPCs), and creatures in these adventures appears in the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

Players and Game Masters (GMs) wishing to set off on an epic journey across rime-shrouded lands, where diabolical cults lurk in the shadows and giants loom in the driving storms—look no further...adventure and glory await!

entries.name: Adventure Path Background
entries: In the Northlands, the threat of Ragnarok—the destruction of the world and its divine pantheon—constantly looms in the future, heralding the eventual death of the gods and of most mortals. The gods are not ignorant of their fate. Thor knows he will be crushed by the World Serpent, Loki and Heimdall understand they will slay each other, and Wotan recognizes that Fernis the Great Wolf will consume him. Though some, like Wotan, may conspire to evade this destiny, most understand their role in Ragnarok and (perhaps unhappily) accept it. Fortunately, Ragnarok remains in the distant future...or does it?

For ages, mortals and deities alike have mistrusted the god Loki, admittedly for some good reasons. Yet, as blood-brother to Wotan and a member of the Aesir, the trickster has long felt deserving of more respect from the gods of the North. Decades ago, Loki secretly allied with the dark deities Boreas and Chernobog to create a series of rumors and bogus prophecies suggesting that Ragnarok grows near. The influence of this divine alliance prompted frightened mortals to form the Cult of Ragnarok, a sect that spread false rumors of prophecies fulfilled and signs witnessed. Since then, the cult has spread, and now many mortals believe the end truly is nigh.

Though only the gods know the divine purposes behind this scheme, one might guess that Boreas and Chernobog seek to weaken or distract the Aesir and Vanir. Loki shrouds the purpose of their involvement in mystery but, as with everything to do with the god of lies, they undoubtedly have a reason. Regardless, the three gods have created a great deal of impact via their cult. But now Loki seeks to change the dynamic for personal reasons.

For, despite a reputation for sowing chaos, Loki doesn't want Ragnarok to happen...at least not yet. However, the wheels the cult has set in motion have spun out of control. Bergelmir and Angrboda, deities worshipped by the giants and jotuns of the Northlands, have suborned the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin, a sect of the Cult of Ragnarok, and launched an alliance between the cultists and the giants with the goal of unleashing Fenris the Great Wolf on Asgard. This scheme capitalizes on a loophole in the Ragnarok prophecy and might actually trigger the End Times—unless Loki can convince some mortals to get involved.

entries.name: Sagas Structure and Adventure Summary
entries: The {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path builds on a cohesive narrative stretched across the various adventures. The individual scenarios are designed to be played in sequence, forming an entire epic saga starring the characters. However, you can easily play them independently of one another instead.

The Sagas' overall narrative arc is structured much like a movie or play. The storyline splits into four narrative "acts," each containing one or more adventures. Characters begin at 1st level and advance one level or more upon completing each adventure.

entries.name: Act 1: Discovering Their Destiny
entries: The god Loki chooses the characters to investigate the machinations of the Cult of Ragnarok. When they foil a few of the cult's activities, they find themselves launched into a mighty quest to prevent the cult and its giant allies from beginning the end of the world.

entries.name: Down the Wolf Barrow (Level 1)
entries: Loki asks the PCs to chase a thief who has stolen a pair of magical shears from an isolated temple. The pursuit leads into an ancient puzzle and trap-filled barrow. Confronting the thief turns the tables a bit—he had merely sought to keep the relic out of the hands of the Cult of Ragnarok, whose members have entered the barrow to dispatch the thief and the meddling adventurers.

entries.name: Ogre's Run (Level 2)
entries: The PCs are contacted about a ratatosk longship captain, one of Loki's agents, held captive by a band of ogres. The heroes venture into the wild Haamu Hills, where they spring the captive sought by the Cult of Ragnarok. With their prize in tow, the characters evade pursuing ogres, gnolls, and trollkin. The escape culminates in a thrilling chase down a frozen river with cultists and giants on every side.

entries.name: Among the Norns (Level 3)
entries: Accompanying their ratatosk ally to fetch an item desired by their patron Loki, the characters step out of the mortal world onto Yggdrasil, the World Tree. A harrowing series of portals brings them face to face with the Norns at the Well of Urd. The three goddesses of fate agree to give them Loki's item and information about the cult if the PCs do a task for them. Delving into the roots of the World Tree, the adventurers battle a foul drake spawned by the dark serpent Nidhogg to receive their promised reward.

entries.name: Assault on Hvalfell (Level 4)
entries: In a coastal Northlands village, the characters' ratatosk ally hurries to fit a new longship with a magical dragon figurehead—the prize gained from the Norns. However, a deadly force of giants and cultists under the command of {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} approaches to seize the relic for themselves. The PCs rally the villagers and prepare what defenses they can before the assault. Fighting waves of cultists and giants, the adventurers struggle to hold back the foes while the longship is finished and launched. As they lead a fighting retreat with village survivors, they meet {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} on the beach in a final confrontation.

entries.name: Act 2: Seeking Allies and Information
entries: The characters gather resources and allies as they continue to meddle in the plans of the Cult of Ragnarok and seek to discover the location of the cult's hidden fortress.

entries.name: Trials of the Lost Skald (Levels 5–6)
entries: The adventurers journey to Skaldholm to gain the aid of the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles} and his skalds. They need their help spreading the call to battle against the cult across the North. However, the bardic leader forces the characters to compete in a deadly martial bardic competition before they can earn his aid.

entries.name: Descent of Cloud Castle (Level 6–7)
entries: The characters arrive at the flying city of Bjarmia to secure an alliance with the cloud giants, who oppose the Cult of Ragnarok and the giants allied with them. Their diplomacy is made harder by a sect of the Order of the Thunderer, which accuses the PCs of being secretly in league with the cult. In the middle of the negotiations, the city suddenly begins falling! The adventurers navigate hazards and enraged cloud giants to reach the heart of the city. There they find that the Order of the Thunderer—revealed as the real cultists—have sabotaged the magical core keeping the city afloat. Defeating them, the characters learn the "core" is actually an imprisoned deity: Gullveig, god of gold and magic. They must choose: Either free the god and doom the city or return her to her imprisonment and gain the alliance they sought.

entries.name: The Redspear Trail (Level 8)
entries: The characters travel to the Isle of Loki in the longship of their ratatosk ally to consult the Loom of Fables, a wondrous artifact that might reveal the location of the cult's hidden fortress. The Redspear party—an adventuring group that went missing on the island some time ago—marked the route to the loom. Following these clues into the caverns below the ice, the PCs battle cultists who also seek the loom. Once they reach the ice-covered heights of Loki's Hall, the heroes confront the mighty dragon {@creature Fafnir|NorthlandsSagas} in a ferocious battle. Defeating the dragon allows them to use the Loom of Fables and learn where to find the cult's fortress.

entries.name: Act 3: Engaging the Cult
entries: The characters actively move against their foes by attempting to disrupt the alliance between the Cult of Ragnarok and the giants and leading their allies to assault the cult's fortress. Matters turn more dire when the giants release Fenris the Great Wolf from his prison den.

entries.name: Murder at the Moot (Level 9)
entries: Summoned to the Moot of Jotunheim by friendly cloud giants, the characters hope to turn the other giants against the Cult of Ragnarok and perhaps even secure allies for the upcoming attack on the cult's fortress. After they arrive, however, the moot's High Speaker is murdered. The PCs work to investigate the crime and prove their innocence—and in the process discover a shapechanger who seeks to eradicate giants who oppose the cult.

entries.name: Attack on Birgkrona (Level 10)
entries: The characters lead their allies on the assault of Birgkrona, the Cult of Ragnarok's hidden fortress. During the siege, they can aid the attacking forces. Then, following a secret path, the PCs infiltrate the fortress to confront the cult leaders. After a cat-and-mouse journey through the besieged castle, they defeat {@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas} and assure the doom of the cult at the fortress. However, the cult's main leaders—{@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} and the jotun {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}—have already departed to awaken the Great Wolf at the Den of Fenris.

entries.name: Storming the Den of Fenris (Level 11)
entries: The characters venture into the underground labyrinth surrounding the Den of Fenris, racing against the clock to reach the imprisoned Great Wolf before the cultists release him. Battling through cult guards, deadly traps, and ancient defenders, they ascend to the vast cavern at the heart of the dungeon. When they arrive, Thyrin is close to completing the ritual to awaken the Great Wolf, but the PCs must battle past a powerful fire giant warlord to reach him. Unfortunately, just as they triumph over their adversaries, the giants betray Thyrin. Fenris, now free, magically departs for Asgard with Skymir and his new giant allies.

entries.name: Act 4: Save the Gods, Stop Ragnarok
entries: The characters journey to Asgard, which lies under attack from the giants and Fenris. They must act swiftly to save the gods before moving toward an epic final confrontation with the Great Wolf.

entries.name: Ashes of Asgard (Level 12)
entries: The characters sail with their ratatosk ally on his magical longship to Asgard. They pass across the blocked Bifrost Bridge that leads to the gods' home and, after defeating Skymir Godkiller's guards, they enter Asgard. Inside the divine city, giants run amok. The Northlands pantheon, rendered mortal by the presence of Fenris, attempts a defense, but some of their strongest members have become isolated and scattered. The adventurers battle or sneak their way to various sites across Asgard to rescue these deities. Then, with the gods by their side, they face a final confrontation with {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} and his giants. During this battle, the heroes must attempt to rechain Fenris and send the Great Wolf back to sleep before it destroys all of Asgard—and the rest of the world.

entries.name: Runestones
entries: During the first adventure, Loki gives each character a Runestone. The stones are carved with powerful, primal runes signifying that the Norns have chosen these individuals. While not guarantees of a heroic destiny, they symbolize the characters' potential for greatness. Rising to this challenge is up to them.

Runestones grant powers and abilities that improve as the adventure path progresses. Note that none of the adventures require the Runestones for success—you can play all adventures without using them if you wish.

Each Runestone aligns to one of the gods of the Northlands and gives a character a special power when they acquire it. At certain locations or after important events during the Sagas adventure arc, the PCs' actions can cause their Runestones to improve, gaining higher levels of power: Least, Lesser, Greater, and Patron. The additional powers tie thematically to the base level ability.

Runestones are available to purchase separately from the store at koboldpress.com. However, you also can copy the options later in this section onto slips of paper and allow players to draw from them.

entries.name: Drawing a Runestone
entries: At the beginning of the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, each player should draw one Runestone randomly.

items: If you have physical stones, players can draw them from a bag or container without looking.
If you have a deck of Runestone cards, place the cards for the "Least" power level face down, mix them up, then invite the players each to draw one.
Or just assign the runes randomly.

entries: Ideally, each character should have a different Runestone without duplicating any. However, some combinations of character and Runestone may not appeal to a player. In that situation, at your discretion, the player can draw a new one, or you can give them one that fits better. The Runestone a player receives should stay with the character throughout the Sagas adventure path.

entries.name: Runestones at Higher Levels
entries: If you introduce a new PC during one of the Sagas adventures, have the player draw a random Runestone for the new character. Do the same for all the players if you're running one of the adventures individually. The characters gain all the powers of their stones as indicated in the Runestone Powers by Level table.

entries.name: Using Runestones
entries: Runestones grant a number of benefits to the characters who possess them. All Runestones operate in much the same fashion. First, the owner sketches the rune in the air—only that character can see its glowing, magical form while it remains in effect.

Some runes remain active for a specific length of time, conferring their benefits while active (or the user can end the rune early to gain a different benefit). Other runes disappear immediately after they are sketched; they instantly confer a benefit but do not remain active.

As your Runestone advances in strength, new powers layer onto the earlier ones, so a single sketch of the rune could create a number of simultaneous benefits. Ending a rune early ends all its ongoing effects.
Remember these rules for using the stones:

items: A Runestone remains linked to the character receiving it and to a specific deity.

A character can use a Runestone once per day per power level, unless noted differently in the descriptions below. So a new Runestone with only its Least power active can be used once per day, but one that has advanced to the Greater power level can be used three times per day.
Characters can't exchange Runestones for different ones, except through the intervention of a deity, the Norns (see the adventure {@adventure Among the Norns|NorthlandsSagas|2}), or the GM.
Runestones don't require {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB}.
Characters automatically know the current powers of their Runestones and how to use them.
A character must have a Runestone in their possession to use its powers, though they don't have to actively wield it to do so.
Runestones have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to all damage. They have AC 18 and HP 100 if unattended.
If a Runestone is destroyed, lost, or stolen, it reappears in its character's possession at the end of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Runestone Advancement
entries: Certain adventures during the Sagas path provide opportunities for the characters to improve their Runestones. These feature interactions with special locations, defeating important foes, or otherwise engaging with major story elements. The locations where one can improve a Runestone appear in the following adventures:

items: {@b Least:} {@adventure Down the Wolf's Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1} (Level 1), Sagas campaign start
{@b Lesser:} {@adventure Ogre's Run|NorthlandsSagas|2} (Level 2)
{@b Greater:} {@adventure Descent of Cloud Castle|NorthlandsSagas|6} (Level 7)
{@b Patron:} {@adventure Ashes of Asgard|NorthlandsSagas|11} (Level 12+)

entries: If you wish, you can create your own Runestone advancement opportunities instead. Consult the Runestone Powers by Level table to determine when characters should unlock the various power levels.

entries.name: Runestone Options
entries: The dozen runestones in this section correspond to twelve gods of the North. For details on these deities, see Chapter 6: Northlands Pantheons in the {@i Northlands Worldbook}.

items.name: Algiz ({@deity Heimdall|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook})
entries: {@i Awareness, danger avoidance, reindeer.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch algiz in the air (no action required). When you do so, for a number of hours equal to your level, you can't be {@status Surprised|XPHB}, and you gain a bonus to Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. Additionally, while your algiz rune is active, you can end your rune early as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain a bonus to an {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: With your algiz rune active, should you fail a saving throw, you can end your rune early to succeed on it instead.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: With your algiz rune active, you can end your rune early to give each {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} creature within 60 feet of you a bonus to their {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} roll equal to half your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: While within 100 feet of {@deity Heimdall|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} with an active algiz rune, you can choose to end your rune early to gain foresight. When you do so, choose one creature you can see. Until the start of your next turn, that creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attack rolls made against you. Then your rune ends. You can sketch algiz as often as you want, provided you remain within 100 feet of {@deity Heimdall|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

items.name: Ansuz ({@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook})
entries: {@i Gods, inspiration, knowledge, outsiders.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch ansuz in the air (no action required) to regain a use of a class ability with a limited number of uses per day, such as Bardic Inspiration or Divine Sense.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: When you sketch ansuz, you can choose to recover a spell slot. The slot recovered can't be of the highest spell level you can cast. Additionally, when you sketch ansuz, you instead can choose a willing creature within 30 feet of you. That creature gains an extra use of one of their class features; the creature must use it within 1 minute or it is lost.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: When you sketch ansuz, you can recover two uses of a class feature with limited uses, such as Bardic Inspiration or spellcasting, or you can recover two spell slots. If you recover spell slots, they can't be of the highest spell level you can cast.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: When you sketch ansuz while within 100 feet of Wotan, until the end of your turn, each time you use a class feature with limited uses (such as Channel Divinity or spellcasting), you have a {@chance 50|50||Not expeded|Expended} percent chance of not expending that use. You can sketch ansuz as often as you want, provided you remain within 100 feet of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

items.name: Berkanan ({@deity Bengta|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook|Bear Maiden})
entries: {@i Birch tree, birth, life, strength.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch berkanan in the air (no action required). When you do so, you can target yourself or a {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} creature you can see within 30 feet of you that is suffering from one of the following conditions: {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, or {@condition Stunned|XPHB}. The target can repeat the associated saving throw immediately, ending the condition on a success.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: When you sketch berkanan, you and your allies become fortified. You can share a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your level, dividing the points between you and {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} creatures within 30 feet of you. The {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} last for 1 minute.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: When you sketch ansuz, you can recover two uses of a class feature with limited uses, such as Bardic Inspiration or spellcasting, or you can recover two spell slots. If you recover spell slots, they can't be of the highest spell level you can cast.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: When you sketch berkanan while you are within 100 feet of the {@deity Bengta|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook|Bear Maiden}, you can choose two damage types, assigning one to yourself and the other one to a {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} creature within 30 feet. You and the other creature each gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to the assigned damage type until the end of your next turn. You can sketch berkanan as often as you want, provided you remain within 100 feet of the {@deity Bengta|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook|Bear Maiden}.

items.name: Eiwaz ({@deity Ratatoskr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook})
entries: {@i Determination, progress, Yggdrasil.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch eiwaz in the air (no action required). When you do so, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} increases by 10 feet for 1 minute, and you gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: With your eiwaz rune active, if a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you can end your rune early as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: With your eiwaz rune active, you can end your rune early as an action to create a portal around a creature you can see within 30 feet. The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or fall through the portal to an unoccupied space you can see within 90 feet.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: When you have an active eiwaz rune while within 100 feet of {@deity Ratatoskr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB|Bonus Speed} increases to +20 feet. Additionally, you can end your eiwaz rune early as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to teleport to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet. You can sketch eiwaz and use it this way as often as you want, provided you remain within 100 feet of {@deity Ratatoskr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

items.name: Gebo ({@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook})
entries: {@i Balance, gifts, hospitality, protection.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch gebo (no action required) and, until the end of your next turn, you can reduce the damage you take from attacks and effects by {@damage 1d10} plus twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. Additionally, if your roll fully prevents the damage from an attack or effect, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to that roll.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: When you sketch gebo, you immediately roll {@damage 1d10} plus your level plus your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. Until the end of your next turn, you reduce the damage you take from attacks and magical effects by that amount. Additionally, choose one willing creature within 60 feet of you. That creature shares the effect of your gebo rune until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: When you sketch gebo, you can choose two willing creatures within 60 feet of you to share the effects of your gebo rune until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: When you sketch gebo while within 100 feet of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, if your roll fully prevents the damage from an attack or effect, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to send an arrow of light at the attacker or source of the effect. Make a ranged spell attack using your Wisdom or Charisma. On a hit, the attacker takes the result of your roll as Radiant damage. You can sketch gebo as often as you want, provided you remain within 100 feet of {@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

items.name: Jera ({@deity Freyr and Freyja|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook})
entries: {@i Harmony, harvest, interconnection.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch jera (no action required) and choose a willing creature within 30 feet of you as your partner. Until the end of your next turn, both you and your partner have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against the same creature.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: When you sketch jera, you and your partner both gain a bonus to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} while you remain within 30 feet of each other. Additionally, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when your partner takes damage to assume up to half of that damage onto yourself.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: When you sketch jera, if you and your partner strike the same creature before the end of your next turn, the person who hit the foe second deals extra Force damage equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: When you sketch jera while within 100 feet of either {@deity Freyr and Freyja|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, choose either Freyr or Freyja. You become associated with the god you chose, and your partner is associated with the other. While within 100 feet of Freyr, the character associated with him can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to recover {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your level. While within 100 feet of Freyja, the character associated with her deals bonus Radiant damage on weapon attacks equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

items.name: Kaunen ({@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook})
entries: {@i Creativity, fire, forge, knowledge.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch kaunen in the air (no action required) to reroll an attack roll or ability check. You must use the new result.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: When you sketch kaunen, you can choose to reroll an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. You must use the new result.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: When you sketch kaunen, you can choose to do so as a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when a creature within 30 feet of you fails an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw. The creature must reroll the {@dice d20} and use the new result.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: When you sketch kaunen while within 100 feet of {@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to give yourself {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls, ability checks, and saving throws until the end of your next turn. You can sketch kaunen as often as you want, provided you remain within 100 feet of {@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

items.name: Laukaz ({@deity Njord|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook})
entries: {@i The sea, water, weather.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch laukaz in the air (no action required). When you do so, you can't become lost while exposed to open air and can predict natural weather for a number of hours equal to your level. Additionally, if your laukaz rune is active, you can end your rune early as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain a magical {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and the ability to breathe underwater, both for 1 minute.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: With your laukaz rune active, you can end your rune early to surround yourself with a whirling vortex of wind for 1 minute. For the duration, Ranged weapon attacks against you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, and the wind hedges out any vapor, gas, and fog that a strong wind could disperse.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: With your laukaz rune active, you can end your rune early to cause a wave of wind and water to spring into existence. The wave emanates from you in a 60-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. All creatures in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 + your Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}). On a failure, a creature takes {@damage 2d8} Bludgeoning damage and {@damage 3d8} Cold damage, and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition; on a success, the creature takes half as much damage and doesn't have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: While within 100 feet of {@deity Njord|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} with an active laukaz rune, you can call upon Njord's power to protect yourself. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of you targets you with a weapon attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to transform your body briefly into water, causing the attack to go right through you and miss you. Then your rune ends. You can sketch and use laukaz this way as often as you want, provided you remain within 100 feet of {@deity Njord|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

items.name: Perto ({@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook})
entries: {@i Deception, fortune, unpredictability.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch perto in the air (no action required). Upon doing do, you gain a {@dice d6}, called a perto die, that you can roll, adding the result to a single {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB} you make before the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to sketch perto. If you do so, roll your perto die. The creature's roll increases or decreases (your choice) by the result of your roll.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: Your perto die increases to a {@dice d8}. Additionally, after you sketch perto and add the result of your {@dice d8} roll to a {@variantrule D20 Test|XPHB}, you can {@action Hide|XPHB} immediately (no action required), providing the terrain and circumstances permit it.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: While within 100 feet of {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, when you sketch perto, you gain two rolls of your perto die. You must use one for yourself and apply the other to a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. You must use both rolls before the start of your next turn or they are wasted. You can sketch perto as often as you want, provided you remain within 100 feet of {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

items.name: Sowilo ({@deity Baldur|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook})
entries: {@i Leadership, light, the sun.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch sowilo in the air (no action required). Upon doing so, you shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 20-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 20 feet until the end of your next turn. While surrounded by this radiance, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks and saves.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: When you sketch sowilo, you and a {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} creature within the radius of your light enjoy {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Necrotic damage. Additionally, Aberrations and Undead entering the radius of your light, or starting their turn within it, take Radiant damage equal to your level.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: When you sketch sowilo, you can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to inspire a {@variantrule Friendly [Attitude]|XPHB|Friendly} creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The creature can use its {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} immediately to move up to half its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} and make one melee attack.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: While within 100 feet of {@deity Baldur|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, when you sketch sowilo, you can use an action to focus your radiance into a beam of pure light. Make a ranged spell attack against a target using your Dexterity or Charisma modifier. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 5d8} Radiant damage and has the {@condition Blinded} condition until the start of your next turn. This immediately ends your rune and its aura of light. You can sketch sowilo and use it this way as often as you want, provided you remain within 100 feet of {@deity Baldur|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

items.name: Thurisaz ({@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook})
entries: {@i Giants, lightning, thunder.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch thurisaz in the air (no action required). Upon doing so, your melee weapon attacks deal {@damage 1d4} Lightning damage until the end of your next turn. Additionally, if you deal this extra Lightning damage to a target, you can cause a clap of thunder to push the target up to 10 feet away from you.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: When you sketch thurisaz, the extra damage increases to {@damage 1d6}. In addition, if you strike a creature with a melee attack and deal the extra Lightning damage, a second creature you can see within 5 feet of your initial target also takes the extra Lightning damage.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: When you sketch thurisaz, the extra damage increases to {@damage 1d8}. In addition, any melee weapon you wield gains the {@itemProperty T|XPHB|Thrown} property with a range of 20/60 ft. If you strike a creature with a Thrown weapon, it magically reappears in your hand at the end of your turn.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: While within 100 feet of T{@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}hor, when you sketch thurisaz, you can use an action to strike the ground with a weapon, causing lightning to arc from the impact to strike up to three targets you can see within 60 feet of you. Make a ranged spell attack using your Strength or Dexterity modifier. On a hit, a target takes {@damage 3d12} Lightning damage. Then the rune ends. You can sketch and use thurisaz this way as often as you want, provided you remain within 100 feet of {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

items.name: Tiwaz ({@deity Tyr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook})
entries: {@i Heroism, honor, justice, loyalty.}

entries.name: Least Power
entries: Once per day, you can sketch tiwaz in the air (no action required). Upon doing so, choose one creature you can see within 30 feet of you to become your focused target. For 1 minute, you automatically know when your focused target is lying, your focused target can't be {@condition Invisible|XPHB} to you, and you can pinpoint its location while it remains within 60 feet of you.

entries.name: Lesser Power
entries: When you sketch tiwaz, if you hit your focused target with an attack, you can choose for the next attack made against it before the end of your next turn to have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}. If this subsequent attack hits, it deals extra damage equal to your level; then your rune ends.

entries.name: Greater Power
entries: When you sketch tiwaz, you can't be {@condition Frightened|XPHB} by your focused target. Additionally, the first time your focused target hits you with an attack, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} against the damage type caused by that attack until the end of your next turn. Then your rune ends.

entries.name: Patron Power
entries: While you remain within 100 feet of {@deity Tyr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, if your focused target is within 60 feet of you and deals damage to anyone other than you, you can use a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to take half the damage upon yourself. If you attack the focused target on your next turn and successfully hit, you deal bonus Force damage equal to the amount of damage you took from your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}. Then your rune ends. You can sketch and use tiwaz this way as often as you want, provided you stay within 100 feet of {@deity Tyr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

entries.name: Runestone Choice—Note for the DM
entries: If you are a player, don't read this—or at least pretend you didn't.

The choice of Runestone for each character directly ties to the last adventure of the arc, {@adventure Ashes of Asgard|NorthlandsSagas|11}. During that adventure, the PCs can rescue certain gods of the North. Characters with Runestones linked to certain gods gain special benefits while interacting with or fighting alongside their aligned deity.

This means the "random" selection of the runestones at the beginning of the adventure arc somewhat determines the gods who require rescue in the final adventure. If this doesn't appeal to you as a GM, you can instead choose which gods you want to feature prominently in {@adventure Ashes of Asgard|NorthlandsSagas|11} and offer players only the Runestones linked to those gods at the start of the Sagas.

entries.name: Running the Adventures
entries: To run the adventures in this book, you need a copy of the Dungeons & Dragons 2024 core rulebooks or the Tales of the Valiant rulebooks, as well as the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

{@i Saga} adventures are not designed to be read as stories but rather to help you build stories with your players. Every effort has been made to make this book easy to use in play—without hours of preparation beforehand and without getting in the way of your preferred style of delivery.
{@i Text that looks like this is meant to convey the player characters' initial impressions of an area or creature. Feel free to build on these descriptions.}

Text that appears in a box like this is meant to be read aloud or paraphrased for the players when their characters first arrive at a location or under a specific circumstance, as described in the text.

While many encounters in the Sagas adventures can be resolved through combat, they have not all been balanced to the capabilities of a party of higher-level PCs. Shrewd use of the characters' social, exploratory, and investigative skills is required to successfully navigate the challenges in them.

entries.name: Reference Books
entries: Monsters, like {@creature Owlbear|XMM|Owlbears}, are presented in bold, as are NPCs, like {@creature Druid|XMM|Druids}. When a creature or its name appears in bold type, that's a visual cue pointing you to its stat block (because you'll need it soon). If a stat block is new, the adventure's text tells you where to find it. Most NPCs' and new creatures' stat blocks appear in the relevant adventure.
