However, those who reappear throughout the adventure path appear instead in the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|12} of this book.
Look in these sources for the stat blocks of the monsters and NPCs in these adventures:

items: {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook} {@book Chapter 8: Monsters of the North|NorthlandsWorldbook|8}
{@book Tome of Beasts 1|ToB1-2023}
The D&D {@book Monster Manual|XMM} or ToV {@i Monster Vault}

entries: Spells, magic items, and equipment mentioned in the adventures are described in the D&D {@book Player's Handbook|XPHB} and {@book Dungeon Master's Guide|XDMG}, or the ToV {@i Player's Guide}, and {@book Chapter 5: Magic and Miscellany|NorthlandsWorldbook|5} in the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}. Those marked with an asterisk (*) come from the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

entries.name: Bulleted Ability Checks and Saving Throws
entries: Ability checks and saving throws called out in bullet points are designed for at-a-glance reference. For example, "{@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) check: A PC knows that magic of some kind has been used to encourage the growth of the coral, which isn't native to this area." indicates that a PC's roll must meet or exceed 20 on an Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) check to know the noted information. This callout also notes consequences, if any, for failing the check or saving throw.

entries.name: Sagas Connections
entries: Each adventure includes a sidebar describing where it fits in the larger adventure path. If elements from previous adventures in the Sagas reappear in this scenario, those connections are mentioned here as a reminder.

entries.name: Handouts
entries: Each adventure has an associated player handout to enhance the gameplay. The adventure text includes large thumbnail images of the handouts. Full versions can be downloaded {@link https://bit.ly/NLSagaHandouts?r=qr|Handouts} for printing or digitally sharing.

entries.name: Dramatis Personae
entries: For quick reference, these are the most important named NPCs in the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, listed in order of appearance. Check the Appendix for stat blocks and descriptions of figures that appear in multiple adventures.

items: {@b {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}:} A god of mischief.
{@b {@creature Finulf One-Hand|NorthlandsSagas}:} A warrior and leader of the Fangs of Vanagandr.
{@b {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas}:} An agent of the Cult of Ragnarok.
{@b {@creature Hekja No-Curl|NorthlandsSagas}:} First mate aboard Kosktup Farleap's longship.
{@b {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas}:} A ratatosk sea captain and agent of Loki.
{@b {@creature Skrolmuk|NorthlandsSagas}:} Great ogre in command of a group of giantkin in the Haamu Hills.
{@b {@deity The Norns|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}:} A trio of surprisingly knowledgeable ladies.
{@b {@creature Henrika Langerkvist|NorthlandsSagas}:} The headwoman of the village of Hvalfell.
{@b {@creature Gretl Gunrsdottir|NorthlandsSagas}:} A master shipbuilder commissioned to build {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} a magical longship.
{@b {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}:} A bard and leader of Skaldholm.
{@b {@creature Keldar Tromma|NorthlandsSagas}:} A Shadowsinger who seeks to thwart the PCs on Skaldholm.
{@b {@creature Uffi Toothless|NorthlandsSagas|King Uffi Toothless}:} A trollkin jarl of Trollheim.
{@b {@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas}:} A bearfolk agent of the Cult of Ragnarok.
{@b {@creature Sanngrior|NorthlandsSagas}:} A Valkyrie from the Isle of Swords.
{@b {@creature Azala Stormsinger|NorthlandsSagas}:} A cloud giant queen disgusted by her people's involvement with Ragnarok.
{@b {@creature Lagertha Giantblooded|NorthlandsSagas}:} A giantkin warrior working for {@creature Krusgr Ironcap|NorthlandsSagas}.
{@b {@deity Gullveig|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}:} A divine, unwilling magical battery.
{@b {@creature Gorm Rotholfsson|NorthlandsSagas}:} Disciple of Chernobog suborned by Angrboda, hired by {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} to stop the PCs.
{@b {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas}:} Disdainful Hallwarden of the Helgihond.
{@b {@creature Sigkva Runigsdottir|NorthlandsSagas}:} A cloud giant murdered to pin the crime on the PCs.
{@b {@creature Queen Sinmara|NorthlandsSagas}:} A jotun and queen of Reykurbrand.
{@b {@creature Izhova|NorthlandsSagas}:} A fire giant necromancer from Sengajordensblod.
{@b {@creature Glytta Weggesdottir|NorthlandsSagas}:} A stone giant priestess of Jormungandr from Thursrike.
{@b {@creature Beli Groundshaker|NorthlandsSagas}:} A thursir from Jotunheim.
{@b {@creature Thulsamir Wolfbrother|NorthlandsSagas}:} Ruler of Wolfheim.
{@b {@creature Krusgr Ironcap|NorthlandsSagas}:} A fire giant warlord working for {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}.
{@b {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}:} Leader of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin, a Cult of Ragnarok sect.
{@b {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas}:} A six-headed giant who works for {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}.
{@b {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}:} A reaaaaaalllly big wolf.
{@b {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}:} Jotun worshiper of Bergelmir who hates the other gods for killing the First Giant. Leader of the Blood Reckoning, a giant sect.
{@b The Gods:} {@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Frigg|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, and all the rest.

data.name: Down the Wolf Barrow
entries: {@i Down the Wolf Barrow} is a first-tier adventure suitable for a party of four to five 1st-level characters, though you can adjust it to accommodate more or fewer players. The infiltration-themed scenario features a dungeon-crawl style adventure. It takes place in the Northlands in a region known as Wolfheim, but feel free to transplant it into a location of your choice.

At the end of the adventure, the characters should reach 2nd level. Be sure to refer to the {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0} for important backstory before starting.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: The work of the gods {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, and {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} has spawned the Cult of Ragnarok, as described under {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in this book's Introduction. Urged by the influence of Angrboda and Bergelmir, cruel gods of the giants, the jotun {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} has struck an alliance with {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}. Thyrin leads the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin, a faction of the Cult of Ragnarok. Together the cultists and giants plan to free Fenris the Great Wolf and unleash him on Asgard itself! While Loki appreciates chaos and disorder, this scheme actually might bring about Ragnarok, even if it's the wrong time. So unless the god of lies wants to perish along with the rest of the Asgardians, he must find some mortal heroes to intervene.

entries.name: Sagas Connections
entries: {@i Down the Wolf Barrow} is the first adventure in the Sagas adventure path. You'll find that many of its encounters foreshadow adventures in the Sagas. For those following the campaign arc, after finishing this adventure, the players proceed to {@adventure Ogre's Run|NorthlandsSagas|2}.

Most recently, the goddess Angrboda visited a cult warlord named {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} in his dreams, ordering him to acquire and deliver a magical relic called {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} from Icehavn Rift, an isolated temple in northern Wolfheim. The shears, reputed to have been forged by one of the Norns, supposedly can cut through any material: even Gleipnir, the chains binding Fenris. {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas|Bolgrim} and a troop of cultists hurried to Icehavn Rift, but before they could seize the relic, it was stolen by a human named {@creature Finulf One-Hand|NorthlandsSagas}. A mercenary and thief, Finulf belongs to the Fangs of Vanagandr, a group long opposed to the cult.

As the adventure begins, Finulf flees toward a barrow hideout where he hopes to secure the relic and keep it out of the cult's hands. But {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas|Bolgrim} and the Cult of Ragnarok remain in close pursuit. Meanwhile, the characters travel toward Icehavn Rift on other business, unaware they are about to be offered a chance to become epic heroes.

entries.name: Wolf Barrow History
entries: Centuries ago, mourning warriors hauled their lord's favorite longship across miles of hills and forests to reach this spot. They placed their lord in the ship, surrounded by his prized possessions, and wrapped his dead hands around the hilt of his sword. Then, around the vessel, they hauled earth and stone to fashion a burial mound fit for a reaving jarl. The halls of the barrow were crafted as described in the great fables of the North, with traps and puzzles to deter thieves. While cunning, the defenses failed as, some decades later, barrow thieves stole the interred treasures. The lord's enraged spirit rose as a vaettir to hunt down those who despoiled his burial. Neither vaettir nor thieves ever returned.
More recently, the Fangs of Vanagandr found the abandoned barrow. They repaired its puzzles and traps, transforming it into a secure lair to use in case of emergency or threat.

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: This adventure starts with a prelude. Two more parts follow, each of which takes place in Wolfheim.

entries.name: Prelude: A Singular Honor
entries: In this brief introduction, the characters fall asleep while on the road, experience a magical dream in which they meet the god Loki, and get a job.

entries.name: Part 1: Into the Barrow
entries: The PCs enter the barrow chasing {@creature Finulf One-Hand|NorthlandsSagas}. They navigate through the protective guardians and puzzles and finally corner the thief, who reveals he is trying to keep a pair of magical shears from the Cult of Ragnarok.

entries.name: Part 2: Escape from the Barrow
entries: With the shears (and perhaps Finulf) in hand, the adventurers must retrace their steps through the barrow, confronting cultists along the way, only to face the cult leader {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas}, who blocks their path to freedom.

entries.name: Factions and Key Players
entries: Various individuals and factions take active part in this adventure, each working toward a unique agenda:

items.name: Alvisa Laufeysdottir:
entries: Loki assumes the identity of {@creature Alvisa Laufeysdottir|NorthlandsSagas|Alvisa} to hire the characters, if the GM uses the call to action below.

items.name: Bolgrim Boar-Scar:
entries: A former reaver, {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas|Bolgrim} belongs to the Cult of Ragnarok.

items.name: Cult of Ragnarok:
entries: A sect of doomsayers who believe Ragnarok is coming. They spread the word of it and work to bring it about.

items.name: Fangs of Vanagandr:
entries: Once an up-and-coming mercenary company, the Fangs have fallen on hard times because of the Cult of Ragnarok.

items.name: Finulf One-Hand:
entries: An impulsive mercenary, Finulf often finds himself in over his head.

items.name: Loki:
entries: A god...no, really.

entries.name: Call to Action
entries: Use or adapt the following adventure hook to suit your campaign or prepare a unique call to action that feels more appropriate to your player characters.

{@creature Alvisa Laufeysdottir|NorthlandsSagas}, a {@creature Wolf Reaver Dwarf|ToB1-2023|Dwarven Wolf Reaver}, represents the Steadfast Company of Mile-Steppers (see {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 3: Factions of the Northlands|NorthlandsWorldbook|3}). Alvisa hires the characters to bring a cache of supplies to Icehavn Rift, an isolated temple in the north of Wolfheim. As payment, she offers 50 GP each, as well as a small box of {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls}.

entries.name: Prelude: A Singular Honor
entries: The adventurers fall asleep on the road to Icehavn Rift. In a shared magical dream, they meet the god Loki. The deity offers them the chance to become epic heroes if they help recover {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas}, a relic stolen from Icehavn by the thief {@creature Finulf One-Hand|NorthlandsSagas}. Upon waking, the characters discover that each of them has received a magical Runestone as a sign of their oath.

entries.name: The Road North
entries: {@i Cold wind. Flicking campfire. Beady-eyed ravens roost on high branches of shadowy trees.}
This sheltered campsite finds regular use from travelers along the northern road. Read or paraphrase the following description:

A circle of high boulders on the side of the road offers some shelter from the night. Moonlight filters coldly through the branches of tall oaks that overhang the campsite. In the distance, a wolf howls. Nothing moves on the packed dirt of the road stretching into the darkness to the north.
Allow the characters to make camp and interact with each other as they wish. The ravens in the trees, easily startled, fly away if approached but soon return to watch the camp.

entries.name: Evening Falls
entries: After the characters have settled themselves for the night, setting watches or making whatever preparations desired, read or paraphrase the following description:
As the moon rises, a strange mist fills the campsite until everything seems shrouded in drifting clouds of gray.

Someone strides from the gloom: a towering, youthful figure, breathtakingly attractive and easily eight feet tall. This individual's sheer presence strikes like a blow, announcing without words that this is a god.

The god grins charmingly. "Rejoice, Mortals!" they say in a voice both young and endless. "I bring glad tidings. Your names are written in the great loom of the Norns as chosen for a heroic destiny—if you have the courage and will to seize it. I am Loki, child of the giant Farbauti, blood-sworn to Wotan. Known as a trickster and shape-shifter. At times I have both troubled and aided the gods, it is true."

The deity's cheerful demeanor turns serious. "Now, however, I have learned of a foul plot to awaken Fenris, the Great Wolf, and trigger Ragnarok before its proper time. Personally, I have no wish to die. Nor, I suspect, do you. So together, you and I will save the world!"
See the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13} for Loki's NPC description.

entries.name: Talking to Loki
entries: Loki pretends to know everything and enjoys acting mysterious and sly. However, while the god holds many secrets, they are not omnipotent. They want the characters' aid, so while they may downplay the dangers involved, they share what they know:

items: A sect of the Cult of Ragnarok called the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin planned to assault the Icehavn Rift temple to acquire a relic called {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas}. However, yesterday, on the eve of their attack, a thief named {@creature Finulf One-Hand|NorthlandsSagas} stole the item.
Loki has learned that Finulf flees toward what he believes is a safe haven, a hideout in a nearby barrow.
The god offers the PCs the chance to embark on a heroic destiny. All they need to do is enter the barrow and recover the relic before the apostles get their hands on the thief or the item.
The shears play some role in the plan to awaken Fenris.
Once the group has {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} and stands under open sky, they can call upon Loki. The god will arrive to retrieve the relic from them.

entries: The characters can consider what they know about the information they hear from the god:

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check:
entries: The Cult of Ragnarok, a broad name for dozens of sects of cultists, preaches that the End Times are almost here. Rumors say the cult performs dark rituals and enacts plans to hasten the arrival of the End.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: Speaking to any deity is a great honor. Loki is a god of trickery. Despite the god's fated involvement in Ragnarok, they aren't a dark deity—merely unpredictable.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check:
entries: Uror is the name of one of the Norns, weavers of fate. In tales, Uror is the Norn associated with the past.

entries.name: Questioning a God
entries: Some deities might consider a mortal questioning them the height of arrogance, but not Loki! That doesn't mean he reveals the whole truth, of course. Characters can attempt a {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) or {@dc 20} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} or {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check; on each success, Loki reveals one of the following pieces of information:

items.name: The Cult:
entries: The Cult of Ragnarok troops follow a fanatical human named {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas}. A most unpleasant man, even for a mortal.

items.name: The Shears:
entries: The shears were created by Uror, one of the Norns. She uses them to clip the thread of a mortal's life and, I've heard tell, they can cut through any material.

items.name: Dark Gods:
entries: It's possible two of the gods the giants worship support an alliance between the cult and the giants.

items.name: Which Gods?
entries: Oh, well...Bergelmir, of course. Bergelmir is the giant deity of glory, revenge, and domination. Always seems to be yelling, that one. And Angrboda. Yes, she and I have...a history. Fine, fine. We were lovers, and she is the mother of three of my children. But she loathes me. Can't imagine why.

items.name: Reward:
entries: You wish payment to save the world? By successfully keeping {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} out of the hands of the thief and the cult, I shall give each of you 300 GP worth of gems.

items: Challenge Accepted!

entries: Assuming the PCs agree to the task, read or paraphrase the following:
Loki grins again. "Excellent. Well now, the night closes on our time together."

If you are playing with Runestones (as described in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0}), read or paraphrase the following, then invite each player to select a single runestone randomly. The characters automatically know the Least power of their Runestone.
Groups that are not using the Runestones can skip to Loki's Farewell.

"But before we part, I shall bestow upon you a gift." Loki raises a hand, revealing a small oval stone with a rune carved into its flat side. "As you step upon the Hero's Path, this Runestone shall serve as a mark of your destiny and, I dare say, provide some small aid. If you are clever, perhaps you will learn how its gifts grow."

entries.name: Loki's Farewell
entries: Loki's voice and form begin to waver as the god issues their final words to the group:
"We shall surely meet again, Heroes. But for now, fare well."

The PCs all awaken at the same time in a different campsite, among a grove of trees atop a low hill. They have somehow been magically transported. The morning sun has just risen, and each of them has the benefits of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Additionally, if using the Runestones, the characters each find a single stone in their hand.

entries.name: {@color From Here...|4d6381}
entries: Drawn on the ground in glowing lines is a map showing that the characters now stand a mile south of Finulf's barrow hideout.

entries.name: Part 1: Into the Barrow
entries: Transported by Loki to a location near Finulf's barrow, the characters arrive just in time to see the thief vanish into the hideout. The pursuing cultists lag just a bit behind, giving the heroes the opportunity to follow Finulf. Inside the barrow, they navigate through the protective guardians and puzzles. At the barrow's heart, they confront Finulf and learn he stole the shears to keep them from the Cult of Ragnarok. The PCs can choose to ally themselves with him or deliver swift justice.

entries.name: Approaching the Barrow
entries: {@i Cold winds. Rustle of pine, elm, and ash trees. Secluded vale.}
The characters have a relatively easy walk north. After a mile they come to the top of a small rise and see a burial mound 100 feet away, resting in a shallow valley.

The chill northern air feels brisk despite the morning sun as you crest a rise looking down into a small valley. Perhaps one hundred feet away, on the valley floor, lies a burial mound—or barrow—covered in grass and brush. Tall boulders flank a rough path that leads to a pair of stone doors set into the southern side of the mound.
Even as you behold this, a one-handed human man runs around the side of the mound to the barrow's stone opening. He glances quickly toward the north, then hurriedly ducks inside.

The fleeing man is {@creature Finulf One-Hand|NorthlandsSagas} (human {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook}). He has just arrived at the barrow, so intent on the cultists pursuing him that he doesn't see the characters.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC spots a troop of warriors (cultist) moving across the valley toward the barrow. They are still quite some distance away.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recognizes that the cultists pursuing the thief will arrive within the hour.

entries.name: {@color From Here...|4d6381}
entries: {@b Down the Hill.} To the barrow entrance ({@adventure Area 1|NorthlandsSagas|1|Area 1}).

entries.name: The Wolf Barrow
entries: The "Inward" view of the Wolf Barrow map is designed for you to use in Part 1 of this adventure. The "Outward" view applies to Part 2, when the encounter areas have all been resolved.

Once, these cunningly wrought halls used deadly traps and clever puzzles to guard shining gold treasures and sparkling, gem-encrusted cups. Given a new purpose, they now provide safe haven. Yet, will these ancient defenses prove enough?

entries.name: Wolf Barrow General Features
entries: Unless otherwise noted, the barrow is dug from natural stone with ceilings 7 feet high.

entries.name: Floors
entries: Smoothed gray stone. Scattered pebbles and debris from the walls or ceiling. No impediments to movement except where noted.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Stone torch sconces set with flickering magic orbs provide {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for the barrow's interior. One can remove a sconce with a {@dc 10} Strength check, but it stops working if removed.

entries.name: Sound
entries: Muffled, oppressive. Sounds don't travel to adjacent hallways or rooms unless noted.

entries.name: Area 1: Barrow Entrance
entries: {@i Clusters of boulders. Tall burial mound. An open door.}

A field of scrub grass and scattered stones surrounds the barrow. On the southern side, two piles of large boulders flank a faint trail leading to the side of the barrow. There, a set of double stone doors stands partially open, revealing a short hall ahead.
Finulf left the doors to the barrow open when he hurried through.

entries.name: North
entries: Short hall to the void chamber (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 2: Void Chamber
entries: {@i Obsidian floor. Low ceiling. Gravity trap.}

The smooth floor of this rectangular chamber is laid with black stone tiles flecked with crystal. The similarly dark walls and the low ceiling give the room an oppressive aura. Any light streaming in from the entrance seems to gutter and fade as if absorbed by the chamber ahead. A whispering voice says, "Before ice, before flame, there was the Ginnungagap—the Yawning Void."

Finulf entered this room, crossed to the hallway leading to the First Giant chamber (Area 3), then used his {@item Cape of the Mountebank|XDMG} to teleport directly to the burial ship (Area 9). By the time the PCs arrive here, he's already sheltering in the burial ship.
The voice is an illusion created by the room to evoke the feeling or themes of the Void.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC understands the tiles evoke the themes or feeling of Ginnungagap, the void-like abyss surrounding Yggdrasil and the mortal world.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC actively examining the floor notices recent footprints leading northeast.

entries.name: Gravity Trap
entries: {@i Nuisance Trap (Levels 1–4)}

entries.name: Trigger:
entries: All black tiled squares hide arcane glyphs.

entries.name: Duration:
entries: Instantaneous

entries.name: Effect 1
entries: A magical {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB} fills the trap area. Nonmagical light can't illuminate it.

entries.name: Effect 2
entries: Gravity reverses and twists, affecting anyone standing on the area marked by the black tiles. "Down" becomes the opening to the hall leading to the First Giant chamber (Area 3).

Each creature in the trap's area must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw to throw themselves toward Area 1, landing with the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition in an unoccupied space on a success. They can reach only the two side-by-side 5-foot squares at the edge of the black tiles this way. If no unoccupied space is available, the saving throw automatically fails.
Creatures that fail the saving throw fall "downward," landing with the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition in the hallway to Area 3.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: A {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} spell reveals auras of Evocation and Transmutation magic around the floor tiles. As a {@action Search|XPHB} action, a creature within 5 feet of the black tiles can examine them and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check, detecting a tiny pair of glyphs on each tile on a success. Once the glyphs are found, a character can take a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine them and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check, ascertaining that the glyphs mean "Darkness" and "Gravity" on a success.
A PC actively examining the trap can use a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check to discern it will cause individuals to slide into the hallway to the northeast.
As an action, a character can use a sharp tool to deface the glyph, which disables the trap for 1 minute.

entries.name: Reset
entries: The trap magically resets at the end of each round unless disabled.

entries.name: East
entries: A sharply sloping hallway leads down to the First Giant chamber (Area 3).

entries.name: South
entries: Back to the barrow entrance (Area 1).

entries.name: Area 3: First Giant Chamber
entries: {@i Stone weapons. Warlike mural. Statue puzzle.}

This irregularly shaped room has a high, sloping ceiling easily reaching sixty feet at the northern end. In the far corner stands a towering statue of a massive giant warrior. Armored with an inscribed shield and wielding a sword, the titanic figure stands defiantly.

The long mural decorating the eastern wall of the chamber depicts a single giant battling three smaller figures. Their conflict runs from south to north, culminating in the giant's death. In the mural, the three smaller figures cut up the giant's body and use the pieces to build a world.
The statue in the corner represents Aurgelmir, the First Giant. The giant stands 60 feet tall, his helmeted head reaching almost to the ceiling.

entries.name: Investigating the Mural
entries: Characters may be able to determine the story told in the mural.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC identifies the story as the death of the First Giant, Aurgelmir, at the hands of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and his brothers, Vili and Ve.

items.name: Statue's Shield
entries: An inscription on the giant's stone shield warns about the Collapsing Statue Trap (below). You can show the players this portion of this adventure's handout. The inscription reads:
Rattle-frame crafted into stone-teeth tall,
Vein-mead spilled to fill whale-road's tide,
Thought-bowl crowning the cloud-vault's hall,
Meat-hoard spread as Midgard's hide.
When unsealed is the hidden wall,
Sky-shoulders break and pieces slide.
Flee, 'ere the stones fall.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence or {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recognizes several of the words as "kennings," a style of Northland poetry. (See {@adventure Kennings|NorthlandsSagas|1|Kennings} sidebar.)

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: A concealed door is set into the wall behind the statue of Aurgelmir, cleverly crafted to blend into the surrounding stone. If opened, it allows access to a curving passage leading to Wotan's tree room (Area 4).

items.name: {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC opens the secret door. This triggers the Collapsing Statue Trap.

entries.name: Collapsing Statue Trap
entries: {@i Nuisance Trap (Levels 1–4)}

entries.name: Trigger:
entries: Secret door opens.

entries.name: Duration:
entries: Instantaneous
When a creature opens the secret door, the statue in front of the door topples forward, falling to pieces in a shower of debris with a 20-foot radius, centered on the statue.
Each creature in the area must make a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw, taking 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Bludgeoning damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: As a {@action Search|XPHB} action, a creature can examine the secret door and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check to detect the wire connecting the door to the statue. Anchoring the wire in place before cutting it prevents the trap from triggering.

entries.name: Reset
entries: At dawn the statue magically reforms, restoring the trap to functionality.

entries.name: East
entries: A snaking hallway to Wotan's tree room (Area 4).

entries.name: South
entries: A sloping passage to the void chamber (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 4: Wotan's Tree Room
entries: {@i Cliffs down. Stone tree. Strange well puzzle.}

The door into this chamber opens onto an uneven cliff with a set of stairs descending fifteen or twenty feet. At the far side of the room rises another craggy cliff without any stairs. The flat hollow between these cliffs holds the statue of a huge stone tree with wide, thick branches and a granite canopy of leaves. The stone statue of a man hangs upside down from one of the branches. Across from the tree is a round well with a casing made of tightly fitted labradorite bricks.

entries.name: Tree and Hanging Statue
entries: The two eyes of the stone statue are black opals. Only the stone dagger (see below) can remove the statue's eyes.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recognizes the story of Wotan hanging himself for nine days and nights on Yggdrasil to gain the knowledge of runes. At the GM's discretion, a bard or a character native to the Northlands gains {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks to recognize stories about Wotan.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC examining the statue finds an inscription carved into the branch where Wotan's feet are tied. It reads, "I hung for nine nights, sacrificing myself to myself. From the tree came the way. To the well, the price." (You can show the players this portion of this adventure's handout.)

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC examining the tree discovers a stone dagger set between two branches near Wotan's feet. The dagger rests in a slot and can be removed.

entries.name: Northern Cliff
entries: This cliff is hewn from the surrounding stone and rises 20 feet high. Its sheer surface lacks handholds or protrusions.

items.name: {@dc 20} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC climbs the cliff at a rate of 5 feet per round. The character must repeat the check each round; a failed check results in a fall to the ground.

items.name: {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC atop the cliff who examines the wall from 5 feet away spots the secret door in the northwest corner of the room. The door can't be opened by normal means.

entries.name: Stone Well Puzzle
entries: The well's interior drops away to darkness. Much like the tree, this well is also part of Wotan's mythology.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC trying to recall the myth recognizes the story of how Wotan sacrificed an eye to the well of Mimir to gain wisdom. Characters who beat a {@dc 20} on this check remember that Wotan sacrificed his right eye to the well.

items.name: Solution:
entries: The characters must use the stone dagger to remove the statue's right eye and throw it into the well. When this occurs, the well begins to glow with a blue light as a staircase rumbles out of the northern cliffface, allowing access up. At the same time, a secret door opens to the Loom of Fate room (Area 5).

items.name: Trap:
entries: Each time someone throws anything other than the statue's right eye into the well, a murder of spectral ravens erupts out of the stone tree. Each creature in the chamber must make a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw, taking 4 ({@damage 1d8}) Psychic damage on a failure, or half as much on a success. Then the ravens vanish back into the tree.

items.name: Reset:
entries: At dawn the room magically resets, including the statue (growing new eyes, if necessary).

items.name: Treasure
entries: The group can safely remove and take the statue's left eye, a black opal worth 1,000 GP.

entries.name: South
entries: Down a snaking hallway to the First Giant's chamber (Area 3).

entries.name: West
entries: Along a winding hall to the Loom of Fate room (Area 5).

entries.name: Area 5: Loom of Fate Room
entries: {@i Weaving loom. Spinning spindles. Deadly threads.}

Emitting a rapid clopping sound, a ten-foot-long stone loom in this chamber weaves by itself, the shuttle, treadles, and weight stones all moving. Arrayed around the loom, six tall stone spindles spin, spooling and unspooling as they whip lengths of different colored thread in all directions.
Stone statues of three women—a crone, a stately lady, and a maiden—stand against the far wall. West of the statues, where the wall angles northeast, a metal plaque is attached to the wall.
This chamber presents a gauntlet for the characters to run: They must feed the correct color threads (iron, white, blue) into the loom to open the secret door in the south wall.

items: This encounter doesn't involve a monster but is best handled in {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} order.
The area within 5 feet of any spindle is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}; the spindles are arrayed in such a way that half of the room is considered {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}.

entries.name: Plaque
entries: A clue on the wall plaque reveals how to open the passage to the next area of the barrow. You can show the players this portion of this adventure's handout. The metal plaque bears the following inscription:
As the thread-weavers knew
Anvil's Spawn, Mountain's Cloak, Wave's Dew
To the shuttle's beam must be fed
If fate's own path shall be tread.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) or {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recognizes several of the words as "kennings," a style of Northland poetry. (See {@adventure Kennings|NorthlandsSagas|1|Kennings} sidebar.)

entries.name: The Statues
entries: The statues on the south wall represent the three Norns, weavers of fate. Skuld the Maiden stands on the western side, Verdandi the Lady in the middle, and Uror the Crone on the eastern side. Each statue shows a Norn wearing flowing Northlands-style clothing.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recalls the Norns are a trio of goddesses who live at the foot of Yggdrasil tending to the tree and weaving the threads of fate for every mortal. The three Norns are Uror, Verdandi, and Skuld. Even the gods heed them; they feature as truth-tellers and fate-spinners in many sagas.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC notices a small round indentation at the base of the neck of each statue, roughly the same size as the Runestones the characters carry. The first character to place a Runestone against one of the indentations receives a Blessing: {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on one ability check of their choice in the next hour.

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: The secret door in the room's southeast corner can't be opened by normal means.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC sees the faint outline of the doorway behind the three statues.
Use the following information for this encounter:

items.name: Spindles:
entries: These are 6-foot stone spindles wrapped with skeins of colored or metallic thread. North of the loom (from left to right) are gold, red, and iron. South of the loom (from left to right) are ash, white, and blue.

items.name: Slashing Gauntlet:
entries: Moving near the spindles is hazardous. On {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} 20, each spindle automatically hits every creature in its range, dealing 1 Slashing damage. When a creature moves into or within the 5-foot area around any spindle, it takes 1 Slashing damage for every 5 feet it travels.

items: Each spindle has AC 17, HP 32, and {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 10. They are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Piercing damage.
If reduced to HP 0, a spindle becomes nonfunctional for {@dice 1d4} rounds, then magically is restored to full health.

items.name: Catch and Haul Thread:
entries: A character within 5 feet of a spindle can attempt to grab a thread from it and drag it.

items.name: {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC grabs a thread out of the air.

items.name: {@dc 18} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC pulls a length of thread they currently hold 5 feet. They must repeat this check every 5 feet they travel. {@actSaveFail} The character drops the thread, which retracts into the spindle and resumes whipping around.

entries.name: Loom
entries: This massive stone-weighted loom, carved of dark pine and reinforced with iron nails, stands nearly 5 feet tall. Its 10-foot-long, upright frame leans at an angle with a large golden oak beam at top (the western side of the device).

items.name: {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC notices three carved "slots" in the golden oak beam at the top of the loom, each large enough for one thread to pass through.

items.name: Feeding the Loom:
entries: One can feed threads into the loom only from one of the two 5-foot squares directly west of the loom. PCs must use an action to feed a thread into the loom.

entries.name: Solving the Puzzle
entries: Pass the iron, white, and blue threads over the beam at the top of the loom on the western side of the device. When this is done, the spindles stop all motion before receding into the floor. Then the statues slide away from the wall, and the secret door behind them opens.

entries.name: East
entries: Along a winding hall to Wotan's tree room (Area 4).

entries.name: South
entries: Through a rough-hewn passage to the Bifrost room (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 6: Bifrost Room
entries: {@i Broken bridge. Deadly pit. Color puzzle}

The western side of this mostly rectangular chamber plunges into a deep pit filled with moving wisps of shadow. Many crystal shards in various colors hang on slender threads from the ceiling above the eastern landing.

To the north, a wall mural depicts Northlands gods standing upon a bridge of shining light that ends, as if broken, with glittering fragments falling below—where the snarling maw of a shadowy dragon awaits.
Below the mural sits a stone arch set with seven empty sockets. The arch frames a metal wall plaque.

entries.name: Crystal Shards
entries: Hanging from the ceiling on threads are 14 colored crystal shards: black, blue, bronze, brown, gold, gray, green, indigo, orange, red, silver, violet, white, and yellow. They are in no particular order but cover the entire ceiling.

items: The crystals dangle about 6 feet off the ground.
One can remove them easily, requiring no check.

entries.name: Pit
entries: Drifting wisps of shadowy vapor fill this large hole in the western half of the room. The pit, 15 feet deep, covers an area 20 feet by 20 feet. Its sheer sides lack any handholds or protrusions.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC spots jagged shards of broken crystals sticking up from the bottom of the pit like spikes.

items: A creature that falls into the pit takes 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Piercing damage from the crystal shards and 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Bludgeoning damage from the fall, then must make a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw, gaining the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 10 minutes on a failure.

items.name: {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC climbs out of the pit. On a failed check, after climbing 5 feet, the PC falls back in, taking 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Piercing damage from the crystal shards.

entries.name: Archway
entries: Below the archway on the north wall hangs a plaque. You can show the players this portion of this adventure's handout. The plaque contains the following lines:
The sky-road must rise anew.
Build the storm-beam's path true
Or fall like sun-sparks into Nidhogg's maw.
To solve this puzzle, the characters must take seven shards from the ceiling and place them into the slots of the arch in the following order: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) or {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recognizes several words of the inscription as kennings, a style of Northland poetry. (See {@adventure Kennings|NorthlandsSagas|1|Kennings} sidebar.)

items: When all the slots are filled, if the order is incorrect, the crystals in the slots vanish. Immediately, all the shards hanging from the ceiling plummet to the ground, dealing 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Piercing damage to every creature in chamber. Then the crystals all magically reappear on the ceiling.

If the characters insert the crystals in the correct order, they all begin to shine. A rainbow bridge of light extends from the landing to the southwestern corner of the room, where a hidden door slides open.

entries.name: North
entries: Through a rough-hewn passage to the Loom of Fate room (Area 5).

entries.name: South
entries: Down a twisting hall to the Fenris room (Area 7).

entries.name: Area 7: Fenris Room
entries: {@i Stone wolf, unchained. Four carved pillars. Sacrifice needed.}

The huge statue of an open-mouthed, snarling wolf crouches in the center of this tall chamber, flanked on four sides by carved pillars. A doorway on the eastern side of the room appears to be sealed by a smooth stone slab. A mural on the northern wall depicts a noble-looking man placing his right hand into the maw of a titanic wolf with glowing red eyes.

entries.name: Mural
entries: The painting looks colorful and vivid yet clearly was not made recently.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recognizes the figure as the god {@deity Tyr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

items: In stories, the gods tricked {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, the Great Wolf, into wearing Gleipnir, magical binding chains. But the wolf would only agree if someone placed their hand into his mouth as a sign of good faith. Only Tyr was brave enough to do so. When Fenris realized he had been tricked and could not break free, he bit Tyr's hand off.

entries.name: Wolf Statue
entries: A stone representation of Fenris 10 feet tall and 15 feet long crouches as if enraged, with its mouth open. Very sharp stone teeth line the inside of the wolf's mouth. On the wolf's stone tongue is the indentation of a hand.

items: If a PC places their hand onto the indentation, glowing magical chains appear, wrapped around each pillar, and golden cuffs appear on each of the wolf's paws. The chains immediately vanish if the hand is removed.

items.name: {@dc 10} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC attaches the chain from one pillar to a cuff on the wolf. Each time a chain is attached, the wolf's mouth opens wider, trembling with tension like a coiled spring.

items: When the last chain is attached, the wolf's mouth instantly appears to snap closed on the PC's hand and the character must make a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, the PC flinches and takes 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Psychic damage. In any case, the PC removes their hand from the mouth, physically unharmed. Then the wolf statue curls up on the floor as if sleeping.

entries.name: Blocked Door
entries: This doorway is filled with a smooth stone slab. When all the chains have been attached to the wolf statue, the door slides open.

entries.name: East
entries: Along a straight passage to the trapped hallway (Area 8).

entries.name: West
entries: Up a twisting hall to the Bifrost room (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 8: Trapped Hallway
entries: {@i Stone corridor. Carved jotun faces. Frost trap.}

This corridor consists of a five-foot wide passage connecting with a wider passage that ends at a richly carved set of double doors. Bearded giant faces adorn each door, rendered almost lifelike by the hand of the unknown sculptor.

entries.name: Trap
entries: The doors to the burial chamber (Area 9) are trapped. All 5-foot squares within 10 feet of the doors are connected to a pressure plate.

entries.name: Frost-Blast Doors
entries: {@i Nuisance Trap (Levels 1–4)}

entries.name: Trigger:
entries: A creature moves onto a pressure plate.

entries.name: Duration:
entries: Instantaneous

When a creature moves onto this trap's pressure plate for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, the carved faces on the door exhale a 20-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} of freezing ice and frost vapor. The blast fills the hallway, wrapping around the corner to reach the door to the Fenris room (Area 7).
Each creature in the {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking 5 ({@damage 1d10}) Cold damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: A {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} spell reveals an aura of Evocation magic around the doors. As a {@action Search|XPHB} action, someone within 5 feet of the doors can examine them and make a {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check; they detect a tiny glyph on one giant face on a success. Once the glyph is found, a character can take a Study action to examine it and make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check, ascertaining that the glyph means "Ice" on a success. As an action, a PC can use a sharp tool to deface the glyph, which disarms the trap.

As a {@action Search|XPHB} action, a character can examine the section of floor that forms the pressure plate and make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check; on a success they detect the plate. Wedging an Iron Spike or similar object under the pressure plate prevents the trap from triggering.

entries.name: Doors
entries: {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}) check: A PC unlocks the double doors.

items: If the characters fail to open the doors, or if none of them have Thieves' Tools, Finulf converses with them through the closed door.
See the burial ship (Area 9) for details on talking to Finulf.

entries.name: North
entries: Through the doors to the burial ship (Area 9).

entries.name: West
entries: Along a straight passage to the Fenris room (Area 7).

entries.name: Area 9: Burial Ship
entries: {@i Longship. Trapped thief. Plot twist!}

Inside the heart of the barrow, a wooden longship rests on stone supports, with a stone sarcophagus in the middle of the ship. Though the vessel lacks mast and oars, the sides of the ship still bear rows of shields, and a dragon figurehead rises from its prow. On the eastern side of the room, a set of stone steps leads up to the deck.
No sooner do you enter the chamber when a voice from the ship calls out, "Not a step farther! I'll bring this whole barrow down on our heads!"

When the characters arrive, Finulf assumes they belong to the Cult of Ragnarok. He has no knowledge of Loki's involvement and probably wouldn't believe it if he did know. Yet he seems willing to talk, hoping to gain some sort of advantage.
He lied about being able to collapse the barrow, but he hopes his foes don't know that. A slim hope, to be sure, but better than nothing.

{@creature Finulf One-Hand|NorthlandsSagas|Finulf} (a human {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook}) takes shelter inside the longship, using the high prow and rail shields as {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover}. If attacked, he uses {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Full Cover} to his advantage, forcing his foes to come up onto the deck one by one to face him. Finulf attempts to talk but fights if left with no other choice. See the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|12} for his NPC description.

entries.name: Talking to Finulf
entries: The adventurers must convince him that they do not belong to the Cult of Ragnarok. While they aren't there to rescue him, he quickly tries to make a deal with them once they convince him of their neutrality.

items.name: {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) or {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC convinces Finulf that they do not belong to the cult.

items: If they have attacked or injured him, any character has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on this check.

entries: Once convinced, Finulf offers an alliance. By now the cultists pursuing him have arrived in the barrow. If the party helps him escape from the Cult of Ragnarok, he will give them the shears. If they agree, he freely shares the following:

items: He belongs to the Fangs of Vanagandr, a mercenary company fighting the cult.

The cult murdered one of the other Fangs, who was bringing back information about {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas}. It is said they can cut through anything, but after you use them once, they vanish. He's not sure why the cult wants them.
Finulf beat the cult to the temple and stole the shears first.
The cult caught him as he was leaving—a whole squad led by {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas}, a particularly nasty individual.

He managed to escape but the cult pursued him, so he fled toward the barrow, which the Fangs found and cleared out long ago. They used the already formidable defenses to make the site a safe house. Finulf planned to leave {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} on the longship using his {@item Cape of the Mountebank|XDMG} to avoid the traps. But since the characters got through all the traps, that plan won't work anymore.

The cultists are now in the barrow, and Finulf can't use his magical {@item Cape of the Mountebank|XDMG} until tomorrow (besides it won't carry all of them, anyway). They have to get out the hard way.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Finulf offers a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} of {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB} to a PC spellcaster who can use it to hide everyone when they emerge from the barrow.

items: If Finulf dies here, the PCs can find his gear, one {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG} per PC (see the {@adventure Need a Rest?|NorthlandsSagas|1|Need a Rest?} sidebar), plus {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} (see the Appendix).
The sarcophagus on the longship is empty but trapped. Finulf warns any character who attempts to open it.

items.name: {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC removes the lid of the sarcophagus, triggering a {@spell Fireball|XPHB} spell centered on the sarcophagus

entries.name: South
entries: Through the doors into the trapped hallway (Area 8).

entries.name: Need a Rest?
entries: By this point, the characters may be in serious need of a rest. A {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} is fine but Finulf warns them against taking a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, since it gives the cultists more time to get into position. He gives each of them a {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG} (one per PC) if they need convincing. If pushed, he tells them that the magic well in the barrow can provide healing and even restore spell slots, if they can get to it (see {@adventure Area 4: Wotan's Tree Room|NorthlandsSagas|1|Area 4: Wotan's Tree Room} in Part 2 of the adventure).

If the characters decide to take a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in the buried ship chamber, they can do so undisturbed. However, in Part 2, they find signs of the cultists' activity—doors that are closed, tracks, etc. The PCs can never have surprise, and all foes get {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on their first attack in each encounter.

entries.name: Kennings
entries: In a kenning, two words (often connected by a hyphen) become a compound word that replaces a noun. For example, "oar-steed" is a kenning for ship. For more information, see {@variantrule Flyting Rules|NorthlandsWorldbook|Kennings} in the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 7: Running Northlands Campaigns|NorthlandsWorldbook|7}.

At the GM's discretion, a bard or a character native to the Northlands recognizes some of the clues as kennings but does not necessarily know what they mean. Such characters also grant {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on ability checks if the players need help discerning the meaning behind the kennings.
The table below translates the kennings in this adventure.

entries.name: Part 2: Escape from the Barrow
entries: Now that they have the shears, the characters—and perhaps Finulf—make their way back through the barrow. They encounter cultists along the way; unless they had a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} in the buried ship chamber (Area 9), the cultists don't know they entered the barrow before them, so they are in for a surprise. At the climax, the cult leader {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} becomes their final obstacle to achieving their goal.
For this part of the adventure, use the "Outward" version of the Wolf Barrow map. Note that some aspects of these encounter areas have changed since the characters last visited them.

entries.name: Area 8: Trapped Hallway
entries: {@i Stone corridor. Carved jotun faces. Expended trap.}

This corridor consists of a five-foot-wide passage connecting with a wider passage that ends at a richly carved set of double doors. Bearded giant faces adorn each of the doors, rendered almost lifelike by the hand of the unknown sculptor.

entries.name: Disarmed Trap
entries: The trap on the doors resets after {@dice 1d4} days, so it remains disarmed.

entries.name: Whispers Ahead
entries: The cultists in the Fenris room (Area 7) lie in wait for Finulf to emerge but have grown bored.

items.name: {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC hears whispering and a soft clatter coming from the room ahead.

items.name: {@dc 10} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC moves without alerting the cultists in Area 7.

entries.name: North
entries: Through the doors to the burial ship (Area 9).

entries.name: West
entries: Along a straight passage to the Fenris room (Area 7).

entries.name: Area 7: Fenris Room
entries: {@i Sleeping stone wolf, chained. Four carved pillars. Foes!}

The huge statue of a sleeping wolf is curled up in the middle of this chamber, bound with golden chains connecting to four pillars arrayed around it. On the northern wall, the mural now shows a titanic wolf with broken chains around it laying waste to a celestial city.

Two cult {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} hide, rolling dice against the western side of the wolf statue. The area within 5 feet of the statue is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} due to the chains connecting the statue to the pillars.

entries.name: Questioning the Cultists
entries: If the PCs capture the cultists, they may "convince" them to reveal information. Use this section for any captured cultists in Part 2 of the adventure.

entries.name: {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check:
entries: On each success, a cultist reveals one of the following pieces of information:

items: More cultists wait in the other chambers of the barrow.
The squad is a dozen strong, a mixture of warriors, trained attack dogs, and a few with some small spellcasting abilities.
{@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} leads the cultists. As unforgiving as he is powerful, Bolgrim is blessed by the sign of Inexorable Ruin.
They all belong to the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin.
The cultists don't know why the cult wants {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas}; it is enough that they were ordered to get them.
The End comes, and nothing anyone does can stop it.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The cultists have their gear plus 15 SP worth of hacksilver and a {@item Gaming Set|XPHB}.

entries.name: East
entries: Along a straight passage to the trapped hallway (Area 8).

entries.name: West
entries: Up a twisting hall to the Bifrost room (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 6: Bifrost Room
entries: {@i Rainbow bridge. Deadly pit. Menacing crossing.}

A brilliant bridge made of a rainbow of colored light stretches across a deep pit on the western side of this chamber. Many crystal shards of various colors hang on slender threads from the ceiling above the eastern landing.

To the north, a mural on the wall depicts the celebratory gods of the North standing upon an unbroken Bifrost Bridge before the gates of Asgard. Below the mural, a stone arch holds seven sockets filled with glowing crystal shards.
Two cult {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} and a cult {@creature Priest Acolyte|XMM} guard the far side of the rainbow bridge.

items.name: {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC moving with stealth doesn't alert foes in this room as they approach.

items: When battle begins, the acolyte immediately retreats to the Loom of Fate room (Area 5) to alert the cultists there. Should the acolyte act first, they use their Radiant Flame attack, then flee.

The bandits attack with Ranged weapons. They also attempt to use an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} to Shove a PC off the bridge; the PC must make a {@dc 10} Strength or Dexterity saving throw, getting pushed 5 feet and receiving the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition on a failure.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: In one corner of the room, one of the cultists left a {@item Backpack|XPHB}. It contains {@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB|Cooking Gear}, {@item Rations|XPHB}, a bottle of {@item Common Wine (bottle)|XPHB}, and a pouch of dried meat snacks (scattering these, like {@item Caltrops|XPHB}, gives carnivorous Beasts {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attacks for 1 round).

entries.name: North
entries: Through a rough-hewn passage to the Loom of Fate room (Area 5).

entries.name: South
entries: Down a twisting hall to the Fenris room (Area 7).

entries.name: Area 5: Loom of Fate Room
entries: {@i Motionless loom. Three statues. Ambushing foes.}

A ten-foot-long stone loom rests on the western side of this chamber. Stone statues of three women—a crone, a stately lady, and a maiden—are arrayed around the room. A metal plaque hangs on the angled eastern wall.

The cult {@creature Priest Acolyte|XMM} from the Bifrost room (Area 6) and 3 cult {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} await the characters in this chamber. They either were alerted by the acolyte or heard the sounds of fighting from Area 6.

items: Each bandit shelters behind one of the stone statues. The acolyte uses the loom as {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover}, if they made it to the room.
They all fight to the death.

entries.name: The Plaque
entries: The metal plaque on the eastern wall has changed since the heroes last visited this room:
Threads lie still, the path winds on.
Heroes climb from shadow to sun.
Blades ahead and barking jaws,
Boar-scarred hunts in Ragnarok's cause.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Aside from their gear, the foes have 25 GP in assorted coin and hacksilver, a silver amulet with the symbol of Hel on it, a {@item Slip-Bane Bracelet|NorthlandsWorldbook}, and a jar containing one dose of {@item Defender Honey|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

entries.name: East
entries: Along a winding hall to Wotan's tree room (Area 4).

entries.name: South
entries: Through a rough-hewn passage to the Bifrost room (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 4: Wotan's Tree Room
entries: {@i Cliffs down. Stone tree. Glowing well.}

The door into this chamber opens onto an uneven cliff with a set of stairs descending fifteen or twenty feet down. At the far side of the room, another set of stairs leads up a different craggy cliff. The flat hollow between these cliffs holds the statue of a huge tree with wide, thick branches and a granite canopy of leaves. The stone statue of a man hangs upside down from one of the branches. Across from the tree, a shimmering blue light emanates from a round well.

Unaware of any battles deeper in the barrow, the cultists in the First Giant chamber (Area 3) have sent one of their number and a few hounds to monitor this room and return to warn them of approaching foes. The lone cultist here feels too wary of the glowing well to risk going down the stairs. Instead, he sent the hounds down.
The 3 hunting hounds (use {@creature Wolf|XMM|Wolves}) prowl around the stone tree. A cult {@creature Bandit|XMM} stands on the cliff on the southern side of the chamber.

items.name: {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC approaches this chamber without detection by the hounds. On a failure, the hounds bark in alarm.

items: As soon as the characters enter the room, the hounds move up the stairs to attack.
The bandit attacks with ranged weapons. If he takes any damage, or if two of the hounds die, he retreats to Area 3.
The cultists in Area 3 can hear any fighting in this room. They wait for the PCs to come to them.

entries.name: Healing Well
entries: Characters can lower the {@item Rope|XPHB} and {@item Bucket|XPHB} attached to the well into the glowing blue liquid.

items: Someone who drinks from the well gains the effects of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} (including restoring all lost {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} and expended spell slots). Once each PC (and Finulf) drinks, the glow vanishes, and the water becomes nonmagical.
The well recharges after 1 week, provided the room's puzzle also resets.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Around the neck of each hound is a woven leather collar set with silver spikes (each worth 5 SP). Stitched into the collars are the hounds' names: {@creature Snati (Sniffer)|NorthlandsSagas|Snati} "Sniffer", {@creature Bjarki (Little Bear)|NorthlandsSagas|Bjarki} "Little Bear", and {@creature Tosti (Stout)|NorthlandsSagas|Tosti} Tosti "Stout."

entries.name: South
entries: Down a snaking hallway to the First Giant's chamber (Area 3).

entries.name: West
entries: Along a winding hall to the Loom of Fate room (Area 5).

entries.name: Area 3: First Giant Chamber
entries: {@i Broken statue. Warlike mural. Guarded exit.}
This room's high, sloping ceiling easily reaches sixty feet high at the northern end. Stone weapons adorn one wall, and chunks of a broken, titanic statue lie strewn across the floor.
A long mural decorating the eastern wall of the chamber depicts different giants—frost, fire, stone, and larger jotuns—fleeing from three charging gods: Wotan, Thor, and Tyr.

The last group of the advance squad Bolgrim dispatched into the barrow lurk in this chamber, waiting to ambush Finulf if he makes it past the other cultists. Unless informed by the bandit fleeing Wotan's tree room (Area 4), they don't realize the characters are about to arrive.
Here, 4 cult {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits} shelter behind the broken statue pieces, as does the cult {@creature Bandit|XMM} from Wotan's tree room (if she made it here).

items: The bandits attack as soon as the characters enter.
When there is only one left, the final cultist tries to escape to the barrow entrance (Area 1) to warn Bolgrim.
Rubble from the broken statue makes the entire chamber {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}.

entries.name: Broken Shield
entries: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check: A PC examining the statue pieces spots an inscription on a fragment of the broken shield (changed from its earlier message):
Boar-scarred rants with war-mouth wide,
One-hand he fears not, nor turns aside.
Stone and fog shroud your guise,
He flees when hidden heroes rise.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Apart from their gear, the cultists have a pouch containing 15 SP and a {@item Potion of Fire Breath|XDMG}.

entries.name: North
entries: A snaking hallway to Wotan's tree room (Area 4).

entries.name: South
entries: A sloping passage to the void chamber (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 2: Void Chamber
entries: {@i Obsidian floor. Low ceiling. Gravity restored.}

The smooth floor of this chamber is laid with black stone tiles flecked with crystal. The similarly dark walls and low ceiling give the area an oppressive aura. Any light streaming in from the entrance seems to gutter and fade as if absorbed by the chamber ahead.
A whispering voice says, "Go then, from corpse-mound to skyfire's hall."

The gravity trap is not functioning and there are no cultists here, but Bolgrim has set an {@spell Alarm|XPHB} spell in the doorway leading to the First Giant chamber (Area 3). A silent signal informs him someone has arrived—he assumes it is Finulf.

entries.name: Bolgrim's Speech
entries: When the characters enter the room, Bolgrim calls from the barrow entrance (Area 1). Read or paraphrase the following:

A gruff voice from outside the barrow calls out. "Come now, One-Hand. You deserve a skald's song for fighting your way from that corpse-mound. But now is the end. Give me the shears, and I promise you a warrior's death. If you make us hunt you down, I will ensure you die from serpent-wine instead of a blade, so only Hel will welcome you."

entries.name: East
entries: A sharply sloping hallway leads down to the First Giant chamber (Area 3).

entries.name: South
entries: Down a hall to the barrow entrance (Area 1).

entries.name: Area 1: Barrow Entrance
entries: {@i Clusters of boulders. Tall burial mound. Final foes.}
A field of scrub grass and scattered stones surrounds the barrow. Two piles of large boulders flank a faint trail leading south, away from the set of stone double doors out of the barrow.

{@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} (see {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|12}) waits here for Finulf to emerge with the last of his warriors: 2 {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultists}, 2 cult {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits}, and 2 hunting hounds (use {@creature Wolf|XMM|Wolves}) hiding among the boulders. While determined to recover the shears for his masters, he won't go so far as to risk his own life. Unless he has been warned, he expects only one thief, so he is ill prepared for the heroes' arrival.
Bolgrim makes sure to stand at least 60 feet from the entrance—far enough away that he can flee if he needs to.

items: The cultists, bandits, and hounds attack as soon as the characters enter the area.
Bolgrim uses {@spell Command|XPHB} ("Kneel before Ragnarok's inevitability") followed by the {@spell Hold Person|XPHB} or {@spell Spiritual Weapon|XPHB} spell.
After casting a spell in the second round, Bolgrim orders his warriors to keep fighting, then flees.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Apart from their gear, the cultists also have a {@item Potion of Climbing|XDMG}, a {@item Potion of Resistance|XDMG} (Cold), and a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} of {@spell Message|XPHB}.

entries.name: North
entries: Short hall to the void chamber (Area 2).

entries.name: South
entries: Up a hill away from the barrow.

entries.name: Recurring Foe
entries: {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} is intended to be a foe who returns a time or two during {@i Northlands Sagas}. This doesn't mean he has "plot armor," but it certainly makes things easier if he survives this encounter. That explains why he flees if confronted with any real danger.

entries.name: If Bolgrim Dies
entries: Should he die, so be it. Subsequent adventures in the Sagas suggest replacements for various recurring characters.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: Once the cultists have fled or been defeated, the characters have (hopefully) secured {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} or put them beyond reach, thus foiling the Cult of Ragnarok's plans. Though the cultists might be in disarray at the moment, their ultimate goal to awaken Fenris remains within reach. Their leaders quickly adjust their strategy and launch new schemes. The PCs' own actions in this matter have certainly garnered attention from several corners.

entries.name: If Finulf Survives
entries: He thanks the characters and acknowledges that he owes them a debt. If ever they need help from the Fangs of Vanagandr, just send him a message and they will come. Then he departs.

entries.name: If the PCs Fail to Stop the Cult
entries: Bolgrim delivers {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} to his master, {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}. Along with their giant allies, the cult uses the shears to cut through the magical chains binding Fenris. Freed, the Great Wolf attacks Asgard with an army of jotuns and giants in tow. Ragnarok begins.

entries.name: Delivering the Shears
entries: The characters have only to call upon their employer to complete their task. When they do so, Loki appears dramatically.

items: If they have {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas}, the god holds out a hand for them.
If the shears vanished after being used, he merely shrugs, saying as long as the cult doesn't have them, he is satisfied.

entries: Once given the shears or shown they are out of reach, Loki congratulates them for a job well done and gives each character the promised reward of 300 GP in gems.

Loki gives a lanky grin and says, "This worked out splendidly, much better than I assumed, if I'm being honest. You've put your thumb in the cult's eye, but they won't be stopped so easily. I trust I can rely upon you in this matter?

"Whether you aid me for glory or hacksilver or altruism—or because I am a deity—I care not. We are all at risk, divine and mortal alike. Ragnarok must be stopped, and so we shall combine forces. You, the plucky mortal adventurers with your blades and spells, and I, the devilishly handsome and clever divine being. Together, we will do great things...oh, and save the world, of course."

The god traces a sigil in the air, which glows faintly. "Be on the lookout for my rune, my friends. One of my minions shall contact you soon, or perhaps I shall once again grace you with my presence. Until then...ta!"
Then the god is gone.

entries.name: Further Adventures
entries: The characters reach a nearby settlement to rest and spend their hard-earned loot. They may even want to proceed to Icehavn Rift with their supplies (assuming they don't realize their employer, {@creature Alvisa Laufeysdottir|NorthlandsSagas|Alvisa}, was Loki.) Soon enough, however, a bald werekin named {@creature Hekja No-Curl|NorthlandsSagas} arrives with a message asking them to come to the Haamu Hills region to help thwart another Cult of Ragnarok plan. The letter she carries bears the distinctive mark of Loki...
But that is a story told in {@adventure Ogre's Run|NorthlandsSagas|2}, the next adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}.

data.name: Ogre's Run
entries: {@i Ogre's Run} is a first-tier adventure for a party of four to five 2nd-level player characters, though you can adjust it to accommodate more or fewer players. The story features a wilderness environment, a ruined fortress, and a thrilling chase. It takes place in the Northlands near a region known as the Haamu Hills, but feel free to transplant it into a location of your choice.

At the end of the adventure, the characters should reach 3rd level. If this is the first adventure you're playing in the Sagas, refer back to {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0} for important backstory.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: The giants are no friends of {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and the other Aesir—they hold the gods responsible for slaying the First Giant Aurgelmir. Most, however, seem content simply to raid the occasional human or dwarf community, focusing their vengeance on their temples and priests. One faction of Jotunheim is much more ambitious, though. Called Blodgjold or "Blood Reckoning," this group seeks to bring down the gods as revenge for killing their progenitor by hastening the arrival of Ragnarok. The leader of the Blood Reckoning is {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}, a jotun. Once the Aesir have fallen, he and his kin once again will rule creation as they did long, long ago. (See {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 3: Factions of the Northlands|NorthlandsWorldbook|3}, for more on the Blood Reckoning and its leader.)

One aspect of the alliance between Blood Reckoning and the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin—one sect of the powerful Cult of Ragnarok—involves sharing resources that might advance their mutual goals. {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} has learned the giants of Jotunheim have captured one of his agents. {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas}, a {@creature Ratatosk|ToB1-2023} longship captain, possesses a great deal of information about the various forces working against the cult and even knows some of the trickster god's plans. The giants plan to hand Kosktup over to the cult as part of their alliance. Should the cultists extract what the ratatosk knows, the growing resistance against the cult could crumble.

entries.name: Sagas Connections
entries: This is the second scenario in the Sagas adventure path. If you played through {@adventure Down the Wolf Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1}, and {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas|Bolgrim} died, the cult sends another warrior named {@creature Rota Slit-Throat|NorthlandsSagas} (using Bolgrim's stat block) as its representative to collect Kosktup. For those following the campaign arc, after finishing this adventure, the players proceed to {@adventure Among the Norns|NorthlandsSagas|3}.

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: This adventure consists of three distinct parts in which the party faces challenges and consequences.

entries.name: Part 1: To Rescue a Ratatosk
entries: The characters are hired to sail aboard Kosktup's longboat, {@i Sly Raven}, to a lonely stretch of beach along the western coast of the Haamu Hills. From there, they travel overland to an encampment of giantfolk forces—mainly gnolls, trollkin, and ogres—to rescue Kosktup. Meanwhile, Kosktup's crew sails south to a meeting spot to wait for them. After traveling to the ruined keep where some ogres hold Kosktup, the PCs have several methods at their disposal to rescue him—but that is only half the battle. Their foes discover the rescue before they get too far, and the alarm horns ring out.

entries.name: Part 2: The Getaway
entries: With their new friend in hand, the characters flee toward their rendezvous point and the waiting ship. The ogres send their forces out to search the land while they alert the giants and the nearby cultists. The PCs must escape the area without drawing the attention of the searching enemy troops, who greatly outnumber the heroes. Avoiding the ranging bands of marauders scouring the area takes skill and cunning. When they reach the river, they face a final confrontation with the great ogre leader.

entries.name: Part 3: Ice River Chase
entries: The ice-choked, but still flowing, waters are the quickest and most direct path back to {@i Sly Raven}, which awaits the characters at the river's mouth. At this point, a chase ensues, with the PCs attempting to navigate the icy river with the giants' minions in hot pursuit. The party also must traverse some nasty rapids before finally sighting their waiting longboat.

entries.name: Factions and Key Players
entries: Several factions in this adventure actively work toward their own agenda. They are summarized here:

items.name: Blood Reckoning:
entries: A faction of giants from Jotunheim, led by the jotun {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}, who seek the destruction of the gods. They have allied with the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin to free Fenris the Great Wolf and bring about Ragnarok.

items.name: Bolgrim Boar-Scar:
entries: An agent from the Cult of Ragnarok who arrives soon to take possession of the captive longboat captain.

items.name: Cult of Ragnarok:
entries: A sect of a doomsayers and misanthropes who believe Ragnarok is coming and work to spread the word and/or bring it about. Within this cult are the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin, a sect run by {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}. Like the Blood Reckoning, they seek to free Fenris.

items.name: Gratch Bad-Howl:
entries: A bugbear warrior who dreams of being a skald.

items.name: Kosktup Farleap:
entries: A ratatosk longboat captain, adventurer, and messenger of Loki. Currently, an unwilling guest of the Blood Reckoning ogres.

items.name: Skrolmuk:
entries: A great ogre who leads the giant forces at the fort.

entries.name: Call to Action
entries: In a letter marked with Loki's rune, a sailor named {@creature Hekja No-Curl|NorthlandsSagas} asks the characters for help. Hekja's longship captain, {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas}—a ratatosk smuggler, adventurer and sometimes agent of Loki—has been captured by a giant faction called the Blood Reckoning. These giants plan on handing Kosktup over to the Cult of Ragnarok as part of their alliance.

The task before the PCs is imperative: Rescue Kosktup from the ogres before they deliver him to the cult. Should the Cult of Ragnarok gain possession of the ratatosk, they will squeeze him for everything he knows. This would destroy the nascent resistance to the Blood Reckoning and their cultish allies, the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin. Once the heroes and Kosktup have boarded, the longship will sail to Stannasgard, where Hekja's agents will pay the group its due reward: the sum of 1,500 GP.
If they agree, Hekja invites the characters to meet her and the rest of {@i Sly Raven}'s crew at a nearby port or natural harbor; they will travel together to the western Haamu Hills.

entries.name: Alternate Adventure Hook
entries: If you are not running this as part of the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, assume Hekja finds the heroes on her own and offers the above reward for the return of her captain.

entries.name: Part 1: To Rescue a Ratatosk
entries: The characters arrive in the wilderness along the western coast of the Northlands and make their way overland toward a ruined keep. There, a group of the Blood Reckoning giantfolk (ogres, trolls, and trollkin) hold {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} while awaiting the imminent arrival of the Cult of Ragnarok representatives. After rescuing the ratatosk, the PCs travel only a short distance before the giantfolk discover the escape and give chase.

entries.name: The Haamu Hills
entries: {@i Lonely coastline. Ice and snow. Sea birds calling.}
