{@i Sly Raven} grounds to a halt on the pebbled shore lapped by icy waters. The battered old longboat rests in a sheltered inlet along a rough coastline, which rises into rocky cliffs that grow into snow-covered hills farther inland. Dotting the waves, floes of blue-white ice drift on the sea.

The crew has pulled the ratatosk's longboat up on the shore. A few burly human crewmembers hold it in place by a while the characters disembark with {@creature Hekja No-Curl|NorthlandsSagas}, a bald werekin and Kosktup's second-in-command.

entries.name: Hekja
entries: The sailor (werekin {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM}) takes the time to go over the mission with the PCs once more (see her NPC description in the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13}).

She provides the group with a map that shows where the Blood Reckoning hold Kosktup prisoner: the crumbling ruins of an old fort. (Give the players the handout for this adventure.) The map also illustrates their current location and the rendezvous point at the mouth of the Ice River.
Hekja instructs them to gain possession of Kosktup by any means necessary and meet back up with {@i Sly Raven} at the rendezvous point as quickly as possible.

entries.name: Questioning Hekja
entries: The werekin relates the following:

items: The prize of this mission isn't some bauble; it's Captain {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas}. Pint-sized, big-mouthed—you can't miss him. The deck feels wrong without his chatter.

He got grabbed sniffing around giant business by those Blood Reckoning bastards, the ones out to destroy the gods and all of us. Soon they're to hand him over to the Ragnarok cult for "questioning." They want the captain's contacts and nuggets of lore about the folk trying to stop the cult. That's sure to mean broken bones, blood, and finally a trip to Hel for Kosktup.
Them's that have the captain are ogres, tundra gnolls, trollkin, and such like.
The captain's patron—Loki, aye, that silver-tongued snake—claims the Blood Reckoning has teamed up with the Cult of Ragnarok to crack old Fenris free. That means the end of the world, by the way.
You're heading into the Haamu Hills: giant country. No safe harbor, no friendly faces. Just giants, wolves, and lots of ways to die until you get back to the ship.

The ogres holed up in an old ruin two hours east of here, waiting to hand Kosktup over to the cultists. That's your window. Get there before the handoff and snatch the captain out from under them. But don't dawdle—by my reckoning, the cultists should arrive today, so you don't have much time.
Once you've got Kosktup free, take him south till you strike the river, then follow it downstream. I'll have {@i Sly Raven} waiting at the mouth of the river, sails ready to get us away.
Alive or dead, just bring the captain home.

entries.name: Reward
entries: Once Hekja is back aboard, the ship sails for Stannasgard, where the characters will receive their cash reward. If any of them is lost or killed on the mission, Hekja promises to pass on their share of the reward to any next of kin or beneficiaries the characters name.
Once the group agrees, the werekin urges them to make all haste toward the ruined fort. As they head inland, Hekja is already putting the ship back out to sea.

entries.name: Journey to the Fort
entries: Once the characters go ashore, their journey overland is designed to be uneventful, as they will have much to contend with after they reach the fort. They have a two-hour hike overland through rocky foothills to reach their destination. Thematically, the trip should feel dangerous and increasingly risky. Roll a {@dice d10} two or three times on the Haamu Hills Sights & Sounds table, presenting the results between descriptions of the march to keep tensions high.

entries.caption: Haamu Hills Sights & Sounds
rows: A pair of large wolves walk a ridge line a few miles away, backlit against the sky.
A cairn of giant's bones sits bleached by sun and storm.
Old sled marks and mammoth tracks bisect the path, leading northward.
A broken spear of unnatural size is sunk deep into a ridge.
A boulder sits embedded in the ground as if dropped, or thrown, from a great distance.
An old footprint, far too large for a human, lies ahead, filled with icy water.
A shallow cavern reeks of wet fur and blood from the half-gnawed old bones littering the area.
Claw marks gouge the side of a boulder, sunk deep into the stone.
Ahead, a single black feather, the size of a human, drifts to the ground.
The unnerving feeling of massive footsteps reverberates through the ground, then fades, as if whatever caused it has moved away.

entries.name: The Ruined Fortress
entries: {@i Crumbling ruin. Rising hills in the distance. A timelost feeling.}
After two hours of marching through the snow-shrouded ridges and rocky ravines of the Haamu Hills, the uneven silhouette of a ruined fortress appears on the horizon.
The crumbling keep nestles at the edge of a series of hills overlooking a small valley. Not scaled for giantfolk, the fortification bears little indication of who built it, when, or why.

entries.name: General Features
entries: Once a motte-and-bailey style castle, the fortress looks like little more than two earthen mounds now—one topped by the collapsed remnants of a stone tower, the other holding a number of crumbling wooden outbuildings. The mounds are surrounded by a moat, partially filled or collapsed in places, and the remnants of a wooden palisade behind it.
{@creature Skrolmuk|NorthlandsSagas|}, a great ogre, leads the giant forces here. He and the other ogre have set themselves up in the tower, with their minions camped in the outbuildings below.
Unless otherwise noted, the following conditions apply:

items: Crossing the moat or ascending either mound, except by the ramp or stairs, is considered {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}.
The palisade walls have AC 12; each 5-foot section has 14 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.
When attacking creatures outside the fortress with ranged attacks, defenders use the palisades to gain {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover}.

entries.name: Approaching the Fortress
entries: This section of the adventure begins about 500 feet from the fortress. The area features many hills, boulders, small groves of scrub trees, and ravines. This terrain provides many methods for approaching the ruin without being seen. However, the giants know this, so they have established two additional lines of defense: first pickets, then traps.

entries.name: Pickets
entries: Located in a rough circle around the ruined keep, guards concealed in the brush watch for intruders. The various pickets are all about 500 feet away from the keep, spaced so the characters encounter a sentry no matter which direction they approach from. They must bypass or eliminate the sentry in order to proceed.

Each picket includes 2 trollkin {@creature Tough|XMM|Toughs}, with 2 {@creature Tundra Gnoll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Tundra Gnolls} posted as advance sentries. On its turn, a sentry who gets attacked or spots the characters shouts a warning before engaging in combat, alerting the two closest sentries. They arrive to assist at the beginning of the next round. The shout also alerts the guards at the fort; they'll be expecting enemies.

items.name: {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC spots the sentry before it notices the group.

items.name: {@dc 11} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC can move past the sentry unnoticed.

entries.name: Traps
entries: Between the pickets and the fort, the defenders have set up a number of trip wire traps in the trees and brush outside the fortress. They set these traps to warn the guards of approaching creatures.

entries.name: Warning Alarm
entries: {@i Nuisance Trap (Levels 1–4)}

entries.name: Trigger:
entries: A creature crosses a trip wire.

entries.name: Duration:
entries: Instantaneous

This trap uses a trip wire to trigger a makeshift alarm. The trip wire stretches 3 inches off the ground between two stakes, one of which has another wire attached to a collection of scrap metal suspended from a nearby bush or tree. The first creature that crosses the trip wire pulls the stakes free, causing the metal to clatter to the ground. It makes a loud noise that alerts all enemies within 60 feet.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: As a {@action Search|XPHB} action, a creature can examine the trapped area and make a {@dc 11} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check, detecting the trip wire and the attached metal on a success. Once it's detected, a character can avoid the trip wire easily or cut it (no ability check required).

entries.name: Infiltrating the Fortress
entries: When the characters arrive, the ogres are not present—they have gone out to meet the cultists on the road and escort them back, eager for their share of the price the cultists owe for the prisoner. This leaves several tundra gnolls and trollkin guarding the captive for the PCs to deal with. How they decide to approach this obstacle is up to them. Importantly, time is limited.
The players may come up with numerous schemes for rescuing Kosktup. Three of the more common methods appear below to facilitate gameplay.

entries.name: 1. Pretend to be Cultists
entries: The characters could pretend to be envoys of the Cult of Ragnarok, here to claim the prisoner.

items.name: Gaining Entry:
entries: When talking to the guards, the PC that speaks on behalf of the party makes a Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check against an opposing Intelligence ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check of 11. On a success, the guards let the group into the camp and show them to the captive in the fallen tower (Area 3).

items.name: Complication:
entries: The guards expect an agreed-upon payment. Only the absent ogres know the actual price, but the guards here know payment is due. A successful {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} or {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check convinces them otherwise with some reasonable excuse (the characters met the ogres on the way here and paid them in advance, for example). Failure to provide payment or successfully deceive the guards makes them {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile}.

entries.name: 2. Sneak In
entries: The characters could attempt to sneak into the fortress, locate Kosktup, and rescue him.

items.name: Gaining Entry:
entries: All participating PCs make Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks. Compare the lowest score to the {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB} score of the creatures in the area. Do this each time the heroes would be visible or audible to creatures in a particular area. If the {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB} beats the lowest {@skill Stealth|XPHB} check result, the creatures react as described in the encounter entry for that area.

items.name: Complication:
entries: Some inhabitants of the keep may have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} to detect the scent of other species, such as Humans, Dwarves, Elves, and others. Any guardian who detects the PCs raises the alarm if not handled quietly.

entries.name: 3. Attack the Keep
entries: The most direct method, but also the most difficult, involves simply attacking the keep.

items.name: Gaining Entry:
entries: Dispatch any foe that stands in the way.

items.name: Complication:
entries: The entire population of the camp makes for a High if not Deadly difficulty encounter. There are effectively 12 trollkin and 14 tundra gnolls spread out through the various locations (including the pickets outside the fort). While the characters could handle these foes in individual areas, the longer they take with their attack, the more likely the forces will respond to their alarm protocol and congregate in the common area between the Sleeping Quarters (marked as Area 2).

items.name: Unlikely Victory:
entries: Should the PCs manage to pull this off and fight their way to Kosktup, rescue him, and retreat, they deserve congratulations. Then move directly to Part 2.

entries.name: Area 1: Guards
entries: {@i Creak of leather scabbards. Wet fur. Low growling.}
Figures crouch in gaps inside the weathered wooden palisade, or lean against it, clutching cloaks tight against the chill. Their eyes scan the surrounding area.
A pair of {@creature Tundra Gnoll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Tundra Gnolls} stands watch here. Ability checks to sneak near the gnolls need to beat their {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB} 13.

entries.name: Alarm
entries: If a gnoll sees an intruder, it yells, announcing its discovery to the rest of the camp. This puts the other gnoll guards on alert and awakens the trollkin (see Area 2).

entries.name: Deeper into the Camp
entries: Toward intact wooden buildings on the southern mound (Area 2).

entries.name: Toward the Northern Mound
entries: Climb up to the fallen tower (Area 3).

entries.name: Back
entries: Through the southern mound and eventually out (Approaching the Fortress).

entries.name: Area 2: Sleeping Quarters
entries: {@i Pungent. Food scraps. Cloying smoke.}
This wooden building looks weathered and crumbling. The roof sags and appears on the verge of collapse. A hanging animal hide covers the doorway.
The gnolls and trollkin have set up camp in these mostly intact buildings on the southern mound. While the gnolls stand watch, the trollkin rest and sleep; then they swap.
Right now, 2 trollkin {@creature Tough|XMM|Toughs} relax here.

items: There is a {@chance 50|||The Trollkin are asleep|The Trollkin aren't asleep} chance that the trollkin in the building are asleep. Otherwise, they repair gear, gamble with bone dice, talk, and eat.
If asleep and awoken by an alarm or sounds of battle outside, the trollkin are surprised and don't enter combat until round 2.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The gnoll and trollkin troops keep their personal possessions in these buildings. If searched, they contain:

items.name: First building:
entries: 24 GP, 72 SP, and 101 CP.

items.name: Second building:
entries: 37 GP, 64 SP, 88 CP, and 3 {@item Moonstone|XDMG|Moonstones} (worth 10 GP each).

entries.name: Deeper into the Camp
entries: Toward intact wooden buildings on the southern mound (Area 2).

entries.name: Toward the Northern Mound
entries: Climb up to the ruined tower (Area 3).

entries.name: Back
entries: Through the southern mound and eventually out (Approaching the Fortress).

entries.name: Area 3: Ruined Tower
entries: {@i Trapped steps. A hide doorway. Off-key singing.}

Steps carved into the hillside, reinforced with split logs, lead up to a stone tower. Only a single story of the structure still stands. A collapsed pile of beams and stone tops it like a makeshift roof. Debris from inside forms a barrier around the doorway, which is blocked with hanging animal hides.
This fallen tower clearly looks like the most protected building in the fortress, judging from the reinforcements and makeshift barricades on either side of the steps.

entries.name: Trap
entries: A hidden pit trap protects the base of the steps leading up to the tower. Use the standard Hidden Pit trap, with one variation: Instead of a hinged lid, a tarp camouflaged with a thin layer of dirt covers this trap. Once a character detects the pit, the group can avoid it easily by walking around it and accessing the stairs from the side, or leaving the steps before the bottom if coming from the other direction. Removing the tarp makes the pit obvious for anyone who can see it.

entries.name: Approaching the Tower Door
entries: When the characters approach within 30 feet of the tower entrance, they can hear {@creature Gratch Bad-Howl|NorthlandsSagas}'s attempts at music.
From within drifts the discordant sound of a poorly tuned lute and a rough voice softly singing...badly.

entries.name: Down to the Camp
entries: Down the hill toward the southern mound's intact wooden buildings (Area 2).

entries.name: Into the Tower
entries: Through the hide-covered doorway (Area 4).

entries.name: Area 4: Tower Interior
entries: {@i Ogre stink. Trapped chest. Bugbear with a dream.}

Sometime in the past, the upper floors of this tower collapsed. Now animal hides cover the gaping hole in the ceiling. The floor has been cleared of rubble to make room for two piles of stinking furs acting as beds. A large wooden chest in the northeast corner has numerous holes drilled into it. A bugbear sits on furs in the southeastern corner, producing something he probably considers music on a patched and battered lute.
The ogres have claimed this space, clearing it out and piling rough furs and hides into two beds. They stuffed Kosktup into the chest, bound and gagged, letting him out for only a few hours a day.

Currently {@creature Gratch Bad-Howl|NorthlandsSagas} is here. She should be guarding and keeping a lookout, but (as usual) she has become distracted by her true passion...music. Gratch, a {@creature Bugbear Warrior|XMM|}, finds her "music" so absorbing that she doesn't hear anyone approach.

items.name: {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC convinces Gratch not to yell or raise the alarm. Complimenting Gratch on her music or otherwise showing interest in it earns a character {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this check.

items: If attacked, Gratch yells to raise the alarm and attempts to push past the PCs to find help.

entries.name: Befriending Gratch
entries: Is it entirely possible the characters befriend Gratch and even invite her to come with them.

items: Embarrassed, she tells them of her dream of becoming a bard or skald.

items.name: {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check if a PC offers to take her along:
entries: Gratch seems tempted but needs to return to her tribe first, so they aren't blamed if she just leaves. She offers to help the characters escape, then slip away herself. A bard or someone who offers to put in a good word for Gratch in Skaldholm or at another bardic college enjoys {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this check.

items: If befriended first, Gratch freely tells the characters the information listed in the Talking to Gratch section.

entries.name: Gratch Bad-Howl (Bugbear warrior)
entries: {@i Dirty, mottled orange-brown fur. Underbite full of teeth. Flattened snout and small, deep-set eyes. Patched hide armor with animal skull shoulders. A spiked hammer on her belt. Clutches a badly repaired and poorly maintained lute.}
{@b Background:} A bugbear guard with a dream.
{@b Personality Traits:} Grumbly, awkward, tender when shown kindness (which doesn't happen often).
{@b Bonds:} Her old lute is the most precious thing in the world to her.
{@b Flaws:} Hides her dreams behind a warrior's façade, terrified the others will learn about her music.
{@b Wants:} To become a skald and make beautiful music.
{@b Talking to Gratch:} The bugbear knows all about the activities in the camp and has a general sense of the ogres' plans and the cultists' imminent arrival.

entries.name: {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) or {@dc 8} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check:
entries: On each success, Gratch reveals one of the following pieces of information:

items: The prisoner talks too much, so the ogres tied him up and shoved him into the chest over there, taking the key with them.
Gratch heard one of the ogres boasting that anyone trying to break into the chest would get a bloody surprise.
The ogres are due back very soon. They went to meet the humans on the road and bring them here.
{@creature Skrolmuk|NorthlandsSagas} leads the ogres. He's an ogre, too, but...very big.
If anyone raises the alarm, all the troops are supposed to gather in the common area between the living quarters.
Gnolls and ogres patrol the surrounding countryside; there are signal horns in the fort to alert them.

entries.name: Locked Chest
entries: One of the absent ogres has the key to this locked chest.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC hears movement and breathing from within. If the group makes their presence known, they hear garbled sounds inside, as of someone trying to talk through a gag.

items.name: {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC unlocks the chest (see Trap).

entries.name: Trap
entries: The chest is rigged with a scything blade inside the lid, set to slice anyone who opens the chest without first unlocking it with the key.

entries.name: Scything Blade
entries: {@i Deadly Trap (Levels 1–2)}

entries.name: Trigger:
entries: A creature opens the chest without first unlocking it with the key.

entries.name: Duration:
entries: Instantaneous

A spring-loaded scything blade is hidden inside the lid of the chest. When a creature opens the chest with any object other than the proper key, the blade springs out when the lid is lifted. The scything blade requires every creature in front of the chest within 5 feet to make a {@dc 13} saving throw, being hit on a failure. On a hit, the target creature takes 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Slashing damage.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: As a {@action Search|XPHB} action, a creature can examine the trapped area and make a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check, detecting the mechanism and blade on a success. Once someone detects the blade, they can avoid it by simply standing behind or to the side of the chest when opening the lid (no ability check required).

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Inside the chest, a bound and gagged ratatosk rests on two lumpy sacks. The sacks hold 603 CP and 545 SP.

entries.name: Development
entries: {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas|Kosktup} (ratatosk {@creature Merchant Captain|NorthlandsWorldbook}) looks battered and dirty but still defiant; see the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13} for his NPC description. If someone unties him and removes the gag, read or paraphrase the following:

"Ahhh, sweet air, and faces that aren't attached to ogres! Things are looking up. Let's see now. No cowls, no monologues, no brooding ennui. You don't have the look of cultists, so I'm guessing you're here for rescue or loot—or both! No matter: Kosktup Farleap, newly un-chest-ed and free, at your service. Now...are we running, fighting, or doing something foolish and daring?"

entries.name: Out of the Tower
entries: Through the hide-covered doorway and back outside the fallen tower (Area 3).

entries.name: Escaping With Kosktup
entries: Whatever means the characters use to acquire the ratatosk, once they have Kosktup, they can leave the fort by sneaking, bluffing, fighting, or some other method. Characters who have Gratch with them have a much easier time.

items: If they bluffed their way in, they automatically succeed on checks to fool the gnolls and trollkin on the way out.
If they snuck in, Gratch distracts the guards at an exit, allowing the characters to succeed automatically at sneaking past.
If they fought their way in, Gratch fights alongside them on the way out.

entries.name: Complication
entries: Ten minutes after the characters travel past the line of pickets, {@creature Skrolmuk|NorthlandsSagas} and the other ogre return to the fortress. They march in from the east with {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} and his cultist delegation in tow, only to find the prisoner missing.

They sound a general alarm, sending messages to nearby outposts. The giants are alerted to the crisis and send out their troops to scour the land for the thieves. From this point, the scenario becomes time sensitive. The longer the PCs' journey takes, the more time the giants and their servants have to track down the party and kill or capture them.

The retreat from the ruined fortress goes relatively smoothly, and soon the sight of the fort is lost as the route leads south through hilly terrain. Suddenly, a deep, resonating horn blast carries across the hills. It is the first of four long notes that echo across the rocky hilltops. Moments later, the same four notes sound again, but from a greater distance off to the left. Then again, from the right, and farther still. It seems the enemy has discovered the prisoner's escape.

entries.name: Part 2: The Getaway
entries: The characters and Kosktup proceed southeast, following the crude map Hekja gave them. They overcome a number of possible encounters with pursuers, depending on how long they take as they flee. Finally, the group reaches an icy river: their path to rendezvous with the ship.

entries.name: The Closing Net
entries: The ogre horns warn other outposts of enemies in their territory and call out the giants' forces to hunt them down. As more groups answer the call, allow the characters to make a {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check. On a success, they quickly realize there are enemy forces on three sides, but a narrow path to freedom lies to the south—the only direction from which they heard no horns. Traveling south also takes them to the river flowing southwest to the ship that awaits them.

entries.name: Travel Pace
entries: It takes the PCs 2 hours to reach the river at a {@table Travel Pace|XPHB|Normal Pace}, 90 minutes at a {@table Travel Pace|XPHB|Fast Pace}, or 3 hours at a {@table Travel Pace|XPHB|Slow Pace}. Note the game effects for the travel pace the party chooses, below. The intensity of pursuit means that time is of the essence. The longer the group spends out in the open, the more time the giants' forces have to track them down.

items.name: Fast Pace:
entries: The PCs have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}) and Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks.

items.name: Normal Pace:
entries: The PCs have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks.

items.name: Slow Pace:
entries: The PCs have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks.

entries.name: Short Rest
entries: If the characters want to take a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, they make a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check. A success means they find a small cave, sheltered grove, or other hidden place to rest.

entries.name: Kosktup
entries: The ratatosk seems not in the best shape due to his mistreatment by the ogres, but he can keep up with the PCs, or they can carry him. He is Small and weighs 25–30 pounds.

entries.name: On the Run
entries: Every 30 minutes of travel, an encounter occurs. Roll randomly or choose one from the Escape Encounters table. Resolve the encounter according to the description below.

entries.caption: Escape Encounters
rows: {@adventure Tundra gnoll ambush|NorthlandsSagas|2|Encounter 1: Tundra Gnoll Ambush}{@sup †}
footnotes: {@sup †} If less than an hour has passed during the PCs' escape, roll again.

entries.name: Encounter 1: Tundra Gnoll Ambush
entries: {@i Sudden snarling. Claw and blades. Cackling.}
As you make your way between two hills, figures burst from the snowdrifts in front of you, snarling and brandishing weapons.
A patrol of 4 {@creature Tundra Gnoll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Tundra Gnolls} managed to get ahead of the characters and stages an ambush, burying themselves in the snow.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC detects the gnolls before they spring the ambush; the gnolls do not gain surprise.

items: If half the gnolls die, the others attempt to flee and inform their allies of the PCs' last known location.

entries: Should this encounter occur more than once, the characters gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on their checks to detect the gnolls on subsequent encounters.

entries.name: Encounter 2: Trollkin Band
entries: {@i Approaching foes. Green-skinned threat. Parlay unlikely.}
Shouts from behind draw your attention. A group of four rangy, muscled humanoids with greenish skin and long, dreadlocked hair is closing fast, weapons at the ready.
A band of 4 trollkin {@creature Tough|XMM|Toughs} has spotted the characters. When the encounter begins, they are {@dice 3d4 * 10|3d4 x 10} feet away.

items: On their turns, the trollkin attempt to close the distance between the groups, preferring to face the PCs in melee combat as soon as possible.
Once half their number have dropped, the remaining trollkin try to flee to gather their allies.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The trollkin's gear as noted in the stat block.

entries.name: Encounter 3: Ragnarok Cultists
entries: {@i Robed zealots. Apocalyptic axioms. Overeager fanatic.}

A group of humans and dwarves appear over the crest of a nearby hill. At the lead, a tall human woman with close-shorn blond hair and an eyepatch points and says, "They have the squirrel! Slay the interlopers and bring it to me!"

An ambitious woman named {@creature Hrefna|NorthlandsSagas} (a {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM}) leads this patrol of 4 {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultists}. When the alarm was raised, they broke away from the main cult group escorted by the ogres. {@creature Hrefna|NorthlandsSagas} wants desperately to advance in the cult and surpass her rival, {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas}. She considers recovering the prisoner her best chance.

items: {@creature Hrefna|NorthlandsSagas} lets her cultists advance into melee with the PCs while she hangs back and supports them with spells.
Only after all her cultists are dead does {@creature Hrefna|NorthlandsSagas} move into melee.
These cultists are determined to recapture Kosktup and fight to the death.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: If the PCs defeat the cultists, they find 3 {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing} in Hrefna's pouch. They also discover a new journal with a single entry on the first page. It reads: {@i Ways to Get the Better of Bolgrim Boar-Scar}, accompanied by a badly drawn caricature of a bald human.
This encounter occurs only once. If you roll it again, reroll and take the new result.

entries.name: Encounter 4: Giant Goats
entries: {@i Loud screaming. Flashing hooves. Weird eyes.}

The path winds back and forth down an otherwise sheer cliff face. Around the next bend stands a goat the size of a warhorse! It lowers its head, yellow eyes fixed on you, and screams, its massive, cloven hooves pawing the earth in obvious agitation. Bellowing bleats and screams come from three others behind it.

The path here measures 20 feet at its widest point, with a sheer cliff face to one side and a steep drop on the other. The 4 {@creature Giant Goat|XMM|Giant Goats} here are territorial and aggressive.

items.name: {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC calms the goats; they do not attack as long as the party does not advance. If the characters backtrack and find another path, add 30 minutes to their travel time.

items.name: {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC calms the goats enough that the group can pass slowly and carefully.

items: If combat ensues, the goats use their Ram attacks. The terrain makes these attacks especially dangerous. Anyone hit by a goat's Ram Attack must make a {@dc 11} Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the character is knocked off the path, tumbling 30 feet down the slope, taking 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Bludgeoning damage, and gaining the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Encounter 5: Ravine
entries: {@i Long ravine. Rugged terrain. Feeling of desperation.}
Your path is blocked by a wide ravine that stretches into the distance to your left and right.

The ravine measures 30 feet deep and stretches on for a mile in either direction. Some methods of circumventing this obstacle, and their effects, appear below. If your players come up with other ways, judge the effects and time needed as you see fit.

items.name: Climb Down:
entries: Climbing into the ravine and back up the other side requires a {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check, reduced to {@dc 8} if someone affixes a rope to the top of the ravine to help with the descent or ascent.

items.name: Go Around:
entries: Going around the ravine adds 30 minutes to their travel time at a {@table Travel Pace|XPHB|Slow Pace}, 20 minutes at a {@table Travel Pace|XPHB|Normal Pace}, or 15 minutes at a {@table Travel Pace|XPHB|Fast Pace}.

items.name: Jump Across:
entries: The characters can find a narrow portion of the ravine and attempt to jump across. On a successful {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check, the PC makes it to the other side. One who failed by 5 or less must make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw, managing to grab the cliff on the far side instead of falling on a success. Those who failed the check by more than 5 or who failed the saving throw fall into the ravine, taking 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Bludgeoning damage.

items.name: Rope:
entries: If one person makes it across, they can affix a rope to both sides, and the others can climb across. Crossing in this fashion requires a successful {@dc 8} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check.

entries.name: Encounter 6: Winter Wolf
entries: {@i Unnerving howl. Fierce wolf. Winter's wrath.}
A chilling howl echoes across the hillsides. A massive white wolf, tall as a man at the shoulder, lopes its way down a slope, vapor streaming from its muzzle.
The characters' route passes through the hunting range of a {@creature Winter Wolf|XMM}. It has caught their scent, overtaking them with its superior speed.

items: The wolf hopes to take down its quarry quickly, using its Cold Breath when in range, before closing for melee.
The winter wolf attempts to flee if reduced to 25 percent of its {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Skrolmuk's Revenge
entries: {@i Icy river. Angry ogre.}
After the characters have completed their encounters above, they face one final challenge before reaching the river.

An ice-crusted river glitters through the stand of trees at the edge of the hill. At last! Then, with the snapping of branches, a massive ogre stalks out from behind nearby boulders to block the way. "Think you can steal from us? Take from us?" the ogre growls. "We take back. We take squirrel. Take your flesh. Your blood. Your lives!"

This is {@creature Skrolmuk|NorthlandsSagas}, leader of the ogres. With help from the cultists and tundra gnoll trackers, he has anticipated the heroes' path and chanced upon them here. This {@creature Great Ogre|NorthlandsWorldbook} is infuriated by the theft of his prisoner and afraid to fail his giant masters. He fights to the death.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Aside from the great ogre's gear (see stat block), victory over this foe gives the PCs the opportunity to upgrade their Runestones.

entries.name: Runestone Upgrade
entries: When {@creature Skrolmuk|NorthlandsSagas} dies, the Runestones the characters carry begin to glow with a golden nimbus, at the same time that the great ogre's body shines with a matching radiance. A character holding a Runestone detects a slight pull, as if the stone wants to go to the body.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns a power unlike anything they've ever sensed radiating from the body and the stones. It doesn't feel harmful or threatening. The stone appears drawn toward the body.

items: A Runestone placed on Skrolmuk's body immediately improves, gaining its Lesser power (see {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0|Runestones}). Then it stops glowing. Once all the Runestones are improved, the glow on the corpse fades away.
When a Runestone improves, the wielder instantly knows the details of the stone's new power.

entries.name: Runestone Upgrades
entries: The upgrade opportunity in this scene is intended to be an "in-game" way to improve the Runestones, as opposed to something hand-waved or done out of character. Hopefully the heroes realize they should place the Runestones on Skrolmuk's body. If they don't, the GM can describe how the pull toward the body grows stronger the farther away they attempt to go. Moving more that 60 feet away ends the pull toward the body.
If you are using Runestone cards, give the players each the card for their Lesser power.
Should the characters fail to upgrade their stones, don't force the issue. The upgrade can always take place at the end of the adventure as an additional reward.

entries.name: Part 3: The Ice River Chase
entries: The characters reach the river. Downstream lies their avenue of escape, but the forces of the giants and cultists are right on their heels. So the group takes to the fast-moving river in a thrilling chase, riding the ice floes as they jostle and smash into one another. They dodge attacks from the shore and deal with enemies attacking from other ice floes. Near the coast, their ship awaits—and escape!

entries.name: The Ice River
entries: {@i River of ice and froth. Enemies closing in. What to do?}

The path leads at last to the bank of the river. Downstream, to the southwest, the longship {@i Sly Raven} awaits. The river moves swiftly, despite being clogged with ice. Slabs of frozen water creak and groan as they slide against each other, carried toward the sea. The far bank lies some sixty feet across the flowing ice.
Hunting horns cry out very close—immediately other horns to the west answer the signal. The pursuers are closing in. Escape on land seems unlikely. But there is always the river...

entries.name: Analyzing the Situation
entries: With ogres, cultists, trollkin, and gnolls closing in rapidly, the characters are left with few good options.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC hears many horns and, from the sounds of them, many enemies to fight off. As the horns continue and other calls reply, it's apparent that more forces await downriver as well. Fleeing along the riverbank isn't an option.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check if someone takes to the high ground for a better view:
entries: The PC notes signs of enemies closing in from all directions on both sides of the riverbank. Dozens of opponents seem due to arrive at the party's location soon.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Insight|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC realizes the river ice is thick enough to walk on, and that the river is flowing fairly fast. Moving on the ice with the additional speed of the river may allow the characters to reach the river mouth before their enemies close off all avenues of escape.

entries.name: The Chase
entries: The escape down the ice river diverges somewhat from the standard chase rules, as the characters are moving atop slippery ice floes, considered {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. Each round of this highly abstracted chase proceeds as follows:

items: First, the movement of the ice flowing in the river counts as movement for the round equal to a character's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. A character achieves this movement even if they do not move on their turn, as long as they remain on the ice floe.

A PC may move half their {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} across the ice, or their full {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} if using the {@action Dash|XPHB} action. However, if a PC does take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action, they must make a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw; on a failure they slip on the ice or trip due to the ice's precarious and unpredictable movements, gaining the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. Consider this a complication that occurs every round on a PC's turn if they take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action, regardless of whether they rolled another complication or not.

Then the player rolls on the Ice River Chase Complications table. Note that the chase rules call for characters who have taken the {@action Dash|XPHB} action a number of times greater than 3 plus their Constitution modifier to make a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw at the end of their turn, gaining 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level on a failure.

entries: Additional pursuers arrive on the river's banks each round to take the lead, effectively countering any attempt by PCs simply to outrun their pursuers. If the PCs manage to make it through 10 rounds, the chase effectively ends, as they go where their pursuers cannot follow. (See The Rapids at the end of Part 3.) Not all these additional foes join the chase; some take actions from the Ice River Chase Complications table. The actual number of creatures pursuing the PCs doesn't affect the outcome of this scene; you can describe new waves of trollkin, tundra gnolls, ogres, and even giants or Bolgrim emerging from the hills onto the riverbanks, making a dogged pursuit of the party, to keep the action going and the tension high.

entries.name: Tracking Movement
entries: In order to keep a general idea of the PCs' location in relation to one another, use their figurines or other markers in a line along a strip designated as the river. Keep them all within a square of one another, unless one or more move a significant distance ahead (due to faster {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} than others) or fall way behind (losing movement due to taking actions other than {@action Dash|XPHB} or results from complications); move those characters 1 space ahead or behind, as required. This helps determine whether a PC is within range for certain effects or actions, such as rolling a 6 on the Ice River Chase Complications table or attempting to pull a friend out of the water.
You don't have to track Kosktup's movement during the chase. The injured ratatosk decides to cling to the back of one of the PCs throughout this scene.

After 10 rounds on the ice, proceed to The Rapids, below. You should take note of how many {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels the characters gained and may choose to deliver them to the rapids earlier if the full chase seems too much.

entries.caption: Ice River Chase Complications
rows: The ice floe you are standing on hits a rock. Make a {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, you are knocked down and gain the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. If you fail by 5 or more, you fall into the water. (See Falling Off the Ice.)

A {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM} on the riverbank casts {@spell Command|XPHB} on you. You must make a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw, halting on a failure; then, on your turn, you do not move or take an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} or {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} (the ice floe continues to travel down the river, however).

{@creature Tundra Gnoll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Tundra Gnolls} on the bank throw a volley of javelins your way. Make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, you take 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Piercing damage.

A fallen tree creates a logjam ahead. Make a {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) check. On a success, you manage to leap to another piece of ice and avoid it. On a failed check, you don't jump in time; the ice floe hits the stationary log, you fall and gain the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, and you gain no river movement until after the end of your next turn. If you fail the check by 5 or more, you fall into the water. (See Falling Off the Ice.)

A trollkin {@creature Tough|XMM} or {@creature Tundra Gnoll|NorthlandsWorldbook} manages to leap onto a nearby ice floe and keep its balance. The GM rolls {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} for the creature and adds it to the {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} order during the chase. On its {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB}, it attacks.

A distant giant hurls a boulder. It plunges into the river, sending ice and water flying. You and all nearby creatures on the ice (GM's discretion) must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, you take 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Bludgeoning damage and get drenched as if you had fallen into the river. If you fail by 5 or more, you take the damage and fall into the water. (See Falling Off the Ice.)

entries.name: Combat On the Ice
entries: One or more enemies may make it to onto the ice river and engage the PCs. In this instance, the creature effectively joins the chase on the ice, following the same movement rules as the characters. Such a creature uses any opportunity to attack a PC, such as moving on a {@condition Prone|XPHB} opponent, using a Ranged weapon, or waiting for a character to pull themselves from the water after falling in the river.

Stable footwork for combat is difficult with the terrain beneath your feet constantly moving. If the PCs engage in actual combat during the chase, remember that the river ice is considered {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}.

entries.name: Falling Off the Ice
entries: A character who falls off the ice into the river gets drenched in the icy water. Treat the PC as if immersed in frigid water, even after they emerge, until they have a chance to dry off. (A creature can stay immersed in frigid water for a number of minutes equal to its Constitution score before suffering any ill effects. Each additional minute spent in frigid water requires the creature to succeed on a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw or gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level.)

When someone is in the water, at the start of their turn, they must make a {@dc 13} Constitution saving throw to withstand the churning ice, taking 3 ({@damage 1d6}) Bludgeoning damage on a failure. The character then can take an action to make a {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check to pull itself out of the water onto a passing piece of ice. Another creature can use its action on its turn to make the same check to pull a fallen ally up onto the ice.

entries.name: The Rapids
entries: {@i What next?!}
The shouts and calls of your enemies are drowned out by a growing roar. Ahead, the land drops away in a sharp descent, turning the river into a frothing, churning section of rapids.

Entering this part of the river ends the enemy pursuit, as any foes on the ice leap to the shore in a panic when they see the rapids. The giants and their allies on the shore shout in frustration, realizing the river's increased speed makes it impossible for them to even keep the PCs in sight.

However, this does not mean the danger ends. The ice floes, which seemed relatively stable upriver, spin and tilt, crashing violently with each other and the rocks on the way down to the meeting point. The descent down the rapids has the following effects:

items: The characters each cling to their ice floe as it swirls about, buffeted by numerous impacts. A PC must succeed at three successive {@dc 13} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) or Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) checks. On a failed check, they lose their grip and fall into the water.

A character in the water must make a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw, taking 5 ({@damage 2d4}) Bludgeoning damage on a failure. If the PC failed more than one Dexterity or Strength check above, they must make a saving throw for each failed check.
A PC who goes down the rapids in the water becomes drenched in frigid water, for a total of 3 minutes of exposure.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: Once free of the rapids, the characters easily ride the ice floes the rest of the way to their meeting point safely. When they sight {@i Sly Raven} ahead, lookouts on board quickly spot them and dispatch a boat to ferry them over.

It takes 10 minutes to collect them and row them back to the ship, for the purpose of any PCs suffering the effects of being drenched in frigid water. Characters struggling with {@hazard Extreme Cold|NorthlandsSagas} effects quickly receive dry clothes, warm blankets, and hot mulled mead, canceling any further effects of their condition.

The ship weighs anchor and is under full sail and oars almost as soon as the PCs board. As it moves farther from shore, the party can spy figures on the cliffs, their gestures and angry cries—and their size despite this distance—marking them as giants. Several hurl boulders, which splash harmlessly in the ship's wake, as Kosktup plots a course for Stannasgard.
For surviving the ice river chase, award the PCs XP as if they had defeated a Hard encounter. Remember to upgrade the heroes' Runestones now if they haven't already done so.

The trip to Stannasgard takes 10 days, providing downtime for the group to rest and otherwise do as they see fit. When they arrive, Kosktup gives them their promised reward. He mentions that, since they have proven themselves capable, Loki no doubt will contact them for further jobs. As they are all agents of the trickster god, they surely will meet again.

entries.name: What If the Heroes Lose?
entries: There is always the possibility that the characters fail. If they fall in battle in the first two parts of the adventure, the story of these brave adventurers ends there. In Part 3, should Kosktup die en route to the ship, it still counts as a "victory," as his death keeps vital information from the Cult of Ragnarok.

If the PCs return to Hekja without Kosktup (or with the ratatosk's body), they find her angry and disappointed. She cannot blame them, given the trials they faced. In this scenario, she transports the group to Stannasgard, to travel on as they choose. Per their agreement, they receive no reward. (A successful {@dc 16} Charisma [{@skill Persuasion|XPHB}] check convinces Hekja to, grudgingly, pay them 150 GP, or 300 GP with a successful {@dc 20} check.)
This isn't the last the PCs see of the ratatosk, though. If Kosktup dies, Hekja brings his body and a chest of gold to a priest of Loki so the captain might return from beyond.

entries.name: Further Adventures
entries: The characters can spend time in Stannasgard or sail to another settlement to enjoy some downtime. Soon however, Kosktup returns to them with a missive from Loki asking them to venture onto the branches of Yggdrasil, the World Tree, to return a certain item belonging to the Norns. While they are there, they might glean information about the cult and their activities...
But that is a story told in {@adventure Among the Norns|NorthlandsSagas|3}, the next adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}.

data.name: Among the Norns
entries: {@i Among the Norns} is a first-tier adventure for a party of four to five 3rd-level player characters, though you can adjust it to accommodate more or fewer players. The story begins in the Northlands, then continues in the planes on the branches of Yggdrasil; feel free to transplant it into a different location, if desired. It pits the characters against planar trials and tests, with the backdrop of the iconic World Tree and figures of Northlands mythology.

At the end of the adventure, the characters should reach 4th level. If this is the first adventure you're playing in the Sagas, refer to the {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0} for important backstory.

entries.name: Sagas Connections
entries: {@i Among the Norns} is the third adventure in the Northlands Saga. It assumes your players have already completed {@adventure Down the Wolf Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1}, and {@adventure Ogre's Run|NorthlandsSagas|2}. You're welcome to use this adventure as a stand-alone experience, but it may require filling in some context these earlier scenarios would have provided, especially regarding Loki's ongoing conflict with the Cult of Ragnarok.

The characters initially recovered the magical relic {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} for Loki in {@adventure Down the Wolf Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1}, and they rescued the longship captain {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas|Kosktup} from captivity in {@adventure Ogre's Run|NorthlandsSagas|2}.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: The boughs of Yggdrasil, the World Tree, connect the realms of the gods and monsters to those of mortals. {@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} the Trickster has tasked some adventurers with locating the Norns, a group of deific figures who dwell at the Well of Urd—one of the three wells that sustain Yggdrasil and, thus, all worlds. The heroes are to deliver a magical relic taken from them and collect the {@item Mother's Comb|NorthlandsSagas}, a treasure that Loki claims they owe him.

To travel to the well, the adventurers must climb Yggdrasil and pass through a variety of portals to the interior of the World Tree itself. There they reach the Norns, hidden away among the roots of the great tree. They typically do not tolerate interlopers and require the heroes to prove themselves worthy to come before their august presence.

As the adventure begins, {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} approaches the characters. The ratatosk longship captain, also in service to Loki, carries a note penned in the god's own hand and bearing a mysterious symbol that may open the path to Yggdrasil's heart and beyond.

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: This adventure consists of three distinct parts in which the party faces challenges and consequences.

entries.name: Part 1: Loki's Due
entries: The adventure begins as the ratatosk {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas}, an agent of Loki in the mortal world, approaches the player characters. He hires them to take a magical relic, {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas}, back to its owners: the Norns! At the same time, he wants them to collect a debt from the trio of fate weavers. The characters must travel to the World Tree and chart a planar path through its boughs to reach the demiplane where the Norns guard the Well of Urd. Kosktup sails them to a little-known branch of the World Tree on a lonely island in the Lung of the Sea, northwest of the Haamu Hills. Climbing the branch transports them to Yggdrasil. They follow a route Kosktup gave them, opening a portal in Yggdrasil and traveling through it to Jotunheim, where they must survive the frigid cold long enough to locate another portal to take them to a different point on the World Tree. In this location, they defeat giant insects infesting Yggdrasil's branch, then leap to an enormous leaf far below and pass through a final portal to the realm of the Norns.

entries.name: Part 2: The Norns' Trials
entries: Once they arrive, the characters meet the Norns and return {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas}. The Norns offer them a treasure to aid in their quest to stop the Cult of Ragnarok's plans to bring about the end of the world—but they must prove their worth first.

entries.name: Part 3: The Drake's Lair
entries: The Norns require the PCs to overcome numerous personal trials before tasking them with the destruction of a great beast: a {@creature Nidhogg-Blooded Drake|NorthlandsWorldbook}, one of the brood of the great dragon Nidhogg, legendary foe of the World Tree. The drake has tunneled up through the planes from its father's deep prison far beneath the tree and taken up residence below the Well of Urd. The heroes must not allow it to spread its spawn-father's pestilent venom any further.

entries.name: Factions and Key Players
entries: Several factions and individuals take active part in this adventure, each working toward a specific agenda:

items.name: Cult of Ragnarok:
entries: A sect of a doomsayers and misanthropes who believe Ragnarok is coming and work to spread the word and/or bring it about. Within this cult are the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin, a sect run by {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}; they seek to free Fenris the Great Wolf.

items.name: Kosktup Farleap:
entries: A ratatosk longship captain, adventurer, and occasional messenger of Loki.

items.name: Loki:
entries: Blood-brother of Wotan, Loki currently works with bands of mortals to prevent the coming of Ragnarok. One day the god might even clue in the mortals as to why.

items.name: The Norns, Weavers of Fate:
entries: Though godlike in their abilities, the Norns stand apart from the Northern deities. A trio of female entities—Uror (past), Verdandi (present), and Skuld (future)—they embody fate and guard the well of fate that waters Yggdrasill. The Norns consider themselves servants of fate and rarely interfere with the doings of gods or men.

entries.name: Call to Action
entries: The adventure opens with {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} (see the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13} for his description) finding the characters in a settlement near Stannasgard, or another area of the GM's choosing. The {@creature ratatosk|ToB1-2023} approaches them carrying a scroll in a waxed leather case. He also bears an odd—or oddly familiar—pair of shears and his usual confident attitude. (If the shears disappeared following a use in the first adventure, they have magically returned to the Norns' possession; GMs should disregard references to them in this adventure.)

"There you are, heroes! Ears up and steady your tails. Loki, our favorite tricky patron, has a glorious opportunity for you! First, you'll scamper up Yggdrasil by secret ways and return these choppers to the Norns at the Well of Urd. If they serve you tea, try the little sandwiches—they're divine. Anyway, there's a few more tasks there, something to pick up, but Loki delves into the particulars in this letter. Word to the wise: The Norns can be cranky. If they don't fry you for trespassing, they'll test your brains and blades.

"Anyway, I'll ferry you aboard the Raven to an isle with a world tree branch on it. A little short-cut, as it were. Drop off the shears, pick up what's owed to Loki, and maybe a tidbit or two of lore, then high-tail it back. Easy, right? So stow your gear, pick a bench, and we'll cast off with the tide."

Kosktup gives them {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} and a scroll case containing a letter to them from Loki (see this adventure's handout; the message comes into play in Area 1). Then he guides them to his battered longboat, {@i Sly Raven}. Along the way to the ship or while sailing, he chats with them and answers questions.

entries.name: Talking to Kosktup
entries: The ratatosk freely shares the following information:

items: Their destination is about 8 hours away, by sail or oar.
Crossing to Yggdrasil is easy: just start climbing the world tree. After a few thousand feet you'll transition to the planar World Tree.
The transition is subtle—you'll likely not notice when it happens.
Keep climbing to a branch that feels like it's about a mile up. You'll see golden acorns there. It contains the portal you need.

Why do you need portals? So, the Well of Urd isn't in our own world—you've got to cross through a few portals to get there. From the Yggdrasil branch, you'll go through a portal back to the mortal world near Jotunheim, then into another portal back to the World Tree. From there it's an easy jump into one last portal to the well. The portals should be simple to find—look for one in each area you arrive in—but planar travel never goes in a straight line!

I've a new longship that's almost complete at Hvalfell, a village in northern Wolfheim on the River Svart. When she's done, she'll be able to carry us across the waves to do Loki's bidding faster than any ship before her.

entries.name: Alternate Adventure Hook
entries: If you are not running this as a part of the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, Loki approaches the characters in the guise of a robust youth, asking the group to visit the Norns to return the shears and acquire an item they owe the deity (the comb). Loki promises them a "great reward," as stated in the handout, and provides Kosktup to offer them transport.

entries.name: Part 1: Loki's Due
entries: Kosktup delivers the adventurers to the shore of an isle from which they can see a towering world tree. He informs them that lore suggests one must climb up about a mile into the boughs of the great tree before it will open its paths to mortals. But he has a jar of magical honey that ratatosks make for non-climbing folk—{@item Honey of the Sacred Bear|NorthlandsWorldbook}. It will help.

He explains that he and his crew will sail on to Wolfheim to await their return and work on the new ship. If the party cannot make it back there, they will have to find their own way to return Loki's treasure to the god. The captain gives them the magical honey, then wishes them good fortune upon their journey.

entries.name: Time to Climb
entries: The PCs must climb the gnarled bark of the World Tree to travel its planar pathways. See the World Tree map for a section devoted to each encounter area below.

The bark feels rough and tough. Its geometric pattern of vaguely diamond-shaped hollows between thick ridges makes it relatively easy to climb—and to stop for a rest among the hollows. The branch they must reach to access the portal waits 1 mile up. The magical {@item Honey of the Sacred Bear|NorthlandsWorldbook}, when consumed, grants them {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) checks related to climbing for 1 hour.

items.name: {@dc 11} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC takes 6 minutes to climb 1,000 feet toward the target branch. On a failure, the character covers the distance but gains 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level.

items: The characters each must make five successful checks to reach the branch holding the portal.

entries.name: Visions
entries: Scattered throughout the climb are small rivulets of sap.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC determines that the sap of the world tree has restorative properties.

items: Rolling a 15 or higher on the above check allows the character to recall that ingesting the sap can cause powerful visions.

entries: Heroes who consume the sap and complete a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} remove 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level but find themselves beset by visions. These visions may be prophetic, they may represent past or current events, or they may be entirely fictitious—the character cannot tell. Choose from one of the following. Avoid repeating the same vision for multiple characters.

items.name: Prophetic
entries: Visions show the gods leading mortal armies across a great battlefield against an army of fire and frost giants. The earth, scorched and frozen in great swaths, is littered with corpses of jotuns and Northerners. One can hear a bone-chilling howl in the distance; the sound echoes through the character's mind for the remainder of the day.

items.name: Past
entries: The god Loki, the size of a giant, argues with a giant woman with ruddy skin and hair the color of charcoal streaked with red; glowing runes are etched or tattooed in a line down her face. The two shout and rage at each other in an unknown language for several minutes before the giant slams her fist into the god's face, sending Loki crashing to the ground. The god rises and the two stare blades at each other as they catch their breath for several moments. Then they leap into a passionate embrace.

items.name: Present
entries: A group of villagers looks out into a dark forest from atop a wooden palisade. They whisper to each other as they catch glimpses of blue flesh stalking among the trees.

items.name: Delirium
entries: A ratatosk and a dwarf of obviously divine stature sit across a chessboard that is somehow also the world. They drink pure light from tiny glasses as they move their pieces across the board. Each of the characters is represented among the pieces as a pawn.
If they proceed without any stops, it takes a half hour to climb high enough to reach the branch with the golden acorns—the first branch of Yggdrasil.

entries.name: Area 1: Yggdrasil Branch
entries: {@i Tree branch bigger than a longship. Thick, crevassed bark and leaves with golden acorns. A cleft in the bark contains a portal.}

You see before you a branch of Yggdrasil, gnarled, ancient, and mightier than the gods themselves. Though they provided such welcome handholds on the ascent, the thick bark ridges grab and catch at unwary ankles here. At the branch's first fork lies a thick mat of gnarled vines and moss. The meeting point of branch and trunk forms an unusually wide cleft in the bark, deep enough to lose the interior in darkness. The sky, so bright and blue, is nearly blinding. The air feels so crisp that each breath leaves lungs aching.

At the large fork in the branch, a gnarled mass of vines and branches serves as a nest for 5 {@creature Red-Banded Line Spider|ToB1-2023|Red-Banded Line Spiders}, CR 1/4 each. As soon as the PCs climb atop the branch, they burst from the nest and attack.

entries.name: Portal
entries: The deep crack in the bark where the branch meets the trunk is the doorway the PCs need to progress along the planar path. Casting {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} anywhere near Yggdrasil proves unhelpful, as the tree's overwhelming magical aura blots out any other mystical signs.
Above the opening, a flat piece of slate is embedded in the bark of the tree. Faint smudges on the slate look like chalk marks.

items.name: {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recalls that openings in world trees like this one are often magical paths, but that they open and close according to the whims of the tree itself.

entries.name: Letter
entries: Loki's message holds the key to the puzzle of opening the portal.

items.name: {@dc 11} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB} or {@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC deciphers one of the runes in Loki's note.

items: {@i ansuz}, symbolizes deity, or vision
{@i dagaz}, symbolizes breakthrough, or day
{@i wunjo}, symbolizes happiness or bliss

items.name: {@dc 13} Intelligence check:
entries: A PC who knows the meaning of all three of the symbols understands that arranging them in the order aligns the runes to the cryptic line from Loki's message: "Remember the joy of seeing the dawn."
Writing the symbols on the slate in the order indicated causes the portal to open in a glowing spiral of leaves and sparks.

entries.name: Ahead
entries: Go through the glowing portal to Jotunheim footprint (Area 2).

entries.name: Down
entries: Climb back down Yggdrasil's trunk to the ground.

entries.name: Area 2: Jotunheim Footprint
entries: {@i Deep canyon of ice. Frigid, howling wind. Unceasing snow fall. Sky wreathed in darkness.}

Through the portal, all is frozen, bitter, biting cold. Steep, slick walls of ice rise dozens of feet high in every direction, forming a narrow canyon. The sky is black and starless and lets loose an endless flurry of snow. Through the canyon is a wider area, dense snow crushed flat in odd patterns, with narrow gaps lining the far wall.
The first Yggdrasil portal leads to an enormous footprint left by a colossal, ancient frost giant in Jotunheim (see detail map).

items: This entire place is subject to {@hazard Extreme Cold|NorthlandsSagas}. Creatures not {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistant} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Cold damage must make a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw at the end of each hour; they gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level on a failure.

Fire magic is suppressed in this area. Every time a creature casts a spell or uses a magical item that causes Fire damage or otherwise creates heat or warmth, they must make a {@dc 11} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the spell dissipates with no effect, and the action to cast or activate it is wasted. If that spell was cast with a spell slot, the slot isn't expended.

entries: In this icy realm, a {@creature Beli|ToB1-2023} and a {@creature Fraughashar|ToB1-2023} are hunting in the footprint. The beli turns {@condition invisible|XPHB}, and the pair stealthily approach to within 60 feet before ambushing the adventurers with ranged attacks when they spot them amid the snow.
After defeating them, the characters may make other observations about their environment.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC realizes that the canyon the group finds itself in is actually a massive giant's footprint.

items.name: {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC spots {@creature Snori|NorthlandsSagas}, a dark-skinned gnome with unkempt white hair, hiding in the snow in one of the "toes" of the giant's footprint. {@creature Snori|NorthlandsSagas} is clearly freezing. If the adventurers offer him something that helps him warm up, {@creature Snori|NorthlandsSagas} thanks them and explains he has been stuck in Jotunheim for days—he fell into the footprint from above as the beli and its companion were hunting for him. If the PCs will point him toward the portal they came through, he thanks them profusely and offers them a {@item Bead of Nourishment|XDMG} that had been sustaining him here.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The beli carries a satchel filled with four frost daisies: frozen crystalline flowers that emit gentle cold and cannot be melted. They are worth 5 GP each.

entries.name: Portal
entries: The portal to exit Jotunheim and continue along the planar road is at the end of the northmost gap in the ice, in the giant's big toe. The portal is already open and glowing.

entries.name: Escalation
entries: If the characters dally here despite the {@hazard Extreme Cold|NorthlandsSagas}, feel free to light a metaphorical fire under them by giving them a chance to feel giant, earth-shaking footprints approaching. Then they see a ferocious looming shadow as big as a castle tor. Play up the drama of their escape as they duck into the portal just as a tree-trunk-sized club smashes down atop it.

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Through the glowing portal at the giant's big toe to Yggdrasil interior (Area 3).

entries.name: Northwest
entries: Through the glowing portal to the Yggdrasil branch (Area 1).

entries.name: The Winding Path
entries: The planar road offered by the World Tree is rarely straightforward. If you would like to extend this section of the adventure, select one or more of the following scenarios to insert between Areas 1 and 2, and between Areas 2 and 3; the portals lead to the chosen scenario instead of the next area. The same portal you used to enter or a nearby portal in each option leads to the next area on the path.

This expansion presumes the PCs will take opportunities to rest at the Well of Urd (Area 4) and at the abandoned dwarven outpost (Area 7). If your group seems insufficiently challenged, select the combat encounter. If you feel they could use a breather, choose the noncombat encounter.

entries.name: Abyssal Trap (combat)
entries: The portal opens onto a barren, nearly colorless plateau under a black sky studded with sickly green and yellow stars. An enormous ruin of a city is visible in the distance, with few other landmarks.

As soon as the adventurers pass through the portal, a horrid voice cackles and says "Patience begets reward" in Abyssal, and a cage of bone springs from the ground, surrounding the portal. Then 2 {@creature Folk of Leng|ToB1-2023} attack the party, intent on capturing them. The bones surrounding the portal can be destroyed by dealing 30 Bludgeoning damage to them. Reentering the portal leads to the next area along the path.

entries.name: Bargain Time (noncombat)
entries: The portal exits in front of a low hovel in what appears to be a garbage dump. A smiling goblin immediately pops out and offers the characters a number of potions for sale at a suspiciously low price. He claims they are {@item Potion of Giant Strength|XDMG|Potions of Giant Strength} and {@item Potion of Comprehension|XDMG|Potions of Comprehension}.

items.name: {@dc 11} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC sees the merchant is up to something fishy.

items.name: {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC determines the potions are all cursed.

items.name: {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC deciphers the scribbled, misspelled labels adhered to the bottles. They read, "Poshun of Baby-Strong!" and "Potian ov Big Tall Dum-Dums What I Trick Gud."

If the PCs show they are not falling for his scheme, the goblin disappears into his hovel as quickly as he appeared. The portal remains open behind the adventurers, leading to the next area along the path when they reenter it.

entries.name: Area 3: Yggdrasil Interior
entries: {@i Narrow, round tunnels through living wood. Gnawed, uneven walls. Cramped, low ceilings.}

There is no light or air movement in this moist, wooden tunnel. Almost perfectly round, the tunnel rarely rises high enough for you to stand up straight. Gnaw-marks on the walls clearly identify it as wrought not by humanoid hands. A strong smell like that of rotten fruit permeates the area.

Within the tunnels, 3 {@creature Giant Ant|ToB1-2023|Giant Ants} burrow new paths, stockpile food for the eggs, and mind the aphid farms. They attack if they meet the PCs. They are always encountered individually and do not call for help (see detail map).

items: If the characters defeat all the giant ants in the tunnels, additional giant ants burrow through the wood of the tree to reach the tunnels every {@dice 1d4} rounds, as long as the adventurers remain within the tunnels. These ants attempt to drive the invaders out through the open tunnel to the northeast.

The interior of Yggdrasil is a wild magic zone. Whenever a creature expends a spell slot to cast a spell while inside the bug tunnels, roll {@dice 1d20}. If you roll a 20 on the die, roll on the Volatile Spell Effect table in the {@i Player's Guide} (or the {@table Wild Magic Surge|XPHB} table in the {@i Player's Handbook}) to create a magical effect. {@spell Cure Wounds|XPHB} spells cast here always restore the maximum number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Giant ant eggs nestle together at the end of most of the bug tunnels.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC finds {@dice 1d4} intact eggs across the area.

items.name: {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB} or {@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC realizes that these eggs act as a {@item Potion of Growth|XDMG} when consumed, as an action.

entries.name: Portal
entries: The easternmost bug tunnel opens onto open air at the underside of one of Yggdrasil's branches. About 40 feet below the branch, a leaf sprouts from another branch. At the far end of the leaf is a tear, inside which lies an open, swirling portal. Fall damage for PCs jumping to the leaf is halved.

entries.name: Southeast
entries: Through the glowing portal in the Yggdrasil leaf to the Well of Urd (Area 4).

entries.name: Southwest
entries: Through the glowing portal to the Jotunheim footprint (Area 2).

entries.name: Part 2: The Norns' Trials
entries: The player characters arrive at the Well of Urd and must face the Norns' trials—or suffer their displeasure.

entries.name: Area 4: Well of Urd
entries: {@i Endless black lake. Yggdrasil's trunk, looming like a mountain. The three Norns, hard at work.}

Clouds of mist fill the area, muffling sound and drifting slowly despite the still air. Revealed by the parting fog is a shallow, circular pond about two hundred feet across, its waters dark and smooth as glass. One of Yggdrasil's titanic roots curves two-thirds of the way around the pond. In the expanse of sand and shrubs left between shore and tree stands a slate-roofed, three-level cottage of black timbers. The wall-like side of the root nearest the dwelling is etched with carved runes and set with hanging spindles of thread in a pattern so complex, it's almost impossible to look upon.

Three tall women stand near the cottage. The Norns. Skuld, the youngest appearing, kneels by the pond as if about to trail her fingers in the water. Verdandi, the mother, carves new runes into the root. Uror, the eldest, spins thread at a wheel. Without looking up from her spinning, she mutters, "And here they are..."
"...come to the well," Verdandi finishes the sentence.
"Finally!" Skuld adds, cheerfully.

The Norns are deific aspects of fate. Their appearances shift and flow as they move and talk, making their race—even their species—hard to ascertain, but their relative ages remain the same. Uror, the eldest, appears as a crone and represents the past. Verdandi, middle-aged, embodies the present. Skuld, the youngest, appears as a maiden and represents the future.

When they speak, the Norns drop and pick up each other's sentences, appearing to share one mind. However, a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check lets a character note glances and body language the Norns direct at each other and the interlopers, which indicate that they have their own individual opinions.
Any object the Norns stop interacting with slowly fades from reality, and objects they desire spring immediately to hand from nowhere.

The heroes must convince the three to listen to them. The Norns are initially {@variantrule Indifferent [Attitude]|XPHB|Indifferent} and may even threaten the PCs, claiming they will cut the thread of their fate short or carve a grisly destiny for them into the bark of the World Tree unless they depart.
Offering them {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} doesn't change their attitude, but it stops their threats. Uror takes the shears, muttering, "I've been looking everywhere for these."

entries.name: Trials of the Norns
entries: If the characters mention that Loki sent them to collect on a debt or ask about the Cult of Ragnarok, the Norns require the characters to prove themselves in a series of trials; the outcomes will determine whether they are worthy of their wisdom or even to remain in their presence.

The first four trials (below) each call for a single adventurer's participation; the players decide which character takes part in which trial. The last one (see The Final Trial) requires the whole group—but the Norns do not mention that yet. In each individual test, the characters involved find themselves transported to a vision orchestrated by the Norns. While in the visions, any item or tool the adventurers could reasonably want appears in their hands at a thought, as if by magic. When they enter a vision, the adventurers have full health and resources; any injuries sustained or resources expended while within the visions are restored when they return to their physical bodies.

entries.name: Trial of Strength and Trickery
entries: The chosen PC is transported to a vision in which they ride a horse through Jotunheim and come upon a deep gorge with a bridge to cross over. When they approach the bridge, an enormous {@creature Stone Giant|XMM} stands up from within the gorge and proclaims himself Hrungnir, god of rocks. He doesn't look too bright. In between the rumblings of his empty stomach, he calls out that the only way to cross the bridge is as a corpse.

If the character attempts to fight the giant, the powerful creature likely will defeat them. If they attempt to trick or bargain with the giant, such as by suggesting they have a contest, gambling for food, or by bluffing their way through, the character may make a {@dc 13} skill check to successfully trick the creature or bargain with him to cross the bridge. If they defeat the giant, or otherwise cross the bridge, they pass the test.

entries.name: Trial of Wisdom
entries: The chosen character is transported into a vision in which they fall upon an enormous tapestry from a great height. They land at the edge of the tapestry, where the threads look ready for someone to continue weaving them. Touching the threads, the hero realizes that each one is the life of a person they know.

items.name: {@dc 19} Dexterity check:
entries: The PC weaves the threads together in an appropriate pattern. Failure causes the threads to snarl into a terrible knot, impossible to untie.

items.name: {@dc 13} Wisdom check:
