entries: The PC determines how to weave the threads. Succeeding here makes the character realize they are not equipped to make such decisions and should not interact with the tapestry.
A character who successfully weaves the threads, or abstains from attempting to do so, passes the test.

entries.name: Trial of Beauty and Wit
entries: The chosen character is transported into a vision in which they stand in a mead hall where two enormous warriors seem about to come to blows. The hero understands immediately that they must prevent bloodshed. Some ways they may do so:

items.name: {@dc 18} Charisma check:
entries: The PC charms the warriors with their beauty.

items.name: {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check:
entries: The PC sings a song of valor that directs their hostility toward a shared enemy.

items.name: {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check:
entries: The PC insults the warriors in an amusing way, deflecting their anger. A player who comes up with a rhyming couplet disparaging each of the warriors has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this check.
A character who defuses the battle in one of these ways—or any other—passes the test.

entries.name: Trial of Endurance
entries: The chosen PC is transported into a vision in which they appear stuck in a room in a stable with Bygul, one of the large cats that pulls Freyja's chariot. The character hold a large metal file and understands that they must file Bygul's nails—but the cat seems uncooperative. It takes 3 rounds of filing per paw to blunt the cat's nails. Unless the adventurer restrains or calms the cat somehow, they take {@damage 1d6+2} Slashing damage each round from the cat's claws and teeth.

items.name: {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}) check:
entries: The PC calms Bygul enough that he allows his claws to be filed.

items.name: {@dc 18} Dexterity check:
entries: The PC ties up the cat sufficiently that it cannot fight.

items: Bribing the cat with a desirable food, like a fish or slab of meat, distracts it enough that the PC can tend to its claws with no check required at all.

entries: If Bygul's claws are filed before the adventurer is reduced to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, they pass the test.

entries.name: The Final Trial
entries: The Norns grant each PC who passes their trial {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the first roll they make in combat in the next 24 hours or, if they prefer, allow them to redraw their Runestone (see "Runestones" in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0}).
Upon completion of the individual tests, the Norns give the adventuring group one final task. They take turns speaking as they describe the last trial:

A creature of great darkness lies trapped within a cage of roots deep beneath the World Tree: Nidhogg, the serpent-dragon. The hero Marduk contained him within the depths at Wotan's request in ages past. It is said that only this monster's fangs and venom can slay Yggdrasil and bring the nine worlds crashing to their end. Fortuitously, we see no indication that Nidhogg has found a means of escape—but we do see something nearly as portentous. Somehow the beast is breeding. While the spawn lack their father's might, the vile brood claw their way up from the depths, slaying all in their way and spreading venom through the great tree's roots. We three, charged with Yggdrasil's watering and care, cannot abide this.

Descend to the roots of the World Tree, slay Nidhogg's spawn, and pour this skin of pure water from the Wellspring onto the injured root. Once this is done, our magic will return you here, and we will tell you of the Cult of Ragnarok. If you fail, there you will remain for all time.
The Norns hand them a water skin. Then they open a portal and gesture at it meaningfully.

entries.name: Portal
entries: Through the portal to the lair entrance (Area 5).

entries.name: Part 3: The Drake's Lair
entries: In the climactic segment of the adventure, the characters follow the bidding of the Norns to do battle with a foul {@creature Nidhogg-Blooded Drake|NorthlandsWorldbook}. See the Drake's Lair map for each encounter area below.

entries.name: Lair Features
entries: The lair of the drake has the following qualities:

items.name: Darkness
entries: The World Tree's roots here shed just enough light to faintly make them out in the shadows, but not enough for most adventurers to navigate by.

items.name: Sounds
entries: The caverns hold a surprising amount of noise. The sounds of burrowing emerge from within the walls, floors, and ceilings of the tunnels.

items.name: Tunnels
entries: Unless otherwise indicated, the walls and floors of the cold tunnels below the World Tree consist of packed earth. The halls and chambers are 10 feet high, and the floors show evidence of considerable traffic.

entries.name: Area 5: Lair Entrance
entries: {@i Cold earth and stone. World Tree roots criss-crossing most openings. Stench of snakes.}

The air here feels suffocatingly close, the earthen walls unnaturally confining. No light penetrates these depths beneath the World Tree. One of Yggdrasil's root-hairs, as wide as a man, is visible in the darkness, limned in a quiet blue glow.

The portal the PCs enter through closes behind them, leaving them in {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}. The corpse of a gnome lies in the northern section of the area. A {@dc 11} Intelligence ({@skill Medicine|XPHB}) check reveals that an ooze consumed him—his flesh is gone but his equipment remains intact. If the PCs have not worked out a source of light, the gnome has a {@item Bullseye Lantern|XPHB} and two {@item Oil|XPHB|Oil Flasks} among his possessions. Otherwise, the corpse instead bears a {@item Shortbow|XPHB} with 50 {@item Arrows (20)|XPHB|Arrows} and 7 SP.

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Drake caverns (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 6: Drake Caverns
entries: {@i Cold earth and stone. World Tree roots wind through stone. Still air.}

Stony rumbles and hissing echoes reverberate through these caverns, their labyrinthine twists and turns reflecting sounds in odd, disturbing directions. World Tree root-hairs break through the rocky roof and walls. Some of them appear gnawed and damaged.

Many of the caverns' sounds come from the Nidhogg-blooded drake quietly tunneling, observing the adventurers through its {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} ability and waiting for the most opportune moment to strike. But the characters can make other determinations about their surroundings.

items.name: {@dc 4} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC can identify the footprints of dwarven boots and reptilian claws, wide paths suggesting the passage of a huge mollusk or ooze, and debris and holes made by large burrowing creatures.

items.name: {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC hears a faint trickle of water to the south.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC in the eastern caverns smells reptilian musk from the southeast.

This section of Yggdrasil's roots is full of subterranean creatures that have come to absorb power from the tree or feed on other creatures attracted to it. Each time the characters enter this large area, roll {@dice 1d6} on the following table to determine what they encounter.

entries.name: North
entries: Abandoned dwarven outpost (Area 7).

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Collapsed tunnel (Area 10).

entries.name: Southeast
entries: Nidhogg-blooded drake's nest (Area 11).

entries.name: South
entries: Underground lake (Area 8).

entries.name: Southwest
entries: Lair entrance (Area 5).

entries.name: Northwest
entries: Spider tunnel (Area 9).

entries.name: Area 7: Abandoned Dwarven Outpost
entries: {@i Sturdy stone walls. Packed earthen floors. Occupants left in a hurry.}

A thick oak door hangs open, unbarred, admitting entrance to this cold, but lived-in structure. Natural stone lines the walls, except in the front, which was clearly quarried elsewhere and brought here to close the cave. Two bunks line the western wall, and toppled weapon racks lie in a heap on the eastern wall, along with two barrels labeled in Dwarf script. One of the narrow roots of Yggdrasil has penetrated the natural rock wall near the rear of the outpost.

The dwarves stationed at this watchpost abandoned it when the Nidhogg-blooded drake attacked them not long after taking up residence in the area. Their bodies lie in a passage to the northeast (see Area 10).
The structure is sound, with a thick bar to hold the oak door closed. It is unlikely that hostile creatures could break down the door easily, making this the safest place under Yggdrasil to rest.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Among the disarray of the weapon racks, characters can find weapons of obvious dwarven make: A {@item Battleaxe|XPHB}, a {@item Mace|XPHB}, a {@item Light Hammer|XPHB}, a {@item Glaive|XPHB}, and a pair of {@item Sling|XPHB|Slings} in a satchel containing 50 lead {@item Sling Bullets (20)|XPHB|Bullets}. Two {@item Barrel|XPHB|Barrels} sit near the front of the outpost, one half full of whole pickled herring and one half full of pickled rutabagas, both in brine.

entries.name: South
entries: Drake caverns (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 8: Underground Lake
entries: {@i Underground lake. Fresh water. Mystical fish.}
Gentle lapping sounds come from the southern end of this tunnel, where an underground lake nudges gently against the stone.

The underground lake is freshwater, suitable for drinking. A PC can spend 5 minutes fishing here and attempt a Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) skill check. Someone surpassing {@dc 10} catches one herring, food for a Humanoid character for 1 day. A character who surpasses {@dc 15} catches a magic fish called a blackgill. Blackgills measure 3–4 inches long; a character can eat one as an action. When eaten, each acts as a {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG}. Once the group has caught two blackgills, no more are available until the following day.

entries.name: North
entries: Drake caverns (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 9: Spider Tunnel
entries: {@i Moist, warm air. Spiderwebs. Danger.}
Sounds dampen in this tunnel, and the air grows moist and still. A few feet inside, thick strands of webbing hang from the ceiling and walls, growing denser farther in.

A {@creature Phase Spider|XMM} has made its nest here. If someone disturbs the webs surrounding the cave entrance, the spider uses its Ethereal Jaunt ability to move to the nearest webbing and attack the creature that touched the web.
In the far back corner of the area lie several Medium cocoons. An {@creature Ettercap|XMM} hiding among the cocoons attacks any creature that comes near.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: One of the corpses wrapped in a webbed cocoon is a dwarf warrior wearing a suit of {@item Plate Armor|XPHB} and a {@item +1 Battleaxe|XDMG} carved with dwarven runes and clan motifs. A dwarf wielding the weapon can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to cause it to shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 10 feet, or to extinguish the light.

entries.name: South
entries: Drake caverns (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 10: Collapsed Tunnel
entries: {@i Dwarf corpses. Caved-in tunnel.}
A faint whistling and a hint of fresher air emanate from this tunnel, along with the stench of decaying flesh. Two corpses lie rotting where the tunnel turns east toward an area of scree and rubble.

The far eastern section of this tunnel appears to have once led farther into the depths, but it has suffered a cave-in. Massive stones and thick piles of scree almost completely seal the passageway, allowing through only the faintest whisper of fresher air from beyond.
Two corpses, slashed from behind and splattered with thick, viscous venom, lie facing the tunnel's end.

items.name: {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Medicine|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC examining the bodies determines they were dwarves.

items.name: {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC examining the corpses' equipment sees that it is of dwarven make.

items.name: {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC concludes that the dwarves fell while fleeing down this tunnel, presumably to the safety now blocked by the rockfall.
If the PCs already visited the abandoned dwarven outpost (Area 7), it is clear that these were the scouts once stationed there.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: A {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check to search the bodies reveals a polished agate with a thick quartz line running down the center of it in a pocket inside of one of the bodies' coats. This is a {@item Stone of Good Luck|XDMG} (luckstone). In addition to its other magical properties, the user, while holding the stone, can take a {@action Magic|XPHB} action to learn which way is magnetic north, provided they are in a location that has a magnetic north.

entries.name: South
entries: Drake caverns (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 11: Nidhogg-Blooded Drake's Nest
entries: {@i Drake nest. Snake stench. Bone piles. Large Yggdrasil root, chewed and poisoned.}

The stench of snake hangs heavily in the air. A pile of bones lies against the western wall, an air of rot wafting from it. In the southern corner, a huge World Tree root breaks through the stone. It has been chewed and clawed. Faintly glowing sap leaks freely from wounds crusted with green-black venom.

The {@creature Nidhogg-Blooded Drake|NorthlandsSagas} has been tunneling through the walls, observing the adventurers as they explored its hunting ground. As they approach its nest, it bursts forth from the ceiling and attacks.

The drake prefers to weaken foes from afar using its Venom Spit ability. While the venom recharges, it Burrows close to enemies before attacking with its teeth and claws. A canny foe, the drake readily uses strike-and-fade tactics to harry those who present a significant threat. Once it has revealed itself, it continues to strike at its enemies from the stone walls and roof of its hunting ground until it is killed.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: A {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check to search the remains in the drake's midden heap uncovers—among the other, more damaged accouterments of its victims—325 SP, 120 GP, and assorted gemstones (worth 500 GP), a pair of engraved bone {@item Dice Set|XPHB|dice} (25 GP), a torn battle flag, a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} of {@spell Longstrider|XPHB}, and a {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG}.

entries.name: Portal
entries: When the PCs pour the water from the Well of Urd upon the injured section of Yggdrasil's large root, its glow brightens, and the patches of dried venom sizzle away. New bark flows over the ragged wounds covering the pulp within, before the glow subsides. As soon as the root has healed, a swirl of leaves and golden light coalesces into a portal.

entries.name: North
entries: Drake caverns (Area 6).

entries.name: Portal
entries: Back to the Well of Urd (Area 4).

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: The adventure can conclude in several ways:

entries.name: Flee from Destined Fate
entries: If the characters flee the World Tree before reaching the Norns, they will be unable to recover the {@item Mother's Comb|NorthlandsSagas} for Loki. If they do not return to Captain Farleap, Loki presumes them dead. Should they return, unsuccessful, to the ratatosk, Loki banishes them from the Northlands and curses them such that their underclothes itch irresistibly during stressful moments for the remainder of their lives. The brood of Nidhogg keeps growing in strength deep beneath the tree, and the Cult of Ragnarok continues its efforts to bring about the End Times.

entries.name: Trapped among Yggdrasil's Roots
entries: Should the PCs prove unable or unwilling to defeat the Nidhogg-blooded drake in its nest, they remain trapped in the Plane of Earth. They might excavate the cave in Area 10, given sufficient time, but Nidhogg's spawn hunting in the area makes it difficult to do so unmolested. If they pass through the collapsed tunnel, they eventually locate a dwarven city. Its leaders would be very interested to know why their outpost has not checked in—and to learn of the threat that Nidhogg's brood represents.

entries.name: Return with Loki's Prize
entries: When the PCs return to the Well of Urd after having defeated Nidhogg's spawn, the Norns appear pleased, going so far as to show faint smiles. They thank the adventurers and grant them Loki's debt and another boon for completing the tasks.

To fulfill Loki's debt, the Norns produce the {@item Mother's Comb|NorthlandsSagas}, an enchanted tool for weaving at a loom, from the aether. They give it to the heroes without explaining why they have it, what it is, or providing any additional assistance. They say this fulfils their debt to Loki. (See the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|12} for more on the comb.)

For completing the tasks, the Norns present the party with the "great reward" mentioned in Loki's note: a magnificent sword named {@item Storrbani|NorthlandsWorldbook|Storrbani, Slayer of the Mighty}. (For a full description of this fabled weapon, see {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 5: Magic and Mayhem|NorthlandsWorldbook|5}.)

The Norns also provide a gift for Kosktup Farleap, to aid the group's tasks to come. They gesture, and a wooden longship figurehead appears nearby. It is carved in the shape of a dragon, hewn from a cast-off branch of Yggdrasil itself. The Norns bid the characters give the magical drakahofud to their ratatosk ally—he will know what to do with it.
If the adventurers ask about the Cult of Ragnarok, the Norns smile thinly. In their peculiar collective speech, they say the following:

Bergelmir the Bellowing Storm, frost giant god of vengeance and domination, and Angrboda, giant deity of nature's fury and also Loki's once-lover, guide the hands of the Cult of Ragnarok. The offspring of Loki and Angrboda—called the Mother of Monsters—include Hel, ruler of the dead; Jormungandr, the world serpent; and Fenris, the colossal, vicious wolf fated to kill Wotan and bring about Ragnarok.
Angrboda has many reasons to stoke her fury at Loki. It remains well within her character to loose her children upon the world purely to avenge herself upon the Trickster.
Return to your patron. Tell Loki that they have woven this bed of thorns through the god's own actions. Now all the worlds of gods and men shall lie in it.

If the characters ask how to return home from the Well of Urd—there is no obvious portal out of this location—the Norns cast {@spell Water Breathing|XPHB} and {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB} on the heroes, with additional magic to protect them from the well's chaotic properties (it has been known to change aspects of those who immerse themselves, from hair color or height to more profound changes like class or species). Then they summon forth a whirlpool within the well and bid them leap into it. The waters suck them down to the bottom of the whirlpool into a portal, which drops them into the sky above the Material Plane. The {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB} spell lasts until they reach the ground (see below).

entries.name: Further Adventures
entries: The characters return to the Northlands in the Wolfheim region and can make their way easily to meet {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} and {@i Sly Raven} in Hvalfell. The captain is overjoyed at the prospect of affixing the magical dragon-shaped figurehead to the prow of his new longship, under construction here. He takes the {@item Mother's Comb|NorthlandsSagas}, promising to give it to their patron, along with any useful information they learned about the cult.

They group can rest in the village of Hvalfell or another settlement and spend their hard-earned loot. Soon enough, however, {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} comes to them or sends a missive, asking them to come back to village, which has fallen under threat from the Cult of Ragnarok.
But that is a story told in {@adventure Assault on Hvalfell|NorthlandsSagas|4}, the next adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}.

data.name: Assault on Hvalfell
entries: {@i Assault on Hvalfell} is a first-tier adventure for a party of four to five 4th-level player characters, though you can adjust it to accommodate more or fewer players. The story takes place in the Northlands near a settlement called Hvalfell in Wolfheim, but feel free to transplant it into the location of your choice. The martial plot calls upon the heroes to be true leaders as they rally the villagers and actively defend Hvalfell against a force of giants allied with the Cult of Ragnarok.

At the end of the adventure, the characters should reach 5th level. If this is the first adventure you're playing in the Sagas, refer to the {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0} for important backstory.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: The village of Hvalfell, in the northwestern corner of the Wolfheim region on the River Svart, is under threat of siege by the Cult of Ragnarok. A force of cultists led by {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} and supplemented with allies is a scant day away from the village. Bolgrim intends to set his force against the settlement and its inhabitants to win a drakahofud figurehead, which the characters gained in the previous adventure, and use it in his plot to unleash Ragnarok upon the world.

Working feverishly near Hvalfell's docks, shipbuilder {@creature Gretl Gunrsdottir|NorthlandsSagas} and a small team of villagers have nearly finished crafting {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} (which means "Leaper"), a longship fine enough for its owner and captain, Loki's own messenger, Kosktup Farleap. Gretl needs at least a day and a half to finish a masterwork fit to mount the figurehead upon. The Cult of Ragnarok will arrive in a day.

The characters need to buy Gretl and Kosktup enough time to finish their work, including mounting the figurehead and launching the ship into the River Svart. They have no more than a day to prepare Hvalfell's defense before an overwhelming force descends upon it.

Perhaps they decide to fortify the settlement's outer defenses by building spear walls and tilling up the earth to make the approach to Hvalfell costly. Or maybe they choose to turn the village homes into collapsing death traps and the yard into a killing ground. Eventually the characters likely find themselves pushed to the beach to defend Gretl and her shipbuilders directly. As long as the longship launches with the magical dragon figurehead affixed to its prow, the characters will succeed at their primary objective—even if the cost to the village and its people is tremendous.

entries.name: Sagas Connections
entries: {@i Assault on Hvalfell} is the fourth adventure in {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path. For those following the campaign arc, after finishing this adventure, the PCs will proceed to {@adventure Trials of the Lost Skald|NorthlandsSagas|5}.

The characters previously earned the magical dragon-shaped figurehead for {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} in {@adventure Among the Norns|NorthlandsSagas|3}. They foiled {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas}'s attempt to get a magical relic called {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} in {@adventure Down the Wolf Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1} and outfoxed his efforts to capture Kosktup in {@adventure Ogre's Run|NorthlandsSagas|2}. If Bolgrim died in one of these encounters, replace him with another warrior, {@creature Rota Slit-Throat|NorthlandsSagas} (using Bolgrim's stat block).

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: This adventure is structured in three parts.

items.name: Part 1: Hvalfell
entries: The first part describes the village of Hvalfell and its prominent figures.

items.name: Part 2: Preparations
entries: The second part describes the preparations and defenses the characters can make prior to the attack. The list of preparations is not exhaustive—if your players have other ideas, work with them to determine what they want to accomplish, what resources they need to complete it, and any benefits or drawbacks to the characters and their allies.

items.name: Part 3: The Assault
entries: The final part details the Cult of Ragnarok's attack, expressed in a quick, simplified large-scale combat system.

entries.name: GM's Note
entries: Because the action takes place in a village under siege, the social and combat pillars of the game feature prominently, with the exploration pillar less so. The scenario stacks the odds heavily against the characters; many adversaries have Challenge Ratings substantially higher than the expected average party level. It is possible for the characters to overcome the Cult of Ragnarok and its giant allies, ensure that Kosktup Farleap's longship launches with its magical figurehead, prevent the destruction of Hvalfell, and save all its residents. But that is not a required outcome—or even expected.
Remind players frequently that their primary goal is to ensure the launch of the ratatosk's longship. Any other successes are a bonus but aren't necessary to continue with the adventure path.

entries.name: Call to Action
entries: {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas}—the group's ally and broker of missions from his patron, Loki—finds the characters and asks for their help urgently (see the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13} for his NPC description). Explaining the information from the Adventure Background section, he begs them to return with him to Hvalfell (if they are not already there together) and lead the village's defense against the waves of approaching cultists and giants.
If you are not running {@i Assault on Hvalfell} as a part of the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, use one of the following hooks to get the characters into the action:

entries.name: A Call for Aid
entries: {@creature Henrika Langerkvist|NorthlandsSagas}, the headwoman of Hvalfell, has put out a call for assistance. A force of grim humans, dwarves, and giants is soon to besiege the village to destroy the longship being built by {@creature Gretl Gunrsdottir|NorthlandsSagas}as an offering to the Aesir.

entries.name: The Enemy of My Enemy
entries: At the behest of a patron, the characters travel to Hvalfell to gain a magical dragon figurehead that is known to have recently arrived there. The characters are sanctioned to use whatever means necessary to take possession of the artifact, but they arrive only hours before the Cult of Ragnarok assaults the village to take it for themselves. The party must work with the villagers to defend Hvalfell—at least until they can get their hands on the figurehead.

entries.name: Factions and Key Players
entries: Below you'll find a roster of the allies and enemies the characters contend with in this adventure.

entries.name: People of Hvalfell
entries: Many potential allies live in Hvalfell and the surrounding environs. Most work avidly toward the defense of the village, its residents, and the magical drakahofud. This list summarizes the key allies, and the most likely location to find them prior to the assault. Each named NPC can be sprinkled among the units in the battle in Part 3 to provide names, faces, and dramatic moments.

items.name: Elthia Flathame: Area 5.
entries: The village blacksmith, an elf.

items.name: Gretl Gunrsdottir: Area 7 or 8.
entries: The master shipbuilder, a human, hard at work on the longship.

items.name: Henrika Langerkvist: Area 1.
entries: The human headwoman of Hvalfell.

items.name: Jerald and Luvaar Calsson: Area 11.
entries: Local ne'er-do-wells, human brothers.

items.name: Kosktup Farleap: Area 7.
entries: The ratatosk commissioner and captain of the longship under construction here.

items.name: Mikkel Ulfsson: Area 4.
entries: The village tanner, a human.

items.name: Myllda Nornsdottir: Area 10.
entries: Hvalfell's seer, a human.

items.name: Ostrod Tunhammer: Area 6.
entries: The village provisioner, a dwarf.

items.name: Pettra Nylsdottir: Area 2.
entries: The dwarf leader of Tyr's temple.

items.name: Thybolg Fredriksson: Area 2.
entries: The human leader of Thor's temple and Henrika's husband.

In addition to the named NPCs above, approximately 300 other residents call Hvalfell home, half of whom can help defend the settlement. The remainder are too young, old, or infirm to aid in the defense. Most villagers are human, with dwarves and a few elves rounding out the population. See how these residents divide into combat units in Part 3, Unit Blocks.

entries.name: Cult of Ragnarok
entries: The antagonists all belong to the Cult of Ragnarok, a religious sect devoted to ushering in the end of the world. While most cult members remain nameless, a few notable figures are summarized here:

items.name: Bolgrim Boar-Scar:
entries: The commander of this group is a male human who appears in the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13}.

items.name: Greggra, Nud, and Flea:
entries: Three hill giants.

items.name: Jrrm and Grrm, and Pas and Myre:
entries: A pair of ettin siblings.

items.name: Urzmil:
entries: Bolgrim's enforcer is a bugbear stalker.
In addition to the named NPCs, the cult's assault force includes numerous rank and file members as well as a small contingent of ogres and some goblin shock troops.

About {@chance 30|||It's a Dwarf|It isn't a Dwarf} of the cultists are dwarves, {@chance 10|||It's a Tiefling|It isn't a Tiefling} are tieflings, and the remainder are human. See how these troops divide into combat units in Part 3, Unit Blocks.

entries.name: Part 1: Hvalfell
entries: The village of Hvalfell sits on the western bank of the River Svart at the north end of the Twistwood. Its residents sustain themselves primarily through fishing, though some rich hunting land lies to the east. Several small farms located within a half-day's ride of the village sell their produce and livestock in Hvalfell, though the land is too rugged for larger farms. Residents used to turn to raiding in lean times, bringing back gold, gems, furs, and food to stave off the harsh winters. Although those days of reaving are in the past, every able-bodied adult has trained to take up spear, axe, and shield to defend the village against raiders or stray horrors from farther north.

The thing that sets Hvalfell apart from similar villages in the region is the presence of Gretl Gunrsdottir, a former raider. Her skill and speed at shipbuilding brings a steady stream of patrons to Hvalfell to commission boats. This in turn brings in coin and valuable trade goods, making the settlement wealthier than its neighbors.

When the heroes arrive in the village, they pass through a surrounding palisade. Headwoman {@creature Henrika Langerkvist|NorthlandsSagas} greets them and shows them around, immediately discussing Hvalfell's defenses and resources. She reveals that the village seer, {@creature Myllda Nornsdottir|NorthlandsSagas}, foretold of their arrival in a prophecy, and that they would direct preparations for the defense of the town and lead them to glory. Because of this, the village has readied their equipment and workers, but has taken no concrete action yet, awaiting the characters' leadership. She's happy to support nearly any plan they make, as the fulfillment of prophecy.

Many encounter areas below include a "Preparations" section noting how the characters can use these locations to prepare for the attack and fortify the village. Details of the time and resources required for each tactic, plus the benefits and drawbacks, appear in Part 2. Some encounter areas below also include "During the Assault" sections noting how they may change while the attack rages in Part 3.

entries.name: 1. Longhouse
entries: {@i Spruce logs. Heavy oak doors banded in steel at each end. Birch bark roof. Racks of axes and spears line the inside wall.}

Double doors lead into the longhouse's common room, which measures 30 feet by 15 feet. It boasts a large central fireplace ringed in stone and three long tables that seat 10 people to a side on a busy night. Racks of spears and axes line the south wall. On the north wall, racks of shields surround the immense stuffed head of a heavily scarred boar.

{@creature Henrika Langerkvist|NorthlandsSagas} (human {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM}) and her husband {@creature Thybolg Fredriksson|NorthlandsSagas} live in a humble room at the east end of the longhouse, which they've partitioned off from the common room with skins hanging from the ceiling. Neither Henrika nor Thybolg keeps any valuables in their living space.

As in all Northlands communities, the longhouse is the heart of the village. After long days of work, many come here to enjoy the central fire, share meat and bread, drink mead and ale, and share tales with their neighbors.

The longhouse also serves as the center of village government. Locals who need to speak to the headwoman can find her in the common area most nights. She generally settles minor disputes and dispenses advice in an ad hoc fashion.

entries.name: Preparations
entries: The characters can build an archer platform on the longhouse roof, as described in Part 2.

entries.name: 2. Temple to Thor and Tyr
entries: {@i Stone construction. Static shock upon entering. A feeling that the gods are watching.}

The tallest building in the village, the new stone temple replaced the old wooden one only two years ago and is the most prominent sign of Hvalfell's growing prosperity. While the two heads of the temple, {@creature Thybolg Fredriksson|NorthlandsSagas} (human {@creature Berserker|XMM}) and {@creature Pettra Nylsdottir|NorthlandsSagas} (dwarf {@creature Priest|XMM}) represent Thor and Tyr, respectively, the village uses this building for all religious observances related to the Aesir. (See {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 6: Northlands Pantheons|NorthlandsWorldbook|6}, for more about these deities.)

The ash wood altar at the temple's center dominates the space, piled with offerings of coin, fur, woven cloth, and food. A longsword with a copper hilt and crossguard rests on a pair of hooks in the center of the north wall. The villagers call the sword (a {@item Vicious Weapon|XDMG}) {@item Tyr's Blade|NorthlandsSagas}.
Stairs along the north wall lead up to a 5-foot-by-15-foot loft, where Pettra lives. Her lodgings are comfortable if sparse. She keeps no valuables there.

Thor and Tyr have blessed the temple. The entire structure, including its doors, has AC 15, HP 100 per 10-foot section, and {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 25. With its stone doors barred from the inside, a {@dc 35} Strength check is required to break down the doors.

entries.name: Preparations
entries: In addition to acting as the primary infirmary during the assault, the temple can serve as a site for supernatural preparation. See Part 2 for details.

entries.name: During the Assault
entries: During the battle, Pettra and two {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoner} attendants tend injured defenders, laying them out on the temple floor. If attackers seem about to reach the temple, Pettra orders the attendants to bar the door.

entries.name: 3. Lumber Pile
entries: {@i Stacks of logs. Smell of pine.}

The villagers collected a great pile of felled trees and large branches to build several more homes. They've already cut most of the wood into manageable 10-foot lengths, with a few 20-foot tree trunks at the base of the pile near the palisade. The pile holds approximately 6,000 pounds of wood, which divides into twenty 300-pound units of lumber.

entries.name: Preparations
entries: Hvalfell's defenders can use the lumber for various purposes as described in Part 2.

entries.name: 4. Tanner's Hut
entries: {@i Stink of tanning oil. Surfaces glisten with a greasy sheen.}

The tanner's hut is an inauspicious wattle-and-daub building. Three 5-foot-diameter vats of oil rest upon stone fire pits outside the hut near the edge of the village. Inside the hut, in the center of the single room on the dirt floor lies a fire pit ringed in stone. Tanned hides hang to dry on hooks from ceiling trusses. Piles of untreated hides sit against the north and west walls.
{@creature Mikkel Ulfsson|NorthlandsSagas} (human {@creature Scout|XMM}), Hvalfell's tanner, has offered his hut and all its contents in the defense of the village, including the three vats of oil.

entries.name: Preparations
entries: The party can commandeer Mikkel's vats of oil for defensive measures as described in Part 2.

entries.name: 5. Blacksmith
entries: {@i Soot-blackened timbers. Smell of ash and metal. Tools and weapons.}

The forge at the smithy stays lit throughout the assault, unless a creature uses an action to extinguish it. {@creature Elthia Flathame|NorthlandsSagas} (elf {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM}), the blacksmith, freely allows the group to use her smithy and its contents to defend the village. Characters can find the following items here, but generally the villagers have all necessary tools to prepare for the attack.
The following materials available at the smithy:

items: {@item Carpenter's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Cobbler's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Cook's Utensils|XPHB} (2 sets)
{@item Jeweler's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Leatherworker's Tools|XPHB} (2 sets)
{@item Mason's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Smith's Tools|XPHB} (3 sets)
{@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}
{@item Woodcarver's Tools|XPHB}
{@item Handaxe|XPHB|Handaxes} (5)
{@item Light Hammer|XPHB|Light Hammers} (5)
{@item Spear|XPHB|Spears} (20)
{@item Battleaxe|XPHB|Battleaxes} (3)
{@item Maul|XPHB}
{@item Warhammer|XPHB|Warhammers} (2)
{@item Breastplate|XPHB}
{@item Chain Shirt|XPHB|Chain Shirts} (2)
{@item Chain Mail|XPHB}

entries.name: 6. Provisioner
entries: {@i Log walls painted orange. Pine-shingled roof painted crimson. Yellow trim.}

Provisioner {@creature Ostrod Tunhammer|NorthlandsSagas} (dwarf {@creature Spy|XMM}) carries every piece of adventuring gear with a cost of 10 GP or less. He also carries all trade goods with a cost of 5 GP or less, excepting livestock. How much of any specific item he has in stock is left to the GM.
In addition, he has the following gear available:

items: 3 vials {@item Acid|XPHB}
3 vials {@item Alchemist's Fire|XPHB}
1 vial {@item Antitoxin|XPHB}
1 {@item Climber's Kit|XPHB}
1 {@item Component Pouch|XPHB}
1 {@item Hourglass|PHB}
5 bottles {@item Ink|XPHB}
6 {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing} (in a cache behind the counter)

entries: Ostrod sells his goods for the standard price; he understands the threat posed by the Cult of Ragnarok, but can't convince himself to let anything go for less than market value. In fact, he hopes to sell the potions at a sharp markup following the assault.

items.name: {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns the presence of the potions.

items.name: {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC convinces Ostrod to sell the {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing} for the standard price of 50 GP each, for the good of the village.

items.name: {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check:
entries: After threatening to tell Henrika, the temple heads, or the blacksmith, a PC convinces him to give the potions freely to the war effort.

entries.name: 7. Beach
entries: {@i Pebble and stones. Driftwood. Longboats.}

The tiny pebbles of the beach shift erratically underfoot, making it {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. Unless the village noncombatants have been sent away on them, four longboats have been dragged onto the beach and can serve as {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Three-Quarters Cover}.

entries.name: 8. Gretl's Hut
entries: {@i Driftwood construction. Sod and seaweed roof. Scattered wood scraps.}

Shipbuilder {@creature Gretl Gunrsdottir|NorthlandsSagas} (human {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM}) lives on the beach in a hut built of flotsam. Wood shavings carpet the driftwood floor inside. She keeps a spare set of {@item Carpenter's Tools|XPHB} against one wall near her pallet bed.

Gretl leads a team of seven {@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners} in the construction of her masterwork: a magnificent longship built to {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas}'s specifications. Though the ship nears completion, Gretl and her team need about a day and a half to complete it—it's due for launch the day of the assault. Ideally the defenders will keep the cult forces away from the shipbuilders long enough to see the boat floated successfully.

Gretl only turns away from her work if someone attacks her and her team directly. She grabs her spear and fights the attackers, with Kosktup's assistance, shouting at the rest of the team to keep working.

entries.name: 9. Yard, Palisade, and Gate
entries: {@i Patchy grass. Weeds. Bare earth.}

The yard features the largest expanse of open ground in Hvalfell. At the beginning of the adventure it is relatively flat and easy to traverse. The Cult of Ragnarok's initial attacks might focus on breaching the gates so the cultists can pour into the settlement.

A 10-foot palisade wall surrounds the village, and a 10-foot-wide wooden gate allows entrance to the yard. If anyone interacts with them outside of the large-scale combat rules, the palisade and gate have AC 15, HP 27 per 10-foot-by-10-foot section, and a {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 10.

entries.name: Preparations
entries: The group can prepare the yard, palisade, and gate for defense in various ways, as described in Part 2.

entries.name: 10. Seer's House
entries: {@i White-painted exterior. Flowering vines. Mossy roof. Stone hearth and chimney.}

Regardless of the time of year, flowering morning glory climbs the exterior of this white cottage. A rune of welcome painted on the door indicates that those in need may enter freely, day or night. Inside, the cottage is cluttered with offerings and bric-a-brac left to the seer as thanks for all she does for the community.

{@creature Myllda Nornsdottir|NorthlandsSagas} (human {@creature Druid|XMM}), Hvalfell's seer, resides here, serving as a third spiritual leader in the village, along with Thybolg and Pettra in the Temple to Thor and Tyr (Area 2). For the most part, she spends her time collecting herbs and performing the ritual to cast {@spell Augury|XPHB} when the headwoman asks. While she defends any resident of Hvalfell to her last breath, she has little advice to offer regarding the village's defense.

entries.name: Preparations
entries: Myllda intends to fight the cult. If asked, she recommends that the group send the noncombatants to nearby villages using the beached longboats. See the evacuation option in Part 2.

entries.name: 11. Jerald and Luuvar's Tunnel
entries: {@i Well hidden. Sandy loam.}

Indoctrinated by their father, {@creature Jerald Calsson|NorthlandsSagas} and his brother {@creature Luvaar Calsson|NorthlandsSagas} (human {@creature Spy|XMM|Spies}) have long been part of the Cult of Ragnarok and have patiently awaited a chance to usher in the End Times. At the south end of the village, they have guarded a tunnel they dug out as children with their father. Through some power unknown to his sons, their father masked the tunnel behind illusions that make the entrance and exit look just like part of the hillside. They have used it for years to smuggle the occasional small stolen treasure out of the village. Despite two years' difference in age, people often mistake the brothers for one another—even villagers who have known them since childhood.

With an attack approaching, the brothers await the right time to use the tunnel to welcome their brethren in the cult into the village. If attacked before the assault begins, they flee to join the cultists and lead them into the village through the tunnel.

entries.name: Detecting the Tunnel
entries: A character who takes a {@action Study|XPHB} action to examine the palisade near the tunnel determines it is an illusion with a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check. Someone who has discovered the deception can see through the image, making the illusion itself appear faint.

entries.name: Preparations
entries: If heroes discover the tunnel, they might think to collapse it or booby trap it, as described in Part 2.

entries.name: 12. Well
entries: {@i Well hidden. Sandy loam.}

A circular stone well with an iron crossbar sits upon two bracketed iron poles. A 10-gallon wooden bucket hangs from the crossbeam by a rope. A handle at one end lowers and raises the bucket. Each of three 10-foot-diameter wells in the village measures 40 feet deep. Each well holds approximately 2,000 gallons of drinkable water, which stands 6 feet deep. It takes 1 minute to lower, fill, and raise a bucket of water.

A creature can climb down the well without a rope with a successful {@dc 13} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check, or without a check if a rope is tied to the crossbar. Up to 16 creatures can squeeze into the space at the bottom of the well to avoid the assault.

entries.name: During the Assault
entries: In 1 hour, a team of 10 people can drain one well to extinguish a number of burning buildings equal to one-third of the total number of buildings in the village.

entries.name: Part 2: Preparations
entries: The characters have about a day to direct preparations for the battle. The villagers, expecting their arrival, have prepared equipment, tools, and resources for their direction. Henrika, the village headwoman, offers suggestions if the characters ask or seem undecided. The villagers appear motivated and ready to work. The PCs have at their disposal:

items: 15 Hvalfell worker units—gangs of workers, ready to follow orders (the PCs together can become 1 additional worker unit).
20 units of lumber from the lumber pile (Area 3).
3 vats of oil from the tanner's hut (Area 4).
All necessary tools.

entries.name: Hvalfell Zones
entries: In the coming battle, forces will fight in Hvalfell across various zones of conflict. The PCs might choose to fortify, trap, or otherwise prepare these zones before battle.
Give the players the handout map showing the following different zones in the village.

items.name: Approach to the Village:
entries: The villagers have cleared the area outside the palisade of obstructions. It might make a good place for spiked trenches or pit traps.

items.name: Northern Palisade, Western Palisade, and Southern Palisade:
entries: These three zones can be fortified and armed with spearwalls separately. The gate is considered part of the Western Palisade.

items.name: Village Yard North, Center, and South:
entries: Characters can prepare the clearing inside beyond the gate with chokepoints and traps. All buildings inside the palisade other than the longhouse are considered part of one of the three yard zones.

items.name: Longhouse:
entries: The party can prepare the longhouse roof as a raised platform for ranged attacks.

Work with the players to help the characters enact whatever they can think of. Some likely preparations appear below, including the relevant map key area if specific to a particular location. Refer to Important Terms in Part 3 for definitions of large-scale combat terms, such as Unit Value.

entries.name: Fortifications
entries: The village has plentiful resources to construct various fortifications before the attack.

entries.name: Archer Platform
entries: 2 lumber units, 2 worker units. (Area 1)
Build a high, protected platform on the longhouse roof for archers to rain arrows on enemies in any zone without taking return fire.

entries.name: Barricade/Cover
entries: 2 lumber units, 1 worker unit. (Area 9)

Build barricades and cover in a zone for defenders to fight from behind. For each barricade, a designated Hvalfell unit has +1 health (due to cover) while in that zone. A barricade can defend only one unit. The barricade remains in its zone, even if the unit it protects moves.

entries.name: Chokepoint in the Yard
entries: 3 lumber units, 2 worker units. (Area 9)

If the cultists breach the palisade and move into the yard, makeshift walls narrow their options. In a yard zone with chokepoints, a maximum of 3 enemy units can add their Unit Value to their attack rolls until they deal 3 hits to the chokepoint. Hvalfell units can attack freely from behind the chokepoint walls.

entries.name: Reinforce Gate
entries: 2 or 4 lumber units, 0 worker units. (Area 9)

Extra lumber can be kept on hand to reinforce the gate during the battle. Villagers can hastily lean unworked lumber into the gate to block entry mid-fight. For each 2 lumber units used to reinforce the gate, the western palisade can absorb 1 hit dealt to a unit of defenders, applied at any time during the battle. Once the reinforcements have absorbed 1 hit, they provide no more defense.

entries.name: Reinforce Palisade
entries: 5 lumber units, 4 worker units. (Area 9)

Reinforce the palisades to withstand assault. Each reinforced palisade zone (northern, western, and southern) can absorb 5 hits from defender units in the zone; Hvalfell units in a reinforced zone can apply any hits dealt to their forces to the walls instead. Once the reinforcements in a zone have absorbed 5 hits, they provide no more defense.

entries.name: Spearwall
entries: 2 lumber units, 1 worker unit.
Spears or stakes jut out to impale incoming attackers. Hvalfell units in a zone with spearwall have a +1 bonus to Unit Value when they take the Attack or Ready action.

entries.name: Traps
entries: If the heroes discover the tunnel (Area 11) before the attack, they might think to collapse it or booby trap it. This could weaken Bolgrim and {@creature Urzmil|NorthlandsSagas}, should they try to sneak in this way. Below are trap options for this and other locales in the village.

entries.name: Firepit Trap
entries: 1 vat of oil, 1 worker unit.
This pit filled with oil ignites when someone falls in. When enemy units enter a zone with a firepit trap, determine randomly which unit it affects. That unit takes 1 hit.

entries.name: Spiked Trench
entries: 1 lumber unit, 1 worker unit.
This is a set of wooden spikes in a large, covered pit. When enemy units enter a zone with a spiked trench, determine randomly which unit it affects. That unit takes 1 hit.

entries.name: Magical Preparations
entries: Arcane or divine measures can prove useful for the villagers for only a modest outlay in resources.

entries.name: Cast Augury or Similar Divinatory Magic
entries: 0 worker units.
Based on the questions asked, the Hvalfell side of one zone gains +1 Unit Value for the duration of the battle.

entries.name: Pray to Thor or Tyr
entries: 1 worker unit.
One Hvalfell unit gains +1 Unit Value for the duration of the battle.

entries.name: Additional Preparations
entries: Some preparations don't directly contribute to the coming battle, but they might make things easier if someone thinks to do them ahead of time.

entries.name: Evacuate Noncombatants
entries: 3 worker units.

Hvalfell has about 150 noncombatants: the elderly, infirm, and children. They won't volunteer to go, but if a character directs them to leave, they willingly evacuate on fishing boats and longships with their honor intact. This reduces the morale test to {@dc 8} for the Hvalfell forces (see Part 3, Test Morale), since they don't have to worry about loved ones amid the fight.

entries.name: Get Help from Nearby Farms and Cottages
entries: Up to 5 worker units.
Teams of recruiters run to nearby farms and villages to scare up help. One additional Warrior Infantry unit arrives for each worker unit deployed.

entries.name: Scout the Cult
entries: 1 worker unit.

More than 100 creatures have massed to attack Hvalfell. Even the PCs can't significantly damage or slow them with individual attacks. Have the scouting party make a {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check. On a success, they discover weaknesses in Bolgrim's command structure to exploit. On a failed enemy morale test, the players choose which unit breaks instead of the GM. If the {@skill Investigation|XPHB} check results in a 1, the defense of Hvalfell loses 1 scout unit for the battle.

If the scouts attempt to assassinate {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Urzmil|NorthlandsSagas}, let them try. But they must sneak past an army to do so, and face overwhelming opposition if discovered.

entries.name: Whatever the Players Think Of
entries: Variable resource and worker units.
Players might well think of ideas that aren't covered here. Loosely speaking, assign a value of +1 Unit Value or +1 health for each lumber/worker unit they spend.

entries.name: Part 3: The Assault
entries: In addition to the characters, the Cult of Ragnarok assault on Hvalfell involves a lot of NPCs, both friendly and foul. To make the attack as easy to run as possible, this section describes what actions the cult and its allies take and the order in which they happen. Handle the series of running battles as separate fights in various zones that occur over a number of combat turns.
Further recommendations to streamline this portion of the adventure:

items: Make sure the players have a copy of the Hvalfell map handout with zones marked.
Photocopy the unit blocks to make it easy to update them throughout the battle (see Unit Blocks).
If the cultist forces breach the palisade, they move toward the closest group of defenders and attack.

When the end of the battle draws near, Bolgrim and {@creature Urzmil|NorthlandsSagas} break off from their units and disappear in the chaos. They move through the secret tunnel under the south palisade (Area 11) to attack the characters at the ship launching (see Final Battle encounter).

entries.name: Large-Scale Combat Rules
entries: The rules in this section present a streamlined method to resolve this clash.

entries.name: Important Terms
entries: Familiarize yourself with the following terminology of the large-scale combat rules.

entries.name: Units
entries: Every participant in the battle is called a unit. Units are usually a vaguely defined mob of creatures banded together, but they also can be a single larger or powerful creature. In this adventure, a unit comprises only one type of creature. Use the creature's unit block (below) to answer questions about a unit's capacity.

entries.name: Unit Value (UV)
entries: Each unit has a Unit Value (UV) that represents its overall strength. UV is both a unit's combat modifier and its health. Unit Value is generally equivalent to the CR of the creature that makes up the unit.

entries.name: Break Value
entries: If a side fails a morale test (below), units with lowest Break value disperse first.

entries.name: Unit Leader
entries: If a unit has a leader (such as a PC or Bolgrim Boar-Scar), that leader raises the Unit Value of the unit through a leader bonus. In addition, leaders boost morale for their side in a zone.

entries.name: Morale
entries: At the end of each combat round, both sides at each zone test for {@i morale} to keep their side in the fight by making a {@dc 10} Charisma check, using the Charisma modifier of the leader with the highest Charisma in the zone. If none of the units in the zone have leaders, this becomes a simple {@dice d20} roll.

entries.name: Sides
entries: There are two sides in this fight: the Hvalfell side and the cultist side. Players direct Hvalfell forces, while the GM directs enemy forces. Generally, all units on a side in a zone roll for whatever they're doing as a group: If one side in a zone attacks, all units on that side attack. When you roll for morale, all units on a side in a zone become part of that roll. If individual units move away from a zone, their Unit Value and potential leader bonus goes with them.

entries.name: Zones
entries: The action takes place in various zones of conflict (see Hvalfell Zones in Part 2). The PCs got a chance to fortify zones of their choice before battle. They will choose their ground for the fight during Set Up under The Assault Begins, below.

entries.name: Combat Turn Sequence
entries: Unlike standard individual combat, many units clash simultaneously in large-scale combat; however, it's played out one zone at a time.
Resolve turns zone by zone—players choose the order, all else being equal. Both sides in a zone take their turns before you move on to the next zone.
Resolve each zone's turn in this order:

items.name: Ranged Attacks:
entries: Units attacking at range (Hvalfell scouts and goblin warriors) act before anything else happens, regardless of zone. They don't have to use their ranged attack if you prefer them to attack with the melee forces in their zone. If they use their ranged attack, don't add their UV for a melee attack later in the round. Ranged attackers can target only their own or an adjacent zone, unless they are elevated, in which case they can target any zone. The order below explains which side starts; when that side finishes, the other side may make ranged attacks.

items.name: a. Leader vs. No Leader.
entries: If one side in a zone has a unit with a leader and the other side doesn't, the side with the leader acts first.

items.name: b. Leader vs. Leader.
entries: If both sides in a zone have a leader, the Hvalfell side acts first.

items.name: c. No Leader vs. No Leader.
entries: If neither side in a zone has a leader, the cultist side acts first.

items.name: d. Detached PCs.
entries: Characters that act independently of any unit act last.

items.name: 2. Players Pick a Zone to Resolve:
entries: It's usually a good idea to start with zones containing reinforcements, so they can move and add their UVs to the fight in the new zone.

items.name: 3. Zone by Zone:
entries: Next, determine the unit actions for each side. Units can take one of the following actions: Attack, Dash, Ready, or Reposition, but all units of one side in a zone must take the same unit action. (See Unit Actions, below.)

items.name: 4. Move and Unit Actions:
entries: Units that need to move can move to an adjacent zone. A unit can't leave a zone that has an enemy unit unless it takes the Reposition action (see below). After moving, a side takes its predetermined actions. To see which side starts, use the order above (under Ranged Attacks). When that side is done, the other side may act.

items.name: 5. Repeat Steps 2–4:
entries: Continue with combat turns until there are no more zones to select.

entries.name: Test Morale
entries: Once all zones that contain units have taken a turn, each side in a zone makes a morale test to determine whether a unit disbands from attrition or demoralization. Test morale zone by zone, in the order that they took their turns.

Morale is a {@dc 10} Charisma check. If a side in a zone has a leader, add that leader's UV (equal to the leader's level) to the check's result. A PC leader can use a Charisma skill ({@skill Deception|XPHB}, {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}, or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) instead of adding their level, if preferred. At GM's discretion, other factors can influence morale tests, granting a bonus or penalty no higher than +3 and no lower than −3.

On a failed morale test, one unit with the lowest Break score on a side disperses. That unit is out of the fight. If two types of unit have the same Break value, the GM decides which one breaks for cultist forces, and the players decide for Hvalfell forces.

entries.name: Unit Actions
entries: During a turn, the units on a given side can move to an adjacent zone and take one of the following actions: Attack, Dash, Ready, or Reposition.

entries.name: Attack
entries: When a unit attacks, the attacker and defender sides in that zone make opposed Unit Value checks ({@dice d20} + total UV for all units on the side). If the creature has "Ranged Attack" in its unit block, it can make a ranged attack.

items: Ranged units can target enemies in their own zone or any zone that touches theirs. They can attack any zone if they're elevated.
Melee units can attack only enemies in their zone.
See Combat for details.

entries.name: Dash
entries: The unit can move one extra zone this turn.

entries.name: Ready
entries: The unit prepares to attack. When an enemy unit moves next to it before the start of this unit's next turn, it can make an attack against the enemy unit. A unit can't use this action if at least one enemy unit is already next to it.

entries.name: Reposition
entries: The unit can move away from an enemy unit next to it when it moves this turn. The unit must make a morale test; on a success, it maneuvers into a more tactically advantageous position and has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next Unit Value check it makes to attack before the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Combat
entries: When a side in a zone takes the Attack unit action, determine which side is the attacker and which is the defender. Each side rolls a {@dice d20} and adds the total Unit Value for all units on its side. (Remember to add leader bonuses, if applicable.) Compare the results of these Unit Value checks—the side with the higher total wins. If a side wins by 10 or more, it has an increased effect. Consult the Combat Outcome table for effects.
Players choose which unit(s) takes hits for Hvalfell forces, and the GM determines the same for the cultist forces. Careful application of hits can turn the fight.

When a unit takes a hit, fill in one of the boxes on the unit block (below) to represent lost health. A unit is neutralized once all its boxes are filled. Its full UV remains in the fight until it is neutralized. A unit reduced to 0 health is not necessarily killed; individual creatures from a unit might survive its destruction (particularly leaders), but the unit is no more.

entries.name: Losing a Zone
entries: If the defenders lose all their units in a zone, and other units aren't rushed into that position during the next combat turn, the zone is lost. Enemy forces take control of the zone and become the defenders against attacks from Hvalfell forces trying to retake the position.

When a unit with a leader is neutralized or disbands, the leader (enemy or PC) is removed from play for the remainder of the assault. They are assumed to have retreated and regrouped for the Final Battle on the beach.

entries.name: Winning the Assault
entries: When either the cultist side or the Hvalfell side has no more units, the battle is over. The side with remaining units wins.

entries.caption: Combat Outcome
rows: Deal 2 hits to attackers, or 1 if this is a ranged attack.
Deal 1 hit to attackers, or 0 if this is a ranged attack.

entries.name: Players and PCs
entries: Players direct Hvalfell forces, while the GM directs cultist forces.

The precise number of creatures in a unit is large enough that a single PC would have trouble taking on an entire unit single-handedly, or would spend the entire combat fighting only one unit. Once PCs enter large-scale combat, they can contribute in one or more of the following ways.

entries.name: Unit Leaders
entries: A PC unit leader is a great boon. A player character adds their level to the UV of the unit they lead as a leader bonus, and to your side's morale tests in your zone.

A PC leader can use magic to bolster a unit's defenses or hinder an attacking unit by creating walls, fog, or other obstacles. Such effects can modify a Unit Value check by no more than +3 and no less than −3, depending on the GM's decision. When uncertain, lean in favor of the characters, especially if they use magic or class features in clever ways to affect the battle.

entries.name: Spellcasters
entries: A character with an applicable class feature (particularly spellcasting) might forego a leader position for surgical strikes. A single PC can act independently of the side vs. side combat tests in a zone, but if detached from a unit, the character goes last in a zone. GMs must use judgment to determine how spells and features interact with an enemy unit. However, as a rule of thumb, a damaging spell deals a number of hits equal to its level, and a class feature deals the PC's {@variantrule Proficiency Bonus|XPHB} (e.g., 2) in hits.

entries.name: Calling Out Enemy Leaders
entries: The PCs might try to engage directly with enemy leaders amid the throng. A PC attempting this is in no personal danger but can't participate in the battle during the round they attempt it.

{@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Urzmil|NorthlandsSagas} have no desire for a fair fight. If targeted directly, they flee battle (removing their bonuses from the units they lead) and make for the tunnel Area 11) in the southern palisade. They have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Stealth|XPHB} checks due to the chaos of combat.

entries.name: Unit Blocks
entries: Unit blocks represent units' capacity in a large-scale combat. The boxes in a block represent a unit's total health. Each time an attack deals a hit, fill in one box to indicate the damage. In addition, each type of unit has a Unit Value and a Break value. Add the unit's UV to the {@dice d20} roll when it attacks or defends in a zone. If a side fails a morale test, units with lowest Break values disperse first.

entries.name: The Assault Begins
entries: {@i Bleak morning. Bustling village. Dread anticipation.}

Remember, the characters need not defeat the entire enemy army in order to succeed. Their goal is to prevent the Cult of Ragnarok from destroying the longship {@creature Gretl Gunrsdottir|NorthlandsSagas}is building. The village expects them to defend Hvalfell until the longship, with its magical dragon figurehead, has safely launched into the River Svart.
Cold drizzle falls from the slate gray sky. Carrion birds wheel above in anticipation of the coming feast.

entries.name: Timeline
entries: The assault begins around 9 a.m. How much time the battle takes remains somewhat abstract and depends on the PCs' decisions.

entries.name: Set Up
entries: First, the players decide which units their characters join as leaders (or they can remain detached from a unit). Then they assign each village unit to a starting zone. (See Hvalfell Zones in Part 2.)
As the cultists' forces approach the palisade, divide the enemy units as follows{@sup †}:

items.name: North Palisade:
entries: 2 hill giants, 3 ogre units, 6 goblin warrior units including {@creature Urzmil|NorthlandsSagas} (23 UVs total);

items.name: West Palisade:
entries: 1 hill giant, 2 ettins (13 UVs total);

items.name: South Palisade:
entries: 8 cultist units including Bolgrim (10 UVs total);
{@note {@sup †} If you wish to arrange the enemy forces differently, feel free, so long as no zone has more than half (23 UVs) the total UVs initially available.}

entries.name: Combat Sequence
entries: The enemy approaches the village from the western path (Zone 1), then attacks the north, south, and west palisade walls (Zones 2N, 2S, and 2W). All foe units engage; you may decide to have the enemy lead with the hill giant and ogre units.

items: {@b Round 1:} Enemies approach up the road and begin to fan out around the village's palisade as described above. If the heroes created an archer platform on the longhouse roof, they get a free shot before the first combat round.
{@b Round 2:} Enemies attack the north, south, and west palisade walls. The GM decides in what order they attack these zones.

entries: This sequence ends when the foes breach either the palisade or gate (in the west palisade wall) and those enemy units begin to move into the village. The ogre, goblin warrior, and cultist units {@action Dash|XPHB} toward the breaches.
Allow a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} after a couple large-scale-combat rounds to let the PCs recover some resources.

entries.name: The Assault Continues
entries: {@i Screams of warriors. Crash of collapsing palisades. Shouts of encouragement from allies.}

The cries of battle and the clang of weapons ring through the heavy air. Smoke has started to appear here and there in the village. Some of your preparations have clearly made a difference, but this fight seems far from over.

entries.name: Combat Sequence
entries: The bulk of this battle takes place in the longhouse and yard zones. Residual fighting may go on in the palisades zones as the rear enemy units make their way through the breach.

Recall that the cultists want to capture the magical longship, so they may send their hill giant and ettin units to the north and south palisade zones to attempt to break through to the beach. Meanwhile, the ogre, goblin warrior, and cultist units move toward the closest village defenders and use their actions to attack them. They favor named NPCs and player characters as targets.

At some point, if the cult leaders have not neared the beach on their own, {@creature Jerald Calsson|NorthlandsSagas} finds {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} and tells him about the tunnel (Area 11).
Feel free to deploy foe units as you like; the above is only a suggestion. Ensure you do not assign more than 50 percent of total enemy Unit Value to a single zone.

This sequence ends when either the enemy wins a zone in the yard and pushes the friendly units back to the beach (Area 7) or when one side's units defeats the other's, and the heroes and key foes move on to the Final Battle.

entries.name: Final Battle
entries: {@i Spellcasting warrior. Mighty bugbear. Climactic clash.}

This encounter occurs at a time chosen by the GM whenever the ship is about to be launched. If the PCs don't move to this area on their own, Kosktup sends a messenger saying they are needed at the beach (Area 7) to cover the vessel's escape.

The clash of steel, screams of pain, and bellowing of giants ring in the ears as battle encroaches from all sides. Near Kosktup's longship, the ratatosk and his crew stand on the deck, readying the sails and rigging. On land near the stern, Gretl and her team yell back and forth as they work to remove the last supports tethering the beached ship to the shore.
Agonizingly slowly, the great longship begins to slide into the water. Gretl spots you and yells, "It's just done! The crew is aboard. Just need a few moments to get her into the water and—"

Suddenly, Kosktup shouts a warning and points toward the south. Two figures storm across the beach toward the ship. One is a bugbear warrior, the other is {@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} himself! A third figure, human-sized, lurks in the shadow of one of the nearby buildings.

{@creature Bolgrim Boar-Scar|NorthlandsSagas} (see {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13}) and {@creature Urzmil|NorthlandsSagas} ({@creature Bugbear Stalker|XMM}) have passed through the secret tunnel to attack the characters at the ship launching. {@creature Jerald Calsson|NorthlandsSagas} or {@creature Luvaar Calsson|NorthlandsSagas} ({@creature Spy|XMM}) also may be on the scene.

items: They begin 60 feet away from the longship or at a distance chosen by the GM.
If Jerald or his brother survived to this point, they lurk near the closest building, looking for a chance to aid Bolgrim.
Bolgrim and {@creature Urzmil|NorthlandsSagas} work to defeat the PCs and board the longship.
They fight to the death.
If the foes are not defeated within 5 rounds, the longship slides into the water, and Kosktup orders the crew to row away from shore.

entries.name: Kosktup and Crew
entries: If the PCs need aid, {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas|Kosktup}, a {@creature ratatosk|ToB1-2023} {@creature Merchant Captain|NorthlandsWorldbook}, engages the foes from range—or closer if he must. Find stats for his vessel in the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13}.

entries.name: Gretl and Builders
entries: The 7 builders ({@creature Commoner|XMM|Commoners}) scatter, and {@creature Gretl Gunrsdottir|NorthlandsSagas|Gretl} ({@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM}) retreats to protect them. If she is engaged, she fights.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Bolgrim's gear, 4 {@item Opal|XDMG|opals} (worth 250 GP each), {@item Ravenflight Axe|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

entries.name: Development
entries: When Bolgrim falls and the longship is launched, any remaining forces attacking the village retreat from Hvalfell into the surrounding mountains and woods, their quarry out of reach. If the village has lost fewer than half its defenders, they give chase and pick off stragglers. Otherwise, they rest, see to the injured, mourn their dead, and assess the damage to their home.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: Skalds will tell tales and sing songs of the assault on Hvalfell for ages, and any characters who displayed great skill, courage, and valor undoubtedly find their names worked into a verse or two.

Henrika declares that surviving characters are friends of Hvalfell and gifts them with a home in the village (this can become a bastion for a player character, at the GM's discretion). If Pettra lives through the battle, she gifts {@item Tyr's Blade|NorthlandsSagas}, a {@item Vicious Longsword|XDMG} (see Area 2), to the character she thinks showed the most courage in the face of long odds and near-certain death.

entries.name: Further Adventures
entries: In a few days, when the coast is clear, {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} returns, and the characters set sail with Kosktup on his new longship. Soon enough, they receive word from Loki to travel to the bardic isle of Skaldholm...
But that is a story told in {@adventure Trials of the Lost Skald|NorthlandsSagas|5}, the next adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}.

data.name: Trials of the Lost Skald
entries: {@i Trials of the Lost Skald} is a second-tier adventure for a party of four to five 5th-level player characters, though you can adjust it to accommodate more or fewer players. The story, which features a deadly bardic contest, takes place in the Northlands on the island Skaldholm, but feel free to transplant it into the location of your choice.

During Part 2 of the scenario, the characters should reach 6th level. If this is the first adventure you're playing in the Sagas, refer to the {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0} for important backstory.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: The characters have accomplished many successes in their battle against the Cult of Ragnarok and its giant allies. However, even as they rest, the gods have further plans for them.

{@creature Keldar Tromma|NorthlandsSagas}, daughter of an important skald in Skaldholm, recently suffered a tragedy. Her dear friend Worlgrim died mysteriously on the isle's north coast, a knife in his back. Keldar brooded on the unanswered question of his death, until one night a dream came to her. In it she saw Worlgrim walking the shores, happy and smiling. Suddenly a figure emerged nearby with a knife and cruelly struck him down from behind. Keldar does not recognize the figure but, cradling the lyre of her fallen friend, she vows vengeance.
She is about to have her chance. The murderer in her dream is one of the player characters.

In truth, Worlgrim's death and Keldar's vision are the doing of the giant deity Angrboda, who seeks to twist events to cast blame on Loki's chosen heroes. If this thwarts her old lover's plans, so much the sweeter for her.

entries.name: Sagas Connections
entries: {@i Trials of the Lost Skald} is the fifth adventure in {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path. For those following the campaign arc, after finishing this adventure, the PCs will proceed to {@adventure Descent of Cloud Castle|NorthlandsSagas|6}.

The characters fought alongside {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} in {@adventure Assault on Hvalfell|NorthlandsSagas|4}, where he obtained {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} with its magical new drakahofud figurehead—which they acquired for him in {@adventure Among the Norns|NorthlandsSagas|3}.

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: Loki asks the PCs to journey to Skaldholm to secure the aid of the Brotherhood of Skalds in gathering allies to confront the Cult of Ragnarok. To do so, they must gain the support of the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles} on the island. From here, this adventure breaks down into two distinct parts.

entries.name: Part 1: Welcome to Skaldholm
entries: When the characters reach Skaldholm, they have an opportunity to meet its leader, the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}, who seems too distracted by the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing to devote any thought to their mission. Ultimately, the matter of their request is left up to the gods: He will aid their cause if the PCs compete successfully in contests of singing, tale-telling, and insults—all of which can prove deadly.

entries.name: Part 2: The Challenges
entries: The characters compete in reenactments of epic stories featuring mythic Northlands creatures and heroes. Victory in the contests earns the group an important ally in the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}. But {@creature Keldar Tromma|NorthlandsSagas} will stop at nothing to prevent the PCs from winning.

entries.name: Factions and Key Players
entries: Various factions take active part in this adventure, each working toward its own agenda:

items.name: Cult of Ragnarok:
entries: A sect of a doomsayers and misanthropes who believe Ragnarok is coming and work to spread the word and/or bring it about.

items.name: Keldar Tromma:
entries: Daughter of an important skald in Skaldholm. She belongs to the Shadowsingers and bears the PCs a grudge.

items.name: Master of Thyles:
entries: Master bard Eirik Ellefsen (human skald)—king of Skaldholm and leader of the Brotherhood of Skalds—is plagued by a disturbing riddle.

items.name: Petal Biteflower:
entries: The {@creature Aridni|ToB1-2023} fey is capricious and almost cruel to most, but she is enamored with Keldar—especially the music she makes on her drums.

items.name: Shadowsingers{@sup *}:
entries: A clandestine group within the Skaldic Brotherhood devoted to solving the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing using any means necessary.

items.name: Skaldic Brotherhood{@sup *}:
entries: An influential bardic school network that stretches across the Northlands.
{@note {@sup *} See {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 3: Factions of the Northlands|NorthlandsWorldbook|3}.}

entries.name: Call to Action
entries: The trickster god Loki visits the group shortly after events of the last adventure, appearing initially as an enormous ginger domestic cat that tries to sit on a PC's lap and eagerly listens to their conversation. After eavesdropping long enough to hear any gossip or malcontent, the cat transforms into Loki's true form right before the heroes' amazed eyes.

Loki does not idle: The characters have work to do. The foes of the Cult of Ragnarok need allies in the coming events, powerful ones. Loki asks the PCs to venture to the Isle of the Bards—Skaldholm—and seek favor with its ruler and leader of the Skaldic Brotherhood, the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}. The man's many alliances and friends could help greatly against the cult. Gaining his aid won't be easy, as the master presently occupies himself with a disturbing riddle.
Loki tells the PCs that time is short. And with that, the god of trickery steps out and is gone.

entries.name: Alternate Adventure Hook
entries: If you are not running this as a part of the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, Loki visits the characters as an old wise woman, complaining about the pains of her old body. She seeks to hire them for a diplomatic mission to seek allies against the foul Cult of Ragnarok.
