In exchange for securing the Master of Thyles's aid, she offers them a reward of one {@filter Uncommon magic item|items|rarity=uncommon} of their choice and provides transport aboard Kosktup Farleap's new ship, {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}.

entries.name: Part 1: Welcome to Skaldholm
entries: The characters have access to {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}, a new longship with a more-than-willing ratatosk captain. The journey is swift but, depending on the distance, you might wish to add an encounter on the way. Otherwise, despite rough seas across the Swive, no further perils await the PCs as they reach the city of Skaldholm upon the island of the same name.

Refer to {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 2: Epic Regions of the North|NorthlandsWorldbook|3} for full details on Skaldholm, its ruler, and the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing. When the group approaches the isle, read or paraphrase the following description:

A lush green island lies ahead, rising to a towering volcano that must be the glowering Bragafjall Mountain. Deep forests cling to the mountain, interspersed with brightly colored settlements, some shrouded in the mists of hot springs. Directly ahead, resting in the curve of a natural harbor, is Skaldholm, the City of Bards. Its pale buildings seem to dance in a confusion of streets, yet everything appears light and airy. A gentleness wafts over the place, and the sounds of song begin to reach you. As you draw into the harbor, smiling faces watch your arrival, and the musical resonance grows into one harmonious cloak of sound.

entries.name: The City of Skaldholm
entries: Although graceful and soaked in song, the streets of Skaldholm can seem confusing. Famous as a place of knowledge and learning, the isle boasts many visitors—and, of course, guides. Upon arrival, the PCs encounter a quartet of broadly-smiling guides vying for their attention and money. Each extols the confusion of the streets, the countless colleges, and the ease of getting lost. Each seeks to impress the PCs: One sings, another recites an epic poem—tears in her eyes as she ends—and a third brings out a horn and a songbird and plays a short serenade to the singing bird. The last fetches a huge drum and pounds it—all the better for clearing the way! It doesn't matter who the heroes pick to guide them (if anyone), but a small payment of 5 GP saves them from having to ask questions, make skill checks, and possibly get lost.

All the guides know the local landmarks, singing (literally) the praises of places like the Archive ("the Tower of All Knowledge, no less!") or the Skaldic Schools ("Beware Tromma's Pit, the new college has a reputation for drumming berserkers!"). They also all do their best to install PCs in shops, bathhouses and lodgings of their relatives ("The finest in the city!").

The characters likely express a wish to meet the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}. A guide tells them the following information; otherwise they must make a {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check to find out these facts from the locals:

entries.name: The Master of Thyles is always extremely busy
entries: It's usually impossible to get past his Herald, {@creature Sylvoll|NorthlandsSagas}: his confidant, adviser, and—some say—lover. She manages the court with an iron grip. However, she, like many in this city, finds herself won over by the charisma, talents, and talk of visitors. Win her admiration, and the master soon becomes available.

entries.name: The master currently puzzles over the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing
entries: He has set his finest and wisest to seek out this thing that he has forgotten, knowing the memory is of the greatest import and yet gone—perhaps stolen from him.

entries.name: To win the master's favor and aid, one can attempt the Four Magnificent Challenges of Skald Thalwyn Rotjun
entries: Everyone knows of them, and some fools even take these challenges! Each one proves perilous, and they change like the storms over the Swive. Each challenge honors the memory of Skald Thalwyn Rotjun, the heroic dwarf warrior who battled the fire giants that once ruled the isles. The perilous tests involve foul monsters, trials of one's art and talent, and opponents of extraordinary gifts that one must overcome through wit and wile. Yes, people have died facing them, but once someone requests the challenge before the master, it must be offered and accepted, or shame falls upon all involved.

entries.name: A Visit to Thyles Hall
entries: The master dwells in Thyles Hall in the center of the city. Its location is public knowledge, as are the short tempers of its many guards. The master selects them for their bragging skills and insults, which normal folk must bear (or cunningly rebuff) to gain entry.

The most important building in Skaldholm is—rather like its locals—a curious amalgam of different styles and influences. Three towers rise from a peculiar collage of parts, yet like the city itself, it somehow works. When considering the attached longhouse, the odd clash of Northern and Southern styles seems integral to the home's grandiosity.

Thyles Hall is surrounded by a square patrolled by dozens of guards wearing white uniforms with golden lyre symbols. They wander among scores of people—some of whom perform for crowds, but all of whom sing, hum, whistle, or play instruments. A long queue stretches out before the hall's very large entrance gate.

The feared and boastful orators of the Skald Guard keep the peace here, each a {@creature Guard|XMM} but with particular magniloquence. The use of long and outlandish (sometimes invented) words strung into insults and boasts rises to an art form here, and visitors may find themselves referred to as {@i flaccid, hircine farmers; a cantankerous hinny;} or {@i a fetid, hirsute cadaver}. Many guards content themselves with simply giving visitors long agonized stares and shaking their heads, extolling their own (usually ridiculously overblown) skills and talents, {@i réclame}, and {@i coruscation}.
The long queue for those wishing to access the hall seems generally orderly. The characters may come up with peaceful ways to circumvent waiting:

items.name: {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC notices one young lad playing a small pipe beautifully who suddenly is taken inside.

items.name: {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC plays or sings well enough to gain entry for the group.

items.name: {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC wittily insults the guards or carries out a similar artful action to jump the queue and is led inside by a trio of guards.
Otherwise, not long after, rain begins to pound down. The heroes stand several hours waiting before gaining admittance.

Once inside, the characters are escorted through a maze of corridors until they arrive in the main timber longhouse they saw from outside. Intricately carved images of gods, legendary heroes, and—most prolifically—skalds decorate the huge chamber. The place has peculiar acoustics; characters can hear people speaking from the raised stage as if they stood next to them. A captivating human male sits on a throne, itself a work of art depicting fire giants in supplication. The man dresses plainly, but the adventurers can see that, unusually, he wears a silk robe. A dozen people surround him, including a striking woman who strides about organizing things. A queue awaits below the stage, everyone hoping for a chance to speak to the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC notices the master's hands look calloused and spots a rather battered harp leaning against the throne. If they meet the master, characters playing a harp make checks with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}, as he loves harp music.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC knows the silk robe—subtly embroidered with patterns of musical notes and ancient runes—is undoubtedly Southern, and clearly of great value. If they meet the master, characters pointing out the robe's possible ancestry learn it was a gift from a Southern emperor that reminds him of his time in the desert courts. Any checks these PCs make to persuade the master also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

The master shares the stage with two other important NPCs. The first is {@creature Rurik Ljodrun|NorthlandsSagas}, a domineering dwarf skald who clearly holds great sway. The dwarf is the Master of Ceremonies, responsible for conducting all Skaldholm events in traditional ways. He has a reputation for a very dark sense of humor and has been said to know every epic in Skaldholm history, word for word. Rurik has never smiled and seems to disagree with everything said here.

The second is {@creature Keldar Tromma|NorthlandsSagas}, the adopted human daughter of {@creature Einar Tromma|NorthlandsSagas}, trollkin leader of a respected college in the city. Like her mother, the hot-headed Keldar enjoys beating drums—particularly in combat. She is renowned for her constant companion, an {@creature Aridni|ToB1-2023} fey named {@creature Petal Biteflower|NorthlandsSagas}. Keldar, a Shadowsinger, can be almost as feral as her companion, yet she is a scholar and has notable skill on her drum. As mentioned in the {@adventure Adventure Background|NorthlandsSagas|5|Adventure Background}, Keldar had a dream sent by Angrboda in which her dear friend died at the hands of a PC (GM's choice). As soon as she sees that character, she locks her eyes on them; a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check reveals the hatred in her stare. For now she watches the party, but she has a large role to play in the coming events. She must avenge her friend's honor!

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC notices the two key NPCs in the hubbub of the hall.

items.name: {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC learns the above information about them from others nearby.

entries.name: Speaking to the Master
entries: Today the characters get a chance for an audience with the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}. If they fail, they must come back again the next day and try afresh. They have only two chances—any subsequent attempts result in their polite ejection.

The PCs may simply try to shout that they wish to face the challenges; however, unless you deem such desperation the only option after two failures, such an announcement generates belittling laughter in the hall.

entries.name: Enter the Herald
entries: After a while, {@creature Sylvoll|NorthlandsSagas} speaks to the PCs, asking their business with the master, who is weary and troubled (she does her utmost to protect him from unwanted visitors). Bear in mind, she has heard hundreds of people say they can answer the Riddle of the Forgotten Thing. She also knows how much time and effort the master and others have to put into any request to face the Four Magnificent Challenges.

The PCs must impress her before they get anywhere near the master. {@creature Sylvoll|NorthlandsSagas} does not hesitate to have guards eject troublesome guests—if they play this wrong, they may not get a second chance. Do not allow a single PC or skill check to dictate the outcome with the herald. Invite the heroes to explain their reason for coming here, embellishing it with some skill checks. {@creature Sylvoll|NorthlandsSagas} speaks with all the PCs, asking each one why they have come.

If the conversation grows spirited, heroic, and passionate, the master himself suddenly asks {@creature Sylvoll|NorthlandsSagas} to bring the strangers to him and invites them to speak. Otherwise she says he is too tired to see them today.

entries.name: An Appeal to the Master
entries: If they meet him, the master looks troubled but calmly listens to their tale. He immediately disregards any appeal for aid against the Cult of Ragnarok from strangers such as they. To get him to listen to their request to face the Four Magnificent Challenges, the characters must succeed at two {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) or ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) checks—or make a suitably impassioned plea. As the discussion continues, they notice that the hall has fallen silent.
If the party succeeds, the master rises, idly playing his harp as he considers.

"I shall grant your wish to face the Four Magnificent Challenges," he announces with a grim expression. "The contests shall take place in three days at the Althing Arena." He gestures at his Master of Ceremonies. "Rurik Ljodrun shall make the arrangements. After you pass the challenges, strangers, you may request a boon of me—if any of you survive."

entries.name: A New Opponent
entries: As he finishes, {@creature Keldar Tromma|NorthlandsSagas} begs the master for the honor of serving as an opponent in the challenges. After he agrees, she walks slowly and purposefully to within an inch of the PC she considers a murderer and speaks:
"It is an honor, master," she states, staring relentlessly not at the Master of Thyles but at one of your number. "And honor must always be satisfied."
As the guards politely escort the characters out, Rurik, the Master of Ceremonies says, he will be in touch.

entries.name: Getting Ready
entries: The characters have a few days to explore Skaldholm and prepare. They surely wish to learn more about what they have just gotten themselves into. They might visit the Archive in the Hall of Sagas to learn rare spells. They could tour the island, visiting the Retreat, a nearby lodge, to relax before their endeavors.

Should they ask about Keldar, they find themselves directed to the home of her mother, who responds that her adopted daughter is passionate about protecting the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles} and the Brotherhood. If she opposes the PCs, it's for that reason—or to ensure that they are truly worthy to make a request of the master.

Build up the atmosphere for this event during the days leading up to the challenges by having people recognize the PCs in the streets and commend them for their courage or folly. Let them overhear snippets about previous challengers who enjoyed legendary successes or spectacular deaths. In addition, two unexpected events occur in the days leading up to the event.

entries.name: 'So, What Are These Challenges?'
entries: Folk celebrate the heroic life of the dwarf hero Skald Thalwyn Rotjun in her battles against the fire giants in eight hundred and eighty verses of an epic poem, which all Masters of Thyles learn. Rotjun's incredible adventures are a mixture of song, deed, and poem. Skaldholm residents regularly perform reenactments of her adventures and occasional recitals of the epic—an event that only the hardiest and most dedicated skalds undertake, as its reading can go for days. See this adventure's handout for short excerpts that hint at the nature of each coming challenge.

Woven into these adventures are the Four Magnificent Challenges. The {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles} determines the tests secretly prior to the undertaking. Some sections become competitive, with the master choosing opponents from among students who have caught his eye.

The characters might already know something of the challenges. Those who make successful Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) checks know the information in the table below corresponding to the DC achieved. Higher results reveal all the information of lesser ones.

Otherwise, the PCs can spend their time asking locals about the event; a single Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check encompasses four hours of chatting. Increase the DC by 5 if asking outside of Skaldholm.

entries.caption: History or Persuasion Check Results
rows: The Four Magnificent Challenges of Skald Thalwyn Rotjun are a way of gaining trust or aid from the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}, ruler of Skaldholm, a wise, and well-connected leader. Challenges change from master to master, year to year, but always retain the same core values—they are entertaining, pay suitable homage to Rotjun's heroism, and are suitably dangerous. Deaths happen. Making the challenges perilous deters whimsical requests for the favor of the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}, ensuring that only matters of great import get determined this way.

The challenges take place at the Althing Arena, a natural amphitheater in the northeast sector of Skaldholm city. A multitude of skalds watch—and in some cases participate. They are a tough crowd, commonly hurling objects at competitors. Wise participants work to get the crowd on their side.

The challenges generally involve a mix of performance and encounters with creatures from the Skaldholm Menagerie. These reflect the perils Rotjun faced, especially her many adventures with fire giants and their guardian beasts. They also pay homage to the dwarf's cleverness—she often outwitted the giants rather than slaughtering them. Common tests involve charming beasts into calmness, driving them away using song, plus reading and enacting various parts of the epic.

entries.name: Unwelcome Attention
entries: {@creature Keldar Tromma|NorthlandsSagas} intends to get revenge. She plans to unmask the murdering character (and their friends) at the end of the challenges and demand justice, betting the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles} would not refuse her request. To test the PCs' relative strengths in the meantime, she directs a few local rogues their way via intermediaries, suggesting the strangers are very rich and gullible.

A duo of local villains—{@creature Freyis Mosjøen|NorthlandsSagas|Freyis} and {@creature Eira Mosjøen|NorthlandsSagas}—famous for their broad smiles and laughter as they rob, hear the rumors and decide to relieve the visitors of their cash. The two human {@creature Bandit Lord|ToB1-2023|Bandit Lords} choose a quiet spot to attack the PCs, but exactly where is up to you—a street late at night or early in the morning is ideal.

Cohorts of Keldar who have learned of the attack hover nearby, watching from a safe distance to report back to her on the PCs' abilities. If the adventurers defeat the villains, they find 42 PP on them. Under questioning, Freyis and Eira say that "word about town" says the PCs are wealthy and easy targets. Depending how the characters handle the situation, the duo might try again if freed, coming back with extra {@creature Bandit|XMM|Bandits}.

items.name: {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC figures out that Freyis and Eira are lying or covering for Keldar, who started the rumor about the party's wealth. (Keldar used {@skill Persuasion|XPHB} to invite her minions to attempt an attack without outright telling them to do so.)

entries.name: Words of Wisdom
entries: A day or so before the challenge, {@creature Rurik Ljodrun|NorthlandsSagas} approaches the group. The dour dwarf explains they are to arrive at Highsun on the day of the challenges, and that all of them are expected to take part. They should come to the entry gate of the Althing Arena in the northeast sector of the city. He pointedly asks each character if they have any particular wishes in the event of their deaths.

Rurik gives little away, but characters who make a successful {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check can get him to reveal that the master always seems impressed by spectacle, flamboyance, and flair. PCs who remember that have a good chance of succeeding, even though the dwarf appears entirely indifferent to their fate.

He adds that two other contestants represent the master in one of the tests, and that it has been almost seventy-five years since anyone succeeded in all four challenges. The master often views succeeding in three as a victory, especially if the contestants have put on an entertaining spectacle, die heroically, or receive life-changing injuries.
A sizable crowd always attends, Rurik notes, adding cryptically that the skalds in the crowd like nothing more than "being part of such a spectacle."

Since the day the master accepted the request for challenge, Rurik has placed the Althing Arena under guard as he and a veritable army of skalds make preparations. Sightseers are kept at least one hundred yards away. But the PCs may find a way to view the preparations. If they are caught doing so, however, guards escort them to the harbor and tell them to leave Skaldholm directly.

entries.name: Part 2: The Challenges
entries: To gain a boon from the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}, the characters have seized the opportunity to attempt the Four Magnificent Challenges of the Skald Thalwyn Rotjun. And "challenge" is definitely the word for these tests.

The Althing Arena lies on the northeast edge of the city, within a natural amphitheater surrounded by cliffs, hills, and buildings. One can access the place safely only from the sea or via the entry tower. On the day of the challenges, two guards await the PCs at the entry tower—perhaps the same ones they met at Thyles Hall.

entries.name: Entry Tower
entries: The group passes into the tower and is asked to wait. As well as the double doors ahead that lead into the arena, this round chamber holds two secret doors (on the north and south sides of the tower) through which four jesters (see {@adventure The Truror|NorthlandsSagas|5|The Truror} sidebar) carry scenery and lead monsters; the jesters currently wait on the other side of the south door. The guards ask any inquisitive characters not to try to open the doors.
Based on the noise coming through the closed double doors, a sizable crowd awaits in the arena beyond.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC also hears half a dozen different low rumbling growls from behind the northern secret door.

items.name: {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC identifies the above sounds as {@creature Elderly Owlbear|NorthlandsSagas|Owlbears}.

A short while later the jesters—dressed as clown-like fire giants and carrying horns decorated with fire symbols are allowed in through the southern secret door. They open the double doors into the Althing Arena and lead the characters out.

A large natural amphitheater opens before you—a broad flat space around twenty yards across. About it, a low rising bank gives way to a gentle hill of grass and stones to the south, and towering rocky cliffs north and behind. Eastward, a small rocky islet lies perhaps thirty yards from the shore, odd cobbled steps vanishing into the sea that way.

Two curiously beautiful towers, built in a chaotic way similar to Thyles Hall, overlook the area. These towers each hold a number of graceful arched viewing platforms about thirty feet above the ground; similar but far more vertiginous arched bays in the cliffs give a dizzying view into the whole area. These spaces, and the hill to the south, are crammed with an eclectic mix of folk, who cheer your entrance heartily. The master himself, with his herald close by, sits on a raised throne beneath the north tower's central archway. A curiously large horn and drum take up the adjacent arched space.

The view immediately before you is odd. A huge tree grows in the center of the arena, its lowest branches far above hung with ropes. They pass through odd platforms positioned perhaps ten feet from the ground before ending five feet or so above the floor. The whole tree shimmers. It is clearly illusory.
The inscrutable figure of Rurik Ljodrun steps out before you, gripping a beautiful wooden megaphone.

entries.name: The Truror
entries: Four jester skalds—known in Skaldholm as the Truror appear throughout the challenges, dressed in a variety of outfits. They carry wide-mouthed horns that act as megaphones. They stir the crowd, keep interest up, and act the fool. They also assist the characters in some instances and, if needed, distract monsters (for example, one attacking a stricken or dying PC). Skilled acrobats and minor mages, these skalds may mock the adventurers, falling over laughing when a character fails a check badly, or wildly applauding if they succeed after failing.

entries.name: Running the Challenges
entries: The arena is a circle of compacted sand surrounded by a small grassy bank. As with the stage in Thyles Hall, the crowd of five hundred or so skalds can hear every utterance made on the floor of the arena. As Master of Ceremonies, {@creature Rurik Ljodrun|NorthlandsSagas} carries a megaphone made of tonrosp, a native hardwood with excellent resonance. He addresses the crowd from the air—he uses his {@item Wings of Flying|XDMG} for every challenge. The dwarf, still unsmiling, seeks to add to the day's spectacle by loudly commenting on events and winding up the crowd, often comparing today's challenges to historic ones that ended very badly.

Rurik introduces each event in a deadpan style, casually using words like "maimed," "magnificent," and "unspeakable horror" with abandon. (Use the read-aloud sections at the start of each challenge for his lead-ins.) He also may have quiet words with the PCs before each new test, as detailed in the text. The dour dwarf is here to ensure fair play and announce any challenge results—blowing a graceful note on the great horn in the north tower to indicate success, and pounding the drum for failures before somberly announcing the result in his deep voice.
Note that certain members of the Shadowsingers intend to cause mischief at Keldar Tromma's prompting; see Challenge 2.

entries.name: Challenge Format
entries: Each test's section below follows the same basic format:

items: First comes the {@b Start} position to launch the challenge.
Then basics of the {@b Challenge} and how to pass it, usually spoken by Rurik.

Next comes the {@b Setting}, which details the arena's layout. When spells are involved, eager spellcasters in the crowd assist and set up the scenes from one challenge to the next. Sometimes props come into play.
The next section discusses {@b Aids} the PCs have in completing the task, then their {@b Opponents}.
Finally, the {@b Obstacles} section notes factors that might come between the heroes and success.

entries: After each event, the Truor jesters—assisted by guards—remove any detritus (dead bodies, sleeping owlbears). Guards escort the PCs back into the entry tower, keeping a watchful eye on them. Generally it takes 10 to 15 minutes to clear up after each challenge and prepare the next one (though, as GM, you may decide to allow the PCs a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} if needed). During this break, various diversions keep the crowd amused; the adventurers may hear odd noises, cheering, howls, and screams from behind the arena's doors.
Challenges are designed for four PCs. Vary the number of owlbears in Challenge 1 for more or fewer characters; the other challenges need no changes.

entries.name: Playing to the Crowd
entries: All the characters should get involved in this event—not just bards and others with high Charisma. In fact, Challenges 1, 3, and 4 involve all the PC (Challenge 2 involves just two, pitting them against the master's champions).

The crowd is there for the characters to win over; indeed, getting the audience on their side can actually help some checks—or hurt them, should the crowd turn nasty. If involved in an event directly, each PC can choose a moment once per challenge to {@i play to the crowd}. Characters not directly involved in a test (in Challenge 2) can play to the crowd three times during it.
The characters use the following methods to play to the crowd:

items: A {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check
Another appropriate skill check
Brilliant roleplay and improvisation

entries: If won over, the crowd cheers and encourages the group, adding a +2 bonus to the next check of the PC's choice during the current challenge. A supportive crowd also can ridicule an opponent of the PCs choice, imposing a –2 penalty on their next check.

Aggressive or overtly violent tactics—such as using {@spell Fireball|XPHB} against owlbears from the Skaldholm Menagerie—turns the crowd against the PCs, as does cowardice such as using {@spell Fly|XPHB} or {@spell Levitate|XPHB} to escape trouble. Such behavior imposes a –2 penalty on all the character's checks for the rest of the challenge.

entries.name: Extraordinary Successes and Lamentable Failures
entries: The crowd is very vocal and active during the challenges. The audience reacts well to extraordinary success and treats failure or dullness harshly.

When a character gets a check result of 25 or higher—or rolls a natural 20 on a check—treat it as an extraordinary success. The crowd goes wild, granting {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} to that PC's next check. Conversely, any check result below 5 or a natural roll of 1 causes a lamentable failure; the crowd boos and hisses, imposing {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on that character's next check.

entries.name: Encourage Roleplaying!
entries: With this whole event, don't get too hung up on dice rolls or use them exclusively to determine results. Some players love rolling dice, others do not. Characters doing extraordinary things—both good and bad—also should use this system. A panicky PC fleeing an owlbear is lamentable, but characters making the crowd laugh by telling owlbear jokes as they retreat is extraordinary; no check needed for either one.

entries.name: Tracking
entries: Keep track of extraordinary successes and lamentable failures throughout the challenges. If a character achieves 5 or more extraordinary successes, then—regardless of success or failure in the challenges—the master presents that PC with a {@item Master's Tonrosp Flute|NorthlandsSagas|tonrosp wood flute} of such extraordinary quality that all Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) checks made using it receive a +2 bonus. The flute is worth 500 GP. If a character somehow manages 10 extraordinary successes, the master adds a further gift of a set of {@item Pipes of the Sewers|XDMG}.

entries.name: Challenge 1: Dance of the Slumbering Bears!
entries: {@i Huge tree festooned with ropes and platforms. Horns and bells. Enter the owlbears.}

"The tales tell," calls out the Master of Ceremonies, "that Skald Thalwyn Rotjun ventured through the brooding forests below Bragafjall Mountain alone. The fire giants' foul-tempered bears dwelled in these forests—they guarded the area ferociously. Legend says the hero picked her way through the great forest, climbing from branch to branch, her gentle singing and horn playing lulling the horrifying bears into a deep sleep. Thus she safely reached the hall of Stomgrunn, the deadly fire giant skald-poet, and dispatched him with her greataxe Maschkarr, the Poet-Slayer.
"Let our heroes form a circle around the tree and prepare themselves for unspeakable horror!"

entries.name: Start:
entries: The guards remove the characters' (obvious) weapons for this challenge. Rurik then directs the group to stand around the tree and make ready. He gives them 2 rounds to compose themselves before shouting, "Bring forth the dancing bears!" The entry gate opens, and a half dozen owlbears enter, looking angry. The crowd begins to cheer and laugh.

entries.name: Challenge:
entries: Put all the owlbears to sleep or render them unconscious by other means, thereby recreating the epic poem.

entries.name: Setting:
entries: The tree is illusory. Seven low-hanging branches—through variant uses of the {@spell Rope Trick|XPHB} spell—feature 20-foot lengths of rope that hang in the air 5 feet above the ground. Some 10 feet above the ground are small platforms that resemble barrel lids about 2 feet across. These platforms appear on the top portion of the map, around the tree. Each rope passes through its platform and connects to a branch above.

items.name: {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC climbs a rope and reaches the platform.

items.name: {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC balances atop the platform without holding on. (A character may hold onto the rope and take one-handed actions without this check.)

entries.name: Aids:
entries: 4 tonrosp wood horns and 4 clubs wreathed in tiny noisy bells lie scattered randomly about the arena.

items: The horns emit a clear and beautiful note with a range of 15 feet, which a character can direct at a single target. On hearing the note, an owlbear must make a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw, falling {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} on a failure.

Characters can sing to an owlbear within 10 feet (no farther due to the crowd's noise), making a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check. A success causes the targeted owlbear to make a {@dc 12} Wisdom saving throw, falling {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} on a failure.

entries.name: Opponents:
entries: The 6 {@creature Elderly Owlbear|NorthlandsSagas|Owlbears} are elderly, as anyone notes with a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check. They remain susceptible to the sound of the horns and to song. The owlbears remain very dangerous and aggressive but quite dim, moving toward random targets each round (unless already engaged in melee), including those on the platforms beyond their reach. Use these variations on the standard stat block:

items: HP 38 ({@damage 7d10})
{@variantrule Speed|XPHB} 30 ft., Climb 30 ft.
CR 2
{@b Rend.} {@i Melee Attack Roll:} +4, reach 5 ft. {@i Hit:} 14 ({@damage 2d8 + 2}) Slashing damage

entries: {@note See {@creature Elderly Owlbear|NorthlandsSagas}}

entries.name: Obstacles:
entries: The magic of the {@spell Rope Trick|XPHB} spells is deliberately weak. Every 3 rounds after the Start, one of the ropes vanishes. Anyone on a platform or clinging to a disappearing rope falls.

The jesters are here to ensure drama. If the PCs seem to be doing too well, they try to wake up the sleeping bears. At least three of them must stand within 5 feet of an unconscious owlbear and yell through their megaphone to awaken one. The jesters do this no more than three times during the challenge, and only at your discretion.

entries.name: Challenge 2: Duel of Bragging, Singing, and Insults!
Getting Personal
entries: In the second challenge, the contestants use mockery and ridicule to win. Some groups love to roleplay these out, using real insults aimed at NPCs and each other's characters to enrich the experience. Others may not enjoy this style of play. There is no right or wrong way to handle this part of the adventure—whatever works for you and your players is the best solution. But be nice. You're with friends.

items: If you prefer, simply indicate that the character seeks to ridicule the other and make a check. After all, you wouldn't expect a player to actually perform a forward-roll in your game room to make an Acrobatics check. This can work the same way.

However, if you and your players enjoy banter, then play it out. Should you wish, modify the check with a bonus or penalty to suit the group's reaction—and maybe even prepare the odd rhyme to use on the PCs.

entries: {@i Great stone megaliths. Calm, misty pool. Opponents.}
When the PCs enter the Althing Arena for the second time, the entire scene has changed:

The arena's central area now looks totally different. A ring of five dolmens stands about a pool. Inside the pool are four more dolmens. Strange mist rises from the pool. Gentle grasses grow around it, wafting in the slight breeze to caress the feet of Rurik Ljodrun, who prepares to speak.

Apart from the four central dolmens, which are wooden props, everything in the arena is illusory magic. A set of simple rungs has been hammered into each of these four 10-foot high props, allowing the contestants to mount them.

"We know that after slaughtering Stomgrunn—whose poetry in truth never rhymed—Skald Thalwyn Rotjun found a place called Lyric's Garden, where she came upon countless menhirs." Rurik takes a breath, then continues. "So peaceful was this garden that she slept. When she awoke, a crowd of angry fire giants surrounded her, led by Grisslorp, Stomgrunn's less talented, two-headed sister.

"Outnumbered and surrounded, the skald used her wits and hurled upon Grisslorp withering insults gathered in countless flytings. So crushing were her insults, even her own kin turned on the giant, showering their erstwhile leader's sister with wasp nests they used as weapons.
"Our next contest reflects that day. The losers may get lucky and merely become horribly maimed! Prepare your own angry wasps, and bring forth the warriors!"

The jesters—now dressed as wasps—enter the area leading two others: a robust-looking dwarf introduced as {@creature Woolnag Dorrow|NorthlandsSagas} of Hrafnaskald's Academy, and {@creature Keldar Tromma|NorthlandsSagas}, who volunteered for this event. The jesters tell the PCs to quickly pick the two of their number best at taunting, rhymes, and wit, for this is a contest of insults! The other two contestants play the crowd as this occurs.
When the PCs have chosen their contestants, one jester speaks to each of the two, whispering something helpful in their ear about the NPCs:

items: "Do you see young Dorrow's hair? It is a hairpiece. It's made, they say, from the pelt of a cave bear, the smell of which still lingers on it."
"Tromma's relationship to that little pixie creature in the audience is a mystery. Some say they're in love. Others claim the fey is a demon. Me, I just think the little thing likes drumming."

entries: If the PC contestants succeed on a {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check, the jesters also reveal the following:

items: "Oh yes, I nearly forgot, young Dorrow—look at his clothing. Isn't it odd? They say his grandmother has dressed him since childhood."
"Ah yes, and one more thing about Tromma. She doesn't abide anyone mistreating her little friend. Broke some poor lad's arm, I heard."

entries: Similar conversations about the selected PCs take place nearby. Keldar also, of course, might know things from the earlier attack on them and use that information to her advantage.

entries.name: Start:
entries: The contestants each climb to the top of one of the central dolmens. The Truror jesters remind them that all outright attacks are discouraged.

entries.name: Challenge:
entries: In turn, each contestant hurls (unanswered) insults at an opponent of their choice. These can be taunting words, rhymes, or songs, all while bragging about their own abilities. The contest goes on until the crowd signals its desire for a challenger to be removed by chanting "Shame!" The jesters then remove that player from the dolmen and the challenge.

It takes several minutes for all the contestants to get ready, giving your players a chance to prepare. The jesters buzz and play while this occurs. Players may just wish to state who their characters are insulting and for what, or the players may actually make up a rhyme or insult to chasten their opponents. If you think their invented work merits it, allow a success—maybe even an extraordinary success—or simply roll the dice.

For this challenge, each contestant has three "lives." They lose a life if they receive an insult backed by a {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check, or a {@dc 17} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check, or if they roll a natural 1. Anyone who loses all three lives or falls to HP 0 or less (see Complication, below) gets eliminated as described above. When only one contestant remains, the contest ends.

For more details, see the {@variantrule Flyting|NorthlandsWorldbook} section of {@book Chapter 7: Running a Northlands Campaign|NorthlandsWorldbook|7|Flyting} in the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}.

entries.name: Setting:
entries: The challengers stand on the dolmens.

entries.name: Aids:
entries: The participating PCs can get help from party members who play to the crowd as the challenge progresses.

entries.name: Opponents:
entries: {@creature Woolnag Dorrow|NorthlandsSagas}, a poet, likes to use rhyming words to boast about his rhyming skills, style, and magnificent head of hair. He makes Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) checks at +4 and Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) checks at +6. Assume Dorrow has HP 25.

{@creature Keldar Tromma|NorthlandsSagas} has a drum, which she beats loudly as she boasts about her physical prowess as opposed to her foes' weakness. Her pixie companion, {@creature Petal Biteflower|NorthlandsSagas}, sits on a post among the audience. If the "murderer" is a contestant, Keldar attacks them constantly, even continuing her insults after she (or the character) is removed from the challenge. Her Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) skill check modifier is +6.

entries.name: Obstacles:
entries: The crowd has received Angry Wasps: hefty darts that make an angry buzzing noise when hurled. Audience members throw them frequently at those who draw their displeasure; the PCs and their opponents may find themselves targeted. The air swarms with buzzing as darts hurtle down.

entries.name: Complication
entries: In the crowd sit agents of the Shadowsingers, friends of Keldar who have covered their darts with poison. If a PC becomes subject to a dart attack, one of the weapons that hits is coated in {@item Carrion Crawler Mucus|XDMG} poison. This can occur twice in this scene.

entries.caption: Angry Wasp Conditions
colLabels: Crowd Hurls Darts at a Contestant Who...

items: Makes a skill check with a result of less than 5
Is on the receiving end of a skill check of 20 or higher

rows: 15 ({@damage 6d4 + 3}) Piercing damage on a failure; half as much damage on a success

items: Rolls a natural 1
Is subject to a {@dc 25} skill check
Is on the receiving end of a natural 20 insult

rows: 24 ({@damage 10d4 + 4}) Piercing damage on a failure; half as much damage on a success

entries.name: Challenge 3: The Epic of Tharl Thrysken!
entries: {@i Unaugmented arena. Truror mice. Obese giant wrapped in chains.}

The Master of Ceremonies introduces the scene: "When Tharl Thrysken laid eyes upon Skald Thalwyn Rotjun, he fell in love. Yet she was herself frozen, her features marble, for she had inhaled the breath of Fenrir and become ice. No sound came from her: no laughter, no tears. Yet as Tharl Thrysken lay weeping in frustration at her curse, his tears brought her back to life—she became whole again and loved him.

"Our contestants will know this daunting challenge now! They must face a creature that has never uttered a single laugh nor shed a single tear. Change that, break a face of stone into smile or sorrow, and the challenge is won!
"Look upon the unspeakable terror from the master's darkest menagerie and despair! Bring forth the Malcontent!"

entries.name: Start:
entries: The jesters remind the competitors that outright attacks are discouraged.

entries.name: Challenge:
entries: Make the Malcontent —a {@creature Flab Giant|ToB1-2023}— laugh or weep. Each character may try, in turn, to do so; failure brings pain. The giant wears a {@item Mantle of Spell Resistance|XDMG} and, while a single well-placed {@spell Command|XPHB} spell or something similar could swiftly reward the PCs, casting it proves dangerous. If the giant makes a successful saving throw against a spell, it lashes out at the caster twice with its Chain Whip.

items.name: {@dc 25} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC makes the giant laugh or weep; the influence of Angrboda has inflated the DC for this check. On a failure, the angry giant lashes out once with its Chain Whip against the offending PC.

entries.name: Setting:
entries: A plain open space with nowhere to hide.

entries.name: Aids:
entries: The jesters, dressed as mice and armed with whips, scuttle about trying to distract the giant, but quickly flee when real trouble starts.

entries.name: Opponents:
entries: The {@creature Malcontent|NorthlandsSagas}, a {@creature Flab Giant|ToB1-2023}, staggers about in hefty chains, which it also wields as whips against those displease or anger it.

entries.name: Obstacles:
entries: Initially, the giant uses its Chain Whip ({@i Melee Weapon Attack:} +7 to hit, reach 15 ft., one target. {@i Hit:} 11 [{@damage 3d4 + 5}] Slashing damage) only at opponents who fail to raise emotions. However, if the PCs succeed, or if enough time has passed with a few failures that the event starts to drag, the giant suddenly roars, pulling away its chains (but not its Mantle) and attacks the characters furiously. Although the Truror are available to help, the master forbids any such assistance (unless the PCs are clearly about to die), assuming the gods have deliberately angered the giant and wish to see this become a test of strength as well as wits.

Actually the master is correct—as he often is. The giant's sudden anger arose entirely due to Angrboda's interference. The flab giant normally remains calm and entirely content if fed; it has never angered before. If the characters slay the giant, the master acknowledges the necessity, and they pass the challenge. If they somehow overpower it but leave it alive, he commends their wit and ingenuity as well as their success at this challenge. He later pays them 1,000 GP from his treasury in admiration of their restraint.

entries.name: Challenge 4: The Four Lamenting Horns of the Thrasvyr!
entries: {@i Path to the sea. Horns sound. A dragon answers.}

"Once Skald Thalwyn Rotjun found a dragon egg, which she nurtured beneath the feathers of Ranwyn, her favorite chicken. When that egg became a dragon, she named it the Thrasvyr, charging it and its offspring to guard her descendants for all time. The Thrasvyr's great-great-great-great granddaughter dwells now, guarding us against those who cross the Swive with ill intent.

"Four horns have we against this calamity. The first raises the Thrasvyr from slumber. The second calls her to us. The third makes a terrible sound like the wailing of her own children, causing her anger, which we lay at our enemies' feet. The final horn, if anyone can sound it, wails like the howl of Fenris the Great Wolf—and even the dragon is driven back below the waters by it.
"That horn—or the four parts of it—lies here before you.
"Challengers, it is time for the Thrasvyr to awaken! Bring forth the Four Lamenting Horns!"

entries.name: Start:
entries: The Skald Guards lead two oxen through the arena and out a door on its east side. They walk along a now-passable tidal causeway to the small islet nearby, harried by jesters dressed as red crabs. The audience has moved to the outer balconies and tower viewing areas to watch this final contest. Meanwhile, Rurik explains this, the deadliest challenge of all, peppering his talk with words like "apocalypse," "swallowed whole," and "breath of doom."

entries.name: Challenge:
entries: To transport and assemble the Four Lamenting Horns and blow them all in order.

The guards have placed all four parts of the historic horn at the westernmost end of the cobbled path to the causeway, now fully exposed as a tricky path of seaweed and rocks. The characters must take each part in order to the isle and successfully blow it. Each part must be carried by only one challenger at a time. No one can move the next part until the previous horn has sounded. Then the next challenger can carry the next part to the isle, and so forth. Each part of the horn fits together into the previous part; a PC can assemble two pieces in a single round. The horn gets progressively larger with each addition, making blowing each new horn more challenging than the last. Characters examining the pieces and making a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check deduce their approximate weights, as shown on the table.
Successfully blowing the final, completed horn drives {@creature The Thrasvyr|NorthlandsSagas} back into the Swive.

entries.name: Aids:
entries: None

entries.name: Opponents:
entries: {@creature The Thrasvyr|NorthlandsSagas}, a {@creature Young Sea Dragon|ToB1-2023}, has no wings so cannot fly but otherwise is a full CR 9 monster. Take extra care with this test: The dragon is tough, but smart and talented PCs should win through. When the first horn sounds, the creature emerges from the Swive, and even young and some distance at sea, she looks daunting.

Blowing the second horn brings her hurtling toward land. It takes the dragon 4 rounds to reach the islet, preceded by a wall of water forceful enough to equal a {@spell Thunderwave|XPHB} spell. As it crashes onto the islet, it affects everyone there as the spell; consider the horn secured by jagged rocks. {@creature The Thrasvyr|NorthlandsSagas} takes a round to devour each of the oxen, swallowing them almost whole.

The third horn's sound enrages the dragon, as it mimics the sound of young dragons being attacked. During this time she attacks anyone on or near the islet. Be wary of using the dragon like a tank and accidentally ending up with a TPK. Use her attacks sparingly and dramatically—perhaps the dragon pauses a round, looking for her kin, or sucks back a tidal breath to use in the next round.
The fourth horn's sound causes {@creature The Thrasvyr|NorthlandsSagas} to roar in fear and head back out to sea, something sure to bring emotional applause from the crowd.

entries.name: Obstacles:
entries: The causeway proves tricky to cross with the tide coming and going, and waves crashing over parts. A successful {@dc 12} Dexterity saving throw allows a PC to cross normally; on a failure the character treats the causeway as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}

entries.name: A New Challenge!
entries: The departure of {@creature The Thrasvyr|NorthlandsSagas} signals the end of the challenges, and everyone returns to the arena. The PCs' performances might draw rich applause, indifference, or boos. A full set of successes is rare indeed and richly appreciated. A group with three successes finds itself warmly applauded, while passing two challenges garners some clapping for effort. Passing just one test is poor and booed, and succeeding at none is almost unheard of—the onlookers let the PCs know what they think of that.

The master tells the assembly how well the characters did and instructs the party to come to his hall at Highsun the next day to speak with him. As the PCs respond, the entry tower doors crash open, and {@creature Keldar Tromma|NorthlandsSagas} enters, followed by {@creature Petal Biteflower|NorthlandsSagas|Petal}, the {@creature Aridni|ToB1-2023}. She demands justice, pointing at the character from her dream and accusing them of murdering her dear friend Worlgrim. They stabbed him in the back, and now they and their friends must pay! Keldar calls for a holmganga, a formal duel, in the name of Skaldholm honor.

The master waves away any objections from the fingered PC and considers a moment. Then he accedes to her request, as it is a matter of honor. He permits the rest of the party to defend their comrade and invites Kelda to summon Petal to make an even matchup. The crowd stirs, eager to see one final spectacle.

Keldar sounds her drum to rally her supporters. She knows of the PCs' skills and, at your discretion, has a potion to help her against them, provided by her Shadowsinger contacts (for example, a {@item Potion of Fire Resistance|XDMG} if a spellcaster in the party used {@spell Fireball|XPHB} against the robbers). Petal's assistance makes her more than a match for the party; she uses her enchanted arrows on obvious spellcasters and her spells to hinder warriors or defend Keldar.

If Keldar dies, the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles} proclaims that the gods have ruled the PC innocent. Any of the Shadowsinger's surviving allies grudgingly accept the verdict. How does {@creature Einar Tromma|NorthlandsSagas} react? You may decide the PCs have another powerful enemy—or perhaps, if they showed mercy to Keldar and explain the truth, some powerful new friends.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: The day after in the crowded central room of Thyles Hall, the characters find the master attended by {@creature Sylvoll|NorthlandsSagas} and Rurik. The dwarf takes everyone back through the challenges, recounting every failure and success. If the PCs succeeded in all four challenges, the officials warmly congratulate them; it has been three-quarters of a century since that magnificent achievement! A new song is composed about them—perhaps heard during future travels. The master asks how he can help and, once told of the situation with the Cult of Ragnarok, agrees to do all he can to assist. In fact, he sends word to his friends across the Northlands by raven that very day.
If they won three challenges, the master offers congratulations and his help. Once he hears of the threat the cult poses, he agrees to contact his allies.

Passing two challenges puts the characters in a spot. If the PCs acted bravely and with suitable panache, they achieve the same result as above for three wins. If not, or if they passed even fewer challenges, the master listens but makes no promises. In time the PCs may see his subtle—and not so subtle—help as he comes to realize what they face at the hands of the cult.
Finally, the master may present any particularly notable PCs with gifts as detailed earlier for exceptional successes.

entries.name: Further Adventures
entries: The characters can rest and recuperate in Skaldholm, but soon a courier arrives with a surprising invitation to the majestic floating palace of the cloud giants...
But that is a story told in {@adventure Descent of Cloud Castle|NorthlandsSagas|6}, the next adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}.

data.name: Descent of Cloud Castle
entries: {@i Descent of Cloud Castle} is a second-tier adventure for a party of four to five 6th- or 7th-level player characters, though you can adjust it to accommodate more or fewer players. The story takes place in (and above!) the Jotunheim region of the Northlands, but feel free to transplant it into the location of your choice. It features dramatic interaction with giants, a calamitous loss of gravity—and a difficult moral decision.

After the end of the adventure, the characters should reach 8th level. If this is the first adventure you're playing in the Sagas, refer to the {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0} for important backstory.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: Ages ago, {@deity Gullveig|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}—deity of gold and magic—taught cloud giants the art of cloud weaving. With her aid, the giants constructed majestic flying cities and palaces, rising high above the peaks of Jotunheim. Over time, the worship of Gullveig waned as her followers gravitated toward gods such as {@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} and Angrboda. Other lost deities became shades of their former selves, or even mortals. But Gullveig vanished. Today, apart from the cloud giants, who still pay her some obeisance, her name appears only in dusty, forgotten tomes or dry scholarly research.

In the ongoing struggle between the Northlands and the Cult of Ragnarok, the giants of the Blood Reckoning are allied with the forces seeking to unleash {@deity Fenris|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, the Great Wolf. The other inhabitants of Jotunheim either maintain a supportive role or try not to get involved. Queen {@creature Azala Stormsinger|NorthlandsSagas}—ruler of Bjarmia, the flying cloud giant city—looks upon the plans of the Blood Reckoning and their cultist allies with growing alarm. She knows many of her people will perish in Ragnarok and does not care to see the end of the world come to pass. Feeling the chance to avert disaster slipping through her fingers, Azala has decided to contact the heroes who recently stood against the cult and their giant allies. She has dispatched an invitation for them to come to Sunreach, one of her floating palaces. If the heroes prove strong enough, perhaps she will ally with them.

Unbeknownst to Azala, however, {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}—the leader of Blodgjold, or the Blood Reckoning—knows of her plans and views them as a treason. Working with {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}, leader of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin within the cult, he has dispatched a trusted giantkin agent named {@creature Lagertha Giantblooded|NorthlandsSagas} to Bjarmia with two objectives: Lay a trap to discredit the heroes and kill them, if possible, then sabotage Sunreach's magical core so the palace crashes to the ground!

entries.name: Sagas Connections
entries: {@i Descent of Cloud Castle} is the sixth adventure in {@i Northlands Sagas}. For those following the campaign arc, after finishing this adventure, the PCs proceed to {@adventure The Redspear Trail|NorthlandsSagas|7}.

The heroes last encountered some Blood Reckoning members in {@adventure Ogre's Run|NorthlandsSagas|2}, when their ratatosk friend {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} was the sect's unwilling guest. The upgrade of the Runestones in Part 1 hearkens back to their last improvement in that adventure.

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: After a brief prelude—in which the characters travel to Sunreach on the backs of giant eagles—the adventure takes place in two parts:

entries.name: Part 1: Above the Clouds
entries: Upon their arrival, the heroes discover a group of paladins discrediting their names and reputation. This group, led by {@creature Lagertha Giantblooded|NorthlandsSagas}, claims to be the Order of the Thunderer and accuses the characters of being agents of the Cult of Ragnarok! The PCs defend their honor in court but must wait until the next day for Queen Azala's ruling. That night, however, assassins attack the characters in their rooms. While they deal with this threat, the entire palace starts to fall from the sky!

entries.name: Part 2: Falling Palace!
entries: The assassins, the so-called paladins, are revealed as Cult of Ragnarok agents. Similar cult foes seek the queen's death, and others are even now sabotaging the magical core that keeps the palace afloat. The characters save the queen and rush to the core. There, they confront Lagertha and discover the palace was powered by the imprisoned Gullveig. The characters must decide whether to return the prisoner to her cell—thus saving the palace and gaining Azala as an ally—or save the deity, earning the enmity of the cloud giants and dooming the palace inhabitants to a crushing death.

entries.name: Factions and Key Players
entries: The various factions and individuals in this adventure each work toward their own particular agendas:

items.name: Apostles of Inexorable Ruin:
entries: A sect of the Cult of Ragnarok led by {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}. They seek to bring about Ragnarok by releasing Fenris.

items.name: Azala Stormsinger:
entries: A cloud giant queen, ruler of Bjarmia, who is disgusted at her people's involvement with the Blood Reckoning and the push toward Ragnarok.

items.name: Blood Reckoning:
entries: A faction of the giants of Jotunheim led by {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}. They strive to destroy the gods of the North for killing the First Giant.

items.name: Eyvora Fiddercall:
entries: A ravenfolk scout loyal to Azala. She acts as the queen's messenger and (occasional) spy.

items.name: Gullveig:
entries: Mostly forgotten god of gold and magic, currently imprisoned and used as a power source for the Sunreach palace.

items.name: Keinen Wand-Weaver:
entries: A {@creature Lightning Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook} elementalist and Azala's court mage.

items.name: Lagertha Giantblooded:
entries: A Storm Giantkin agent of the Blood Reckoning and the Cult of Ragnarok masquerading as a paladin of Thor.

items.name: Orator Vikar:
entries: A court official from Bjarmia who mediates disputes and judges legal matters.

entries.name: Call to Action
entries: The characters were enjoying a brief rest in Skaldholm after the events of their last adventure. With no word from their patron Loki or any of Loki's agents, they have enjoyed some all-too-rare downtime as guests of the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}. Just as the festivities come to an end, a rather unique messenger arrives with an invitation...

entries.name: Alternate Adventure Hook
entries: If you are not running this as a part of the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, consider the following adjustments to the above: The characters enjoy a feast in Skaldholm to celebrate a recent accomplishment, a wedding, or other appropriate reason. The invitation they receive at the end of the festivities asks them to come to Sunreach for one of the following reasons—or the GM can create one more suitable to the campaign's needs:

items: Concerned about a cult gaining too much influence among the giants, Azala calls for the heroes to advise her. Perhaps this cult is run by individuals in league with aboleths, fey lords, some dark god, or an alien entity from the starless void.

The cloud giant queen summons the heroes to reward them for a recent deed, but in secret she hopes they can aid her in resolving Sunreach's increasingly unstable magical core. They arrive to discover Lagertha besmirching their name and reputation.

entries.name: Prelude: A Royal Summons
entries: The adventure begins in Thyles Hall, the home of the Skaldic Brotherhood's leader in the capital of Skaldholm. There, the characters are just about to take their leave of their host, the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}, when a guard reports that a flight of giant eagles approaches!

entries.name: The Invitation
entries: Read or paraphrase the following:
The night sky above Skaldholm is bright with moonlight and stars as a convocation of eagles lands in front of the longhouse. A figure on the lead eagle's back leaps down.
The rider—a young, black-feathered ravenfolk woman—wears fur-trimmed cold weather gear and a pair of overlarge goggles on her birdlike eyes. She cocks her head to one side as she glances around.

"I am Eyvora," she announces. "My mistress, the illustrious Azala Stormsinger, queen of the flying city of Bjarmia, sends greetings to you, Master of Thyles, and to your honored guests. She has bid me come to deliver an invitation to these heroes, that they might attend her in her palace of Sunreach. She seeks them to discuss matters of import."
Eyvora pulls a folded parchment from her coat, holds it in an outstretched hand, and says, "Take this and decide. I'll wait with the flock."

{@creature Eyvora Fiddercall|NorthlandsSagas|Eyvora} is a {@creature Ravenfolk Scout|ToB1-2023} with a number of {@creature Giant Eagle|XMM|Giant Eagles} equal to the number of characters, plus one for herself.
The folded parchment she hands them (see handout) is of the finest vellum and secured with a painted wax seal bearing the symbol of a golden tower on a gray cloud.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recalls cloud giants are one of the tallest species of giant, reaching almost 25 feet in height. They inhabit high mountain peaks or settlements magically resting on clouds. Cloud giants culturally believe themselves superior to most creatures. Their capital of Bjarmia, the largest city of cloud giants, floats magically high in the sky, seldom descending close to the ground.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check:
entries: When viewing the wax seal, a PC identifies the symbol as the heraldry of Bjarmia.

entries.name: A Visitor
entries: At a moment during the discussion chosen by the GM, Loki appears among the characters. Only the PCs seem able to see the god.

Loki suddenly speaks, appearing among you as if always there. "What a delicious little errand!" the deity exclaims. "You simply must accept dear Azala's invitation. Perhaps you'll drive a wedge between the cloud giants and the Cult of Ragnarok, even lure the giants onto our side, eh? While you are there, I've a task for you. A side quest, as the skalds might say.

"In a cache, deep beneath Sunreach, the cloud giants hold a number of powerful items in a place they call the Tear of the Gleaming One. One trinket in particular has caught my eye: Skirnir's Wand. Fetch it for me. The other items you can keep. Once you're out of the palace, call upon me thrice, and I'll take the wand off your hands."

entries.name: Eyvora Fiddercall (Ravenfolk Messenger)
entries: {@i Sleek feathers. Large amber eyes. Thick protective goggles.}
{@b Background:} Her family has served the cloud giants for generations, and she is the latest in a long line of royal messengers.
{@b Personality Traits:} Chatty and curious, birdlike mannerisms.
{@b Bonds:} Loves her "flock" of eagles.
{@b Flaws:} She is a trifle flighty. Doesn't pay much heed to future problems.
{@b Wants:} To do a good job for her queen.
{@b Talking to Eyvora:} The ravenfolk messenger freely relates her background (above) plus the following:

items: Sunreach is a palace of wonders. It stays at a comfortable temperature no matter the altitude, kept afloat by magic (which Eyvora doesn't really understand).
Though strong-willed and serious the queen always has been kind to Evyora and her family. (She can chat endlessly about the wonders of Bjarmia and the beneficence of the queen.)

entries.name: Questioning Loki
entries: The god allows the characters to ask three questions. As always, Loki is cagy, playful, and sharp-witted. Some common questions and their answers appear below:

items.name: What does the wand look like?
entries: About a foot long. Bone-white wood, runic carvings, you can't miss it.

items.name: What does the wand do?
entries: A little of this, a little of that. It makes that which is into that which isn't.

items.name: Why do you want the wand?
entries: No spoilers, little mortal. Let's just call it insurance for a rainy day.

items.name: How did the giants get the wand?
entries: That foolish Freyr lost it while wooing a giant.

items.name: Where is this Tear of the Gleaming One?
entries: Below the palace in a vault they call the core.

items.name: Is the place they keep the wand guarded?
entries: Of course! You don't leave something like that sitting around unguarded!

items.name: Who/what guards the wand?
entries: I'm honestly not sure. It's a palace of giants though—so I expect...giants?

As GM, answer other questions evasively using the information provided in the {@adventure Adventure Background|NorthlandsSagas|6|Adventure Background}, remembering that Loki is seldom direct. After answering three questions, Loki vanishes.

entries.name: Departure
entries: Having accepted Queen Azala's invitation, the characters travel to Sunreach with Eyvora on the backs of her giant eagles—one eagle per PC. The city of Bjarmia currently floats high above a peninsula in southern Jotunheim, east of the giantkin settlement of Eikinstad. Eyvora's eagles—faster at long travel than others of their kind—get them there in only three days. The journey may be uneventful or you could stage a couple random encounters for the characters (either in the air or on the ground during a rest).
When the characters arrive at the Sunreach palace, go on to Part 1: Above the Clouds.

entries.name: Part 1: Above the Clouds
entries: The characters arrive in Bjarmia and get a brief tour of the wondrous palace before having to defend their names and reputations from unfounded accusations. Their hosts make them comfortable in palatial accommodations, but in the night, assassins attack them, and the entire palace starts to fall from the sky! Refer to {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 2: Epic Regions of the North|NorthlandsWorldbook|3} for full details on Bjarmia, its palace, and its sky queen.

entries.name: Sunreach Features
entries: Unless otherwise stated, the ornate and towering palace buildings are sized for Huge creatures, including all doors, windows, and furnishings. Palace areas share the following common features:

entries.name: Construction
entries: The palace is built of a mixture of yellow/white stone and magical solidified clouds (treat as stone).

entries.name: Doors
entries: Doors are 30 feet tall and 15 feet wide, though some arched doorways are larger. Doors remain unlocked unless noted.

entries.name: Halls and Walls
entries: Hallways measure 30 feet wide and 40 feet high. The walls are smooth, painted with murals or other decorations.

entries.name: Light
entries: Magical light orbs hang from wall or ceiling sconces every 60 feet, providing {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Temperature
entries: The palace's magical nature maintains a comfortable, temperate climate.

entries.name: Palace Garden
entries: {@i Above the clouds. Soaring towers. Sized for giants.}

The late afternoon sun illuminates a white cloud hanging in the sky ahead. From it rises a fantastic palace of pale-yellow stone glittering in the sunlight. Two wings of buildings encircle a massive garden, where marble pathways wend between tall trees, flowering planters, and dappled benches.

To the north, a monumental spire rises from the middle of the larger building. The smaller structure is marked with wide windows, graceful balconies, and colonnades on its exterior. In the gardens, fluted columns hold aloft gold-clad domes. Statues of noble figures stand in decorated niches.

As the giant eagles circle down toward the lush space, the sheer size of the palace comes into sharp focus. Figures of towering height stroll the garden paths or stand on the palace balconies, their height demonstrating that this place is scaled for giants.

The eagles land near the center of the garden, where a large plaza encircles the life-sized golden statue of a beautiful female cloud giant. She appears to stand on a fifteen-foot-tall gently roiling cloud. The statue spreads its hands wide, as if holding apart the two sides of the palace. Near the edge of the cloud sits a small altar.

Eyvora brings the eagles to land and indicates the PCs should disembark. Once they have, the eagles depart. Eyvora tells the characters she will guide them to the oration chamber, where Queen Azala awaits.

entries.name: Gardens
entries: The gardens appear lush with plant life, a cacophony of color on what is otherwise a stark canvas of cloud and stone.

entries.name: Statue
entries: The enchanted cloud emanates from a stone pedestal beneath the statue. The cloud creates a {@variantrule Heavily Obscured|XPHB} area radiating 15 feet from the pedestal, making it appear the statue strides upon the moving cloud.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns the pedestal at the center of the thick cloud that magically produces the effect.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: The statue represents {@deity Gullveig|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, god of gold and magic. She once was venerated by the giants and early dwarves of the Northlands, but her worship waned long ago. She remains all but forgotten to most.
If asked directly, Eyvora tells the PCs the statue, called "The Mother's Beneficence," commemorates Gullveig teaching the first cloud giants how to build floating palaces and cities.

entries.name: Altar
entries: A 10-foot-high stone altar near the statue is engraved with repeating patterns of coin-shapes.

entries.name: Runestone Upgrade
entries: Before the characters leave the garden, the Runestones they carry begin to glow with a golden nimbus. At the same time, the altar shines with a matching radiance. A character holding a Runestone detects a slight pull, as if the stone wants to go to the altar.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns a power radiating from the stones. It doesn't feel harmful or threatening. The stone appears drawn toward the altar.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recalls sensing a similar power once before: near the body of a great ogre*, when the Runestones all gained a new power.

items: A Runestone brought into contact with the altar immediately improves, gaining its Greater power (see {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0|Runestones}). Then it stops glowing. Once all the Runestones are improved, the glow on the altar fades away.
When a Runestone improves, the wielder instantly knows the details of the stone's new power.

entries.name: Runestone Upgrades
entries: The upgrade opportunity in this scene is intended to be an "in-game" way to improve their Runestones, as opposed to something hand-waved or done out of character. Hopefully the heroes realize they should place the Runestones on the altar. If they don't, the GM can describe how the pull toward the altar grows stronger the farther away they attempt to go. Moving more than 60 feet away ends the pull toward the altar.
If you are using Runestone cards, give the players each the card for their Greater power.
If the characters fail to upgrade their stones, don't force the issue. The upgrade can always take place at the end of the adventure as an additional reward.

entries.name: North
entries: Through a series of hallways and suspicious giants to the Oration Chamber.

entries.name: South
entries: Through a network of passageways to the Guest Chambers.

entries.name: Oration Chamber
entries: {@i Booming voices. Grand hall. Debates and accusations.}

A boisterous voice echoes through a wide archway leading into a vast chamber. Pillared walls and statues rise one hundred feet up to support a vast golden dome above the center of the room. Tiered stages against the east and west walls hold wide stone seats for giants; a scattering of them is occupied. To the south, a half dozen smaller humanoids of various species occupy a smaller array of seats. Two archways to the west lead out to a wide balcony, and two the east lead back into the palace.

At the north side of the room, a higher stage holds an alabaster throne of massive proportions, upon which sits a beautiful cloud giant queen. She leans forward slightly, glaring at a small group of humans and dwarves wearing the armor and heraldry of Thor standing in the center of the chamber.

A giantkin woman at the head of this party points toward you and says, "For it is only though deception and murder that this group of false heroes has gained the renown—no, the infamy—that attracted your attention, Queen Azala. If not for the blessings of Thor, they may have swayed even the paladins of the Order of the Thunderer with their lies. These are not heroes...they are hidden fanatics of the Cult of Ragnarok!"
The gathered giants mutter angrily. The giantkin woman glances at you, her pale blue eyes glinting, a disdainful sneer twisting her dark lips.

Crashing a staff upon the floor three times, a dignified older cloud giant steps into view. "A moment, my queen," he says. "As is the law, the accused may refute their accuser before any decision is made." He bows toward the queen and steps up to you.

entries.name: The Orator
entries: The older giant introduces himself as {@creature Orator Vikar|NorthlandsSagas}. He lays out the situation the characters have stepped into:

items: A group of Thor-worshipping paladins from the Order of the Thunderer arrived a few hours ago.

Their leader, a storm giantkin named {@creature Lagertha Giantblooded|NorthlandsSagas}, asked to speak with the queen and her council concerning the characters and their alleged heroic deeds against the Cult of Ragnarok.
She claims the characters are secretly in league with the cult, that their "deeds" mask evil acts as well as fulfill various plots designed to hasten the End of Days.
The queen has not decided as to the truth of Lagertha's words. But she feels angry at the thought of the cultists fooling her, if the paladin speaks true.
Should the queen rule against the characters, they likely would be imprisoned—if not killed outright.

According to cloud giant law, they have until the end of the day to state their case and refute Lagertha's accusations. Then the queen will render her decision. However, it is almost sundown; only minutes remain.

entries.name: Accusations and Response
entries: As "evidence," Lagertha presents some of the characters' past actions, cast into the worst light possible. Her NPC description offers examples that reference events from previous Sagas adventures, but as GM you can insert other items if preferred.

items: She can present up to six pieces of evidence before sundown.
After Lagertha presents each item, one of the PCs can refute the information verbally. Then that PC must succeed at an ability check to convince the queen.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}), Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}), or Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} or {@skill Persuasion|XPHB}):
entries: A PC makes a good argument to Queen Azala to refute the evidence presented.

items: If the characters succeed more often than they fail on checks to refute the evidence, the queen seems inclined to believe them.

entries.name: Development: Decision Postponed
entries: Once the characters have attempted to refute the last piece of evidence, the ringing of the palace bells signals that the sun has set. Queen {@creature Azala Stormsinger|NorthlandsSagas} tells them she will deliberate on what she has heard and to expect an answer in the morning. In the meantime, the visitors may enjoy the palace's hospitality.

entries.name: Hospitality of Giants
entries: Vikar guides the group into the hallway once again, where Eyvora awaits them. He orders her to take the characters to guest chambers where they may rest for the night.

If asked, Vikar freely tells the characters that the members of the Order of the Thunderer received quarters away from the party's. (Not wishing violence to break out among her visitors, Azala commanded they be quartered in different buildings.)

items.name: Lagertha Giantblooded (Storm Giantkin Warpriest)
entries: {@i Gray-blue skin. Ice eyes. White, braided hair. Old battle scars on her face.}
{@b Background:} A member of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin.
{@b Personality Traits:} Appears smug and confident. Well-hidden ruthlessness and cruelty.
{@b Bonds:} Fanatically loyal to {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} and his cause.
{@b Flaws:} Can't resist being scornful.
{@b Wants:} To fool the giants into turning against the characters and to murder any disloyal to the Blood Reckoning.
{@b Other Notes:} Disguised as a paladin of Thor, {@skill Deception|XPHB} +5
{@b Talking to Lagertha:} Among other details, the giantkin "false paladin" gives the following evidence for her accusation:

items: The characters aided the known criminal {@creature Finulf One-hand|NorthlandsSagas}, even though they knew he was a thief who'd stolen an important relic from a temple of Wotan in Wolfheim (in {@adventure Down the Wolf Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1}).
After slaughtering a remote outpost, the characters freed a heretical ratatosk, leaving a trail of destruction across the Haamu Hills (in {@adventure Ogre's Run|NorthlandsSagas|2}).

Aided by a disreputable ratatosk, the characters consorted with fell entities near the lair of Nidhogg, the creature gnawing at the roots of Yggdrasil (in {@adventure Among the Norns|NorthlandsSagas|3}).
