The characters prevented the villagers of Hvalfell from fleeing a force of ogres and trolls because they needed time to finish building a longship (in {@adventure Assault on Hvalfell|NorthlandsSagas|4}).

While participating in a bardic competition in Skaldholm, the characters organized the murder of a prominent bard to gain influence over the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles} (in {@adventure Trials of the Lost Skald|NorthlandsSagas|5}).

entries.name: Azala Stormsinger (Cloud Giant Queen)
entries: {@i Blue-white skin. Serious and focused expression. Thoughtful blue eyes. Long golden hair tied into a single thick braid. White robes and a belt of golden disks. Ceremonial scepter. Diadem of silver and diamonds on her brow.}
{@b Background:} Considers cloud giants superior to all others.
{@b Personality Traits:} Determined, strong, and unyielding.
{@b Bonds:} Truly cares for her people.
{@b Flaws:} Fears she will make the wrong decision and lead her people to ruin.
{@b Wants:} To keep her people safe from Ragnarok.

entries.name: East
entries: Deeper into the palace.

entries.name: South
entries: Long hallway connecting the oration chamber to the Guest Chambers.

entries.name: West
entries: Balcony overlooking open sky.

entries.name: Guest Chambers
entries: {@i Opulent accommodations. Warm and comfortable but awkwardly sized.}

This suite of attached bedchambers, bath, and sitting room appears grand and kingly. The white walls of solidified clouds look like the finest marble. The entrance from the hallway passes through a circular foyer with a mosaic floor depicting a sky of drifting clouds. Plush furniture and chairs rest in the central common room near a wooden bar stocked with wine and spirits of all sorts and baskets of fruits, dried meats, breads, and sweets.

Sliding doors from the common room open onto two covered verandas, one of which features a steaming hot bathing pool. Doors open into three bedchambers featuring wide beds with silk sheets, fine wood vanities, and similar rich furnishings.
As opulent as the chambers seem, they are built for giants. The beds are twenty feet across and ten feet high, and the bathing pool is larger than some ponds.
Eyvora helps the group settle into their suite. She informs them the queen has requested they remain within their rooms for the night, until she makes her ruling.

items: The ravenfolk woman stays with them to help with the accommodations unless they otherwise instruct her to leave. She sleeps in one of the cozy chairs in the common area whenever the group is ready to bed down.

Eyvora attempts to discourage anyone from leaving the guest chambers. If she discovers that anyone has left, she alerts the 4 giantkin {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} in the central rotunda, who rouse other guards and search the palace for the missing guest.

entries.name: Other Floors
entries: These guest chambers are on the fourth floor of the palace. Other suites on the same floor, arranged in a spiral, connect by long hallways to a central rotunda.

items: The ceiling of the party's suite lies only 20 feet from the top of the palace.
Every floor features four suites, each spaced so as to be barely visible from the others' windows and verandas.
Stationed in each floor's central rotunda, 4 giantkin {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} stand watch. They enjoy an unobstructed view down the hallways to the entrance of each suite.

entries.name: Exploring
entries: Despite Eyvora's warnings, some PCs may decide to leave the chambers and prowl about the palace.

items: Leaving via the main doors is risky without spells like {@spell Invisibility|XPHB}, due to the guards' presence in the rotunda.
Climbing down to the floor below, or up to the roof of the palace, requires a successful {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check for each 10 feet traveled, due to the wind and conditions.

items.name: Suite Below:
entries: If the PCs descend to the floor below, they find a similar guest suite occupied by storm giants.

items.name: Palace Roof:
entries: If the characters ascend to the roof of the palace, they run right into the assassination team sent by Lagertha (see Daggers in the Night)

entries.name: {@color From Here...|4d6381}
entries: Once the characters settle down for the night (or at an opportune time the GM chooses), a group of foes descends from the roof of the palace to assassinate them. Go to Daggers in the Night.

entries.name: Daggers in the Night
entries: {@i Sleep interrupted. Cloaked attackers. Flashing blades.}

Several hours after dark, two groups of assailants drop by ropes from the roof of the palace and swing into the covered verandas of the guest suite. They then move into adjoining rooms to dispatch the party.

items: The assassins work in two groups, North and South squads, each containing 2 {@creature Tough|XMM|Toughs} (1 human and 1 dwarf) and 2 {@creature Vedaja|NorthlandsWorldbook}.
North squad moves into the western bedroom.

South squad moves into the common room and stabs Eyvora before she awakes. They leave her, unconscious, to die. To make things more dramatic, when combat begins, Eyvora can begin making death saving throws each round at {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} 10. The squad then moves into one of the eastern bedrooms.

entries.name: Identifying the Attackers
entries: When the PCs see the toughs clearly, give them each a free attempt to recognize them.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recognizes the foe as a member of the Order of the Thunderer from the oration chamber.

items: Anyone examining the body of a slain tough finds it branded with the symbol of the Cult of Ragnarok: a black wolf's head, breaking chains with its jaws.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The human toughs carry {@item Goggles of Night|XDMG} along with their weapons and armor.

entries.name: Weightless!
entries: When the party has reduced the total number of attacking foes to 3, the entire palace starts falling toward the ground.
With a lurching shudder, the palace suddenly drops in the sky, hurtling downward at great speed. At the same time, everything not attached to the floor rises up, abruptly weightless.
The sudden descent simulates weightlessness; the Gravity in the Palace section, below, offers specific rules.

entries.name: Flying Furniture
entries: Once the weightless conditions begin, at the start of a creature's turn, it must make a {@dc 13} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage on a failure from objects hurtling around the room.

entries.name: Changing Gravity
entries: The weightless conditions last until the end of the next round. At the start of the following round (and every round after that during combat), roll {@dice 1d6} on the Palace Gravity table and follow the instructions to determine gravity conditions.

entries.name: Development
entries: Once the party has dealt with the assassins, the palace levels out for the moment. The entire building continues to shake and shudder periodically, however.

items: The group can hear shouts, screams, peals of thunder, and the clash of weapons from elsewhere in the palace.
They hear thudding footsteps and detonations from other floors. Fires burn throughout the palace, and the characters spy flashes of light in random areas.
Eyvora (or a giantkin guard rushing in from the hallway if she perished) says the palace is under attack!

entries.name: {@color From Here...|4d6381}
entries: Go to Part 2, Guest Chambers, Continued.

entries.name: Part 2: Falling Palace!
entries: Something has gone seriously wrong with the flying palace. Sunreach now randomly plummets toward the ground or soars upward, causing near-weightless environments or moments of increased gravity. The characters hurry to save the life of Queen Azala, then make their way to the heart of the palace to confront {@creature Lagertha Giantblooded|NorthlandsSagas}.

entries.name: Sunreach Features (Addendum)
entries: In addition to the features described earlier, the palace now has the following conditions:

entries.name: Erratic Gravity
entries: Whenever the characters reach a new area or spend more than 5 minutes in any location, roll on the Palace Gravity table. During combat, roll every other round.

entries.name: Gravity Conditions
entries: Each location in Part 2 bears a label indicating its gravity conditions. If this tag says "Random," follow the rules below.

entries.name: Gravity in the Palace
entries: This section explains the rules for navigating the wildly changing conditions in Sunreach.

The Palace Gravity table determines current gravity conditions. To use it, find the current direction the palace is moving (the far left column), then roll {@dice 1d6} to determine its new heading and gravity conditions.

entries.name: Moving While Weightless
entries: If a creature moved last turn, then at the beginning of its next turn it continues moving in the same direction the same number of feet it moved last turn, unless a solid object obstructs its path.
As part of its movement on its turn, a creature whose path intersects with a solid object (or passes within 5 feet of one) can attempt to use the object to redirect itself.

items.name: {@dc 10} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC either grabs hold of the object, dropping their {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} to 0 until the start of their next turn, or pushes off the object in a new direction, moving up to their {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} as desired.

items: On a failure, the PC takes {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage from the uncontrolled impact and moves past the object at half their previous speed. If the character can't move past the object, their {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} drops to 0 until the start of their next turn.

entries: Keep in mind these other movement-related notes as well:

items: Creatures can't take the {@action Dash|XPHB} action while weightless.

If a creature throws an object weighing at least 15 pounds (or one-tenth of the creature's weight), the creature moves 10 feet in the opposite direction. If the creature throws the object in the direction it is currently moving, the toss instead slows the creature's speed by 10 feet.
A creature with a {@variantrule Fly Speed|XPHB} can move normally in near-weightless conditions.
GMs may wish to track creatures' height as they move, as weightlessness can end abruptly, causing them to fall.

entries.name: Weightless Combat
entries: Fighting in zero-gravity presents even more challenges. Remember the following:

items: Attacks against a weightless creature have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} if the attacker holds onto a solid object with a free hand. Otherwise, attacks between weightless creatures all have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

Each round, a thrown or launched projectile moves its normal range and continues to move that distance on subsequent rounds until it strikes a solid object. Its maximum range is equal to its long range multiplied by 10.

Creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity saving throws to avoid spells or effects. If a creature fails a saving throw against a spell or effect that creates a {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}, {@variantrule Cylinder [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cylinder}, {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}, or {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere}, they are pushed directly away from the point of origin a number of feet equal to 5 times the spell's level (or half their {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, whichever is greater).

entries.name: High Gravity
entries: Simple actions may require more effort in increased gravity.

items: At the start of its turn, a creature must make a {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw, suffering 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level on a failure. Any {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels gained this way disappear when the high gravity ends.
Jump distance and height are halved.
Falling damage doubles.
Creatures have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Strength and Dexterity checks and saving throws.

entries.name: Guest Chambers, Continued
entries: {@b Gravity Conditions:} Level
The sounds of distant battle ring through the halls of the shuddering palace.

entries.name: Aid Request
entries: Eyvora (or the giantkin guard) believes this attack is aimed at the queen. From the sounds of fighting elsewhere, Azala is surely in danger. The ravenfolk urges the characters to save her. If they need encouragement, she says a royal rescue would go a long way to proving their true heroism—and cement the cloud giants' aid against the Cult of Ragnarok.

If the characters agree, Eyvora suggests they head north from the rotunda on this floor. A long hallway leads from there to the oration chamber. If Azala isn't present, someone there will know where to find her.

entries.name: Different Destination
entries: The characters may decide to confront Lagertha in the quarters the Order of the Thunderers were given or visit some other location. If they don't go to the oration chamber, they need to cross the palace garden to reach other areas of Sunreach.

entries.name: Eyvora's Plans
entries: Eyvora goes to rouse the guards but, if asked, accompanies the characters.

entries.name: North
entries: Down a long hallway to the Oration Chamber Redux.

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Along a different passage to the Palace Garden Redux.

entries.name: Oration Chamber Redux
entries: {@b Gravity Conditions:} Random
{@i Echoing battle cries. Bloody hall. Betrayal and confrontations.}

A pitched melee between three giant guards and a force of humans and dwarves rages across the northern end of the vast oration chamber, threatening to spill out onto the balcony to the west. At the back of the group of wounded defenders, Queen {@creature Azala Stormsinger|NorthlandsSagas} tries to rally her guards.
Without warning, one of the guards—a giant wreathed in crackling lightning—turns his attacks on his companions and bellows, "For ruin and Ragnarok!"

When the characters reach this area, the tide of battle has turned against Azala and her defenders. Only a couple cloud giants remain, the third having just betrayed them. Without immediate aid, Azala surely will perish.

The queen's foes are 1 {@creature Lightning Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook}, 1 {@creature War Chaplain|NorthlandsWorldbook}, 2 {@creature Knight|XMM|Knights}, and 5 {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultists}. At the start of the first round of combat, the 2 {@creature Cloud Giant|XMM} guards retreat onto the balcony, ushering Azala before them. If foes approach them in subsequent rounds, they fight, but otherwise they leave the battle to the PCs.

items: The guards have only HP 50 each and already exhausted their spellcasting powers.
Azala is a cloud giant with full {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} but no spellcasting remaining.

entries.name: Development
entries: When the foes lie dead, Azala hurries to the characters. She extends her thanks for the timely intervention and asks what they have seen of the attacks taking place. Once they tell her about the assassination attempt against them, she warns them the danger is not over. The queen freely tells them the following:

items: This assault from the Cult of Ragnarok and the Blood Reckoning is aimed to cut away any giant they consider disloyal to their disastrous cause.
From the widespread assaults taking place, the so-called "guests" from the Order of Thunderer must have teleported in more troops!

However, these attacks are but a distraction. The rising and falling of the palace means that someone—probably that false-paladin Lagertha—works to sabotage the Tear of the Gleaming One, the magical core that keeps the palace in the sky.
If the core isn't restored, the entire palace will plummet to the ground, killing everyone inside.
Azala's court mage, Keinen, should be in the core, but no one has heard from them.
The queen implores the PCs to defend and secure the core while she purges the palace of the rest of the attackers and organizes her people to flee in case the worst befalls them.
The entrance to the core lies at the base of the statue at the center of the palace garden.

entries.name: South
entries: Up a long hallway to the Guest Chamber, Continued.

entries.name: East
entries: Through a passageway to the Palace Garden Redux.

entries.name: Palace Garden Redux
entries: {@b Gravity Conditions:} Level
{@i Moonlit clouds. Threatening shadows. Blood on the tiles.}

The rising and falling of the palace stabilizes for the moment. The fires burning in various parts of Sunreach cast a flickering radiance onto the night-dark paths of the palace garden. The cloud emanating from beneath the tall statue in the central plaza looks larger and more foreboding than before.
The golden arms of the statue seem to have moved—they now gesture toward the statue's feet. Dimly visible below, through the cloudy wisps, the dark opening of a doorway appears.

The cloud around the base of the statue now extends in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} centered on the 15-foot wide plinth. Lagertha has already entered the core with several followers but has poisoned the cloud to deter anyone from following them.

entries.name: Poison Cloud Trap
entries: {@i Deadly Trap (Levels 1–4)}

entries.name: Trigger:
entries: A creature enters the cloud around the base of the statue.

entries.name: Duration:
entries: Instantaneous

Each creature entering the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation}, or starting its turn there, must make a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw, taking 16 ({@damage 3d10}) Poison damage on a failure; it also has the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 10 minutes. On a success, the creature takes half as much damage and does not have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: A creature within 10 feet of the cloud with a {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB} higher than 15 automatically smells the distinctive acidic odor of the poisonous cloud. As a {@action Search|XPHB} action, a creature within 5 feet of the cloud can make a {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check, detecting a small clay tablet on a successful check.

Once the tablet is found, a character can make a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check, ascertaining the tablet bears a glyph that produces the poison effect. As an action, a character can shatter the clay tablet, which disarms the trap and removes the poisonous nature of the cloud.

entries.name: Statue Plinth
entries: A doorway set into the wide stone base holding the golden statue hangs open, revealing a curved set of stairs leading down.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC detects a constant breeze wafting up from the staircase, indicating something below is open to the outside air.

entries.name: Southwest
entries: Through a passageway to the Guest Chambers, Continued.

entries.name: West
entries: Through a passageway to the Oration Chamber Redux.

entries.name: Down
entries: Stairway to the Tear of the Gleaming One.

entries.name: Tear of the Gleaming One
entries: {@b Gravity Conditions:} Random
{@i Staircase suspended in open air. Sounds of renewed battle below. Harsh voice uttering curses.}

The curving steps emerge into open air and continue to curve around toward an immense tear-shaped structure suspended from a platform at the bottom of the stairway like a droplet of water from a twig. No railing or barrier safeguards the sides of the stairs. There is no floor beneath you, either—the tops of the nearest mountains glitter in the moonlight, so far below.

The sounds of battle—and, oddly, a gravelly voice uttering vile profanities—emerge from the tear-shaped building at the bottom of the stairway. At the base of the stairs, near an archway leading into the structure, Lagertha glances up for a moment before shouting, "Kill them all!"
As she steps into the Tear, three warriors rush past her up the stairs ,while a fourth individual readies spell components.

This staircase descends from the bottom of the cloud. It connects the palace to the Tear of the Gleaming One, the massive arcane device holding {@deity Gullveig|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}. From the outside, both the stairway and the Tear structure remain invisible; magical barriers guard them.

When the palace assault began, Lagertha entered the Tear building with her elite warriors and used a ritual spell to sabotage the core, but the arrival of Keinen, the cloud giant court mage, interrupted her efforts. Though wounded, Keinen erected a {@spell Wind Wall|XPHB|Wall of Wind} to keep the cultists away. The mage weakens quickly, though, and soon will no longer be able to maintain the spell.
Unfortunately, enough damage has been done to awaken a very angry Gullveig. Still partially trapped in the core, she attempts to free herself while swearing at her captors.

Arrayed against the party are 4 human {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook|Vikings} and 2 {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics}. Lagertha trusts her warriors to engage the PCs while she tries to bring down the {@spell Wind Wall|XPHB|Wall of Wind} and deal with Keinen. The Cult of Ragnarok forces fight to the death.

entries.name: Gullveig's Gravity Effects
entries: When combat begins, the odd gravity effects start to occur more frequently. Before the PCs can see into the Tear (see below), they don't know what is causing this.

items: Each round of combat, on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} 20, Gullveig can choose to focus on making the palace fall or rise, or on pushing herself free. In her rage, her focus shifts moment to moment.
Roll {@dice 1d6} at {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} 20. Even Result: Roll on the Palace Gravity table. Odd Result: Gullveig uses her turn to struggle to free herself.
Gullveig can push herself free after 10 successful rounds of attempting to escape.

entries.name: A Long Way to Fall
entries: Given the fighting and the odd gravity effects, it is entirely possible that one of the characters (or one of their foes) may fall off the staircase or the platform from which the Tear hangs. Without magical intervention, this surely means the creature's death.
While it's realistic, most players aren't really fans of such an end. A few possible options appear below if a character falls; apply them in order, if desired:

items.name: The Grab:
entries: {@dc 10} {@actSave dex} On a success, a PC grabs the edge of the staircase or platform and doesn't fall after all.

items.name: The Tolkien:
entries: Eyvora (if she lives) swoops down on one of the giant eagles, catching the falling PC and returning them to the top of the stairs at the start of the character's next turn.

items.name: The Bounce:
entries: A strange magical updraft slings a falling PC back up to the top of the stairs. Loki speaks into the character's ear, "You owe me a favor—and I always collect."

items.name: The Feather:
entries: Keinen (inside the Tear) casts {@spell Feather Fall|XPHB} on the falling PC. The next time the gravity change sends the palace downward, the palace passes the floating character, allowing them to grab the top of the stairs and return to the combat.

entries.name: Inside the Tear
entries: {@b Gravity Conditions:} Random
The first time a character can see into the Tear of the Gleaming One, read or paraphrase the following:

The chamber beyond the archway is of strange construction, teardrop in shape. The walls are formed not of clouds, but of pure adamantine, shimmering with brilliant shades of yellow, green, and purple radiating from thousands of magical glowing runes inscribed in the dark metal. The archway entrance lies halfway up the side of the Tear.

Items of all sorts hang upon the walls, surrounded by cages of arcane energy. A few of these protections seem to have failed, dropping the items they once held. Four of these treasures—a wand, ring, dagger, and horn—lie scattered on an iron walkway, which extends out from the archway entrance to disappear into a vertical beam of scintillating light at the center of the room. This column of arcane energy stretches the entire height of the room. Before you, fifteen feet from the light, a swirling barrier of wind blocks the way forward.

Ahead of you, {@creature Lagertha Giantblooded|NorthlandsSagas} hammers at the wind wall with a bolt of energy. A strange nimbus surrounds her, pulsing in time with the beam of light. Three figures stand guard near her. On the other side of the obstruction, a cloud giant who must be Keinen, Sunreach's court mage, rests on one knee. The mage holds a hand against a gaping wound in their side, appearing to focus on the wind wall.

Behind the cloud giant, at the edge of the beam, a human-sized woman appears to be stuck half in the light and half out, with one foot resting on the iron walkway. She heaps profane expletives at the wounded mage. Though her face is twisted in fury, she looks almost exactly like the statue from the garden above.
The 100-foot-tall chamber is wide at the top but narrows to a point 50 feet below the walkway that bisects the room.

entries.name: Hanging Items
entries: When an item falls from the wall, the Tear's curved shape sends it into the beam of light, destroying it. Four items, however, rest on the walkway. The list below features items from the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, plus alternates if desired. GMs may place these in the area as they wish. The other items in the room remain sealed with powerful magical protections that can't be removed.

items: Bone wand—this is Skirnir's Wand, sought by Loki. This relic resists any attempt to identify its features.
{@item Ring of the Cragtop Jarl|NorthlandsWorldbook} or {@item Ring of Evasion|XDMG}
{@item Dagger of Insults|NorthlandsWorldbook} or {@item Giant Slayer Dagger|XDMG}
{@item Stormhorn|NorthlandsWorldbook} or {@item Horn of Valhalla, Brass|XDMG|Brass Horn of Valhalla}

entries.name: Lagertha
entries: The nimbus surrounding Lagertha, a storm giantkin {@creature Warpriest|NorthlandsWorldbook}, and her 3 {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultist guards}, is the spell she is using to attempt to free Gullveig.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns that the light around the giantkin is an ongoing ritual spell that seemingly interacts with and weakens the beam of light at the center of the room. Disrupting the spell could have...unpredictable consequences.

items.name: GM Note:
entries: It isn't possible to dispel or break Lagertha's spell, as Gullveig's divine nature powers it. Only killing Lagertha can halt the process.

items: When any characters reach the platform outside the Tear, Lagertha stops attacking the {@spell Wind Wall|XPHB|Wall of Wind} and turns her attention on them. She fights to the death.

entries.name: Keinen
entries: The {@creature Cloud Giant|XMM} mage has only 100 HP remaining and loses 10 HP per round. They can't participate in the fighting, as they devote all their effort to holding Gullveig's prison together and maintaining the {@spell Wind Wall|XPHB|Wall of Wind} spell. The effort of their concentration is writ plainly on their face. PCs easily recognize the giant as one of Azala's counselors.
During the fighting, Keinen entreats Gullveig to stop fighting and "return to the light," but the mage doesn't say her actual name.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: A note found in Lagertha's belongings instructs her to travel to Sunreach and destroy the magical core of the city as punishment for the queen's opposition to the Cult of Ragnarok and the Blood Reckoning. The note is signed "{@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}."

entries.name: A Choice to Be Made
entries: {@b Gravity Conditions:} Level
As the last of the foes fall, the golden nimbus of light surrounding Lagertha leaps to surround all of you. The ongoing spell's thrumming power hammers in your ears.
Keinen slumps to the ground, dropping the wind wall at last. At the same time, the gaze of the woman trapped in the column of light seems drawn to you.

"You have the power now. Please, free me!" She croaks out in her gravely voice, "Gullveig, I am. Once the God of Magic and Gold, reduced to but a source of energy for this flying palace these many centuries. Free me, and when my powers have returned, great boons I shall grant you!"

"No!" Queen Azala Stormsinger shouts as she comes down the stairs to stand on the platform. "If you free her, Sunreach is doomed. We shall smash to the ground, and all of my people shall perish! You can force her back into the Tear. Aid us, and you shall have your alliance against the Cult of Ragnarok!"

The woman claiming to be a god spits on the ground. "That for an alliance with these imprisoners! If you need allies, what better ally can you desire than a god! Free me, and both magic and gold can be yours for your quest against this cult."
The golden light surrounding you seems to await your decision.
The characters must choose whether to help contain Gullveig or help her escape her prison. Admittedly, this is a terrible choice, but the PCs must make it.

items: Gullveig was trapped long ago by an early cloud giant ruler and imprisoned in the Tear of the Gleaming One. The multitude of runes engraved on her prison walls sapped her power, granting boons of arcana and prosperity to the palace and the city of Bjarmia. While Gullveig's magic doesn't keep other cloud giant settlements flying, it does give Sunreach the power to fly. Her absence certainly will cause it to fall.
The golden nimbus around the characters reacts to the group's decision—either forcing Gullveig back into the Tear or freeing her.
If 10 minutes passes with no decision, Gullveig breaks free of her own accord (see the Conclusion).

entries: The two sides of the argument appear below, should the players have questions for Gullveig or Azala.

entries.caption: The Two Options
colLabels: Azala: Impassioned ruler protecting her people.
Gullveig: Imprisoned deity yearning for freedom.

entries: If Gullveig is freed, Sunreach falls from the sky, killing everyone in the city. There isn't enough time to evacuate everyone.
Though Azala didn't personally trap the god, she rightly fears Gullveig would seek revenge against her and her people.
Azala refuses to consider any agreement that would ever free Gullveig, no matter how it is phrased—she doesn't trust Gullveig to not seek to destroy Bjarmia and the cloud giants.
Forcing Gullveig back into the Tear dooms her to centuries of more torture, as the arcane chamber continually drains her power.
The cloud giants have committed a vile crime by imprisoning Gullveig in the first place. Even though the ones directly responsible are long dead, their descendants are guilty by shared blood.
Gullveig refuses to consider any agreement that would return her to the prison even for a short time, as she doesn't trust the cloud giants to ever free her if she goes back

With a {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check, a PC can convince Gullveig to swear to not take revenge on all cloud giants, if freed. However, the god demands the destruction of Sunreach and those within it as the least she will accept.

rows.name: Offer:
entries: If the PCs choose her, Azala will sign an alliance with them against the Cult of Ragnarok and the Blood Reckoning, promising cloud giant troops and information about the other giants.

rows.name: Offer:
entries: If the PCs choose her, Gullveig swears an alliance with them against the Cult of Ragnarok and the Blood Reckoning, promising arcane secrets and funds to support their forces.

entries.name: Development
entries: Once the PCs announce their decision, one of two things happens:

items.name: They Choose Azala:
entries: Screaming in fury, Gullveig is reabsorbed into the Tear and vanishes into the beam of light.

items.name: They Choose Gullveig:
entries: Cackling in glee, Gullveig steps free of the beam of light. She snaps Keinen's neck with a look and makes an arcane gesture. The PCs and Gullveig are teleported to a high ledge, where they watch Sunreach hurtle from the sky to smash into a mountain.

entries.name: Gullveig (God of Gold and Magic)
entries: {@i Long unkempt blond hair. Molten gold eyes. Very thin. Ansuz rune tattooed on her brow. Tattered robe with embroidery of feathers, coins, and glyphs. Torc of twisted silver vines around her neck.}
{@b Background:} A long history of causing problems for the Aesir (see {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 6: Northlands Pantheons|NorthlandsWorldbook|6}).
{@b Personality Traits:} Eerie and defiant, geyser of anger barely contained.
{@b Bonds:} Herself, though she feels some responsibility to those who aid her.
{@b Flaws:} Has trouble controlling her emotions.
{@b Wants:} Freedom from imprisonment, revenge on her cloud giant captors, and to regain her place in the divine pantheon (in that order).

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: The aftermath of the PCs' choice has the potential to shake the foundations of the Northlands. No matter what their decision was, the PCs have identified themselves as a major obstacle for the Cult of Ragnarok and the Blood Reckoning.

entries.name: The Wand
entries: When the characters call upon Loki as instructed, if they picked up Skirnir's Wand in the Tear, he arrives to take it from them. In return, he gives them a {@item Wand of Wonder|XDMG}.

entries.name: Alliance with the Cloud Giants
entries: If the PCs chose to aid Azala, the queen is true to her word. She puts her seal on an alliance between her people and the PCs. This commits the cloud giants to aid them when they make their move against the combined forces of the Cult of Ragnarok and the Blood Reckoning. Queen Azala also promises to keep the PCs informed as to the activities of their common foes.
Eyvora (or another scout) transports the characters back to Skaldholm on her giant eagles.

entries.name: Alliance with Gullveig
entries: If the characters chose to aid Gullveig, the deity makes an arcane oath of alliance. She grants each PC a supernatural gift (a {@filter Blessing|rewards|type=blessing}) as chosen by the GM. Further, she promises to come to their aid when they make their move against the combined forces of the Cult of Ragnarok and the Blood Reckoning.
Gullveig magically teleports the characters back to Skaldholm before departing on her own business.

entries.name: Gullveig Breaks Free
entries: If the characters don't make a choice within 10 minutes, Gullveig breaks free on her own. She curses them all and then teleports away. Sunreach plummets toward the ground, crashing into a mountain in 5 rounds. Unless the PCs have some magical method of travel, they may perish along with the inhabitants of Sunreach.

entries.name: Runestones
entries: Remember to upgrade the party's Runestones, if they haven't already done so.

entries.name: Further Adventures
entries: Either by giant eagle or magic, the characters return to Skaldholm. After they recount their tale to the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles}, the ruler announces his intent to speak with {@creature Uffi Toothless|NorthlandsSagas|King Uffi Toothless} of Trollheim, urging him to commit his forces to aid the PCs in their stand against the Cult of Ragnarok.

After some downtime (if they wish), the PCs are asked to meet their ally {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} in the town of Eyrsvik in Wolfheim. Apparently, Loki has a task for them that plots their course toward the mysterious Isle of Loki...
But that is a story told in {@adventure The Redspear Trail|NorthlandsSagas|7}, the next adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}.

data.name: The Redspear Trail
entries: {@i The Redspear Trail} is a second-tier adventure for a party of four to five 8th-level player characters, though you can adjust it to accommodate more or fewer players. The story offers sea combat and enough excitement to heat up an icy isle of legend. It takes place in the western region of the Northlands on the Isle of Loki, but feel free to transplant it into the location of your choice.

At the end of the adventure, the characters should reach 9th level. If this is the first adventure you're playing in the Sagas, refer to the {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0} for important backstory.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: In the Uttermost Sea, off the western coast of the Northlands, lies the Isle of Loki: perpetually encased in a towering glacier and surrounded by billowing clouds of frost fog. Few have dared to land on the island, let alone explore it. Legends proclaim it the seat of Loki and his private estate. As such, dwarven reavers, giants, and humans have avoided this ice-swathed expanse for centuries.

For a time, ages ago, a ring of towering ice ran along the coastline, the product of a bargain between Loki and {@deity Boreas|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, god of the North Wind. Within, the land was lush and warm, full of strange beasts and pleasures for the trickster god to enjoy. About fifty years ago, however, Loki turned on then-allies Boreas and {@deity Chernobog|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, when the Trickster realized their plans to promote a "false" Ragnarok weren't "false" at all. As punishment for such betrayal, Boreas caused the glacial walls to spread inward across the whole island, covering Loki's private garden beneath a five-mile-deep blanket of blue-white ice.

Subsumed by the ice was Loki's Hall, a fabulous palace of riches and wonders—the greatest of which, an artifact called the Loom of Fables, interfaces with the skein of fate woven by the Norns. The loom does not change reality or fate but copies the Norns' warp and weft, threading divination magic through its heddles (the pins that guide the threads and create the pattern), which one places where desired. Those who know of the loom speculate that one could use it to view particular strands of fate to learn about a specific individual or even to pluck specific information about places or items from the weave. But how to actually accomplish this task remains unknown.

In the ongoing struggle to stop the cabal of giants and the Cult of Ragnarok, the characters have learned that the cult operates out of a fortress hidden somewhere in the Northlands. Unfortunately, standard divinations grant no vision of the fortress's whereabouts, leaving them at an impasse. Where other magic has failed, the Loom of Fables offers tantalizing hope.

Unfortunately, the loom lies deep in Loki's Hall. The god sent a previous group of heroes led by Heide Redspear to use the loom, but they vanished, leaving behind nothing but some fragments of a journal. Worse, they took with them the {@item Mother's Comb|NorthlandsSagas}, an item from the Norns required to make sense of the loom's workings.

entries.name: Sagas Connections
entries: {@i The Redspear Trail} is the seventh adventure in {@i Northlands Sagas}. For those following the campaign arc, after finishing this adventure, the PCs proceed to {@adventure Murder at the Moot|NorthlandsSagas|8}.

In {@adventure Among the Norns|NorthlandsSagas|3}, the heroes collected a magical relic owed to Loki called the {@item Mother's Comb|NorthlandsSagas}; they gave it to their patron (who, we now know, passed it to the doomed Heide Redspear). They likely haven't seen their ratatosk friend {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} since he transported them to Skaldholm at the beginning of the {@adventure Trials of the Lost Skald|NorthlandsSagas|5}. His first mate, {@creature Hennrik|NorthlandsSagas}, once hired the PCs to rescue Kosktup from cultists (in {@adventure Ogre's Run|NorthlandsSagas|2}).

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: This adventure has three parts. The shortest involves the trip to and across the Isle of Loki. The others take place on the island and within Loki's Hall.

items.name: Part 1: Trip to the Isle
entries: The characters board {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}, Kosktup Farleap's wondrous longship, and sail toward the Isle of Loki, encountering various dangers along the way. When they arrive on the island, they must find Boreas Glacier and the caverns that lead to Loki's Hall.

items.name: Part 2: Beneath the Glacier
entries: The PCs venture into the caverns below the glacier, following the path left by the Redspears. They encounter the giant deity Angrboda's cultists and various other creatures that call the place home.

items.name: Part 3: Loki's Hall
entries: Once they reach Loki's Hall, they encounter and overcome its denizens before battling the dragon {@creature Fafnir|NorthlandsWorldbook} to recover the {@item Mother's Comb|NorthlandsSagas}. Once they do, they use it upon the Loom of Fables to determine the location of the cultists' fortress.

entries.name: Factions and Key Players
entries: The various factions and individuals in this adventure each work to further their own goals and motivations:

items.name: Angrboda's Cultists:
entries: The cultists, nominally allies of the Cult of Ragnarok, have come to the island following various agendas, including invading Loki's Hall to destroy the Loom of Fables and prevent anyone else from reaching it. Some of them used to serve Chernobog but have switched their allegiance. More information on them appears in the {@adventure Actions of the Cultists|NorthlandsSagas|7|Actions of the Cultists} sidebar in Part 2.

items.name: Gorm Rotholfsson:
entries: Hired by {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}, head of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin, Gorm leads the cultists here. He wears a set of stag antlers on his otherwise bald head.

items.name: Inga, the Skein Witch:
entries: Priestess of Loki and Angrboda, sworn to protect Loki's Hall from harm. With her patron deities at odds (see their descriptions in the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 6: Northlands Pantheons|NorthlandsWorldbook|6}), she feels a bit conflicted. {@creature Inga|NorthlandsSagas} doesn't interfere with or side with any of the other factions, but becomes a deadly enemy if riled.

items.name: Kosktup Farleap:
entries: Daring and charming ratatosk merchant captain.

entries.name: Call to Action
entries: If you're using {@i The Redspear Trail} as part of the Sagas campaign, the previous adventure in the path ({@adventure Descent of Cloud Castle|NorthlandsSagas|6}) left the characters heading to meet their ally {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} in the town of Eyrsvik in Wolfheim. The adventure assumes Kosktup tracks them down there and invites them onto {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}, his magnificent longship. The story begins as the characters walk down the docks toward the ship.

entries.name: Alternate Adventure Hooks
entries: If you are not running this as a part of the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, the characters may have very different reasons for seeking out the Loom of Fables:

items: Kosktup wants to be responsible for locating it. He hires the heroes to protect him and his ship from the dangers of Loki's Isle and the glacier.
The PCs need to undo a powerful curse laid upon a patron or ally. The answer lies with the loom.
One of the characters is directly related to Heide and wants to locate her remains.

entries.name: Part 1: Trip to the Isle
entries: The PCs board {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} in Eyrsvik, a coastal settlement in Wolfheim, or another community depending on your campaign, and sail through the Nieder Straits out into the Uttermost Sea and north to the isle. This voyage covers hundreds of miles, though the actual length of the trip in game time and its precise route depends on your needs, as GM, as well as the players'.

entries.name: Boarding Stokkvari
entries: {@i Waves lapping. Creaking rigging. Shanties being sung.}

A cold wind blows down from the looming Rygg Mountains to wash across the coastal town of Eyrsvik. By the docks, gruff sailors sing traditional shanties as they load bundles of food and supplies onto Stokkvari, Kosktup Farleap's magnificent longship.

Spotting you, Kosktup leaps ashore, a fur-lined cloak trailing behind him above his bushy tail. "Well, well, look who washed up with the tide at last. I almost sailed off without you, but then I remembered, you still owe me at least one drink and one act of wildly irresponsible heroism."

He bids you to gather round and speaks quietly. "Loki sent word...well, not so much a 'word' as a nightmare full of firesnakes and bad poetry, but I got the gist of it. We've got a chance to ferret out the location of the cult's hidden lair. But it's not going to be easy."

entries.name: Speaking to Kosktup
entries: The {@creature ratatosk|ToB1-2023} {@creature Merchant Captain|NorthlandsWorldbook} freely provides the following information (see his NPC description in the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13} for roleplaying suggestions).

items: There is a relic called the Loom of Fate. It's tied to the Norns' own weavings—a copy of fate, you might say. But it's nearly impossible to understand.

That's where the {@item Mother's Comb|NorthlandsSagas} comes in. It's from the hands of the Norns themselves, and with it you can pull secrets right from the skein. Like, say, the location of a fortress crawling with cultists who want to end the world.

Two small hiccups to the plan. First, the loom is on the Isle of Loki. An island to the west, frozen under an eternal glacier, thanks to the god Boreas. Full of dangers, that place. Second, Loki already sent a bunch of heroes to read the loom, and they never came back. Worse, they had the {@item Mother's Comb|NorthlandsSagas} with them, and now it's lost on the island someplace.

The dead folk were led by Heide Redspear. In the sending from Loki, I saw a few fragments of Redspear's journal, which I transcribed as best I could (see handout). Loki seemed right mad that these were the only parts recoverable. But you might be able to piece together a route from these scraps.
So that's the game. Travel to the island, follow the Redspear trail, find the comb, find the loom, put 'em together, and boom! The location of the cult fortress is yours. Easy, right?

If asked about a reward. A sell-sword after my own heart! I wouldn't dream of denying you compensation for your acts of wanton violence and chaos! Loki has promised you can take anything you find in the hall. Who wouldn't want to loot the home of a god?
So! What do you say? Ready to ruin some cultists' day before they ruin the world?

entries: Assuming the characters agree, Kosktup welcomes them aboard the ship and orders his crew to cast off.

entries.name: The Journey
entries: Soon enough, {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} clears the harbor and heads for the open sea.
Wind fills the sail and the ship lances through the water like a seal. Handing the tiller over to Hekja, his second-in-command, Kosktup gathers you for a chat.

"All right, here's the shape of it. On any other longship, this trip takes two weeks. Stokkvari? She'll get us there in eight days. Straight sailing through cold seas, possible monsters, giants and worse. Maybe a fight, maybe not.

But there's a third path. We use the Dragon, our magic figurehead. Cut sideways across planes into the Sea of the Dead. One day's sail through Hel's tide, then we slip back into the world in sight of Loki's ice-cursed island.
Faster? Absolutely. Safe? Not a chance. That route guarantees a fight.
So. Do we sail safe the long way with maybe a battle? Or take the shortcut, and earn every mile with blade and blood?"

Based on the players' choice, continue either with The Long Way or The Shortcut. See {@variantrule Ships and Sea Combat|NorthlandsWorldbook} in {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 7: Running a Northlands Campaign|NorthlandsWorldbook|7} for ship rules. {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}'s stat block appears in the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13} of this book.

entries.name: The Long way
entries: Throughout the eight-day journey to the island, {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} experiences various seagoing encounters. For each day, roll {@dice 1d6} on the {@table Ship Encounters|NorthlandsSagas} table, pick one encounter of your choice, or invent your own. Each encounter occurs only once (unless otherwise noted).

entries.name: Targeting PCs
entries: Losing a portion of the crew can derail the entire journey or make it take much longer. Most of the following encounters target the heroes directly, rather than the longship or its crew. If {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} loses more than half her {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} or crew, she limps to the nearest port to make repairs and gather new sailors. This adds {@dice 1d6} days to the journey.

entries.name: The Shortcut
entries: {@i Oppressive. Void sea. Stench of bones and death.}
{@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} transitions to the Sea of the Dead using the drakahofud, a magical dragon figurehead.

The ship appears on an inky black sea beneath a sky filled with a bruise of pale blues, greens, and other colors, eddying with no understandable pattern. In the distance, jagged storm clouds send down bolts of lightning. Around the ship, the void sea swirls with stars and spectral shapes—yet it remains still as glass.
"To the oars," Kosktup whispers, as if afraid to speak loudly. "Let's not stay any longer than we need to."

After a day of travel, Kosktup orders a halt and begins the ritual to shift back to the mortal world. But the ritual disturbs a group of undead beneath the ship: 8 {@creature Drowned Raider Vaettir|NorthlandsWorldbook} rise up on all sides of the vessel.

items.name: {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC notices the vaettir swimming up from beneath the ship.

items: 12 of the crew ({@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook|Vikings}), the individuals closest to the railing, fight during the battle.

At the prow, {@creature Hekja No-Curl|NorthlandsSagas|Hekja} ({@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM}) guards {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas|Kosktup} ({@creature Merchant Captain|NorthlandsWorldbook}), who continues the magical ritual to transport the ship. The ritual requires 4 rounds to complete. If Kosktup is forced to fight, each round he isn't conducting the ritual adds 1 round more.
The deck is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} due to the crew on the benches, cargo bundles, and so forth.

To ease gameplay, hand-wave fighting not directly involving the PCs. Assume that each round, every crew member involved in the battle takes 5 Slashing damage, and each vaettir not fighting the PCs takes 4 Slashing damage.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: One slain vaettir has an {@item Amulet of Health|XDMG}.

entries.caption: Ship Encounters
rows: When the PCs sail within 100 feet of the coast, 4 {@creature Hill Giant|XMM|Hill Giants} emerge from some brush to hurl abuse and trash at the ship. If they sail on, {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} endures 4 rounds of bombardment before moving out of range. Engaging the giants means leaving the longship. (The giants each carry 50 SP in hacksilver; one uses a {@item Javelin of Lightning|XDMG} as a hair pin.)

While Kosktup navigates through heavy fog, {@dice 2d4} {@creature Will-o'-Wisp|XMM|Will-o'-Wisps} emerge from the mist to pick off sailors, killing one each unless the PCs intervene. The creatures flee once half are destroyed.

The PCs see a pitched battle between a sailing ship from Stannasgard (crew of 15 {@creature Pirate|XMM|Pirates} and a {@creature Merchant|NorthlandsWorldbook} in command) and a raider longship from Wolfheim (20 {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook|Vikings} and a {@creature Pirate Captain|NorthlandsWorldbook}). If they don't help, the sailing ship is captured within minutes. If the PCs capture (rather than sink) one or both ships, they collect bags of grain, casks of wine, 155 GP worth of hacksilver, and a {@item Potion of Water Breathing|XDMG}.

Roll on the {@table Unusual Weather|NorthlandsWorldbook|Unusual Weather} table in the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 7: Running a Northlands Campaign|NorthlandsWorldbook|7}.

2 {@creature Lindwurm|ToB1-2023|Lindwurms} emerge from the ocean to attack, focusing their attention on the PCs. They aren't up for a serious fight; once one dies or both are {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, they flee.

entries.name: Isle of Loki
entries: The Isle of Loki, an enormous island of plains and mountains, remains perpetually trapped in ice that stretches over five hundred miles. Home to various cold-dwelling creatures, the isle is otherwise bereft of civilization. Those traveling across its surface must contend with the bitter cold and raging blizzards.

entries.name: Small Rocky Beach
entries: Kosktup finds a small rocky beach, only 20 feet wide, where he can drop off the party. A crisscrossing trail marked with wooden stakes leads up the side of the looming glacier. The PCs must travel at least 2 miles up and onto the glacier to find the entrance to the caverns that lead to the hall. Thankfully, Angrboda's cultists and Heide's party have left their mark on the glacier, and PCs can follow the trail they left.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC finds a rowboat partially buried in the ice near the beach with the letters "HR" engraved on its side, the mark of Heide Redspear.

entries.name: Island Features
entries: The Isle of Loki has the following features:

entries.name: Encounters
entries: Random encounters have a 1 in 6 chance of occurring once every 8 hours. If one occurs, roll on the {@table Isle of Loki Encounters|NorthlandsSagas} table.

entries.name: Fafnir's Aura
entries: When they have traveled about a mile toward Loki's Hall, the characters have unknowingly drawn to within a mile of Fafnir's lair (Area 6 in Part 3)—in range of his Aura of Avarice (see {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 8: Monsters of the North|NorthlandsWorldbook|8}). From this point on, they all have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on saves or spell effects that compel them to take or steal things. Also, they feel deeply protective of their own belongings and covetous of others'.

entries.name: Snow
entries: Snowstorms ravage the island once every {@dice 1d4} days. When the PCs arrive on the island, it isn't snowing. Everything in a snowstorm's area is {@variantrule Lightly Obscured|XPHB}, and creatures suffer {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks that rely on sound.

entries.name: Temperature
entries: The temperature on the island is always below freezing, even during the warmest days. PCs setting foot on the island experience the effects of extreme cold (see the rules for {@hazard Extreme Cold|NorthlandsWorldbook} in the core rulebooks and the {@book Northlands Weather|NorthlandsWorldbook|8|Northlands Weather} section of the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 7: Running a Northlands Campaign|NorthlandsWorldbook|7}).

entries.caption: Isle of Loki Encounters
rows: {@dice 1d2} {@creature Frost Giant|XMM|Frost Giants} hunt for walruses along the coast. If they spot the PCs, they attack. The giants know of Loki's Hall but have never been inside the glacier and are not allied with the cultists there.
{@dice 1d3} {@creature Lindwurm|ToB1-2023|Lindwurms} skate across the frozen plains looking for prey. They are keen to add some humanoid flesh to their diet.
{@dice 2d4} hungry {@creature Winter Wolf|XMM|Winter Wolves} stalk a wounded {@creature Mammoth|XMM} (hobbling on HP 65) across the tundra. The wolves happily attack any PCs who get in the way.

An earth tremor causes a nearby snowdrift to collapse on the party (use the crumbling monument hazard in {@i ToV Game Master's Guide} or {@hazard Rockslide|XDMG} hazard in {@i D&D Dungeon Master's Guide}). The snowdrift deals 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Bludgeoning damage and 11 ({@damage 2d10}) Cold damage.
A {@creature Young White Dragon|XMM} flies over the PCs' heads. It attacks but retreats quickly if they prove formidable targets.
A {@creature Rime Worm|ToB1-2023} erupts from the snow and attempts to drag a character back into its hole to devour.

entries.name: Part 2: Beneath the Glacier
entries: The characters follow the path across the glacier and into a cavern entrance leading below. Once inside the Boreas Glacier, they contend with cultists of Angrboda as well as natural hazards and fell monsters while following the Redspear trail.

entries.name: Features of the Glacier Caverns
entries: The Boreas Glacier's caverns have the following qualities in common.

entries.name: Floors
entries: Layers of snow cover the frozen stone floors. In Areas 4 and 6, the floor is ice-covered water.

entries.name: Halls and Walls
entries: Passages measure at least 10 feet wide and 20 feet high, while cave heights often surpass 30 feet. The walls of the passages and caves are composed of incredibly thick and hard bluish-white ice.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: The caves and passages have {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}—light filters a little through the ice.

entries.name: Snow
entries: Small snow drifts (2 to 4 feet high) cover some spots. The ground in these areas is {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}. The snowy ridges shown on the map each rise 5 to 10 feet off the ground. A PC can descend the ridges safely by spending 10 feet of movement. The ridges become an issue only if people fight atop them.

entries.name: Temperature
entries: See above under Island Features.

entries.name: Glacier Locations
entries: To get to Loki's Hall, travelers must traverse the Boreas Glacier, a massive ice field that covers the entire island.

entries.name: Area 1: Entrance
entries: {@i Ragged cleft in the ice. Humanoid footprints in the snow lead within.}

The entrance to the ice caverns is little more than a tear in the glacier's side. Beyond this narrow opening, the tunnel widens, a passage of white ice that heads deep into the glacial gloom. The footprints of numerous humanoids remain visible in the snow leading into the tunnel. Sticking out of the ice near the tunnel entrance is a spear adorned with a tattered scrap of frozen red cloth.
Thankfully, this tunnel is unguarded.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC hears the sounds of the berserkers in the cultist cave (Area 2) chatting and eating.

items.name: {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC can tell the spear bears the mark of the Redspear company (the initials "HR" in bold black lettering).

entries.name: {@color From Here...|4d6381}
entries: The entrance tunnel continues east to an intersection.

entries.name: North
entries: A passage to the cultist cave (Area 2).

entries.name: East
entries: A passage to the watch cavern (Area 3).

entries.name: Actions of the Cultists
entries: Throughout the adventure, the characters face multiple groups of cultists allied with Angrboda. The cultists want to kill off the dragon {@creature Fafnir|NorthlandsSagas} and take the Loom of Fables for themselves—or, at the very least, prevent others from reaching it. The cultists arrived on the isle three weeks ago and have been exploring the region ever since. They have lost members to both the dragon in the Hall of Loki and the jorumungkyn in the southern cavern (Area 4) and currently are deciding what to do about the situation.

While powerful as a group, the cultists are split between those who once followed the god Chernobog, sent to guard the caverns, and those loyal to Angrboda from the start. As a result, the cultists don't necessarily aid each other in battle, but wait to see what transpires as a result of any commotion. This is especially true in the cultist cave and watch cavern (Areas 2 and 3).

entries.name: Area 2: Cultist Cave
entries: {@i Large cave. Lit braziers. Smell of cooking meat.}

At the end of the tunnel lies an oblong cave of ice that sparkles in the firelight. Two lit iron braziers, each surrounded by fur-lined bedrolls, take up space in the cave. A haunch of meat slowly roasts atop the northeastern brazier. A dark shape lies beneath the ice of the floor.

If the PCs haven't announced their presence, some brutish-looking humans rest and talk in this cave. These are 6 {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics} who once worshipped Chernobog but have turned their service to Angrboda (seeing in her the true face of Ragnarok). They have orders to slay anyone entering the glacier and happily attack the party while offering prayers to their giant deity. They fight to the death; if one is captured, the cultist happily talks to the PCs, boasting about Angrboda's power, the coming of Ragnarok, and Chernobog's weakness.

The cultist fanatics know the caverns' general layout (except for Areas 6 and 8). They understand a fearsome sea monster lurks in the southern cavern (Area 4), which they have yet to deal with. They have not been allowed entry into Loki's Hall and know of it only by name. They don't get on well with the berserkers in the watch cavern (Area 3) and refuse to aid them in a fight.
Each cultist wears an iron holy symbol of Angrboda.

entries.name: Bedrolls
entries: The bedrolls are thickly lined with fur and in good condition, though most stink of human sweat.

entries.name: Braziers
entries: The braziers are constructed of nonmagical iron. Keeping them lit is a chore in the icy conditions, and the supplies of wood grow short. The braziers shed {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 30-foot radius.

entries.name: Meat
entries: The haunch of meat comes from a caribou the berserkers killed. This piece of meat is the only part of the animal left; once cooked, it provides the PCs with 5 days' of rations.

entries.name: Frozen Body
entries: Encased in the floor lies the body of a human with a look of horror on his face. This is Lars Larsson, a warrior who served Redspear and was killed by cultists. He has marked his gear with a red spear symbol. Removing the body from the ice takes 20 minutes.

entries.name: South, then East
entries: Back to the intersection, then east to the watch cavern (Area 3).

entries.name: South, then West
entries: Back to the intersection, then west to the entrance tunnel (Area 1).

entries.name: Area 3: Watch Cavern
entries: {@i Frozen cavern. Smoking braziers. Rows of ice boulders and wooden barricades. Berserkers standing watch.}

The tunnel opens into a vast cavern that stretches east and south for over one hundred feet. A row of large, ice-covered boulders splits the cavern in half, blocking off much of the southern part from sight. Between the boulders, bundles of sharpened wooden logs strapped together with rope form crude barricades. Cracks in the ceiling let through flurries of snow and filtered beams of light, while three braziers placed at intervals in front of the boulders provide additional illumination for the creatures guarding the area.
This cavern, the largest in the glacier, rises over 50 feet into the air. The southern cavern is detailed later (see Area 4). This part contains the following features:

items: Between the braziers (as in Area 2) and the light streaming in from above, the cavern enjoys {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} even at night.
The snow boulders are wedged firmly into the ground. Most of them are too big to affect without magic. Standing behind a boulder provides {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Full Cover}.

The wooden barricades vary in size, but most of them take up a 5-foot square. Each 5-foot square barricade has AC 13, HP 25, {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 5, is {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Poison and Psychic damage, and is {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerable} to Fire damage. A creature attacking a barricade with a Melee weapon without reach must make a {@dc 9} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage on a failure. A barricade provides {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover}.

entries: Wearing holy symbols of Angrboda, 6 {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers} guard this cavern against intrusion from the southern cavern (Area 4) and the troll lair (Area 6). They respond to the PCs' presence with immediate hostility and refuse to surrender. These berserkers are currently at odds with the cultist fanatics in the cultist cave (Area 2) because of their previous god and don't come to their aid, though if they hear signs of battle they stand ready to attack the PCs as soon as they appear.
They know the same information as the cultist fanatics in the cultist cave.

entries.name: North
entries: Ridge and short tunnel to the mammoth bone cave (Area 7).

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Ridge and short tunnel to the frostbitten tree cave (Area 8).

entries.name: South
entries: Past the barricades and boulders to the southern cavern (Area 4).

entries.name: Southwest
entries: Sloping tunnel to the cold storage cave (Area 5).

entries.name: Northwest
entries: Atop the ridges and back along the tunnel to the entrance (Area 1) and cultist cave (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 4: Southern Cavern
entries: {@i Frozen lake of ice. Cracking and creaking sounds. A hole of frigid water in the center of the lake.}

Beyond the boulders and barricades lies a roughly circular area filled with a lake of frozen, translucent blue ice. It cracks in various places, forming jagged, interlocking sheets. In the center of the lake is a circular hole of dark, foreboding water. The ice-encased form of a human is partially visible at the eastern edge of the hole. A passage disappears from view as it exits through the cave's southeastern wall.

The ground here is frozen water instead of permafrost soil. While the ice is a good 3 to 4 feet thick along its edges, it's only a few inches thick toward the middle. Unlike the northern section of the cavern (Area 3), this section has {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Frozen Body
entries: Near the edge of the hole is the frozen body of Venna, a Redspear party member poisoned and killed by the jorumungkyn that lives here. In actuality, it is only the upper half of her corpse; the jorumungkyn ate the lower portion and placed the rest of the body here to eat later. Her gear is marked with a red spear symbol.

entries.name: Bad Ice
entries: The cracked ice shown on the map counts as thin ice for movement purposes and can tolerate 120 pounds of pressure before it shatters. Any attack that deals at least 20 damage (or 10 Bludgeoning or Fire damage) causes a 10-foot-square section of thin ice to shatter, plunging anyone standing on it into the lake. See Freezing Water in the {@i ToV Game Master's Guide} or {@hazard Frigid Water|XDMG} in the {@i D&D Dungeon Master's Guide}.

entries.name: Lake
entries: The lake measures over 150 feet deep and connects to the nearby ocean via a submerged tunnel. The lake has the following features:

items: It is a combination of fresh water near the surface and salt water as one descends more than 30 feet. It's bone-chillingly cold (see Freezing Water in the {@i ToV Game Master's Guide} or {@hazard Frigid Water|XDMG} in the {@i D&D Dungeon Master's Guide}).
While the lake water is clear, it's also very dark due to the ice covering it (though one can illuminate it normally).

items.name: {@dc 10} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC can swim in the water. This check increases to {@dc 15} if the jorumungkyn is within 50 feet of the swimmer (it stirs up the water with its massive bulk).

entries.name: Sea Serpent
entries: A {@creature Jorumungkyn|NorthlandsWorldbook} lurks in the lake, coming and going via the sea tunnel. It created the hole in the ice with its massive bulk and has already consumed poor Venna, a cultist fanatic, and four berserkers. It currently swims in the depths of the lake but is attracted to any light or noise on the surface and bursts out of the hole to investigate. Once the jorumungkyn senses prey, it uses its Glare of the Deep ability, then attacks.

items: If it misses with an attack against a character in the watch cavern (Area 3), it has a {@chance 25|||Destroy the section|Do not destroy} chance of destroying the 10-foot section of ice the PC stands on (see above).
Any berserkers still alive in the watch cavern (Area 3) take the opportunity to pick off the PCs while the jorumungkyn occupies them.

entries.name: North
entries: Back past the ice boulders and barricades to the watch cavern (Area 3).

entries.name: Southeast
entries: A short tunnel to the troll lair (Area 6).

entries.name: Southwest
entries: A sloping tunnel to the cold storage cave (Area 5).

entries.name: Area 5: Cold Storage
entries: {@i Dead-end cave. Numbing chill. Ice-covered containers.}

This wedge-shaped cave is filled with wooden barrels and a large crate, all covered in a thin layer of ice. The back of the cave also contains a single fur bedroll. No fire illuminates or warms this dim space.

The cultists store their meager provisions in this cave. Because of the temperature, everything here is frozen; PCs spending too long in the cave become subject to extreme cold (see extreme cold rules in the {@i ToV Player's Guide} or {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG} in the {@i D&D Dungeon Master's Guide}).

The bedroll belongs to the cave's sole occupant, a {@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook} named {@creature Kolmurag|NorthlandsSagas}. A fervent believer in Angrboda, {@creature Kolmurag|NorthlandsSagas} currently sits atop one of the barrels, devising a battle plan to take out the jorumungkyn on a scrap of paper. He jumps up as soon as the PCs appear and charges, shouting a war cry to Angrboda.

items: Aside from his standard gear, {@creature Kolmurag|NorthlandsSagas} wears a silver {@item Ring of Cold Resistance|XDMG|Ring of Resistance (Cold)} on his right hand.
The scrap of paper describes the jorumungkyn in the southern cave (Area 4) and outlines a plan to drag it out onto the ice with ropes and attack it.

entries.name: Barrels
entries: One barrel contains thick black oil, while the other two contain salted herring.

entries.name: Crate
entries: The PCs must succeed on a {@dc 13} Strength check to open the long wooden crate covered in ice. It contains 16 {@item Torch|XPHB|Torches}, 4 {@item Greataxe|XPHB|Greataxes}, 6 {@item Spear|XPHB|Spears}, 12 flasks of {@item Oil|XPHB|Oil}, and 4 sets of Winter Clothing.

entries.name: Development
entries: If the PCs take more than 5 rounds to dispose of the berserkers in watch cavern (Area 3), or if they begin combat with the jorumungkyn in the southern cave (Area 4), {@creature Kolmurag|NorthlandsSagas} investigates the disturbance.

entries.name: North, then Northeast
entries: Back along the tunnel to the watch cavern (Area 3).

entries.name: North, then Southeast
entries: Back along the tunnel to the southern cavern (Area 4).

entries.name: Area 6: Troll Lair
entries: {@i Cave of blue ice. Frozen spikes emerge from the floor—scratches on the walls. Carved boulder.}

Spear-shaped pillars of ice jut out from the walls, floor, and ceiling of this cave, creating a hazardous yet entrancing spectacle. The walls and floor are an almost transparent azure, and a fine mist fills the air, illuminated by light streaming in from a wide, irregular opening in the ceiling.
The otherwise beautiful scene is ruined by the frozen blood and broken bones littering the floor. The ice wall partially encloses a carved boulder in the southeast corner.

A pair of {@creature Glacial Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Glacial Trolls} inhabits this cave. They used to have free run of the caverns. Unfortunately, they have been limited to this cave for over a week after their last attempt to kill the cultists failed (leaving the trolls seriously injured) and following the jorumungkyn's arrival. They can leave through the opening in their ceiling but bemoan the loss of their cavern home.

The ravenous glacial trolls viciously attack anyone who enters their territory. If the PCs don't enter this cave but kill off the cultists and the jorumungkyn, the trolls exit this cave after a few hours to investigate and could meet the heroes as they try to leave the caverns; should this occur, the glacial trolls are in the watch cavern (Area 3) feasting on any dead berserkers there.

entries.name: Pillars
entries: The spear-shaped pillars in this cave span 3 to 12 feet in height. A creature can hide behind a Medium or Large pillar for {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover}. An average pillar has AC 15, HP 20, {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 3, is {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Poison and Psychic damage, and is {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerable} to Bludgeoning and Fire damage.

A glacial troll can grapple a PC and ram them onto one of the pillars with a successful check. If it wins the check, it shoves the character onto one of the ice pillars, dealing 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Piercing damage. This breaks the grapple, but the PC must spend at least 5 feet of movement to exit the pillar's space.

entries.name: Carved Boulder and Body
entries: A frozen body is encased in the wall in the southeast section of the cave. Carved onto a nearby boulder is a message left by Heide: {@i In honor of Askel Hvarling, who bravely fought a sea beast and was taken. May Thor guide him to the halls of Valhalla. HR.}

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Scattered among the pillars and refuse lies the following treasure:

items: A dozen gold trade bars (worth 25 GP each) spilling from a torn sack.
A moonstone statuette of a blink dog with green chrysoberyls for eyes (worth 550 GP).
An adamantine {@item Lance|XPHB}.

entries.name: Northwest
entries: Back along the tunnel to the southern cavern (Area 4).

entries.name: Area 7: Mammoth Bone Cave
entries: {@i Giant bones in the snow. Fuming brazier. Smell of incense.}

In this cave, the skeleton of a massive beast with great tusks lies partially buried in the snow. To the east, a glowing orange brazier emits an oddly sweet scent. Two bedrolls next to the brazier soak up its warmth.

This cave is occupied by two arcane cultists who once served Chernobog but now help Angrboda's minions for the chance to gain even greater power: a human {@creature Mage|XMM} named {@creature Delina|NorthlandsSagas}, with a shock of red hair and black tattoos covering her face, and a {@creature Dwarven Ringmage|ToB1-2023} named {@creature Serevok|NorthlandsSagas}, with a pot belly and a thin black moustache. The cultists are currently considering how to deal with the dragon guarding Loki's Hall and whether to attempt to animate the mammoth skeleton to help them.
The two cultists react poorly to the characters' appearance and demand that they leave immediately unless they choose to serve Angrboda (but see Development, below).

A PC can pretend to acquiesce to the cultists' demands with a {@dc 17} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB} or {@skill Performance|XPHB}) check. While this stops the cultists from becoming {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile}, it's still a risky move; if the PCs attempt to destroy the mammoth skeleton or enter the frostbitten tree cave (Area 8), the cultists attack immediately.
Should the characters somehow remain on their good side, the cultists share the following information:

items: Beyond the easternmost cave lies the entrance to Loki's famous hall.
A mighty dragon defends the hall from outsiders; it killed two berserkers during the last foray.
The hall is also home to a strange, ethereal witch who maintains the hall's shrines. She isn't hostile unless attacked.

entries.name: Brazier
entries: The cultists filled the brazier with medicinal herbs to produce the smell mentioned above. Any creature taking a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} within 10 feet of this brazier heals {@damage 1d6} {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}. The brazier burns out {@dice 1d4} hours after the PCs enter the cave.

entries.name: Mammoth Skeleton
entries: The skeleton is inanimate. The mammoth's tusks are worth 100 GP each.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Canny PCs who have read Heide's journal (see handout) should realize a treasure lies nearby (apart from the cultists' gear).

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discovers a small iron box with "HR" carved into the lid underneath a pile of snow-covered rocks. Someone can extract the locked box after 1 minute of digging.

items.name: {@dc 17} Dexterity ({@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC unlocks the box. It contains 4 {@item Potion of Greater Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing (Greater)}, an {@item Elixir of Health|XDMG}, and a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} of {@spell Raise Dead|XPHB}.

entries.name: Development
entries: If the PCs attack the berserkers in the watch cavern (Area 3) or the jorumungkyn in the southern cavern (Area 4), the cultists here don't initially react to the commotion, expecting that it's just the jorumungkyn or glacier trolls attacking the barricades again. If the fight lasts longer than 5 rounds, {@creature Delina|NorthlandsSagas} moves to investigate, but immediately pulls back when she sees the party and alerts {@creature Serevok|NorthlandsSagas}, who prepares for battle.

entries.name: South
entries: Back down the short passage and ridge to the watch cavern (Area 3).

entries.name: Area 8: Frostbitten Tree Cave
entries: {@i Desolate cave. Snow-covered tree. Split in the ceiling.}

A solitary, long-dead tree dominates this otherwise bare cave, its gray branches and trunk petrified by the endless cold and covered in layers of snow. A crevasse opens in the ceiling, letting in gusts of freezing air.

Three figures occupy this cave, including 2 {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics} (both trollkin) and a senior human cultist (use the {@creature Warpriest|NorthlandsWorldbook} stat block) named {@creature Gorm Rotholfsson|NorthlandsSagas}, who wears a set of stag antlers on his otherwise bald head (see below). Gorm and the cultist fanatics plan a foray into Loki's Hall and are offering prayers to Angrboda for their success.

entries.name: Gorm
entries: Gorm is the leader of the cultists here, hired by {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} to kill the characters and keep them from the Loom of Fables. He knows that {@creature Fafnir|NorthlandsSagas} serves Chernobog but opposes everyone who enters the hall.
When Gorm sees the PCs, he immediately recognizes them and orders his people to kill them while he casts spells in the background. He would rather die than face capture.

entries.name: Crevasse
entries: The ceiling in this cave measures 40 feet high, though much of its space is taken up by the bottom of a crevasse that extends from the 40-foot mark upward another 80 feet to the top of the glacier. Ascending the crevasse is extremely difficult without magic; it leads beyond the scope of this adventure.

entries.name: Tree
entries: Standing at the back of the cave is an ancient rowan tree, frozen solid by the perpetual cold and never allowed to rot. The followers of Loki planted the tree many centuries ago when the island was a lot warmer than today. Though impressive in its cold solitude, the tree is not magical.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: In addition to their standard gear, Gorm and the cultists each carry a fur-lined bedroll and enough wood to light a fire.

entries.name: Development
