entries: If Gorm hears signs of combat from the watch cavern (Area 3), he sends the cultist fanatics to investigate and quell the disturbance. Should this occur, he waits here alone for the PCs, telling them they are a mere trial he must overcome to serve Angrboda.

entries.name: Southeast
entries: Long ice tunnel (over 180 feet) to Loki's Hall (Part 3).

entries.name: South
entries: Tunnel back to the watch cavern (Area 3).

entries.name: Part 3: Loki's Hall
entries: The characters at last enter the former palace of the god Loki. Here they can investigate the interior, contend with its last caretaker, and finally face an unexpected foe before reaching the Loom of Fables.

entries.name: Features of the Hall
entries: This grand structure, originally made of stone and wood, was built for a god. The hall possesses the following features:

entries.name: Doors
entries: Portals are stout wooden double doors a total of 10 feet wide and 20 feet tall. An iron pull ring in the center of each door allows one to open it easily. No doors are locked.

entries.name: Halls, Floor, Ceiling, and Walls
entries: Passages measure 10 feet wide. Rooms are 20 feet high (60 feet in Area 6). The hall's walls, floor, and ceiling are composed of magically hardened and condensed ice almost as strong as mithril. The walls, floor, and ceiling are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Fire and Cold damage. Every surface radiates powerful Conjuration and Enchantment magic.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: A pale blue-white light radiates from the ceiling, illuminating every passageway and chamber with {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Locations in the Hall
entries: In recent centuries the hall has undergone a startling transformation from a deity's palace to a magical ice prison containing a relic of incredible power, the Loom of Fables.

entries.name: Area 1: Entrance Corridor
entries: {@i Utterly silent corridor of magically wrought ice.}

After eighty feet, the natural glacial tunnel transforms into a corridor of ice that appears to have been shaped by powerful magic. At the end of the corridor stands a pair of large oak doors with iron pull rings in the middle of them.
In recent weeks (since Heide came through here) this corridor has seen more use than it has in decades.

items.name: {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}):
entries: A PC sees multiple humanoid footprints in the light snow leading up to the doors. The prints coincide with those of the cultists.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}):
entries: A PC notices that these doors once were trapped; someone removed the trap about the same time that the Redspear group would have passed through the caverns.

entries.name: East
entries: Through the door to the broken looms room (Area 2).

entries.name: West
entries: Back down the passage to the frostbitten tree cave (Area 8) of the Boreas Glacier.

entries.name: Area 2: Broken Looms
entries: {@i Wooden splinters all over the floor. Piles of detritus in the corners. Multiple doors.}

This space contains the remnants of dozens of discarded looms and three other sets of double doors. The looms have been pushed haphazardly into the corners of the chamber, forming large piles of broken, twisted, and frozen wood. A palpable sense of loss and waste fills the room.

The looms in this chamber are copies, prototypes, and even parallel versions of the Loom of Fables that have all lost their power and been destroyed. Because of the divine magic used to create them, the room still holds a modicum of divine power. The looms are in various stages of decomposition, though all appear similar in design and materials. They carry a special curse affecting creatures that examine them.

entries.name: Curse of the Broken Looms
entries: {@i Magical Curse}
This curse takes effect when a creature that isn't a Construct or Undead spends at least 1 round investigating the looms discarded here (simply passing through the chamber doesn't activate it).

entries.name: Effects:
entries: Everything in the chamber (including creatures) takes on a cold, grayish, desaturated appearance. Every creature in the chamber that isn't a Construct or Undead must make a {@dc 14} Wisdom saving throw, becoming {@condition Slowed|XPHB} (as the {@spell Slow|XPHB} spell) on a failure and taking 10 ({@damage 3d6}) Necrotic damage as their bodies wither and ebb. Creatures must repeat the saving throw each round they stay in the chamber; the effects end when the creature moves into any adjoining corridor.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: A {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} cast on an affected creature ends it immediately and prevents the creature from being affected again for 24 hours.

entries.name: North
entries: Through the doors to a corridor leading to Loki's shrine (Area 3).

entries.name: East
entries: Through the doors to a trapped corridor (Area 5).

entries.name: South
entries: Through the doors to a corridor (Area 4) leading to Angrboda's shrine.

entries.name: West
entries: Back to the entrance corridor (Area 1).

entries.name: Area 3: Loki's Shrine
entries: {@i Decorative pillars. An altar of solid ice. Feeling of piety.}

This chamber is clearly a place of worship. Elaborate pillars of steel and ice run up the sides of the chamber, and at the end sits a large block of ice that appears to serve as an altar. Carvings adorn the walls and pillars.
This shrine is dedicated to Loki—his symbol figures prominently in the carvings on the walls and pillars.

entries.name: Altar
entries: The altar is constructed of magically hardened ice: AC 17, HP 50, {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 10, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Cold, Fire, Poison, and Psychic damage, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistance} to all other damage.

If the characters attack the altar while {@creature Inga|NorthlandsSagas} (see Area 4) is alive, she rushes here to investigate. When she arrives, she warns the PCs to cease. If they don't, she attacks them until she or they are dead.

entries.name: Praying at the Altar
entries: A hero who offers an honest prayer to Loki here has a 10 percent chance that the god hears the prayer and responds, granting the PC {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB} if they don't already have it. A character gains this benefit only once.

entries.name: South
entries: Back down the corridor to the broken looms (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 4: Angrboda's Shrine
entries: {@i Octagonal chamber. Pillars and altar of carved ice.}

Twin rows of icy pillars banded with steel lead up to an altar carved from ice. Monstrous symbols of titanic wolves and world-circling serpents decorate the shrine. The chamber appears in pristine condition, as if brand new.

Angrboda's symbol features prominently on the walls, pillars, and altar of this chamber; the berserkers and cultists in the ice caverns have been here to pray to their deity with Inga's blessing (see below).

items.name: {@dc 13} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC remembers that Angrboda is often depicted as Loki's wife and the mother of Loki's children. The two gods were once close allies (hence the shrine honoring her in this hall).

entries.name: Altar
entries: The altar is constructed of magically hardened ice: AC 17, HP 50, {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 10, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Cold, Fire, Poison, and Psychic damage, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistance} to all other damage.
If the characters attack the altar and {@creature Inga|NorthlandsSagas} is alive (see below), she warns them to cease. If they don't, she attacks them until she or they are dead.

Despite the current animosity between Angrboda and Loki, this altar still holds a portion of the giant god's divine power, and {@creature Inga|NorthlandsSagas} maintains it. Such are the strange connections between the gods.

entries.name: Inga
entries: Floating in the center of this chamber is {@creature Inga|NorthlandsSagas}, a powerful {@creature Skein Witch|NorthlandsWorldbook} whom Loki has tasked with watching over the shrines. {@creature Inga|NorthlandsSagas} doesn't react aggressively to those who offer their respects to the gods or appear otherwise inoffensive. But she defends herself if attacked and defends the shrines from harm. She's not allied with the dragon {@creature Fafnir|NorthlandsSagas}, but neither does she assist those preparing to fight him.
If the PCs remain amicable with the skein witch, she willingly shares the following information:

items: A trap (Area 5) guards the passage to the dragon's lair. She doesn't know what it would do to the PCs if they passed through the corridor, since she cannot activate it herself.
The terrible dragon {@creature Fafnir|NorthlandsSagas} now guards the way to the Loom of Fables. Despite her power, {@creature Inga|NorthlandsSagas} knows she cannot defeat him in battle.
{@creature Inga|NorthlandsSagas} knows nothing of the recent troubles between Angrboda and Loki. She will guard her shrine until Loki tells her otherwise.

The cultists showed up not long ago. They are a crude lot, but their leader (a trollkin with stag antlers) has stopped them from causing any harm. A few have lost their lives to the dragon and the other dangers of the hall.

A group of polite adventurers led by a beautiful woman named Heide Redspear passed through here a few weeks ago. Sadly, the trap in Area 5 killed some of them, and Heide herself perished fighting {@creature Fafnir|NorthlandsSagas} in his lair (Area 6).

entries.name: North
entries: Back along the corridor to the broken looms (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 5: Corridor of Snowy Death
entries: {@i Thick snow covers the walls. Snowflakes swirl through the air.}
This short corridor stretches for about twenty feet before ending at another set of double doors. Snow cakes the walls and floor of this passage and falls from the ceiling in shifting spirals.
This trapped corridor has slain two cultists already. When she passed this way, Heide managed to get through unscathed.

entries.name: Snow Trap
entries: {@i Deadly Trap (Levels 5–10)}

entries.name: Trigger:
entries: A warm-blooded creature reaches the corridor's midpoint.

entries.name: Duration:
entries: Instantaneous

An avalanche of snow and ice falls from the ceiling, filling the passage. A creature in the corridor or within 10 feet of it (in Areas 2 or 6) must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking 22 ({@damage 4d10}) Bludgeoning damage on a failure and becoming trapped beneath the snow. A trapped creature takes {@damage 1d6} Cold damage at the end of each of its turns and begins suffocating.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: A PC notices the danger presented by the snow with a {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check. To render the trap inactive for 1 hour, someone can cast {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} ({@dc 15}). Once the eastern doors are open, they can bypass the corridor with spells such as {@spell Dimension Door|XPHB}.

entries.name: Escape
entries: A trapped creature can free itself from the snow with a {@dc 17} Strength check (made with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} if another creature helps pull it out). The snow melts if it takes more than 30 Acid or Fire damage, though creatures within the snow take half damage.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Buried in the snow in the corridor lie the bodies of two cultist fanatics.

items.name: {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC sees a foot sticking out of the snow. Further investigation uncovers the bodies, though it also exposes characters to the trap.

items: The cultist fanatics have their usual gear. The armored warriors wear {@item Chain Shirt|XPHB|Chain Shirts}, carry {@item Shield|XPHB|Shields}, and wield {@item Battleaxe|XPHB|Battleaxes} and {@item Spear|XPHB|Spears}.

entries.name: East
entries: Through the doors ahead to Fafnir's lair (Area 6).

entries.name: West
entries: Back through the doors to the broken looms (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 6: Fafnir's Lair
entries: {@i Massive two-tiered chamber. Broken pillars. Claw marks and skeletons. Statue of ice.}

Slender pillars of ice, each towering over sixty feet in height, run in two rows along the lower section of this enormous two-tiered chamber. Three of the pillars have toppled to the ground, creating piles of icy, jagged rubble, and there is a blast mark in the center of the chamber, as if from an explosion of some kind. Numerous skeletons lie scattered about the chamber, and many pillars bear deep gouges, as does the floor.

A statue of Loki, carved from pure white ice, stands resplendently at the back of the chamber, surrounded by a hoard of glittering treasure. Above the statue, a hole in the ceiling looks big enough for a wagon to fall through.
This giant hexagonal chamber is Fafnir's lair. It is split into two sections, the upper part 10 feet higher than the lower. Stairs carved into the ice separate the two sections.

entries.name: Battle Scene
entries: The skeletons belong to humanoids who once faced {@creature Fafnir|NorthlandsSagas} in battle, including Heide Redspear. Most of them aren't intact, and those that are have been stripped of their belongings.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC examining the gouges determines that they come from a dragon or similarly large monster.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC realizes that the blast mark is from a {@spell Fireball|XPHB} cast in this chamber at some point.

entries.name: Dragon
entries: {@creature Fafnir|NorthlandsWorldbook} typically lies coiled about the statue of Loki. The dragon allies loosely with Chernobog but doesn't care about the god's current troubles with Loki or the Cult of Ragnarok. He destroys anyone who enters his lair.

entries.name: Statue
entries: The statue of Loki stands around 20 feet tall and appears to have been carved from a single block of unblemished ice. Because of the potent divine magic used in its construction, no magic or weapons the PCs have can even scratch the statue. Even fire proves useless against it.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The gems and coins embedded in the scales of Fafnir's underbelly amount to 4,300 GP. As befits Loki, god of trickery, the hoard of coins and gems here in his hall is mostly a permanent illusion. Any creature reaching for the treasure finds that their hands pass right through it. Still, some real items (from Heide and from Fafnir's hoard) lie amid the phantasmal coins:

items: A {@item +2 Spear|XDMG} with a red banner attached to it bearing the initials "HR" (Heide's magical spear).
A silver necklace with red diamonds worth 2,500 GP.
A {@item Headband of Intellect|XDMG} attached to a skull.
A wooden {@item Scroll Case|XPHB} containing {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG|Spell Scrolls} of {@spell Arcane Vigor|XPHB}, {@spell Cone of Cold|XPHB}, and {@spell Summon Fey|XPHB}.
The {@item Mother's Comb|NorthlandsSagas}.

entries.name: North
entries: Through the doors to the loom chamber (Area 8).

entries.name: South
entries: Through the doors to the divine bedchamber (Area 7).

entries.name: West
entries: Back through the doors to the trapped corridor (Area 5).

entries.name: Area 7: Divine Bedchamber
entries: {@i Sumptuous study. Cozy fireplace. Fur-covered bed and red cedar chest.}

The door opens into a chamber that wouldn't look out of place in a king's palace. It contains a bed draped in luxurious furs, a chest of reddish wood, a table and chair made of translucent blue ice, and a roaring fireplace.

Loki created this bedchamber for select guests staying in his hall to use the Loom of Fables. It hasn't been used in over a hundred years, though the furnishings remain in pristine condition thanks to the deity's power. PCs can rest here without being interrupted, even if they haven't slain {@creature Fafnir|NorthlandsSagas}.

entries.name: Bed
entries: The bed, comfortable and warm, is protected by preservation magic.

entries.name: Chest
entries: The unlocked chest contains two sets of {@item Fine Clothes|XPHB|noble clothing} (outdated fashion but still valuable), a pair of worn leather boots, and a bottle of {@item Fine Wine (bottle)|XPHB|Fine Wine}.

entries.name: Fireplace
entries: The fireplace of gray, volcanic stone holds a blazing, magical flame. An iron poker sticks out of the fire.

entries.name: North
entries: Back through the doors to Fafnir's lair (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 8: Loom Chamber
entries: {@i Icy chamber. Exotic loom.}

A horizontal loom constructed of rich alder and mithril dominates this otherwise bare, cold chamber. The loom is decorated with intricate runes and engravings of fauna and flora, both fantastical and mundane. A simple stool sits in front of it.
This chamber holds the Loom of Fables, a powerful artifact the PCs can use to locate Birgkrona, the secret fortress of the Cult of Ragnarok.

entries.name: Loom of Fables
entries: Created by the ancient Norns countless millennia ago, the Loom of Fables has stood in Loki's Hall for many centuries and has been used only a handful of times. Due to Loki's influence, no one can damage the loom or remove it from this chamber with anything short of divine intervention or {@spell Wish|XPHB}-level magic. While someone can use the loom to weave cloth—someone proficient with {@item Weaver's Tools|XPHB} can even create entire tapestries on it—it primarily acts as a potent source of Divination magic. It can answer almost any question put to it.

entries.name: Operating the Loom:
entries: While holding the {@item Mother's Comb|NorthlandsSagas}, a creature can ask the loom a single question, such as the location of a hidden fortress, or anything else whose answer could be depicted on cloth. Once the command has been given, the loom magically weaves the answer into being, using a combination of words, symbols, and pictures as appropriate to convey its response. Virtually infallible, the loom cannot be circumvented or suppressed by mortal magic.
A creature can ask only one question of the loom in its lifetime, though multiple creatures can use it. It takes the loom {@dice 1d4} hours to give its answer, regardless of the question asked.

entries.name: Cult Fortress
entries: When asked, the loom reveals the hidden fortress of the Cult of Ragnarok, called Birgkrona, is located in the far west, in the giant-controlled land of Thursrike.

entries.name: South
entries: Back through the doors to Fafnir's lair (Area 6).

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: The adventure concludes once the heroes have asked the Loom of Fables the location of the Cult of Ragnarok's fortress. They can rest warmly in the bedchamber (Area 7) before retracing their steps toward the ship. It's unlikely they have left any enemies behind, but if they have, these foes happily attack the group when they exit the hall.

Kosktup awaits the PCs and cheerfully greets them, telling them that everything has been cold but boring while they were gone. He eagerly desires to know what they have learned, telling them that their allies have begun to gather to move against the Cult of Ragnarok. At the moment, the priority is to get everyone to a mustering location in Wolfheim.

entries.name: Further Adventures
entries: The characters can ask Kosktup to take them to almost any coastal settlement in the Northlands, but they are expected in Wolfheim to meet the allies gathering to confront the Cult of Ragnarok and their giant comrades.

After some downtime, the army of allies makes ready to sail to Thursrike. However, before the PCs can leave, a message arrives in Wolfheim begging them to attend the great Moot of Jotunheim to discuss the treaty between the giants and the cult...
But that is a story told in {@adventure Murder at the Moot|NorthlandsSagas|8}, the next adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}.

data.name: Murder at the Moot
entries: {@i Murder at the Moot} is a second-tier adventure for a party of four to five 9th-level player characters, though you can adjust it to accommodate more or fewer players. The story—a murder mystery among the giants—takes place in the Jotunheim region of the Northlands, but feel free to transplant it into the location of your choice.

At the end of the adventure, the characters should reach 10th level. If this is the first adventure you're playing in the Sagas, refer to the {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0} for important backstory.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: The unique fortress named Helgihond is a sacred place among the giants. They believe that one of Aurgelmir's enormous children survived the loss of the First World only to emerge during the Vanir Wars. When no weapon could fell him, clever Loki and Angrboda fooled the giant with illusions and trickery long enough to expose him to winter's short-lived sun. Turned to stone by the light, he sank into the ground until only his upraised right hand remained.

The giants delved out the stone interior of the petrified ancient to create Helgihond, a neutral meeting place for giants of all sorts. Of course, these meetings are not always peaceful. A century ago, a fight during a particularly contentious moot sheared off the fortress's thumb, killing several giants in the process. The subsequent moot's attendees patched the hole left by the thumb's loss, and the giants have left the rubble alone as a reminder of the fragile nature of peace.

The giants hold the Moot of Jotunheim in Helgihond every five to ten years to discuss relationships between various clans. Giant kings, queens, jarls, and their designated representatives attend these moots, which end with signed treaties—garnered either through mutual agreements or after ritual combat between the arguing parties. A High Speaker, chosen in rotation from among the attendees, oversees each moot. The current High Speaker is the cloud giant {@creature Sigkva Runigsdottir|NorthlandsSagas}.

The rise of the Cult of Ragnarok and their allied giant sect forms the backdrop for this year's occasion. The cloud giants have the greatest objection to the cult's plots, and {@creature Sigkva Runigsdottir|NorthlandsSagas} decides to invite the humanoid heroes opposing it to attend. She hopes they will disclose the evil group's plans and convince other giants to break with the cult, if not actively aid the assault against it.

Meanwhile, the cult and its giant allies in the Blood Reckoning sect—or Blodgjold—have sent their agent {@creature Beli Groundshaker|NorthlandsSagas} to infiltrate the meeting and eradicate those in the moot who oppose them. The jotun {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} has bestowed upon Beli the magical abilities to shapechange and influence other giants. To create chaos, Beli also makes use of a dangerous reawakened ancient plant-creature: {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go}, thought to have perished in the ice long ago. These creatures implant egg-like spores in giant corpses, triggering horrifying racial memories of "Belly Eaters" for the giants.

entries.name: Sagas Connections
entries: {@i Murder at the Moot} is the eighth adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}. For those following the campaign arc, after finishing this adventure, the PCs proceed to {@adventure Attack on Birgkrona|NorthlandsSagas|9}.

The NPC the characters allied with at the end of {@adventure Descent of Cloud Castle|NorthlandsSagas|6}—either Queen {@creature Azala Stormsinger|NorthlandsSagas} or the deity Gullveig—has sent the group invitations to the moot.

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: After receiving an invitation to the moot, the heroes travel to Helgihond, Fortress of the Hand.

items.name: Prelude: Traveling to the Moot
entries: The party journeys to the moot, experiencing a strange encounter along the way.

items.name: Part 1: The Moot Begins
entries: The meeting's first day proceeds uneventfully; the next morning the PCs make their case, but a resolution is tabled until the next day.

items.name: Part 2: The Investigation
entries: During the night, {@creature Sigkva Runigsdottir|NorthlandsSagas} is murdered, throwing the moot into chaos. The heroes must prove their innocence and investigate the death while keeping the giants from attacking each other out of mistrust.

items.name: Part 3: Matters Escalate
entries: The murderer plays his final card, causing even more chaos at the moot—and forcing the characters to make a difficult choice.

entries.name: Factions and Key Players
entries: The various factions and individuals in this scenario each work to further their own agendas:

items.name: Apostles of Inexorable Ruin:
entries: A sect of the Cult of Ragnarok led by {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}. They seek to bring about Ragnarok by releasing Fenris.

items.name: Beli Groundshaker:
entries: A thursir agent of the Blood Reckoning who can shapechange into other giant forms and cast {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} on giants, thanks to his patron, {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}. He infiltrates this moot to sow chaos and kill as many high-profile giants as possible. Other giants treat him as a simpleton, even though he is well-spoken.

items.name: Blood Reckoning:
entries: A faction of the giants of Jotunheim led by {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} that strives to destroy the gods of the North for killing the First Giant.

items.name: Bralt and Bremman:
entries: A pair of hill giantkin brothers working as Beli Groundshaker's aides.

items.name: Glytta Weggesdottir:
entries: A stone giant priestess of Jormungandr who represents the community of Brotdalr and seeks to settle a territorial dispute with the jotuns of Reykurbrand. Though sent by Karn Rune-Sworn, Jarl of the Stone Giants, to resolve things peacefully, Glytta believes a war between the stone giants and the jotuns would finally redeem her people in the eyes of the other giants, win or lose. Beli uses her as a pawn to smuggle in the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} that kills Sigkva.

items.name: Izhova:
entries: An advisor to a powerful fire giant chieftain, this fire giant necromancer is an accomplished diplomat, mostly through subtle threats. He may heed the call to help in negotiations during the moot.

items.name: Katlaug:
entries: The dignified and proud thursir majordomo and caretaker of Helgihond.

items.name: Sigkva Runigsdottir:
entries: The cloud giant High Speaker asked {@creature Azala Stormsinger|NorthlandsSagas} (or Gullveig, if Azala didn't survive the adventure) to invite the heroes to the moot.

items.name: Sinmara:
entries: Co-ruler of Reykurbrand (with her husband Surtr), {@creature Queen Sinmara|NorthlandsSagas} attends the moot to settle a territorial dispute with the stone giants—ostensibly without resorting to war. However, she actually would prefer the dispute to flare up, ensuring a deadly conflict. Though she is a jotun, the queen magically reduces her size to fit more comfortably in this fortress.

entries.name: Call to Action
entries: As the heroes help prepare the forces to assault the cult's secret headquarters in Thursrike, they each receive an invitation from {@creature Azala Stormsinger|NorthlandsSagas} (or Gullveig) to attend the Moot of Jotunheim. If they don't believe steering the giants away from the cult is worth the trip, another ally encourages them to accept the invitation.

entries.name: Alternate Adventure Hook
entries: If you are not running this as a part of the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, the PCs may become involved through a cloud giant ambassador. Perhaps the giants have been researching an apocalyptic cult and realized that one or more of the party's previous encounters touched on cult concerns. Sigkva hopes to employ their knowledge to convince the other giants of the cult's threat.

entries.name: Reward
entries: Either way, the invitation to the moot promises a reward for attending: 2,000 GP in gems plus a {@item Sword of Wounding|XDMG} (or other {@filter Rare magic item|items|rarity=rare} appropriate for the group).

entries.name: Prelude: Traveling to the Moot
entries: With their invitations to the moot, the PCs each receive directions to Helgihond, the Fortress of the Hand, located just below Sengajordensblod in Jotunheim. Apart from the encounter below, how they get to the fortress is for the GM to decide. Their longship captain ally {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} could take them as far as the port of Gastropnir aboard {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}, but the rest of the path is overland. Belligerent giants who challenge the characters' presence in giant-dominated realms back down upon seeing their invitations to the Moot of Jotunheim.

entries.name: A Curious Corpse
entries: In the wild country the characters happen to pass through, {@creature Beli Groundshaker|NorthlandsSagas} supervised the first use of the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} (ToB1 variant: INT 5 only). The test run claimed a hill giant as its victim, but the larvae have long since grown and left the area.
A hill giant lies just off the trail up ahead.

entries.name: Examining the Body
entries: The characters can learn about the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} and the giant's death.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC realizes blows from a bludgeoning weapon killed the hill giant, and a residue of spores coats the corpse—something burst out of the giant's body from within.

items.name: {@dc 19} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discovers another set of tracks, sized smaller than the giants. These tracks indicate someone observed the attack, then left the scene.

items.name: {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC finds a pouch containing 20 GP and an invitation to the moot.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Nature|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recalls a giant legend of a supposedly extinct plant-like monster called Kvideta or "Belly Eater." According to the myth, it hunted the early giants and deposited egg-like spores in their prey. The spores mature quickly, and new plant monsters voraciously devour the corpse before exiting it.

entries.name: Complication
entries: When the heroes finish examining the body, 2 {@creature Lightning Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Lightning Giants} happen upon the scene. They immediately assume the party killed the hill giant.

items.name: {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check:
entries: As an {@variantrule Action|XPHB} on their turn, a PC convinces the giants the characters are not responsible for killing the hill giant.

entries.name: Journey's End
entries: The characters complete their journey without further incident. When they arrive at the towering fortress, read or paraphrase the following:

A pair of cloud giants stands at the base of a titanic stone arm, which reaches a hundred feet upward before ending in a massive hand missing its thumb. After a moment's observation, it's clear that an entire fortress has been carved into the stone hand high above.
The cloud giants inspect the PCs' invitations before allowing them to climb the set of stairs leading up to the hand.

entries.name: Up
entries: To Arrival (Part 1).

entries.name: Part 1: The Moot Begins
Fortress Features
entries: The interior of the giants' fortress spans a single level; guards and staff sleep in makeshift buildings erected not far from the base of the fortress. Helgihond has the following qualities.

entries.name: Bedchambers
entries: Rather than try to accommodate every type of giant visitor, fortress staff assume guests will bring their own bedding to suit them. If the staff receive instructions otherwise, they set up the room to the given specifications.

entries.name: Ceilings and Walls
entries: The fortress's 25-foot ceilings accommodate all but the tallest giants comfortably. Its stone walls, carved long ago from the petrified giant's form, have no special qualities.

entries.name: Doors
entries: Unless noted otherwise, the wooden doors remain closed but unlocked.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Magical lights provide {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} throughout the structure. Giants, or their designees, can speak command words as an action to brighten, dim, or extinguish the lighting.

entries.name: Stairs
entries: The giants constructed the stairs down to the ground below the fortress for visitors of their stature, so they are {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for Medium or smaller creatures.
This chapter describes the events that occur during the first two days of the moot. It also includes the locations where these events take place and descriptions of the NPCs involved in them.

entries.name: Arrival
entries: {@i Proud. Composed. Disdainful sniff.}

At the top of the stairs lies a titanic meeting hall. Huge tables and chairs dominate the space, along with some furniture for human-sized creatures. A chandelier hangs over the main table, providing magical illumination. A number of giants already in attendance loudly discuss territorial rights and wergild.
A thursir blocks the way. Her simple clothing is elegantly cut and decorated with small gems. She seems to gaze at everyone with an air of unflappable poise.

"You must be the smallfolk the High Speaker summoned. I am Katlaug, Hallwarden of Helgihond. To me falls the duty of ensuring that the needs of those attending the moot are met. I shall show you to your chambers."

entries.name: Area 1: Meeting Hall
entries: {@i Brightly lit. Gargantuan table.}

The giants use this hall for their debates. Key attendees sit at the long table with the High Speaker at the center. Those directly involved in the business at hand arrange themselves around the High Speaker. If the focus of the discussion shifts, the giants change seats. The other tables hold the giants' retinues and guests with lesser standing who were invited to speak here (such as the PCs).
In the southeast corner, a mound of rubble reminds attendees of the fortress's "thumb," sheared off during a fight at a previous moot.

If the characters wonder about the number of attendees—not every type of giant is currently represented in this room—{@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} explains that only those with items on the agenda may enter.
This location also serves as a banquet hall. Sigkva expects all guests to show up for dinner each day of the moot.

entries.name: Down
entries: To the base of the Fortress of the Hand.

entries.name: Northeasternmost Doors
entries: Closed double doors to the kitchen (Area 11).

entries.name: Northeast-Central Door
entries: Closed door to the honored guests' hallway (Area 7, off limits).

entries.name: Northwest-Central Door
entries: Closed door to the associates' hall (Area 3, off limits).

entries.name: Northwesternmost Doors
entries: Closed double doors to the lesser quarters (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 2: Lesser Quarters
entries: {@i Haphazard layout. Dim lighting. Musty smell.}
Cushions and a pair of small chests fill this room in no discernable pattern. The light permeating the rest of the fortress fails to manifest here.

If it wasn't obvious to the characters before that the giants have little regard for humanoids, the state of this room should make it abundantly clear. This area is in {@variantrule Darkness|XPHB}. Dust, collecting from the previous moot years ago, covers everything. A variety of pests may live in the threadbare cushions left as "bedding."

entries.name: Rules
entries: On the way to show the heroes their accommodations, {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} says they can move freely around Helgihond but may not enter any of the giants' chambers, on penalty of expulsion. She insists they stow any weapons in their quarters.

items: {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} brooks no argument about this demand, but PCs can use Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) checks to hide smaller weapons.

As they passed through the meeting hall (Area 1), the characters easily noted that {@creature Queen Sinmara|NorthlandsSagas}, {@creature Glytta Weggesdottir|NorthlandsSagas}, and {@creature Sigkva Runigsdottir|NorthlandsSagas} each possessed their weapons (peace bonded).
{@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} doesn't insist giants stow their weapons.

If asked, the thursir {@creature Beli Groundshaker|NorthlandsSagas} (Area 5) and the fire giant {@creature Izhova|NorthlandsSagas} (Area 4) claim to stow their weapons in solidarity with the humanoids.

entries.name: Bralt and Bremman
entries: Beli's giantkin aides also sleep here.

entries.name: Chests
entries: One of the supplied chests has a broken lock; {@creature Bralt|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Bremman|NorthlandsSagas} have claimed the working chest for their items.

items.name: {@dc 14} Dexterity ({@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC rigs the broken chest to accept a lock. Creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on checks to break or pick the lock, unless the character exceeded the DC by 5 or more.

items.name: {@dc 16} Dexterity ({@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC picks the lock on the giantkin's chest. It contains a pair of {@item Dagger|XPHB|Daggers} and 105 GP.
When the PCs feel prepared, they can exit their quarters to attend the debate.

entries.name: Katlaug (Thursir Hallwarden)
entries: {@i Prim and proper. Caretaker and majordomo.}
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 6.
{@b Background:} Has served as hallwarden for several moots and takes great pride in performing her duties to the letter.
{@b Personality Traits:} Dignified, proud, expects a level of respect.
{@b Bonds:} Protective of Helgihond.
{@b Flaws:} Dismissive of "smaller" species.
{@b Wants:} To ensure that no one questions the hospitality of Helgihond.
{@b Talking to Katlaug:} The thursir freely relates information about Helgihond's amenities. She neither knows nor cares about the hall's history. She focuses on the here and now.

entries.name: Bralt and Bremman (Hill Giantkin Cultist Fanatics)
entries: {@i Clean-shaven. Gruff voices. Seemingly uncomfortable noble attire.}
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 2.
{@b Background:} Joining the Cult of Ragnarok gave these otherwise unremarkable brothers the only reason to feel special that they'd ever had.
{@b Personality Traits:} Bored, cagey, coarse.
{@b Bonds:} Each other and the Cult of Ragnarok.
{@b Flaws:} Protective of each other.
{@b Wants:} Wealth, hedonism as they await the world's end.
{@b Talking to Bralt and Bremman:} The giantkin freely relate the following (in order):

items: They work for {@creature Beli Groundshaker|NorthlandsSagas} but claim not to know his real agenda. He put out a notice for aides to accompany him to the moot, so he would seem more important.

items.name: {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC thinks this isn't entirely the truth.

entries.name: South
entries: Double doors to the meeting hall (Area 1).

entries.name: Debate
entries: {@creature Sigkva Runigsdottir|NorthlandsSagas} presides over the debate in the meeting hall (Area 1) during the moot, demonstrating fairness and an even temper. When they enter, she points the characters to human-sized tables in the corner of the room. They may listen to the debating giants and can present their own arguments against the cult when called upon.

entries.name: Day 1 Discussion
entries: The topic under debate is the ongoing disagreement between the stone giants of Brotdalr and the jotuns of Reykurbrand. The stone giants have claimed a fertile valley near Reykurbrand. Though the jotuns have never used the land, it falls under their traditional territory.

items.name: Stone Giant Viewpoint:
entries: We woke the soil. We raised the walls. We made it ours. We will pay a reasonable price for the land, but it is ours.

items.name: Jotun Viewpoint:
entries: What is ours is ours. It matters not whether we use it. This is trespass, a theft of land by those of lower status. We have no reason to part with what is ours.

Other giants at the table may weigh in with questions or opinions. The giants grudgingly allow the PCs to attend the discussion, but it becomes clear they do not care to hear from them on the first day, as other concerns take priority.
Should the PCs interrupt the discussions, Sinmara and Glytta angrily rebuke them. If they continue to interrupt, Sigkva calls for their silence.

items.name: {@dc 11} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC understands they could anger the giants by insisting on discussing their business.

items.name: {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC promises to cease their interruptions and convinces the giants of their sincerity. On a failure, the PC has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on future Charisma-based checks against Sinmara and Glytta.

entries.name: Banquet
entries: At the end of the proceedings, the kitchen serves a banquet in the meeting hall. This less formal setting allows the characters to talk to other attendees and get a sense of how the various giants stand on the issue of allying with the cult.

items: Armed with notes from Azala (or Gullveig), Sigkva—representing the cloud giants—opposes the alliance with the cult.
Ostensibly representing the frost giant chieftains, Beli opposes the alliance (to throw suspicion off his covert mission).
Sinmara stands for the mighty jotuns. She regards the return of their complete rulership over the Northlands after Ragnarok with anticipation and favors the alliance.

Glytta represents the stone giants and offers to stand for the hill giants as well, as their delegate did not arrive (see A Curious Corpse). She favors the alliance but wishes for a less chaotic and destructive way to achieve giantkind's goal.
As the fire giant delegate, {@creature Izhova|NorthlandsSagas} is on the fence; he considers it foolish to free Fenris but does not recommend actively trying prevent the cult's plan.

The storm giants and other absent clans have formally joined the Blood Reckoning already and actively work with the cult. The picture of confidence, Skymir saw no reason they should send delegates to the moot, as he feels no need for other giants' support.

items.name: Sigkva Runigsdottir (Cloud Giant Chieftain, High Speaker of the Moot)
entries: {@i Light blue complexion. Short-cropped golden hair. Formally attired.}
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 10.
{@b Background:} Enjoys good relations with other cloud giant clans; frequently interacts with storm and lightning giant tribes.
{@b Personality Traits:} Attentive, kind, humble.
{@b Bonds:} Her family and the cloud giants in her charge.
{@b Flaws:} She naively assumes the best intentions in everyone with whom she interacts.
{@b Wants:} A successful moot with no hard feelings among the attendees, as well as assent from the assembled giants to help fight the Cult of Ragnarok.
{@b Talking to Sigkva:} She freely relates the following (in order):

items: She trusts {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} implicitly. The hallwarden understands the PCs' reasons for attending, and Sigkva tells them the thursir will attend to their needs while at the moot.
She hasn't met {@creature Izhova|NorthlandsSagas} or Beli previously but knows {@creature Izhova|NorthlandsSagas}'s reputation as an accomplished diplomat.

She must resolve the dispute between the stone giants and jotuns before she can turn to the PCs' discussion. She figures smoothing things over between Sinmara and Glytta will entice them to pay attention to the party.

entries.name: Day 2 Discussion
entries: The main topic under debate is the Matter of the Alliance with the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin.

entries.name: Speaking to the Giants
entries: Sigkva invites the characters to lay out why the giants' involvement with the Cult of Ragnarok is bad for everyone. (She has promised concessions to both Sinmara and Glytta, so they allow the PCs to speak. However, Sinmara in particular has little patience for them usurping her agenda.)

See the "Banquet" section under Day 1 Discussion for each delegate's initial stance on the alliance. To sway giants to their side of the argument, the PCs must succeed on three of the following checks before they suffer three failures. Anyone swayed by the heroes' testimony pledges their support against the cult. The PCs can attempt up to two checks from each selection:

items.name: {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC makes an impassioned plea that compels the giants to pay attention.

items.name: {@dc 17} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC embellishes the threat to the giants if they don't oppose the alliance.

items.name: {@dc 19} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC appeals to the giants' better nature to foster a spirit of cooperation.

items.name: {@dc 16} Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC frames the rise of the Cult of Ragnarok against previous doomsday cults and conveys the real danger this cult presents.

items.name: {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC stresses the impact to the giants, should they allow Ragnarok to devastate the world.
If the heroes fail three checks, read the following:

Sinmara shoves her chair back, stands, slams her fist on the table, and yells, "We have survived many of these so-called death cults! These fools don't know what they are talking about—they're trying to stir up trouble for their own benefit." She looks ready to storm out of the meeting hall.
Characters who act fast can attempt to defuse Queen Sinmara's anger:

items.name: {@dc 19} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC gains Sinmara's respect by standing up to her.

items.name: {@dc 20} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC convinces Sinmara to return to the meeting.

The High Speaker listens to all arguments, then announces that, considering the magnitude of the Matter of the Alliance, she has decided to wait until the next day before taking the final vote. She then calls for the next topic, and the rest of the day proceeds without incident.

entries.name: Banquet
entries: At the end of the day's debate, the kitchen serves another sumptuous banquet. The PCs may attempt to make inroads with the more stubborn giants.

items.name: Queen Sinmara (Jotun)
entries: {@i Towering woman, even for a giant. Gleaming, golden eyes. Crimson garments bedecked with melted and reformed gold concealing a suit of crimson plate armor. Smells of sandalwood.}
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 8.
{@b Background:} As wife of the dreaded Surtr, she has become accustomed to his wanderings across the globe and takes personally her leadership responsibility.
{@b Personality Traits:} Decisive, driven, imperious.
{@b Bonds:} Her husband, Surtr; her land, Reykurbrand; and her people, the jotuns, in that order.
{@b Flaws:} Underestimates non-giants.
{@b Wants:} The appearance of peacefully resolving her territorial dispute with the stone giants.

{@b Talking to Sinmara:} The PCs first must convince the reduced-size jotun to deign to talk with them with a {@dc 14} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check or {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check. Afterward, the queen freely relates the following (in order):

items: She expects {@creature Glytta Weggesdottir|NorthlandsSagas}, the stone giant, to give in to her demands eventually.
She's heard about so many doomsday cults that come to naught, she has no interest in discussing another one.

entries.name: Exploring the Fortress
entries: The characters initially have a limited range for exploring, as {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} barred them from visiting the giants' private chambers (through the two central doors off the meeting hall). However, they do have access to one additional area.

entries.name: Area 11: Kitchen
entries: {@i Busy. Smell of roasting meat. Warm.}
Several humanoids busy themselves at various stations in the kitchen. An older giantkin woman barks orders at the assembled workers.

After considerable vetting, the fortress's staff selected {@creature Vorbis Glynssdottir|NorthlandsSagas} to lead the kitchen. When not sleeping in her quarters near the base of the fortress, the chef is a constant presence here. At nearly every hour of the day, someone prepares a meal or a snack, and kitchen workers flow in and out of the adjoining pantry (Area 12) and to and from the meeting hall (Area 1).
The chef does not allow visitors into the pantry.

entries.name: North
entries: Closed double doors to the pantry (Area 12, off limits).

entries.name: South
entries: Double doors to the meeting hall (Area 1).

entries.name: Part 2: The Investigation
entries: Unfortunately, Sigkva is murdered during the night after the second debate session. The Timeline table outlines pertinent events leading up to the murder.
Beli uses the enchanted birdcage below to render the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} docile for transport.

items: Glytta arrives in Helgihond with a birdcage containing a songbird.
Beli arrives. In his trunk is an enchanted birdcage holding a {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go}.
During the first night's banquet, Beli sends his two minions ({@creature Bralt|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Bremman|NorthlandsSagas}) into Glytta's room to swap her birdcage for his enchanted one.
Beli uses {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} on Glytta so she wouldn't notice the swapped cages.
Beli uses {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} on Glytta again. She moves the swapped birdcage to Sigkva's room for "safekeeping," then is compelled to forget all about it.
Later, Beli sends {@creature Bremman|NorthlandsSagas} to the kitchen (Area 11) to poison Sigkva's food and dose {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas}'s evening wine with sleeping potion.
After the banquet, Sigkva returns to her chamber, succumbs to the poison, and becomes {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}.
{@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} drinks her evening wine and falls sleep.
Beli sneaks into Katlaug's chamber and moves through the hidden passage (Area 6A) into Sigkva's room.
Beli opens the enchanted birdcage, releasing the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go}, which kills Sigkva and plants spores in her chest.

Beli releases the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} back into the wilderness through a loosened board in the secret passageway (Area 6A), plans a note in the passage to throw suspicion on the PCs, then returns to his own chambers.

items.name: Glytta Weggesdottir (Stone Giant Priest of Jormungandr)
entries: {@i Granite skin. Bald. Bittersweet perfume. Decorative yet functional chainmail.}
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 9.

{@b Background:} Frustrated over her clan's lower status due to a stone giant transgression so long ago as to be meaningless. She won't discuss this offense other than to say her chieftain, Karn, is working to address it.
{@b Personality Traits:} Belligerent, devious, muddled.
{@b Bonds:} Her community of Brotdalr.
{@b Flaws:} Hates being patronized when she is wrong.
{@b Wants:} A "victory" over Sinmara in the negotiations.
{@b Talking to Glytta:} The stone giant freely relates the following (in order):

items: She feels frustrated at the treatment her fellow stone giants receive from other giants. Glytta hopes to return her people to equal status with other giants.

If the PCs help her get leverage over Sinmara, she will happily entertain their proposal, up to a promise of stone giant fighters to help in the assault. She won't remember this unless the PCs get it in writing, a delicate task requiring a successful {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Deception|XPHB}) check or {@dc 17} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check.

entries.name: Accusations
entries: Early in the morning, {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} discovers Sigkva's body and summons the guards. She then orders everyone to the meeting hall (Area 1).
The doors to your chamber burst open, revealing Katlaug and two lightning giants. "There has been a murder," says the hallwarden, her eyes cold. "Rise and answer for yourselves before the moot."

She departs with a guard; the other stays to supervise the PCs. This {@creature Lightning Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook} refuses to answer questions and tells them only to dress and come to the meeting hall. When the party arrives, read or paraphrase the following:

All the moot's attendees and Helgihond staff have gathered in the meeting hall. At the far side of the chamber, Katlaug stands on a chair to address the gathering. In the southeast corner of the room, a giant's body lies on the floor, covered by a cloth.

"The High Speaker is dead," Katlaug says to the stunned room. A guard slowly draws the cloth from Sigkva's still face for all to see, then reverently replaces it. "She was murdered in the night. As hallwarden, I order everyone to surrender their weapons. Further, everyone shall remain in Helgihond until the one responsible for this cowardly act has been exposed."
The towering Queen Sinmara scoffs. "It is clear as ice. When a giant falls, we need look no farther than the smallfolk." The giants turn angry eyes toward you.
Izhova speaks. "Nonsense. These heroes have little to gain from this killing and, indeed, much to lose. In fact, I believe of all of us here, they are best suited to investigate this crime."
Katlaug regards you skeptically. "Well, what say you? Are you responsible for this murder or are you 'heroes' who might solve it?"

entries.name: Vorbis Glynssdottir (Storm Giantkin Chef)
entries: {@i Tall. Stained uniform. Platinum hair tied in a bun.}
{@b Found In:} Area 11.
{@b Background:} When not cooking for the moot, Vorbis serves as chef at Thrymheim, the mountain castle of storm giant jarl Berfinn Thjazason.
{@b Personality Traits:} Demanding, professional, untiring.
{@b Bonds:} Her kitchen and kitchen staff.
{@b Flaws:} Expects other humanoids to follow her orders without question.
{@b Wants:} An exemplary set of meals for the moot's attendees.

{@b Talking to Vorbis:} The giantkin has little time to indulge in conversation. Vorbis keeps the kitchen open as much as possible to accommodate the giants' appetites. Her underlings deliver food to the banquet (Area 1) and to individual rooms upon request.

The hallwarden seems unsure whether the PCs could have murdered Sigkva—she believes "smallfolk" would stand no chance against a giant. Thanks to support from {@creature Izhova|NorthlandsSagas}, she entertains the idea of them investigating.

items.name: {@dc 12} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC convinces Katlaug of the party's innocence and value in uncovering the cause of Sigkva's death. On a failed check, the thursir accompanies them in their investigations and questions everything they do.

items: Once {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} allows them to investigate, she grants them access to the entire fortress—including Sigkva's chamber—and lets them examine the body.

On Beli's orders, {@creature Bralt|NorthlandsSagas} and Bremman (see Part 1, Area 2) offer to accompany the PCs as guards, to keep an eye on them for {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas}—but really to keep Beli informed of their progress and guide their investigation toward the "obvious choice" of Glytta as culprit.

entries: Before the PCs begin their investigations, {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} warns:

"If you do not find the true culprit and prove their guilt, the blame will fall on you and your people. For the crime of murdering the High Speaker, all of Jotunheim will rise up and erase your clans from this world."

entries.name: Sinmara's Ploy
entries: Once Katlaug appoints the characters to investigate, Sinmara demands the delegates reopen her complaint against the stone giants, since they are all stuck in Helgihond anyway. Helpfully, this isolates the giants in the meeting hall during the investigation.

entries.name: Weapon Chests
entries: The guards collect weapons from everyone present, and even go into the PCs' quarters to take their armaments. They place them all in chests in the northwest corner of the meeting hall. The characters can easily spot which chest holds their weapons.

entries.name: Detective work
entries: The PCs learn several things while scouring the fortress for clues. You'll find some information tagged with "{@color [CLUE]|4d6381}" immediately below, while other tagged details appear under Key Locations. The heroes can take all the time needed on Day 3 to search the desired locations.
If they question the servants, they learn additional clues, in the following order:

items: On the afternoon of the second day, a giant servant saw Glytta carry a birdcage into the High Speaker's chamber.
Several individuals entered the kitchen (Area 11) before the second day's banquet.

items.name: {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) or Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC extracts the following names: {@creature Bremman|NorthlandsSagas}, Glytta, and {@creature Izhova|NorthlandsSagas} (and the PCs, if they entered the kitchen).

entries.name: Key locations
entries: Once permitted to investigate, the PCs may visit the giants' quarters as well as the rest of the fortress. No section of Helgihond is off limits to them now. If Part 1 introduced an area's description, this section offers only new information for that area.

entries.name: Area 1: Meeting Hall
entries: {@i A table with chairs sized for giants fills most of the chamber. Several smaller tables and chests dot this meeting hall. A chandelier hangs over the main table, providing magical illumination.}

After the High Speaker's murder, {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} ordered her body placed in the southeast corner of this chamber, covered in a cloth, while awaiting the investigation and proper burial.

items.name: {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discovers Sigkva died from Piercing damage. If the check exceeds DC by 5, the PC realizes the High Speaker was {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} when attacked.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC learns Sigkva suffered the same wounds as the hill giant they found on the way to the moot (check made with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} if the PCs learned about the wounds on the body in A Curious Corpse).

entries.name: Questioning Katlaug
entries: Regarding Sigkva's murder, she feels reluctant to talk out of turn about the dignitaries. However, a successful {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check convinces her to share the following:

items: The dispute between the stone giants and Sinmara's people has the potential to erupt into full-scale war
{@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} knows Glytta arrived with a covered birdcage, but the attendees sometimes exchange unusual gifts.
Her habit is to drink a mug of wine before bed to help her sleep. The kitchen delivered the one currently next to her bed.

entries.name: Down
entries: To the base of the Fortress of the Giants.

entries.name: Northeasternmost Doors
entries: Closed double doors to the kitchen (Area 11).

entries.name: Northeast-Central Door
entries: Closed door to the honored guests' hallway (Area 7).

entries.name: Northwest-Central Door
entries: Closed door to the associates' hall (Area 3).

entries.name: Northwesternmost Doors
entries: Closed double doors to the lesser quarters (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 2: Lesser Quarters
entries: Should the characters question Beli's giantkin retainers after the murder, {@creature Bralt|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Bremman|NorthlandsSagas} freely relate the following details (in order), in addition to those noted in Part 1:

items: They have grown disillusioned by the dull proceedings and the lack of fights or shows of physical prowess. Other than laughing at their boss picking radishes out of his food (see clue in Area 11), they have been bored.

Regarding Sigkva's murder, they become defensive, claiming there's no way they would incur the giants' wrath by killing one of them. (They know Beli had something to do with it, but they don't willingly betray a fellow cultist.)

entries.name: South
entries: Double doors to the meeting hall (Area 1).

entries.name: Area 3: Associates' Hall
entries: {@i Torchlit. Warm. Unadorned.}
Other than the stout wooden doors providing access to the meeting hall and guest lodging, only magical torches in elaborate sconces decorate this hallway.
The hallwarden and lesser giant attendees lodge in the fortress's second-longest "finger." The doors here are closed but unlocked.

entries.name: North
entries: Door to Katlaug's lodging (Area 6).

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Door to Beli Groundshaker's lodging (Area 5).

entries.name: Southeast
entries: Door to {@creature Izhova|NorthlandsSagas}'s quarters (Area 4).

entries.name: South
entries: Door to the meeting hall (Area 1).

entries.name: Area 4: Izhova's Quarters
entries: {@i Brightly lit. Stone bed. Sharp and pungent smell.}

Besides a raised bed made of smoldering charcoal, the only apparent furniture here is a trunk at one end of this chamber. A lingering odor indicates the staff has recently cleaned. Light shines from a hemisphere fastened to the ceiling.
{@creature Izhova|NorthlandsSagas} sleeps on heated charcoal. The staff cleaned and prepared the room just before his arrival.

entries.name: Chest
entries: The staff also provided a chest for the fire giant to hold his items. His {@item Longsword|XPHB} rests behind the unlocked chest, which contains some spare clothing, his invitation to the moot, and a modest 40 GP.

entries.name: West
entries: Door to the associates' hall (see Area 3).

items.name: Izhova (Fire Giant Necromancer)
entries: {@i Dark red coloration. Close-cropped hair. Angular features. Adorned in simple yet elegant shift. Smells faintly of spices.}
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 4.
{@b Background:} A skilled diplomat from Sengajordensblod, the giant capital; feels humbled to be here, as he is not a leader like many other delegates.
{@b Personality Traits:} Fastidious, soft-spoken, coercive.
{@b Bonds:} His chieftain, who sent him to the moot.
{@b Flaws:} Relies on diplomacy, bordering on intimidation.
{@b Wants:} A smooth negotiation between Queen Sinmara and {@creature Glytta Weggesdottir|NorthlandsSagas}, and a chance for the PCs to speak their piece.
{@b Talking to Izhova:} The fire giant freely relates the following (in order):

items: He expresses dismay at the PCs' treatment by some giants and attempts to provide insight into the giant perspective.

Sigkva's death has shaken him. He didn't know her except by reputation, which he describes as positive among most giants. He gets right to the heart of the matter by suggesting the Cult of Ragnarok's involvement.
He went to the kitchen yesterday to ask about the ingredients of the entrees (he has culinary interests).
If asked whether he noticed anything amiss the night of the murder, he reports that he fell asleep quickly after the feast and slept through to the morning.

entries.name: Area 5: Beli Groundshaker's Lodging
entries: {@i Strewn clothing. Earthy odor. Torchlit.}

This chamber's inhabitant has scattered his bedroll and belongings throughout, making it a disorganized mess. The chest against the east wall appears stuffed with more clothing. A massive club pokes out of the chest.

{@creature Beli Groundshaker|NorthlandsSagas} sleeps here. The mess is no affectation, as Beli truly stores his belongings chaotically. He hopes it leads those who see it to believe in his persona's simplistic nature.

entries.name: Alarmed Chest
entries: Beli protects the chest with an {@spell Alarm|XPHB} spell, which alerts him mentally when someone opens it. Beli pretends he has nothing to hide. However, he must keep his tools somewhere, so he attached a false bottom to the chest.

items.name: {@dc 19} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check or {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB}:
entries: A PC determines an Abjuration spell protects the chest.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discovers the chest has a false bottom.

items.name: {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: After discovering the false bottom, a PC locates the latch to release it.

Finding and opening the false bottom reveals two vials of a liquid version of the {@item Essence of Ether|XDMG} poison and a {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG}. Inside the {@item Bag of Holding|XDMG} is a golden birdcage containing a dead songbird. This is the cage Glytta brought to Helgihond.

entries.name: West
entries: Door to the associates' hall (see Area 3).

items.name: Beli Groundshaker (Thursir)
entries: {@i Stout. Somewhat paunchy. Simple clothing. Coarse voice.}
{@b Found In:} Area 1 or 5.

{@b Background:} A longtime member of the Blood Reckoning, Beli discovered the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} and devised this plot. He spent enough time in Thursrike to gain the trust of frost giant king Haakon Drakechoker and met Glytta there.
{@b Personality Traits:} Amiable, blunt, insightful. (After being uncovered as the murderer: arrogant, calculating, cruel.)
{@b Bonds:} The Cult of Ragnarok, provided it continues supplying Beli with items to create mayhem.
{@b Flaws:} Murderous.
{@b Wants:} To sow chaos at the moot, while learning about the PCs' and the giants' plans.

{@b Unique Powers.} Beli has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Charisma checks against other giants. He can cast the {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} spell at will and the {@spell Shapechange|XPHB} spell twice per day.

{@b Talking to Beli:} At first, Beli speaks of himself in the third person. Once he drops his simplistic guise, he refuses to divulge information. Until that time, the thursir freely relates the following (in order):

items: Beli hasn't heard about the hill giant's death (see A Curious Corpse) and is saddened to learn about it. He recalls that a hill giant was supposed to attend the moot.
Being invited to the moot surprised Beli. He confides that thursir rarely get the opportunity to attend.
He shows interest in allying with the giants and PCs in the assault on Birgkrona and hopes to hear more about their plans.
Regarding Sigkva's murder, he expresses his regrets and offers to help in any way he can. He also (truthfully) suggests the murderer has framed {@creature Glytta Weggesdottir|NorthlandsSagas}.

entries.name: Area 6: Katlaug's Lodging
entries: {@i Brightly lit. Austere and stark. Sharp and pungent smell.}

A raised bed made of stone and covered with furs—the only apparent furniture here—stands against the far wall of this chamber. A lingering odor indicates the staff has recently cleaned here. Light shines from a hemisphere fastened to the ceiling.
{@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas}'s quarters look formal and devoid of personal touches. When not attending the moot, she dwells in a nearby settlement.

entries.name: Mug and Bowl
entries: Next to the bed on the floor, an empty steel mug sits on a tray from the kitchen.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC notices a strange residue mixed with the dregs of wine at the bottom. {@color [CLUE]|4d6381}

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC can tell the residue comes from a strong sleeping potion.

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: Forty years ago, an impatient giant jarl built a secret passageway (Area 6A) between this room and the High Speaker's chamber (Area 10). {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} knows about it but hasn't thought about it in decades.

items.name: {@dc 17} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discovers the secret door in the stone wall.

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Hidden door to the secret passageway (Area 6A).

entries.name: South
entries: Closed door to the associates' hall (Area 3).

entries.name: Area 6A: Secret Passageway
entries: {@i Dark. Scent of mahogany.}
The fortress's only wooden construction connects two of its "fingers."

This passageway connects {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas}'s lodging (Area 6) with the High Speaker's chamber (Area 10). It proves incredibly cramped for giants, but it's not noticeable from the ground below.

entries.name: Assassin's Note
entries: After killing Sigkva, Beli crumpled up a piece of paper containing a purported assassin's note inscribed with runes and placed it in the passage to give the appearance of an attempt to hide it. See handout.

items.name: {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC sees a scrap of paper peeking out from between wooden slats.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence check (or can read {@language Giant|XPHB}):
entries: A PC determines the meaning of the runes in clockwise order from the upper left, as follows: Reversed {@i laukaz}: poison; {@i laukaz} and {@i turisaz}: cloud giant chieftain; four {@i mannaz} runes covered by red {@i isaz}: imprisonment of four humanoids; {@i fehu}: payment for successful assassination; {@i berkanan}: new beginning brought on by assassination; {@i uruz} and {@i turisaz}: a signature line meaning "strong giant."

entries.name: Trap
entries: When Beli loosened a few floor boards to facilitate the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go}'s escape, he inadvertently destabilized the passageway.

entries.name: Collapsing Floor Trap
entries: {@i Deadly Trap (Levels 5–10)}
The wooden beams are weakened and can't support much weight.

entries.name: Trigger:
entries: When more than 50 pounds is placed in any of the spaces in Area 6A, the floor gives way.

entries.name: Duration:
entries: Instantaneous
Each creature in the passage must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, falling 100 feet to the ground on a failure and taking 35 ({@damage 10d6}) Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: A creature can notice the trap with a successful {@dc 14} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check.

Creatures can shore up the wooden beams with other pieces of wood. This takes 10 minutes. A creature can perform the task hastily, reducing the effort to 1 minute but must succeed on a {@dc 14} Intelligence check and a {@dc 14} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check to place the wood securely. A failure on either check causes the trap to trigger as above, but each affected creature has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on its saving throw. Failing both checks confers no {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Door to the High Speaker's quarters (Area 10).

entries.name: Southwest
entries: Door to Katlaug's lodging (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 7: Hallway for Honored Guests
entries: {@i Brightly lit. Gleaming stone. Sense of majesty.}
This hallway is clearly meant for the fortress's most important guests. Five domes provide warm, welcoming illumination.
The walls are decorated with precious metals and gems, which would fetch 3,000 GP—and a lot of wrath from the giants—should a group take the time to tear the material from the walls.

entries.name: Locked Door
entries: Sigkva keeps the door to her chambers (Area 10) unlocked for the moot. However, after she died, {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} locked the door to preserve any evidence.

items.name: {@dc 20} Dexterity ({@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC unlocks the door.

items.name: {@dc 25} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC breaks down the door. This alerts everyone in Areas 8 and 9.

entries.name: North
entries: Locked door to the High Speaker's quarters (Area 10).

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Closed door to Glytta Weggesdottir's lodging (Area 9).

entries.name: Southeast
entries: Closed door to Queen Sinmara's lodging (Area 8).

entries.name: South
entries: Door to the meeting hall (Area 1).

entries.name: Area 8: Queen Sinmara's Temporary Lodging
entries: {@i Unbearably warm. Brimstone and wood odor.}

This room, meticulously maintained by its inhabitant's servants, features an enormous, well-appointed bed over which hangs a massive painting of a mountain scene. An open jar sits atop a small chest resting against the wall.

This richly decorated chamber feels unnaturally warm and has an odor mixing brimstone and sandalwood. The bed and furnishings are giant-sized; the jotun queen magically reduces her size for comfort in this fortress.

entries.name: Jar and Chest
entries: The chest isn't trapped and contains Queen Sinmara's clothing and personal items.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC identifies the substance in the jar as a sandalwood balm.

items: Sinmara always wears this balm; all her clothing bears its scent. {@color [CLUE]|4d6381}

entries.name: Coffer
entries: Under her bed, the queen keeps a coffer filled with paperwork, including her invitation to the moot and information about the territorial dispute, as well as a ruby that glows with an inner fire (worth 750 GP). She hasn't opened the chest since arriving at the moot.

entries.name: Trap
entries: During the moot's first night, Beli and his minions trapped the coffer with a cold-based trap, to implicate {@creature Glytta Weggesdottir|NorthlandsSagas}, without waking the queen. Opening the coffer triggers the frost blast trap (see below).

entries.name: Frost Blast
entries: {@i Deadly Trap (Levels 5–10)}
When the inscribed rune breaks, it releases a condensed {@spell Cone of Cold|XPHB}.

entries.name: Trigger:
entries: When a creature opens the coffer bearing the inscribed rune, the trap activates.

entries.name: Duration:
entries: Instantaneous

The rune creates a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} of cold, emanating from the coffer. Each creature in the area must make a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw, taking 36 ({@damage 8d8}) Cold damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.

entries.name: Detect and Disable
entries: A creature can notice the trap with a successful {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) or {@dc 17} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check. Someone within 5 feet of the rune can disarm it by succeeding on a {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check. If a creature fails the check to disarm the trap, the trap triggers. Alternatively, a successful {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} ({@dc 15}) cast on the rune destroys the trap.

entries.name: Questioning Sinmara
entries: The PCs first must convince the jotun to deign to talk with them with a {@dc 14} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check or {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check. Afterward, the queen freely relates the following (in order), in addition to what is noted in Part 1:

items: She believes Glytta is deliberately provoking her by making her own room (Area 9) unnaturally cold and by bringing a cage full of songbirds, which everyone knows Sinmara detests.

Regarding Sigkva's murder, Sinmara mostly expresses frustration that the moot might end without a decision about her concerns. The fact that the murder might involve cult agents doesn't make her reconsider the threat they may pose. She didn't notice anything amiss until Sigkva was found dead.

entries.name: West
entries: Door to the honored guests' hallway (see Area 7).

entries.name: Area 9: Glytta Wessesdottir's Temporary Lodging
entries: {@i Frigid. Frosty. Dimly lit.}
This room's temperature suits only those accustomed to it. The magical lighting has frosted over, muting the room's illumination. A large bed and a chest rest against the east wall.

The fortress staff has altered the room's temperature to well below freezing, to accommodate the Glytta's instructions. The wall adjoining this chamber and Queen Sinmara's (Area 8) sweats profusely, but the water quickly freezes, creating a rippling appearance.

entries.name: Missing Birdcage
entries: Glytta arrived with a birdcage holding one songbird and placed it in her room. She brought it because Sinmara is known to hate birdsong. If asked about it, she doesn't remember giving it to anyone and doesn't recall what she did with it.

entries.name: Locked Chest
entries: Glytta keeps her clothing in the room's chest, along with several maps displaying historical territorial boundaries as proof for the stone giants' case. The chest also holds a jar of scented Myrrh oil and a diamond worth 770 GP, ostensibly a gift for {@creature Queen Sinmara|NorthlandsSagas}.

items.name: {@dc 17} Dexterity ({@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC unlocks the chest.

items.name: {@dc 23} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC pries the lid open.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC examining the oil identifies it as Myrrh oil and can smell the distinctive bittersweet odor on Glytta's clothing. {@color [CLUE]|4d6381}

items.name: {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check or 2 minutes of searching:
entries: A PC finds a vial of liquid {@item Essence of Ether|XDMG} poison, which Beli hid here.

entries.name: Questioning Glytta
entries: The stone giant freely relates the following (in order), in addition to the information noted in Part 1:

items: She brought a birdcage for {@creature Queen Sinmara|NorthlandsSagas}, but she's certain the queen won't appreciate it. When pressed on the gift's location now, Glytta becomes flustered at (truthfully) not remembering what she did with it.
She assumes {@creature Queen Sinmara|NorthlandsSagas} perpetrated Sigkva's murder to end the negotiations, which the stone giant confidently assumes benefitted her.

entries.name: West
entries: Door to the honored guests' hallway (Area 7).

entries.name: Area 10: High Speaker's Quarters
entries: {@i Sumptuous décor. Petrichor. Brightly lit. Wisps of fog.}
This room—decorated with peaceful, mobile cloud motifs—contains a comfortable giant-sized bed and a dressing table covered in stacks of paper. A silver birdcage sits on the floor next to the table.
Should the characters visit the room after the murder, read or paraphrase the following as well:
The floor next to the table has scattered papers and splashes of blood. The birdcage's wire door hangs open.

This dignified and richly appointed chamber is set aside for the High Speaker. Sigkva's converted the dressing table to a desk, which holds all the material she expects to need at the moot, including paperwork regarding the Cult of Ragnarok's recent activities received from Azala (or Gullveig). She spends little time in this room apart from her scant amount of sleep.

entries.name: Birdcage
entries: Before Sigkva's murder, {@creature Glytta Weggesdottir|NorthlandsSagas} (acting on Beli's {@spell Suggestion|XPHB} spell) left the covered birdcage in this chamber (see the beginning of Part 2 for its stat block). The spell erased her memory of doing so. After Beli enacted his plan, he left the birdcage open, staging it to look like Sigkva opened it.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check or {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB}:
entries: A PC realizes the birdcage is magical, combining Enchantment and Illusion magic.

items.name: {@dc 19} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC detects a faint rime of frost coating the cage's underside.

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: After Sigkva's murder, the secret door in the room's northwest corner stands open.

items.name: {@dc 17} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discovers the secret door set into the stone wall before the murder.

entries.name: South
entries: Closed door to the honored guests' hallway (Area 7).
