entries.name: Northwest
entries: Hidden door to the secret passageway (Area 6A).

entries.name: Questioning Vorbis
entries: In addition to what is noted in Part 1, the giantkin chef freely relates the following (in order):

items: She is sorry to hear about Sigkva's murder but says she has more pressing concerns managing the kitchen.
She takes offense at any accusation about her subordinates' potential involvement.

items.name: If asked whether anyone has been acting oddly
entries: a successful {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check gets Vorbis to reveal reluctantly that Glytta requires no fish with her meals, Sinmara never drinks spirits, and Beli requests no radishes in his food, as it causes a terrible skin rash. {@color [CLUE]|4d6381}

entries.name: North
entries: Closed double doors to the pantry (Area 12).

entries.name: South
entries: Double doors to the meeting hall (Area 1).

entries.name: Area 12: Pantry
entries: {@i Cool. Dark. Smells of ale, food, and spices.}

Barrels of alcohol and hanging cuts of meat take up most of the space in this magically chilled room. In addition to the crowded pantry also contains various spice containers, sacks of grain and flour, and a smattering of fresh vegetables.

entries.name: Empty Vial
entries: After {@creature Bremman|NorthlandsSagas} poisoned Sigkva's meal on Day 2, he decided to hide the vial rather than risk someone finding it.

items.name: {@dc 18} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or {@dc 14} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discovers the vial.

items.name: {@dc 19} Intelligence ({@item Alchemist's Supplies|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC determines the poison's effects from the residue.

entries.name: South
entries: Double doors to the kitchen (Area 11).

entries.name: Part 3: Matters Escalate
entries: Partway through the third day, Beli orchestrates a significant event: The {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} implanted in Sigkva's body emerge and attack. He intends for this distraction to give him cover to shapechange to Glytta's, Katlaug's, or Sinmara's form.

entries.name: Beli's Goal
entries: Beli wants to sow chaos and murder. If he manages just one of the following, he will have accomplished his mission:

items: Assassinate the giant whose form he steals in the chaos of the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} attack.
Fool the other giants into believing the target of his impersonation is the fake, leading them to kill the target as the supposed assassin.
Create enough confusion to escape.

entries.name: The Attack
entries: At a time the GM chooses—after the PCs have investigated Sigkva's chambers (Area 10)—those in the meeting hall (Area 1) notice Sigkva's shrouded body moving. The GM should arrange for the party to be nearby or just entering the hall. When they are in position, read or paraphrase the following:

"Sigkva is alive!" someone yells, pointing at the cloth-covered corpse in the corner. Sure enough, the body shudders and twitches, as if waking. Just as suddenly, five human-sized, fungoid, insectile creatures burst up out of the body's chest in a spray of gore and torn fabric.
"Kvideta!" Katlaug screams. "The legends are real! They'll infect us all!" The room erupts into chaos.
The giants use the {@action Dodge|XPHB} and {@action Dash|XPHB} actions to stay away from the 5 {@creature Mi-go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} ({@i ToB1} variant: INT 5 only).

entries.name: Giants' Fear
entries: Everyone in the meeting hall saw the creatures erupt from Sigkva's body. Because of a cultural fear based on legend, the giants panic when the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} emerge, as they fear infestation. The giants gain the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition and don't engage in battle until one minute after the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} have been dispatched.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC notices that Beli doesn't seem to react with fear at the sight of the mi-go {@color [CLUE]|4d6381}.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC notices the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} fly past Beli to attack another giant. {@color [CLUE]|4d6381}

entries.name: Complication:
entries: 2 rounds into the battle, the Shapeshifter event (below) occurs.

entries.name: Option
entries: If the infesting creatures die too early, an additional 2 {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} can emerge from either {@creature Bralt|NorthlandsSagas} or {@creature Bremman|NorthlandsSagas} ({@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM}) at {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 20. This immediately kills the individual. No more than 5 {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} should be active at any time.

entries.name: Shapeshifter
entries: Just 2 rounds after the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} emerge, to further confuse matters, Beli shapechanges to take Glytta's, Katlaug's, or Sinmara's form. Beli chooses as his target whichever giant seems closest or most isolated.
Read or paraphrase the following, adding the target Beli chose in the [Target Name] place:
In the midst of the battle, a gasp echoes through the meeting hall. "By Aurgelmir's back teeth! What witchery is this?!?"
Across the room, [TARGET NAME] stands facing an exact duplicate of themselves!
One of the identical figures bellows, "A shapechanger! They must be the assassin! Kill them!" The one who spoke immediately attacks the duplicate.

Beli (shapechanged {@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thusir}), along with {@creature Bralt|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Bremman|NorthlandsSagas} ({@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics}), attacks the giant being impersonated. Maintaining he is the original, Beli claims the "duplicate" must be the assassin who killed Sigkva. The other giants don't attack either figure—they look to the PCs to sort out the truth.

entries.name: Guards Arrive
entries: 2 rounds after the Shapeshifter event began, 2 {@creature Cloud Giant|XMM|Cloud Giants} and 2 {@creature Lightning Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Lightning Giants} arrive:
With thundering footsteps, four giants storm up the stairs into the meeting hall. Two towering cloud giants draw their greatswords, and two lighting giants wreathe their hands in crackling energy.

The guards immediately attack the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} (if still alive) and order the duplicate giants (and {@creature Bralt|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Bremman|NorthlandsSagas}) to stop fighting. Once the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} are dead, they keep everyone from fighting but seem at a loss for what to do next.

With the fighting over, the individuals in the hall look around, confused and suspicious. Finally, Katlaug points at you and says, "Well? You've been investigating. Which one is real, and which is the assassin?"
All the giants look toward you.

entries.name: Chronology
entries: This last part of the adventure takes place in the meeting hall (Area 1). Let this brief timeline guide you through the complex set of events:

items: The PCs finish investigating Sigkva's chambers (and other fortress areas as desired).
{@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} emerge from Sigkva's body in the meeting hall and attack.
The giants panic, leaving the PCs to protect everyone.
2 rounds into the battle, Beli assumes the form of Glytta, {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas}, or Sinmara; he accuses the target of being the murderer.
When the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} die, giant guards from outside enter and stop the fighting.
The PCs must decide which figure is the real Glytta (or {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} or Sinmara), and which is the killer.

entries.name: Exposing Beli
entries: The fact that Beli took the form of the other giant reveals his guilt in the murder. However, discerning which giant is Beli is up to the characters. Due to the nature of the thursir's shapechanging gift, no one can discern his true form with spells lower than 6th level.
A few ways the PCs can expose Beli appear below; the information tagged with {@color [CLUE]|4d6381} throughout the adventure supports these actions and observations.

items: Smelling the suspects reveals that only one has a specific scent. Two of Beli's potential targets (Glytta and Sinmara) wear specific perfumes or balms; Beli does not.
Clues revealed Beli's allergy to radishes. If someone makes both suspects eat a radish—or rubs radish on their skin—Beli develops a painful rash within 1 minute.
Bring a dead {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} near the giants. The real target becomes {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, but Beli doesn't.
Beli didn't react with fear when the {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} appeared.
The {@creature Mi-Go|ToB1-2023|Primordial Mi-Go} avoided attacking Beli.

entries.name: Holmganga
entries: If the PCs expose Beli, he calls for a holmganga duel against them, using whatever form he currently occupies. Beli stays in combat until reduced to 48 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, at which point he shapechanges into an appropriate form and attempts to flee.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: In thanks for uncovering the killer, {@creature Katlaug|NorthlandsSagas} invites the party to Sigkva's funeral and provides the promised reward for attending the moot. The cloud giants redouble their efforts against the cult.
Depending on whom the carnage claimed, the PCs may gain allies or enemies after the moot abruptly ends.

entries.name: Fate of Beli Groundshaker
entries: If he survives and escapes, Beli plots against the party in revenge for thwarting his plans. He still takes time to sow discord among various giant clans to ensure they won't help fight the cult. Should the PCs capture Beli, he promises information about fire giant warlord and Blood Reckoning member {@creature Krusgr Ironcap|NorthlandsSagas} and the jotun cult leader, {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}, in exchange for his freedom. If he dies, the PCs learn slightly less about these two cult allies from missives Beli carries.

entries.name: Fate of Glytta Weggesdottir
entries: If she survives, she offers additional support to the party above and beyond what she intended during the moot. Should she die, the stone giants under her command decide to remain neutral in the conflict against the cult.

entries.name: Fate of Queen Sinmara
entries: If the queen dies, the cloud giants—and possibly the PCs—meet with her successor and manage to secure assistance from the jotuns.

entries.name: Further Adventures
entries: The characters leave the moot to rejoin the forces preparing to attack the Cult of Ragnarok's hidden fortress in Thursrike. They should have at least one {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before the attack begins. When next we see our heroes, they are aboard a longship about to make landfall on the contested shore near the fortress...
But that is a story told in {@adventure Attack on Birgkrona|NorthlandsSagas|9}, the next adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}.

data.name: Attack on Birgkrona
entries: {@i Attack on Birgkrona} is a second-tier adventure for a party of four to five 10th-level player characters, though you can adjust it to accommodate more or fewer players. The story—which requires stealth and canniness to infiltrate an enemy fortress—takes place in the Thursrike region of the Northlands, but feel free to transplant it into the location of your choice.

At the end of the adventure, the characters should reach 11th level. If this is the first adventure you're playing in the Sagas, refer to the {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0} for important backstory.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: Long ago, the fortress of Birgkrona was a minor outpost built by the jotuns during one of their fabled wars against the gods. Spared from destruction, the fortress sat abandoned for millennia before the Cult of Ragnarok rediscovered it. Under the command of {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}, the cult has restored the once-mighty Birgkrona from ruin, transforming it into a nearly impervious fortress at the edge of the known world. Here, an army of berserkers, giant allies, and other monsters guards the cult leaders as they guide scores of agents across the Northlands—all aiming to bring about Ragnarok.

But the cult does not stand unopposed. The realms of the Northlands have gathered their own armies to strike back and put an end to Cult of Ragnarok for good. After several hard-won battles, the allied forces finally located this hidden redoubt and even now move upon Birgkrona, the last remaining cultist stronghold.

entries.name: Sagas Connections
entries: {@i Attack at Birgkrona} is the ninth adventure in {@i Northlands Sagas}. For those following the campaign arc, after finishing this adventure, the PCs will proceed to {@adventure Storming the Den of Fenris|NorthlandsSagas|10}.
Many of the allies the PCs made in previous adventures gather to attack the cult's secret headquarters.

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: The adventure is divided between two parts: the siege and the infiltration.

entries.name: Part 1: Siege of Birgkrona
entries: When the characters arrive, their allies already battle the cultists and giants in front of the fortress. The adventure begins with the PCs thrown into battle, as they beach their longship and help to secure a beachhead for their newly arrived reinforcements. Afterward, the characters meet with the leaders of the allied forces to plan the siege, but an ambush by the Cult of Ragnarok interrupts them. Upon defeating the fell undead foes, the party discovers a hidden tunnel that offers a tantalizing route inside the fortress.

entries.name: Part 2: Infiltrating the Fortress
entries: The characters enter the secret tunnel and make their way through the giant crypts below the fortress, and from there to the Upper Keep of Birgkrona: lair of the Cult of Ragnarok's leaders. The layout of the Upper Keep may allow for cunning or courageous parties to take the cult by surprise and confront {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} and his minions.

entries.name: Factions and Key Players
entries: In this adventure, the party is supported by NPC allies from earlier Northlands Saga adventures and opposed by some familiar foes. Add the leaders who pledged their support in the previous adventure, {@adventure Murder at the Moot|NorthlandsSagas|8}.
If you are running this adventure as a standalone, feel free to use the details below or add your own NPCs with connections to the party.

entries.name: Allies

items.name: Azala Stormsinger{@sup †}:
entries: Cloud giant and ruler of Bjarmia, the flying city of cloud giants.

items.name: Finulf One-Hand:
entries: An impulsive human mercenary and leader of the Fangs of Vanagandr.

items.name: Gullveig{@sup †}:
entries: The god of magic and gold, a former prisoner of the cloud giants.

items.name: Kosktup Farleap:
entries: Daring and charming ratatosk merchant captain of {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}.

items.name: Jutta Valdisdottir:
entries: A young human viking attached to King Uffi's court as a page and messenger.

items.name: Master of Thyles:
entries: A bard and leader of Skaldholm.

items.name: Thulsamir Wolfbrother:
entries: Ruler of Wolfheim.

items.name: Uffi Toothless:
entries: King of Trollheim.
{@note {@sup †} May or may not be present, depending on the events of a previous Sagas adventure.}

items.name: Blood Reckoning:
entries: A faction of giants of Jotunheim led by {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}. They strive to destroy the gods of the North for killing the First Giant.

items.name: Cult of Ragnarok:
entries: A sect of a doomsayers and misanthropes who believe Ragnarok is coming. They seek to spread the word of it and work to bring it about.

items.name: Krusgr Ironcap:
entries: A fire giant warlord and member of the Blood Reckoning (off-stage).

items.name: Skymir Godkiller:
entries: A jotun and leader of the Blood Reckoning (off-stage).

items.name: Thyrin the Black:
entries: Leader of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin, a faction of the Cult of Ragnarok (off-stage).

items.name: Ylsa Ice-Eye:
entries: Bearfolk warrior and agent of the Cult of Ragnarok.

entries.name: Call to Action
entries: After the events of {@adventure Murder at the Moot|NorthlandsSagas|8}, the characters join the army gathered to finally take the fight to the Cult of Ragnarok. Stopping them here could mean the salvation of the world. Most of their allies are already attacking the fortress. Onboard the longship {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}, the PCs accompany the last vessels toward the landing point as the adventure begins.

entries.name: Alternate Adventure Hook
entries: If you are not running this as a part of the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, the characters join the expedition to root out a dangerous cult because they have lost loved ones or patrons to the machinations of the cultists.

entries.name: Running this as a StandAlone
entries: GMs running {@i Attack on Birgkrona} as standalone adventure, rather than as part of the {@i Northlands Sagas}, should make the following small alterations:

items: {@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas} becomes the mastermind and driving force behind the Cult of Ragnarok. From Birgkrona, she deploys her cultists on schemes across the realm. Replace all references to "{@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}" with "{@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas}."
The Strange Beam (see Part 2, Lower Courtyard) doesn't power a teleportation circle, it enhances Ylsa's powers.
Remove the line in the read-aloud-text for Thyrin's Hall (in Area 23) that begins "'Too late,' she says..."

entries.name: Part 1: Siege of Birgkrona
entries: {@i Beachhead. Screams and waves. Fortress in the distance.}

Waves crash against the longship's hull, and the roar of battle echoes through the mountainous fjord, growing louder with each pull of the oars. Ahead, a beach of black sand is lined with other longboats bearing the familiar shields and symbols of the allies standing against the Cult of Ragnarok. Those same allies now battle against raging cultist berserkers, trying to secure a foothold on the beach. Axes and blades clash with shields and helms, while arrows and spellfire flash over the battlefield.
In the distance, perched high in the mountains like a jagged crown, is Birgkrona: the mighty fortress of the Cult of Ragnarok. Today, if fate and the gods favor it, the cult will fall.
The longship grounds against the sand; time to leap into the icy shallows and charge ahead into battle!

As the characters disembark from {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}, a band of roaring warriors—some human and some trollkin—rushes toward them, axes and shields at the ready as they shout battle cries and oaths to Ragnarok. As soon as the party hits the beach, 4 {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers} and 2 {@creature Trollkin Reaver|ToB1-2023|Trollkin Reavers} attack the PCs. GMs can arrange this battle how they please. In general, the beach is wide, with four longboats lined up along the shore to the south of the characters. The berserkers and trollkin reavers approach from the northwest, beginning at 75 feet away.

entries.name: Cultist Complication
entries: While the berserkers attack the PCs, 3 {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultists} enter the battle from the northwest. Armed with torches, they try to set fire to the longships, dealing {@damage 1d4 + 1} Bludgeoning damage plus 1 Fire damage on a hit instead of their normal damage. Cultists prioritize attacking the ships over other enemies.

items: A longboat that takes 5 Fire damage or more catches fire. A burning longboat is destroyed if it burns for 1 minute.
A character can douse the flames on a longboat in two actions (or divide the work between multiple PCs).
If two or more longboats burn, the allied armies lose valuable supplies.
See the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13} for {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}'s stats.

entries: When the fight ends, Jutta, a young human {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook} approaches:

As the last foe falls, you take a moment to catch your breath. Farther up the beach, warriors beneath the banners of Trollheim and Wolfheim finish off the last of this wave of cultists and form up into units. Farther north, the sounds of battle mix with the familiar cadence of skald-song.
A young warrior wearing the heraldry of Trollheim runs up. "The kings ask to meet with you," she says breathlessly. "I'm to take you up to the camp!"
Assuming the PCs agree, Jutta leads them north to the Siege Camp and Command Tent.

entries.name: Siege Camp and Command Tent
entries: {@i Clanging iron. Distant horns. Smoke and blood.}

To the north, the battle lines stand opposite each other on a wide field south of the fortress: the cultists and their giant allies on one side, and on the other, the combined forces gathered by skald-song and the promise of glory. Banners of Trollheim and Wolfheim number the most, but others flutter in the chill winds as well. Even now, horns ring out as one clash ends. Warriors on both sides hurry to regroup behind makeshift barricades and shield walls.

South of the fighting, the siege camp is a sprawling, chaotic tangle of crude fortifications, smoky fires, and tents. The air hums with the clamor of iron, war horns, and skald songs. Smoke from cookfires and forge pits coils upward, mingling with the reek of sweat, blood, and pitch. Sharpened stakes encircle the camp. War banners flap in the wind—boar tusks, wolf-heads, and rune-marked ravens—each bearing the crest of a jarl, clan-chief, or warlord.
The largest tent commands the center of the camp, flanked by guard stations and another ring of sharpened stakes.
The characters follow Jutta (or make their own way) to the command tent. Its interior measures 60 feet by 30 feet, with openings on each short end. A 10-foot-by-10-foot table stands in the center.

entries.name: The Leaders
entries: Inside the tent, the leaders of the allied forces converse. These include the following individuals, but others may appear depending on how previous Sagas adventures went (also see Factions and Key Players).

items: {@creature Uffi Toothless|NorthlandsSagas|King Uffi Toothless} of Trollheim (human {@creature Jarl|NorthlandsWorldbook})
{@creature Master of Thyles|NorthlandsSagas text}, Leader of Skaldholm (human {@creature Skald|NorthlandsWorldbook})
{@creature Thulsamir Wolfbrother|NorthlandsSagas} of Wolfheim (dwarf {@creature Jarl|NorthlandsWorldbook})
{@creature Longtooth|NorthlandsSagas} ({@creature Winter Wolf|XMM}, Thulsamir's companion)

entries: After greeting the PCs warmly, the leaders discuss the current situation around the table, referring often to a crude map of the fortress (see handout). Read or paraphrase the following:

Uffi points to the geography around the fortress as marked on the map. "Our forces face an uphill battle, quite literally. Thanks to the giants, the cult has thus far kept us from carving out a foothold secure enough to bring our siege weapons to bear. Ideally, we need to push the cult back behind the walls of their fortress. Once we contain them, we can batter them to submission."

Now, the Master of Thyles speaks. "That will take time we may not have, Uffi. The mages and those with a touch of druidic magic report the weather is changing unnaturally. I fear the arcanists in the fortress are conducting an eldritch ritual to bring the breath of Boreas or a strong blizzard upon us. We don't have the supplies or appropriate shelter to weather such a storm here. If it comes, we'll have to retreat."

"Meanwhile," Jarl Thulsamir growls, "the cult's leaders—especially this 'Thyrin the Black'—will make their escape while we waste time battling their minions or the weather. We need to move swiftly and cut the head from the serpent. So, whatever we choose to do, we need to decide now."

From outside the tent comes the sound of alarm horns and the bellowing of giants. The camp is under attack! Suddenly, the ground explodes upward from beneath the tent, sending the table and those around it flying backward. Skeletal warriors climb out of the fifteen-foot-wide hole now occupying the center of the area.

entries.name: A Magical Rest
entries: Time is of the essence. If the characters stop to take a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} before venturing into the tunnel, the enemy will realize their assassination attempt has failed and either block the tunnel or collapse it completely.

If they need a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, {@creature Finulf One-Hand|NorthlandsSagas} (human {@creature Viking|NorthlandsWorldbook}) is called into the tent. He brings a glass vial containing a glowing blue liquid for each PC. He calls them "presents from the Wolf Barrow." This special concoction, known only to the Fangs of Vanagandr, gives the imbiber all the benefits of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, including healing and recovery of spell slots. Any vial not used here loses its potency in 1 minute. Finulf had only enough components to make these potions. (If Finulf died in the first adventure, {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas} takes his place here.)

A {@creature Runewright|NorthlandsWorldbook} named {@creature Hamruna|NorthlandsSagas} leads 12 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} in a surprise attack against the PCs and the allied leaders. They used magic to burrow beneath the tent from a mostly-forgotten tunnel attached to the fortress catacombs. The foes climb out of the hole in waves; if the PCs defeat the skeletons too quickly, or if you want a deadlier battle, add 1 {@creature Wight|XMM} to the first two rounds:

items.name: Round 1:
entries: 6 skeletons

items.name: Round 2:
entries: 6 skeletons

items.name: Round 3:
entries: {@creature Hamruna|NorthlandsSagas}

The allied leaders fight if they must, but most flee. In particular, Uffi and the {@creature Eirik Ellefsen|NorthlandsSagas|Master of Thyles} are a bit too old for this sort of thing; Thulsamir guards them as they retreat out of the tent.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: {@creature Hamruna|NorthlandsSagas} carries a {@item Lantern of Revealing|XDMG} and a {@item Spell Scroll|XDMG} of {@spell Fabricate|XPHB}. The runewright also had a strange rune painted on a scrap of parchment (see {@adventure Glamsyni Rune|NorthlandsSagas|9|Glamsyni Rune} sidebar). Jutta brings these items to the PCs if they don't discover them.

entries.name: Development
entries: After the undead foes are defeated, King Uffi and the other leaders return to the tent. The giants' attack has been halted, but the fighting continues—at a great cost of lives.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) or {@dc 15} Wisdom check:
entries: A PC deduces that the hole the skeletons made must connect to a tunnel beneath the fortress—the undead had to come from somewhere. The cultists may not anticipate an attack from this direction.

items: Alternatively, King Uffi can make this realization, if the GM prefers.

entries.name: New Mission
entries: The leaders of the allied forces ask the characters, while their armies keep the cultists busy, to use the tunnel to get to the fortress. There they can disrupt the weather-changing ritual and strike at the cult's leaders before they escape. The leaders say they can maintain the siege for at least four days—until the changing weather buries them in snow and ice.

entries.name: Glamsyni Rune
entries: The runewrights of Birgkrona have uncovered a forgotten rune called {@i glamsyni}. Its origin has been lost, but experiments have connected it to illusions, fog, and uncertainty. The runewrights have inscribed glamsyni in locations throughout Birgkrona to hide passageways and traps, as noted throughout the adventure. {@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas} wears a {@item Glamsyni Shield|NorthlandsSagas}, described under Thyrin's Hall (Area 23).

entries.name: Part 2: Infiltrating the Fortress
entries: The characters enter the hidden tunnel, traveling beneath the battlefield until they reach the crypts beneath the fortress. After dealing with any defenders, they move into Birgkrona proper. There, they can disrupt the ritual that summons the blizzard and overcome other complications. Finally they reach a former throne room to confront the leaders of the Cult of Ragnarok.

entries.name: The Ancient Crypt
entries: The crypts below Birgkrona have long served as the lair of a pair of runewrights: undead wizards obsessed with gathering power. Except where otherwise noted, the ancient crypts have the following features.

entries.name: Doors
entries: Doors are wood reinforced with iron and 5 feet wide, scaled for Medium creatures. Double doors (10 feet wide) suit the giants.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Unless otherwise noted, chambers have sconces that provide {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Walls, Floors, and Ceilings
entries: The crypt, scaled for giants, has 20-foot ceilings. Burial niches line the walls. The floor is slate.

entries.name: Area 1: Hamruna's Lair
entries: {@i Giants' crypt. Undead lair. Glamsyni rune.}

This ancient chamber is shrouded with cobwebs and dust, with long burial niches in the walls holding giant-sized bones. But someone has repurposed the place into a lair of sorts; they've scattered old books and scrolls haphazardly around the room. There is no visible bed, clothing, food, or drink—only bones, and the tools and collected lore of someone hunting for knowledge. Archways lead to two similarly adorned chambers.

This was the lair of {@creature Hamruna|NorthlandsSagas}, the runewright. Here, they researched the magic of runes and sought a way to steal the power of the Runestones from the gods. Their research has borne little fruit, much to their frustration. {@creature Hamruna|NorthlandsSagas} planned to kidnap a Runestone-bearing character for various experiments, as indicated in their notes.

entries.name: East Chamber
entries: The characters arrive here first after traveling through the hidden tunnel from the siege camp. Disorganized shelves and crates hold books and scrolls the runewright found of little interest.

entries.name: Central Chamber
entries: A worktable holds bones and rune carving tools. The wooden doors at the north end of this room stand closed but unlocked.

entries.name: West Chamber
entries: A table here holds Hamruna's notes, written in a mix of {@language Giant|XPHB} and {@language Common|XPHB}. They propose many complex (often unhinged) theories regarding rune magic. Displayed on the walls are repeated versions of a strange rune (see {@adventure Glamsyni Rune|NorthlandsSagas|9|Glamsyni Rune} sidebar), which the party saw on the parchment found after the battle with the undead.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check after 10 minutes reading the notes:
entries: A PC finds sections that reference the characters and the Runestones they carry.

items: These notes refer to the PCs as "individuals of interest," along with various half-formed plots to kidnap them. The notes also theorize about which rune each character may possess. Instead of referring to them by name, the notes refer to each character by one or two physical features or personality traits, like "the dwarf," "the furious one," or "the blundering human."
It also references "scouts" taken prisoner who had provided warning of the current attack from the "fools currently besieging Birgkrona." This is a reference to the prisoners in the cell (Area 3).

entries.name: North
entries: Into the crypt hallway (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 2: Crypt Hallway
entries: {@i Dark stone. Dust and webs. Giants' bones in wall niches.}
This corridor is made of dark stone and lined with enormous burial niches: a crypt for giants. The hallway extends to the east and west.
This area is unlit. Searching the burial niches reveals no treasure but plenty of places to hide.

entries.name: East
entries: To the branching corridor (Area 5).

entries.name: West
entries: To the cell (Area 3) and berserkers' lair (Area 4).

entries.name: Area 3: Cell
entries: {@i Crypt cell. Captured warriors. Warnings and clues.}

Someone has cleared this corner of the crypts of bones and sectioned it off with iron bars, turning the western chamber into a dismal cell. Beyond the bars, three dirty prisoners—all trollkin—stand shackled to the wall.

This area is unlit. Three Trollheim {@creature Warrior Veteran|XMM|Warrior Veterans} named {@creature Ogdan|NorthlandsSagas}, {@creature Bodil|NorthlandsSagas}, and {@creature Signa|NorthlandsSagas} are imprisoned behind iron bars. They were on a scouting mission for {@creature Uffi Toothless|NorthlandsSagas|King Uffi Toothless} when the giants attacked and sank their longboat near Birgkrona. Alone of the crew, these three managed to reach the shore, only to be captured by the Cult of Ragnarok.

The runewrights, {@creature Hamruna|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Vardi|NorthlandsSagas}, used magic to interrogate them and learned of the incoming armies, giving the fortress a day's warning of the siege. Ashamed of their defeat, the warriors long for freedom and a chance to redeem themselves on the battlefield.

entries.name: Speaking to the Prisoners
entries: In addition to the information above, they freely share the following:

items: They warn the characters that there are two undead mages. They used magic to interrogate them and asked them many questions about the coming siege, the leaders, and especially the PCs and the runes they carry. The two seemed more concerned with runes than the threat of a siege.

{@creature Bodil|NorthlandsSagas} mentions being blindfolded when captured, so they don't know the layout of the fortress. But she remembers hearing the gate opening and passing down a long stairway before being imprisoned here.

{@creature Ogdan|NorthlandsSagas} warns the PCs about the berserkers in a room to the west (Area 4)—they come occasionally to torment the captives. Their leader, a swordsman, offered them freedom several times, but it was only a cruel trick. The berserkers also complained about a giant named {@creature Hofgir|NorthlandsSagas} and threatened to feed them to the "giant's hound."
{@creature Signa|NorthlandsSagas} thinks the berserkers must be guarding something; she overheard a runewright executing a berserker for shirking their duties.

entries.name: Freeing the Captives
entries: {@creature Ljugar the Liar|NorthlandsSagas|Ljugar} the bandit lord (in Area 4) holds the key to the captives' manacles. If freed, they thank the party for the rescue. Tired and bruised, they each have 2 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} levels and half their maximum {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}.

If given weapons and armor (perhaps scavenged from the berserkers' lair), they offer to join the characters in battle or perform a task for them, such as guarding an area like the hidden path leading to Hamruna's lair (Area 1) or the gatehouse tower (Area 8). Though desperate to redeem their honor or die a warrior's death, they will deliver messages back to {@creature Uffi Toothless|NorthlandsSagas|King Uffi Toothless} if the PCs insist.

entries.name: South
entries: To the crypt hallway (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 4: Berserkers' Lair
entries: {@i Dirty barracks. Carousing berserkers. Treacherous captain. Secret passageway.}

This dirty, refuse-strewn barracks is lit by flickering torches exuding a smoky haze. Filthy beds line the walls, and supplies and trinkets lie scattered around. In the center of the room, a band of scarred and surly warriors sits on stools, drinking from horns and talking loudly of past conquests. The largest of them idly sharpens a longsword and raises an eyebrow as the door opens.

This is the barracks for a band of cult warriors assigned to defend the gatehouse tower (Area 8). The band finds guard duty boring and hates being constantly berated by {@creature Hofgir|NorthlandsSagas} the frost giant for their lack of valor. The band spends its time here instead, half-heartedly guarding the hidden passage to the Gatehouse.

entries.name: Ljugar the Liar and the Berserkers
entries: The berserkers are loudly sharing tales of bloody battle and dishonorable behavior when the characters arrive; those who listen at the door automatically hear the conversation. The berserkers follow Ljugar's orders.

entries.name: Holmganga?
entries: When the PCs arrive, Ljugar tries to speak with them, praising their cunning and courage for getting into the fortress. He then challenges the mightiest-looking character to {@variantrule Reputation|NorthlandsWorldbook|holmganga}, a formal duel (see {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 7: Running a Northlands Campaign|NorthlandsWorldbook|7}). He offers to lead them straight to {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} if they can defeat him.

items: If the PC agrees, Ljugar orders the berserkers to stand aside so the duel may commence.
Ljugar ({@creature Bandit Lord|ToB1-2023}) is lying, of course: As soon as he or his foe is {@variantrule Bloodied|XPHB}, all 4 {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers} attack.
Ljugar and the berserkers fight to the death.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Aside from their gear, the berserkers' spoils lie scattered around the room.

items: Jewelry, drinking horns, and weapons collected from around the room are worth a total of 250 GP.
Gear stolen from the captives in the cell (Area 3).

entries: Ljugar's bed and chest are in the northeast corner of the chamber, some distance from the rest.

items: The chest is locked ({@dc 18} to unlock or break) and trapped.

items.name: Trap:
entries: Poison needle, triggered by opening the chest; {@dc 15} to notice the trap or disable it. After triggering, the PC opening the chest must make a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw, taking 1 Piercing damage plus {@damage 3d8} Poison damage on a failure.

items: The chest contains a pouch with 178 GP, a {@item Potion of Cold Resistance|XDMG|Potion of Resistance (Cold)}, and a note written in {@language Giant|XPHB} that reads "Glamsyni's gaze shows the way."

entries.name: Hidden Passage
entries: A secret door is built into the wall in the northwest corner of this room. Behind the door, a ladder ascends to a narrow passage inside Birgkrona's southern wall. Following it leads to the trapdoor in the gatehouse tower (Area 8). Traversing the passage takes 1 minute.

items.name: {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC actively examining the area finds the door.

items: A character with {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB} 18 or higher spots the door automatically.

entries.name: East
entries: To the crypt hallway (Area 2).

entries.name: Up the Ladder
entries: To a closed trapdoor in the gatehouse tower (Area 8).

entries.name: Area 5: Branching Corridor
entries: {@i Rune in the floor. Crypt doors. Illusion hides a secret passageway.}
This area is unlit. The two doors leading into Vardi's lair (Area 7) are unlocked.

entries.name: Hidden Passage
entries: A door located where the corridor branches has been hidden by an illusion spell.

items: PCs with {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB} 20 or higher notice a glamsyni rune incorporated into the stonework of the floor in this corridor.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns that the rune maintains a permanent {@spell Silent Image|XPHB} spell on the east wall, which otherwise looks like a normal part of the crypt. Any physical interaction with the wall reveals it as an illusion. A {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} spell ends the effect.

entries.name: Northeast Door
entries: To Vardi's lair (Area 7).

entries.name: East Door
entries: To the hidden staircase (Area 6).

entries.name: Southeast Door
entries: To Vardi's lair (Area 7).

entries.name: West
entries: To the crypt hallway (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 6: Hidden Stairs
entries: {@i Secret passage up to the fortress.}

Behind the illusion in the branching corridor (Area 5) lies a narrow spiral staircase, which ascends to the secret door in the dragon tower hallway (Area 10) in the Upper Keep. Traversing the staircase takes 1 minute.

entries.name: West
entries: To the branching corridor (Area 5).

entries.name: Up the Stairs
entries: To the dragon tower hallway (Area 10).

entries.name: Area 7: Vardi's Lair
entries: {@i Undead wizard's lair. Shelves and books, tables and tools. Giant sarcophagus full of bones.}

This chamber of the crypt arcs around in a horseshoe shape. It's full of arcane materials. Bookshelves line some walls, holding worn tomes and scrolls, and several cluttered tables hold bits of bones and tools for carving runes. Against the northeast wall, a giant-sized sarcophagus has been opened and filled to the brim with the bones of dead giants.

This area is unlit. {@creature Vardi|NorthlandsSagas} ({@creature Runewright|NorthlandsWorldbook}) researches the secrets of runes here. The cultists have been warned to leave {@creature Vardi|NorthlandsSagas} alone, so the runewright responds to any intrusion with violence.
Upon hearing combat or a door opening, {@creature Vardi|NorthlandsSagas} drinks a {@item Potion of Invisibility|XDMG} before investigating.

entries.name: Sarcophagus
entries: The sarcophagus has been imbued with necromantic power, allowing it to animate giant skeletons—but only when the lid is open.

In combat, {@creature Vardi|NorthlandsSagas} can use a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to animate a giant skeleton (use the {@creature Minotaur Skeleton|XMM} stat block without the Charge trait or Gore attack). These skeletons follow Vardi's commands and attack until destroyed. The sarcophagus has enough bones to create 4 giant skeletons in this manner.

The sarcophagus is a Huge object with AC 17, HP 40, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunity} to Poison and Psychic damage. Destroying or closing the sarcophagus prevents {@creature Vardi|NorthlandsSagas} from using it.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns that the sarcophagus only functions with the lid open.

items.name: {@dc 20} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC closes the lid of the sarcophagus.

entries.name: West
entries: To the branching corridor (Area 5).

entries.name: Upper Keep and Gatehouse Tower
entries: The Upper Keep is the northeastern part of the fortress. A long section of wall, marked Area 9, runs from the dragon tower (Areas 10 to 14) to the gatehouse tower (Area 8). PCs typically arrive in this area via the ladder from the berserkers' lair (Area 4) or by the secret staircase in the crypts (Area 6).
Except where otherwise noted, the Upper Keep and Gatehouse have the following features.

entries.name: Doors
entries: Doors are wood reinforced with iron and either 10 feet wide (scaled for giants) or 5 feet wide (scaled for Medium creatures).

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Unless otherwise noted, chambers have sconces that provide {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Walls, Floors, and Ceilings
entries: The fortress, scaled for giants, has 20-foot ceilings. Walls are thick stone block, and floors are worked stone.

entries.name: Area 8: The Gatehouse Tower
entries: {@i Barricaded tower. Rickety scaffolding. Disabled gate.}

A sturdy winch occupies the center of this tower, but the heavy chains it controls have been disconnected from it. The air hangs heavy with the stench of beast and giant, and the room is cluttered with supplies and detritus. The towering door to the east is easily fifteen feet wide. Much of the tower has been reinforced with supports and scaffolding.

The gatehouse holds the mechanisms that open and close Birgkrona's main gate, critically important to the fortress's defense. The defenders have barricaded the gatehouse tower shut, sealing three of their number inside as guards. These forces—{@creature Hofgir|NorthlandsSagas} ({@creature Frost Giant|XMM}) plus {@creature Gravemaw|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Cuddles|NorthlandsSagas} ({@creature Garmr|NorthlandsWorldbook})—have orders to attack any intruders they see, but not to leave this chamber.
When the PCs arrive, roll {@dice 1d6} on the table below.

entries.name: View from the Tower
entries: Characters who look out the arrow slits in the north wall can see across the fortress to Areas 16 to 20.

entries.name: Barred Doors
entries: These giant-sized doors are closed and barred from the outside.

items: The double doors are a Huge object with AC 16, HP 60, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunity} to Poison and Psychic damage.

items.name: {@dc 25} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC forces the doors open.

entries.name: Scaffolding
entries: Wooden scaffolding runs along the northeast wall of the tower, 15 feet above the ground. The courtyard below is beyond the scope of this adventure but likely contains giants, cultists, and other foes.

items: Medium creatures can squeeze through an arrow slit on the tower's north wall without an ability check.

items.name: {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC with a running start makes a {@variantrule Long Jump|XPHB} from the scaffolding outside the tower to the fortress wall (Area 9). On a failure, a character must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, catching the edge of the wall on a success but taking 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Slashing damage from the broken stones on the wall's edge.

entries.name: Trapdoor
entries: A heavy iron trapdoor on the western end of the room leads down to the secret passage in the berserkers' lair (Area 4).

items.name: {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC opens the trapdoor.

items.name: {@dc 17} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC opening the door does so quietly. {@actSaveFail} A garmr hears the door opening.

entries.name: Gate Mechanism
entries: A giant-sized winch built into the gatehouse can open or close Birgkrona's main gate. {@creature Hofgir|NorthlandsSagas} has disabled the mechanism, which must be repaired in order to function. If it's repaired, and the barricade removed, a creature can take a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to pull the mechanism's lever to raise or lower the gate.

items: Two creatures with a combined Strength of 35 can open or close the gate manually by pulling the chains connected to it.

items.name: {@dc 18} Dexterity ({@item Smith's Tools|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@item Tinker's Tools|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC repairs the gate in 30 minutes.

items: {@creature Blodhamar|NorthlandsSagas} from the thursir's forge (Area 18) can repair the mechanism in 10 minutes.

entries.name: Opening the Gate
entries: Opening the gate causes the cult army outside the fortress to withdraw into the keep and has the following additional effects:

items: As long as the main gate stays open, the allied armies can move in to attack the cult's army directly in the lower areas of the keep.
The Cult of Ragnarok cannot send reinforcements to the Upper Keep with the main gate open.
Opening the main gate has consequences in some locations throughout the Upper Keep, noted in those sections.

entries.name: East
entries: To the fortress wall (Area 9).

entries.name: Down through Trapdoor
entries: To the berserkers' lair (Area 4).

entries.name: Area 9: Fortress Wall
entries: {@i Long, high wall.}

The fortress's outer wall is topped by a walkway broad enough for a giant to patrol, with the outer face protected by broad crenellations. On either side, the wall drops sixty feet or more to the ground below.
This section of wall connects the gatehouse tower (Area 8) with the dragon's tower hallway (Area 10). A set of giant-sized double doors stands closed at the far end of the wall walk.

items: If the characters opened the main gate, this area is unpatrolled. Otherwise, 3 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} patrol the wall.

items.name: {@dc 10} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC can move along wall and stay out of sight from the rest of the fortress.

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Through the doors to the dragon tower hallway (Area 10).

entries.name: West
entries: To the gatehouse tower (Area 8).

entries.name: Area 10: Dragon Tower Hallway
entries: {@i Ancient tower. Cult decor. Damaged section.}

Heavy wooden doors sized for giants lead into an equally large corridor, which curves with the tower's outer wall. Tapestries and engravings in the stonework display the ancient wars of giantkind and imagery of the Cult of Ragnarok.
The hallway has 30-foot ceilings and is not patrolled, though combat here may alert enemies in the cultists' chamber (Area 11) or Tetra's chamber (Area 12).

entries.name: Damaged Wall
entries: Siege weaponry has damaged the southern portion of this tower, collapsing a part of the outer wall on this level.

items.name: {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC climbs over rubble to reach Tetra's chamber (Area 12).

items: If the check fails by 5 or more, the character must make a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw, falling 150 feet to the sea below on a failure.

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: One tapestry hides a secret door leading to a hidden staircase to the crypts (Area 6). The door is unlocked.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC spots the hidden door.

entries.name: North
entries: To the stairwell (Area 13).

entries.name: Northeast
entries: To the northeastern wall (Area 16).

entries.name: South
entries: To the cultists' chamber (Area 11).

entries.name: Southwest
entries: To the fortress wall (Area 9).

entries.name: Area 11: Cultists' Chamber
entries: {@i Cultist living quarters. Cult symbols.}
This room holds a handful of beds and simple furnishings. The walls are scrawled with bone-white symbols of wind, winter, and ruin.

{@creature Elhild|NorthlandsSagas} resides here with the eight cultists under her command. They take turns maintaining the ritual on the Runestone (Area 20), so when the characters enter, only half of them are here off duty. The cultists answer to a mage named {@creature Tetra|NorthlandsSagas} (Area 12). The nonmagical symbols on the walls praise Ragnarok with grim propaganda.

If they encounter the PCs here, {@creature Elhild|NorthlandsSagas} (a {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM}) and 3 {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultists} do their best to hold them off while a fourth {@creature Cultist|XMM} runs to alert {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas}. If {@creature Tetra|NorthlandsSagas} (Area 12) hears combat, he enters in the second round.

entries.name: Disguises
entries: Using spare cultist clothing, up to four creatures can spend 10 minutes here disguising themselves as members of the Cult of Ragnarok.

items: Disguised characters have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@skill Deception|XPHB} checks when interacting with berserkers, cultists, and giants in the fortress.

They also have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Charisma-based checks when interacting with the prisoners in the crypt's cell (Area 3) or {@creature Blodhamar|NorthlandsSagas} in the forge (Area 18).
{@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}, {@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas}, and other cult officers recognize imposters on sight.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The cultists have meager possessions: coins totaling 37 GP, 3 {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing}, and a {@item Potion of Poison|XDMG}.

entries.name: North
entries: To the dragon tower hallway (Area 10).

entries.name: Southwest
entries: Through a doorway to Tetra's chamber (Area 12).

entries.name: Area 12: Tetra's Chamber
entries: {@i Wind wizard. Trapped fey.}
Cold wind blows through the broken corner of this room, rustling the furnishings. Next to the bed is a desk, atop which sits a large clay urn.

A human arcanist named {@creature Tetra|NorthlandsSagas} traveled from a distant southern land to join the Cult of Ragnarok, drawn by cruel whispers that came to him on the wind. He specializes in wind magic and remains utterly devoted to the cult's cause.

On his first turn, {@creature Tetra|NorthlandsSagas} (a {@creature Mage|XMM}) uses an action to break the urn on the table and free a {@creature Swarm of Sluaghs|ToB1-2023}, which attacks any creatures other than {@creature Tetra|NorthlandsSagas}.
{@creature Tetra|NorthlandsSagas} has the following spells available to cast instead of the mage's normal spells:

items: {@b At Will:} {@spell Elementalism|XPHB}, {@spell Fog Cloud|XPHB}, {@spell Mage Armor|XPHB}
{@b 2/Day Each:} {@spell Lightning Bolt|XPHB} (level 4 version), {@spell Invisibility|XPHB}
{@b 1/Day Each:} {@spell Arcane Hand|XPHB}, {@spell Gaseous Form|XPHB}

entries.name: Clay Urn
entries: {@creature Tetra|NorthlandsSagas} keeps a swarm of sluaghs trapped in the clay urn on his desk.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Nature|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC examining the urn discerns it is imbued with magic to imprison creatures that feed on warmth.

items: The jar is a Small object with AC 13 and HP 5; it weighs 10 pounds. An adjacent creature can take the {@action Utilize|XPHB} action to break the jar automatically.

entries.name: Damaged Wall
entries: Siege weaponry has damaged the southern portion of this tower, collapsing a part of the outer wall on this level.

items.name: {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC climbs over rubble to reach the dragon tower hallway (Area 10).

items: If the check fails by 5 or more, the character must make a {@dc 10} Dexterity saving throw, falling 150 feet to the sea below on a failure.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: In the desk is a {@item Wind Fan|XDMG}.

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Through a doorway to the cultists' chamber (Area 11).

entries.name: South
entries: Through the damaged wall to the dragon tower hallway (Area 10).

entries.name: Area 13: Stairwell
entries: {@i Stone staircase. Two choices of direction.}
Stone stairs spiral upward and downward from this landing.
PCs can ascend the stairs to arrive at the roost atop the tower (Area 14) or descend them to the courtyard (Area 15). It takes 30 feet of movement to ascend or descend.

entries.name: South
entries: To the dragon tower hallway (Area 10).

entries.name: Down
entries: To the courtyard stairs (Area 15).

entries.name: Up
entries: To Odri'vetr's roost (Area 14).

entries.name: Area 14: Odri'vetr's Roost
entries: {@i Crumbling tower platform. Grumbling dragon. Balcony lair.}

The stairs ascend to a platform near the top of the tower. This area once encompassed the southeastern half of the tower's width, but damage has collapsed the southernmost portion. The remaining platform is littered with frozen remnants of reindeer carcasses and humanoid bones. Against the wall stands a giant-sized metal urn coated with a thick layer of ice, with only the metal handles protruding. The wind here feels bitingly cold and carries a mix of beastly odors and chemical sharpness.

Coiled in a pile of snow and ice near the edge of the platform is a white dragon the length of a longboat. It cracks open an eye and growls, "Have you brought my tribute? Not a disappointing one this time, I hope. For your sake."
This is the lair of the {@creature Young White Dragon|XMM} {@creature Odri'vetr|NorthlandsSagas}. He considers his time with the cult very unrewarding so far.

items: If {@creature Odri'vetr|NorthlandsSagas} notices the PCs, the dragon assumes they've come from the cult to deliver an offering.
If they express any willingness to talk, the dragon interrogates them, considering how he might benefit from their arrival.

items.name: {@dc 13} Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check after speaking to the dragon for a bit:
entries: A PC realizes the dragon is curious and shows little loyalty to the Cult of Ragnarok.

entries.name: Talking to Odri'vetr
entries: See the Odri'vetr sidebar.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The dragon keeps his treasure safe in a giant urn full of frozen seawater. It weighs 500 pounds and takes a day to thaw if left unattended. It contains 2,900 GP and 6,100 SP, a {@item Circlet of Blasting|XDMG}, and a {@item Decanter of Endless Water|XDMG}.

entries.name: Odri'vetr (Young White Dragon)
entries: {@i Discontented dragon with territorial ambitions.}
{@b Background:} Was lured to the Cult of Ragnarok's service by promises of treasure, territory, and prey.
{@b Personality Traits:} Direct, greedy, "predator-or-prey" mentality.
{@b Bonds:} Avoids or submits to any creature bigger than himself.
{@b Flaws:} Thinks very literally; often forgets other creatures may lie.
{@b Wants:} Territory all to himself, with no cult and no giants to compete with.
{@b Talking to Odri'vetr:} If the PCs speak to the allied armies and guarantee Odri'vetr rulership of Birgkrona, the dragon agrees to stop fighting on behalf of the cult.

items.name: {@dc 18} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC convinces Odri'vetr to abandon Birgkrona, at which point the dragon grabs its treasure urn and flies into the wilds to the north. The PCs can gain a +5 bonus on the check by offering a {@filter Rare magic item|items|rarity=rare} or treasure worth at least 1,000 GP as "tribute."

items.name: {@dc 20} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB} or {@skill Intimidation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC makes a separate check to convince Odri'vetr to assist in one battle in the Upper Keep. All the PCs need do is call out his name, and he will arrive to help.

entries.name: North
entries: To the stairwell (Area 13).

entries.name: Southwest
entries: Down through the damaged wall to Tetra's chamber (Area 12); requires a {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) or Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check, made with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} if the character uses a rope.

entries.name: Area 15: Courtyard Stairs
entries: Characters who descend the stairwell (Area 13) arrive at the base of the stairs in the southeastern corner of the courtyard.
The first time the PCs enter the Lower Courtyard locations (Areas 17 to 21), be prepared to read the description from the {@adventure Strange Beam|NorthlandsSagas|9|Strange Beam} section.

entries.name: Up
entries: To the stairwell (Area 13).

entries.name: Forward
entries: To lower courtyard locations (Areas 17–21).

entries.name: Area 16: Northeastern Wall
entries: {@i Bored hill giants. Long drop to the water below.}

Three hill giants wearing unkempt furs lean against the outer wall, staring emptily into the distance. Open crates of stinking food sit next to each giant; one of them takes a handful of food and shoves it sloppily into their mouth.

A trio of hill giants—named {@creature Kruug|NorthlandsSagas}, {@creature Crall|NorthlandsSagas}, and {@creature Bort|NorthlandsSagas}—guard this section of the wall. As the siege takes place mostly on the other side of the fortress, they have seen very little action and have grown bored and inattentive. They stand near the middle of the wall, roughly 60 feet apart.
From the wall it is a 30-foot drop to the courtyard and 150 feet down to the sea.

Unless alerted to trouble nearby, the 3 {@creature Hill Giant|XMM|Hill Giants} have the {@condition Surprised|XPHB} condition against any sudden attack from the Upper Keep. The giants have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on their {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB} scores (giving them {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB} 7).
The crates hold moldering food scraps too foul for the rest of the cult to eat. The giants use it as snacks and as ammunition for their Trash Lob attacks.

If the characters have not convinced {@creature Odri'vetr|NorthlandsSagas}, the dragon from Area 14, to leave, roll {@dice 1d6} at the end of each round of combat; on an odd number, the {@creature Odri'vetr|XMM|Young White Dragon} notices the combat and joins in.

entries.name: Crates
entries: Additional crates of refuse are piled here, behind which characters may hide or take {@variantrule Cover|XPHB}.

entries.name: Stairs
entries: Stairs on the northwest side of the wall descend 30 feet to the courtyard below. As a reminder, the first time the characters enter the Lower Courtyard, read the description from the {@adventure Strange Beam|NorthlandsSagas|9|Strange Beam} sidebar.

entries.name: Northwest
entries: Stairs down to the Lower Courtyard (Areas 17–21).

entries.name: Southwest
entries: To the dragon tower hallway (Area 10).

entries.name: Lower Courtyard
entries: The Lower Courtyard lies below the Upper Keep in the northeastern part of the fortress. PCs typically arrive via the courtyard stairs (Area 15) or by the stairs from the northeastern wall (Area 16).
Except where otherwise noted, the Lower Courtyard has the following features.

entries.name: Doors
entries: Doors are wood reinforced with iron and 5 feet wide (scaled for Medium creatures). They are unlocked.

entries.name: Floors
entries: Bare stone, smoothed by weather and age, covered by a layer of earth.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Unless otherwise noted, torches, lamps, and lanterns provide {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for courtyard locations at night.

entries.name: Strange Beam
entries: When the characters enter the Lower Courtyard for the first time, read or paraphrase the following:

At the center of this wide, windswept courtyard, the chanting voices rise in pitch and fervor. A number of swaying cultists kneeling around a runic standing stone throw their heads back as a crimson beam of eldritch light lances up from the stone. The beam arcs toward the tall tower in the northwest of the keep, striking a circle of runes etched onto the exterior wall. Immediately, a golden light begins emanating from the arrow slits of the tower.

Unbeknownst to the characters, {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} and the other cult leaders in the tower (Area 23) have just activated a teleportation circle to transport them to the Den of Fenris. The cultists in the courtyard carry on chanting after the light appears.

entries.name: Area 17: Berserkers' Barracks
entries: {@i Crude log building, built from wrecked ships.}
This wooden building looks to be crudely assembled from the wreckage of longboats. It now serves as a leaky barracks. A central fire provides not enough warmth.
The fire in this area provides {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for the barracks.

In this barracks, 3 {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers} work at repairing gear. They ignore sounds of combat on the walls (such as Area 16) but notice combat within the courtyard; they enter courtyard combat in the next round.

entries.name: East
entries: To the rest of the Lower Courtyard (Areas 18–21).

entries.name: Area 18: Thursir's Forge
entries: {@i Enslaved giant. Huge forge. Grumbling.}
Chained to a huge anvil is a giant with a soot-singed beard and a deep scowl of displeasure. He hammers the dents out of a shield, which looks like a child's toy in his massive hands.

A {@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thursir} named {@creature Blodhamar|NorthlandsSagas} has been forced to serve as the cult's smith. Sensing the group's impending fall, {@creature Blodhamar|NorthlandsSagas} will betray the cult in exchange for survival. He is working when the PCs arrive; initially he yells at them to wait their turn for repairs, but soon realizes they are not cultists.
The open side of this forge faces southwest. It provides {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in this area of the courtyard.

entries.name: Blodhamar (Thursir Blacksmith)
entries: {@i Disgruntled giant thinking about his future.}
{@b Background:} Former smith to thursir jarl Ulli Wotanson at the Kjothall fortress in Thursrike.
{@b Personality Traits:} Mutters curses in {@language Giant|XPHB} with every swing of the hammer.
{@b Bonds:} His tools and his craft.
{@b Flaws:} Few things smaller than him seem worth his attention.
{@b Wants:} Blodhamar does not care to die in service to the cult. He fights only in self-defense.
{@b Talking to Blodhamar:} He can tell the PCs that {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} and the other leaders are in the northwestern tower (Area 23).

items: In exchange for amnesty, Blodhamar agrees to repair the gate mechanism in the gatehouse tower (Area 8), should the PCs succeed on a {@dc 14} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check.
Blodhamar refuses to fight any of the cult's defenders and expects the PCs to protect him in exchange for his service.
Blodhamar can break his chains with an action.

entries.name: Southwest
entries: To the rest of the Lower Courtyard (Areas 17, 19–21).

entries.name: Area 19: Skull-Splitter's Tent
entries: {@i Old mead. Musty canvas. Deadly berserker's tent.}
A canvas tent stands near the wall. Strands of grim trophies hang along the tent's walls: skulls, broken weapons, shattered shields, all of different origins.

This tent belongs to a {@creature Trollkin Berserker|NorthlandsWorldbook} named {@creature Skull-Splitter|NorthlandsSagas}. During the day, she spends 50 percent of her time here; at night she sleeps here. She investigates if she hears combat in the courtyard.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Skull-Splitter's tent holds a trove of weapons taken from fallen foes, including a {@item Dagger of Venom|XDMG} called Spite.

entries.name: West
entries: To the rest of the Lower Courtyard (Areas 17–18, 20–21).

entries.name: Area 20: Ancient Runestone
entries: {@i Chanting voices. Swirling wind. Glowing Runestone.}

Fingers of chill wind swirl around a standing stone that rises to a height of thirty feet. Engraved with forgotten sigils and unfamiliar runes, it looks even older than the ancient fortress around it.
Oblivious to their surroundings, four cultists kneel around the stone, chanting and swaying with frost clinging to their robes.

The Cult of Ragnarok has managed to reawaken ancient magic within this Runestone, which they can use to influence the weather in a 3-mile radius. Every morning, eight cultists and a cultist fanatic named {@creature Elhild|NorthlandsSagas} perform an hourlong ritual to cause the weather to grow colder and windier. The cultists work in shifts to maintain the ritual from morning to dusk; 4 {@creature Cultist|XMM|Cultists} are here now. (See the cultists' chamber, Area 11, for other information on them.)

entries.name: Weather Ritual
entries: Unless someone disrupts these cultists, the weather grows worse each day until a massive blizzard strikes. If three or more of the cultists fall, the ritual fails, and the weather returns to normal over the next hour.

entries.name: All Directions
entries: To the rest of the Lower Courtyard (Areas 17–19, 21).

entries.name: Area 21: Stairs To Lower Fortress
entries: Giant-sized stairs descend to the Lower Fortress, which is outside the scope of this adventure.

entries.name: Upper Fortress Locations
entries: Except where otherwise noted, the Upper Fortress has the following features.

entries.name: Lighting
entries: Unless otherwise noted, chambers have sconces that provide {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Walls, Floors, and Ceilings
entries: The fortress, scaled for giants, has 20-foot ceilings. Walls are thick stone block. Rugs cover a portion of the tiled floors.

entries.name: Area 22: Tower Entryway
entries: {@i Ancient hall. Grim cult decor. Hidden foes.}
At the base of this tower, a once-grand hall now holds the bleak symbols and relics of the Cult of Ragnarok. The hallway turns north past a pair of wolf statues into the tower proper.
Around that corner, a golden radiance suddenly becomes almost blinding, then just as abruptly is extinguished. Then the sound of hammering and splintering stone echoes from up ahead.
A glamsyni rune engraved in the floor near the stairs creates an illusion over two small alcoves on either side of the hallway, hiding a berserker in each.

entries.name: Hidden Alcoves
entries: Characters with {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB} 20 or higher notice the glamsyni rune as they approach; others who actively search those wall sections can attempt a {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check to spot it. Anyone who previously noticed glamsyni in the crypt's branching corridor (Area 5) gains {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this check. The 2 {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers} hidden here wait for sounds of combat from Thyrin's Hall (Area 23), then leave their alcoves and attack.

entries.name: Golden Light
entries: The shine and extinguishing of the golden light marks the successful activation of the teleportation circle in Thyrin's Hall (Area 23).

entries.name: Wolf Statues
entries: These unremarkable statues transform into {@creature Wolf|XMM|Wolves} when Ylsa in Thyrin's Hall (Area 23) commands them to do so.

entries.name: East
entries: Down the steps to the Lower Courtyard (Areas 17–21).

entries.name: North
entries: To Thyrin's Hall (Area 23).

entries.name: Area 23: Thyrin's Hall
entries: {@i Shattered throne and back wall. Cult shrine. Discharged teleportation circle.}

The sound of breaking stone and rhythmic hammering echoes in this once-grand chamber. Cold air flows in through a gaping hole, where long ago something shattered the northern wall and broke a giant-sized stone throne into pieces.

A ways from the ruined throne, bathed in light from candles atop a bloody sacrificial shrine in the center of the room, a powerful-looking bearfolk warrior with white fur slams a maul down on a silver and stone circle set into the floor. This last blow shatters the circle, scattering pieces across the floor. She drops the maul, and from her belt pulls an axe that shimmers with an arctic radiance.
"Too late," she says. "They are gone to wake the Wolf. Ragnarok Kemir! Ragnarok comes! But you won't live long enough to see it."

{@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} commanded the Cult of Ragnarok from this chamber, coordinating Birgkrona's defense and the cult army's movements. He has tasked one of his chiefs, {@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas}, to destroy the teleportation circle that Thyrin, {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}, and {@creature Krusgr Ironcap|NorthlandsSagas} recently used. While her leaders head to the Den of Fenris to free the dread wolf, Ylsa is ready to lay down her life to delay the characters.

entries.name: Command Phrase
entries: The words "Ragnarok Kemir" alerted the berserkers in the tower entryway (Area 22) and transformed the statues there into real wolves.

{@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas} first converses with the PCs, pretending to consider surrender or negotiation, stalling long enough for the 2 {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers} and 2 {@creature Wolf|XMM|Wolves} to arrive from the tower entryway.

items: When she gains an advantage, she attacks. {@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas} fights to the death.
In battle, she taunts the PCs for falling for the deception and for allowing the cult's leaders to escape. "While we fight, my master Thyrin goes to awaken Fenris."

entries.name: Shrine
entries: This small altar holds flickering candles and bloody sacrifices given in service to the Cult of Ragnarok.

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC finds a scrap of partially burned parchment.

items: The parchment reads: "...reports the Great Wolf slumbers in a site in the northeast of Vargrike, 85 miles or so from the Moon Palace. The circle shall bring us to..."

entries.name: Ruined Teleportation Circle
entries: This shattered ring of rune-etched stone and silver was once a masterwork of arcane invention.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC identifies the ruined device as a teleportation circle keyed to a specific destination. If it were whole, they could use it to follow {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} and the other cult leaders. However, repairing it requires special knowledge of giant magic or divine intervention.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence check:
entries: A PC realizes that their ally Azala (or Gullveig, depending on which of them is present in the siege camp) may be able to repair the teleportation circle.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Aside from her gear, Ylsa has a {@item Glamsyni Shield|NorthlandsSagas}.
On the shrine, the characters can find these items:

items: Bowl of small black sapphires and purple spinel prisms (worth a total of 5,000 GP).
One of the prisms is an {@item Ioun Stone, Reserve|XDMG|Ioun Stone (Reserve)}.
1 {@item Potion of Necrotic Resistance|XDMG}.
1 vial of {@item Keoghtom's Ointment|XDMG}.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: Once Ylsa falls, the characters can turn their attention to defeating the remaining cult defenders. If they haven't yet raised the main gate (Area 8), that should be their next objective. As soon as the gate opens and Ylsa is dead, the fortress falls to the characters and their allies.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: The PCs' actions in this adventure count as a deed for each of them (see the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 7: Running a Northlands Campaign|NorthlandsWorldbook|7}), and skalds certainly will sing of them for generations. In addition, {@creature Uffi Toothless|NorthlandsSagas|King Uffi Toothless} offers each character a reward of their choice:

items: Rank as a minor Thane and the rulership of a small steading on the borders of Trollheim.
2,000 Gold Pieces.
A {@filter Rare magic item|items|rarity=rare} of their choice (with GM's approval).

entries.name: If They Defeat the Cult
entries: The PCs now must pursue {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} and the other cult leaders, who even now work to awaken Fenris. From the information found in Thyrin's Hall, the Den of Fenris is located in Vargrike, far to the east. The quickest method of getting there involves repairing the magical teleportation circle. Either {@creature Azala Stormsinger|NorthlandsSagas} or Gullveig can repair the item in 8 hours (giving the party a chance to rest).

If you are playing this as a standalone adventure, it ends with the defeat of {@creature Ylsa Ice-Eye|NorthlandsSagas}. The Cult of Ragnarok is shattered, and any remaining forces are either captured or flee into the wilderness.

entries.name: If the Cult Prevails
entries: If the party falls in battle, the Cult of Ragnarok is victorious. {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} and the cult awaken Fenris, and new heroes are needed to avert Ragnarok.

entries.name: Further Adventures
entries: The characters can regroup and get a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, but the threat of Thyrin the Black's plan looms large. Azala's (or Gullveig's) aid in restoring the teleportation circle means the characters can follow the cultists to Vargrike—at least 8 hours behind them...
But that is a story told in {@adventure Storming the Den of Fenris|NorthlandsSagas|10}, the next adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}.

data.name: Storming the Den of Fenris
entries: {@i Storming the Den of Fenris} is a third-tier adventure for a party of four to five 11th-level player characters, though you can adjust it to accommodate more or fewer players. The story—a Viking-style dungeon crawl with an unexpected twist—takes place in the Vargrike region of the Northlands, but feel free to transplant it into the location of your choice.

At the end of the adventure, the characters should reach 12th level. If this is the first adventure you're playing in the Sagas, refer to the {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0} for important backstory.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: Ages ago, the god Loki fell into a relationship with Angrboda, a god of the giants. Though their love was not immortal, some of their children are well known, including {@deity Hel|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}, goddess of death; Jormungandr, the World Serpent; and Fenris, the Great Wolf. Each of them was foretold to have a prominent role in Ragnarok. Filled with fear, the gods cast Jormungandr into the sea, where it encircled the world, and relegated Hel to the underworld. Fenris was reared in Asgard, so they could keep their eyes on him, but he grew so large and powerful that eventually they decided to bind and imprison the wolf.

Tricking Fenris into believing they were testing his strength, they attempted to chain him, but he broke every fetter. Finally, the gods created a magical chain called Gleipnir to hold him. However, when they tried to place it upon him, canny Fenris suspected trickery. He said he would agree to be bound by Gleipnir only if one of the gods placed their hand in his mouth. Only {@deity Tyr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook} was brave enough to do so. When Fenris realized he could not break the magical chain, he furiously bit off Tyr's hand before Gleipnir forced him into a sleep from which he could not awake. The gods imprisoned the chained wolf in a remote and isolated place, where they hoped he would stay until Ragnarok.

Recently, the leaders of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin and the Blood Reckoning were driven from their fortress in Thursrike by an army of allied Northland powers. After escaping via a teleportation ring, {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} now launch their final push to begin Ragnarok. While Skymir goes now to rally the jotuns and giants to war, Thyrin leads an elite force of cultists and warlords in the far northeastern land of Vargrike. They have broken the arcane seals laid upon the dungeon around Fenris and battled their way through the guardians to where the wolf lies sleeping. However, only {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas}, a divine relic of the Norns, can break Gleipnir.

entries.name: Sagas Connections
entries: {@i Storming the Den of Fenris} is the tenth adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}. For those following the campaign arc, after finishing this scenario, the PCs proceed to the climactic {@adventure Ashes of Asgard|NorthlandsSagas|11}.

The characters have met Uror before: when they returned her lost magical shears to her in {@adventure Among the Norns|NorthlandsSagas|3}. {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} just barely escaped their clutches in {@adventure Attack on Birgkrona|NorthlandsSagas|9}.

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: As the characters arrive in pursuit of {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}, the cultists have begun a long ritual to summon one of the Norns, gain {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas}, and release Fenris. It proceeds as one great dungeon delve through a complex series of sculpted chambers and natural caverns.

The heroes discover Thyrin, his cultist minions, and their giant allies have already entered the den but, as they took the most direct route to Fenris, much of the dungeon remains unexplored. The PCs battle through the chambers and tunnels, dealing with traps and monsters, until they activate a series of runic devices to open the way to the cavern where Fenris lies imprisoned.

Reaching the cavern, the characters find Thyrin and the thrudgelmir giant {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} close to completing a powerful arcane ritual at the feet of the sleeping wolf.
