The characters' path to stop the ceremony is blocked by {@creature Krusgr Ironcap|NorthlandsSagas}, a fire giant warlord.

Just as the PCs triumph over the giant, Thyrin completes the ritual summoning Uror, one of the Norns. In a shocking betrayal, {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} attacks Thyrin as a blood price to the Norn and gains {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas}—the one item capable of cutting Fenris's chains. The giant releases Fenris and escapes with him to destroy the gods in Asgard, leaving the characters to deal with the cult leader.

entries.name: Factions and Key Players
entries: Various factions and NPCs operate in this adventure:

items.name: Apostles of Inexorable Ruin:
entries: A sect of the Cult of Ragnarok led by {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}. They seek to bring about Ragnarok by releasing Fenris. Almost all the humans and trollkin in this adventure belong to the cult.

items.name: Blood Reckoning:
entries: A faction of the giants of Jotunheim led by {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}. They strive to destroy the gods of the North for killing the First Giant. Secretly, they plan to betray Thyrin and lead Fenris to Asgard to attack the gods.

items.name: Einherjar:
entries: Powerful humanoid guardians of the Den of Fenris. These spirits made flesh unswervingly serve Wotan and his Valkyries.

items.name: Krusgr Ironcap:
entries: A fire giant warlord and member of the Blood Reckoning.

items.name: Malfngur:
entries: A six-headed giant and minion of {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}.

items.name: Thyrin the Black:
entries: Leader of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin, a faction of the Cult of Ragnarok.

entries.name: Call to Action
entries: After the events of {@adventure Attack on Birgkrona|NorthlandsSagas|9}, the characters were urged to use a repaired teleportation circle to follow {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} and his allies to the Den of Fenris. They are 8 hours or more behind the cultists, depending on the previous adventure.

entries.name: Alternate Adventure Hook
entries: If you are not running this as a part of the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, the characters learn of Thyrin's plan to awaken Fenris from a patron or ally. They travel magically to Vargrike to stop the cultists before it is too late.

entries.name: When to Release Fenris?
entries: When the characters arrive at the dungeon complex, they have a narrow window of time in which to stop Thyrin from freeing Fenris from his chains. The exact amount of time purposely remains nebulous for gameplay reasons, so that when the PCs arrive in the Great Wolf's prison cavern (Area 21), Thyrin is close to completing the ritual.

Regardless of how much time you give the PCs, they should not be able to take more than a couple {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short Rests} in the dungeon. If they take a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, Thyrin completes the ritual, and Fenris is released (leading to the next adventure). You can communicate this sense of urgency to the party:

items: Every few rooms the characters venture into, a rumble rolls down from somewhere ahead and causes them to grab hold of something to keep their balance. Was that a distant howl?
Some of the cultists they meet happily tell them that Thyrin is just about to release Fenris, and that they won't be able to stop him.

entries.name: Den Locations
entries: The Den of Fenris comprises two distinct areas: a complex of chambers hewn from volcanic stone and a separate series of underground natural caverns.

entries.name: Temperature
entries: The entire dungeon remains uniformly dry and cold, with all water sources frozen. PCs not dressed in winter clothing or otherwise protected from the cold suffer from exposure to Extreme Cold after 1 hour in the dungeon (see {@hazard Extreme Cold|XDMG|Dungeon Master's Guide} and {@hazard Extreme Cold|NorthlandsWorldbook|Northlands Weather} in {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 7: Running a Northlands Campaign|NorthlandsWorldbook|7}).

entries.name: Locations in the Volcanic Complex
entries: Unless otherwise noted, the dwarf-constructed portion of the Den of Fenris has the following features.

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: Most corridors are 15 feet high, with most ceilings in chambers at least 20 feet high.

entries.name: Construction
entries: Worked, smooth, volcanic black stone decorated with golden runes throughout.

entries.name: Doors
entries: Most doors are slabs of worked stone bound with iron. Those 5 feet wide are scaled for Medium creatures; double doors (10 feet wide) are scaled for giants. They stand unlocked.

entries.name: Lightning
entries: The dungeon is unlit. A few areas have incidental illumination (noted in their descriptions).

entries.name: Traps
entries: Many areas contain traps the characters can activate themselves from the trap controls chamber (Area 10) or that are already active. If the PCs struggle to deal with the traps or you find them too punishing, feel free to remove them from some areas (such as the trapped passages) or reduce the damage they inflict.

entries.name: Area 1: Cliff Entrance
entries: {@i Windswept cliff-face. Frozen waterfall.}

Bitter winds swirl and dance upon the jagged face of a mighty cliff that soars hundreds of feet into the cobalt sky. A waterfall, frozen in mid-cascade, empties from a cave high above. Nearby, stairs meticulously carved from stone and blanketed with snow lead upward to a set of closed doors.
Two entrances provide access to the Den of Fenris: One leads to a cave inhabited by a fierce drake, the other to a set of doors crafted of thick, unyielding stone. The cultists used the doors.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC finds traces of humanoid and giant passage in the snow leading up the stairs to Area 2.
The cliff is over 300 feet high, and the waterfall is 60 feet high. Scaling them requires some skill:

items.name: {@dc 12} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC scales a portion of the cliff (new check required every 60 feet).

items.name: {@dc 18} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC climbs the slick, frozen waterfall.

entries.name: Deep Drake
entries: There's a {@chance 33|2 in 6 chance|rolled by name|Deep Drake appears|Deep Drake isn't in the cave} that the {@creature Deep Drake|ToB1-2023} from the drake cave (Area 8) is out hunting when the PCs arrive and spots them as they make their way toward the waterfall or stairs. If it sees them, it flies down to attack. If reduced to less than HP 100, it pulls back and retreats to its lair. The drake isn't associated with the cultists.

entries.name: East
entries: Up the frozen waterfall to the frozen river cave (Area 3).

entries.name: South
entries: Up the snow-covered exterior stairs (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 2: Exterior Stairs
entries: {@i Snow-covered stairs.}

The stairs here lead up to a small stone landing before continuing to another landing even higher up. They stop at large white double doors set into the cliff. Thick snow coats the stairs and landings.

entries.name: Stairs
entries: The stairs are constructed from worked black volcanic stone, similar to the stone used in the dungeon they lead to. Their cover of snow looks recently disturbed. Several broken potion bottles also litter the landing. They once contained {@item Potion of Diminution|XDMG|Potions of Diminution} that {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} and the other giants with Thyrin consumed before entering the dungeon (to allow them to navigate its confines).

items.name: {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC finds traces of humanoid and giant passage on the stairs and landings.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC recognizes that the bottles once held magical potions.

entries.name: Double Doors
entries: The closed double doors into the dungeon are fashioned from thick, white marble and decorated with shattered golden sigils. Powerful magic once bound the doors, but the cultists forced their way through with Malfngur's aid.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC realizes a powerful creature recently broke through these doors.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC notes the sigils were once magical.
Now that the doors have been forced open, PCs can shove them inward to enter.

entries.name: South
entries: Through the doors to a trapped passage (Area 4).

entries.name: West
entries: Back down the stairs to the cliff entrance (Area 1).

entries.name: Area 3: Frozen River Cave
entries: {@i Frostbitten cave. Frozen stream leading back into darkness.}
A stream, trapped in blue-white ice, takes up most of this cave. The stream enters a tunnel that winds its way into the icy depths of the cliff.

The stream through the tunnel here remains perpetually frozen. One might trace it some 200 feet up through a series of frozen cascades (hidden on the map) into Fenris's cavern (Area 21), then on to other parts of the Northlands. However, roughly 30 feet past the bridge to the drake cave (Area 8), the ice river flows beneath a stone wall and becomes impassible.

The stream measures 3 to 5 feet deep in most spots, with ice almost as hard as steel. Innovative PCs may attempt to burrow through it or thaw the stream, but such a task would take several hours—if not days—leaving the cultists to complete their ritual easily.

entries.name: East
entries: Through the tunnel to a walkway above the ice (Area 4).

entries.name: West
entries: Back down to the cliff entrance (Area 1).

entries.name: Area 4: Trapped Hallways
entries: These hallways contain traps to protect the dungeon from exploration and prevent anyone from freeing Fenris. The cultists and giants set off several on their way through the dungeon, but most have reset. Circles on the floor indicate the presence of a trap but nothing about the trap itself.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or {@variantrule Passive Perception|XPHB} check:
entries: A PC notices strange, concentric patterns on the floor where the traps are.

items: Whenever a creature passes through a hallway marked on the map with concentric circles, they have a 4 in 6 chance of finding the trap active. If it isn't active, it reactivates after {@dice 1d6} hours.

entries.name: Hallway Trap
entries: {@i Nuisance Trap (Levels Vary)}

entries.name: Trigger:
entries: When someone triggers an active trap by stepping on the pattern, roll on the Trap Effects table.

entries.name: Duration:
entries: Varies.

entries.name: Detect and Disarm
entries: The heroes can find and deactivate the hallway traps in various ways:

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB} or {@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discovers the trap. If they have already encountered this type, they get {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the check.

items.name: {@dc 17} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC can deactivate the magical trap for 24 hours by smudging out the triggering runes. If they have already encountered this type, they get {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the check.

items: A successful {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} against a 6th-level spell destroys the trap.

entries.caption: Trap Effects
rows: Tendrils of radiant energy in the form of chains arc from the walls and floor in a 10-foot radius. Creatures caught in the area must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 4d10} Radiant damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.

A giant stone hand appears out of the ground and attempts to grab a random creature. The hand has a +11 attack bonus and deals {@damage 6d10} Bludgeoning damage on a hit. A creature the hand strikes remains {@condition Restrained|XPHB} until it frees itself with a {@dc 20} Strength check, someone frees it with magic, or the hand is destroyed (AC 17, HP 50, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Poison and Psychic damage).

A giant wolf head appears and breathes a stream of frost in a 30-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}, filling the hallway. Creatures caught in the Cone must make a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 5d6} Frost damage on a failure, or half as much on a success.

{@dice 1d4} shimmering arrows appear out of the walls to strike creatures. Those struck must make a {@dc 15} Wisdom saving throw; on a failure they take {@damage 2d8} Force damage and get teleported back to the exterior stairs (Area 2).

entries.name: {@color From Here...|4d6381}
entries: Varies.

entries.name: Area 5: Northern Device Room
entries: {@i Intricately carved pillars. Glowing sphere device on the wall.}

This bleak, rectangular chamber features four pillars of gray stone, shot through with veins of blue light and adorned with elaborate runes. Mounted on the eastern wall is a circular device of glowing sapphire crystal and gold. The air hums with a strange, eldritch tone.

This chamber contains one of the three runic devices created by ancient dwarves to seal shut the golden doors in the den entrance (Area 20). When the cultists passed through, Thyrin deciphered the device's workings before moving on. He also placed a guardian here to prevent others from using the chamber.

entries.name: Guardian
entries: A {@creature Stone Golem|XMM} fashioned from cast-off bits of stone and made to look like a disfigured dwarf warrior stands in the northeastern part of the chamber. It activates as soon as someone other than Thyrin or one of his followers enters the room. It doesn't follow anyone leaving the chamber.

entries.name: Pillars
entries: The pillars were part of a potent conjuring that killed a few cultists before Thyrin could deal with it. They still hold a sliver of magical power, though not enough to cause the PCs any issues.

entries.name: Runic Device
entries: The device on the wall resembles a vast mirror of polished blue crystal with a gold frame. Some 8 feet across, it radiates powerful Enchantment magic. At its center is a crimson dial crafted from blood-red crystal, featuring three black metallic notches. A creature can move the dial to any of the notches; it is currently set to the third.

items: Moving the dial to the first notch unlocks the western lever of the northern row in the chamber of levers (Area 16), allowing that lever to be moved.
Shifting it to any other notch does nothing or locks the corresponding lever back in place.

entries.name: South, then East
entries: Back to the corridor, then through a door into the eldritch intersection (Area 7).

entries.name: South, then South
entries: Back to the corridor, then through a door into the einherjar barracks (Area 6).

entries.name: South, then West
entries: Back to the corridor, then through double doors to the trapped hallway (Area 4).

entries.name: Runic Device Shortcut
entries: Three rooms in the complex hold runic devices whose dial one can manipulate to unlock certain levers in the chamber of levers (Area 16). Positioning these levers precisely—once unlocked!—is required to open the golden doors to Fenris's Den. You may wish to give characters a skill check to determine the correct position for each room's dial to unlock a lever if you don't want them wasting time traveling between the various runic device rooms and the chamber of levers.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns the proper position for the runic device's dial.

items: This applies to the northern device room (Area 5), eastern device room (Area 9), and southern device room (Area 14).

entries.name: Area 6: Slain Einherjar Barracks
entries: {@i Torn and scattered bodies. Plain furnishings. A musty, charnel stench.}

Simple cots and a plain wooden table decorate this chamber. The bodies of dead humanoids with recent wounds sprawl over the stone floor, indelibly tattooed with blue markings. The chamber smells of fresh blood and old dust.

This room housed four {@creature Einherjar|ToB1-2023} warriors, ancient humanoids placed here to safeguard the dungeon from invasion. They died after a fierce struggle with Thyrin and his most powerful followers, who left their bodies to crumble to dust.

entries.name: Einherjar Bodies
entries: The body of each einherjar bears tattooed blue runes in the same pattern (see handout). They form the second part of an incantation that awakens the other einherjar in the complex. The first half of the incantation is tattooed on the slumbering einherjar in Area 13.

items.name: {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC reads the runic words: "Call the einherjar / Bid them rise." The text looks like an incomplete ritual.

entries.name: Gear
entries: The einherjar held {@item Battleaxe|XPHB|Battleaxes} and carried wooden {@item Shield|XPHB|Shields}. The armor they wore was destroyed when they fell in battle.

entries.name: North, then East
entries: Back to the corridor, then through a door into the eldritch intersection (Area 7).

entries.name: North, then North
entries: Back to the corridor, then through a door into the northern device room (Area 5).

entries.name: North, then West
entries: Back to the corridor, then through double doors to the trapped hallway (Area 4).

entries.name: Runic Device Shortcut
entries: Three rooms in the complex hold runic devices whose dial one can manipulate to unlock certain levers in the chamber of levers (Area 16). Positioning these levers precisely—once unlocked!—is required to open the golden doors to Fenris's Den. You may wish to give characters a skill check to determine the correct position for each room's dial to unlock a lever if you don't want them wasting time traveling between the various runic device rooms and the chamber of levers.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns the proper position for the runic device's dial.

items: This applies to the northern device room (Area 5), eastern device room (Area 9), and southern device room (Area 14).

entries.name: Area 7: Eldritch Intersection
entries: {@i Octagonal chamber. Fierce statue of an armored warrior.}

The only significant feature in this bare stone chamber is the twenty-foot-tall black stone statue of a Northlands warrior, his shield and spear raised to defend from attack. The figure wears an eye patch and a winged helm. A corridor leaves the room via a stone door in every cardinal direction.
A statue of Wotan, carved from a single piece of volcanic rock, dominates this chamber. All the doors stand closed (except the one the PCs entered through).

entries.name: Investigating the Statue
entries: The statue is part of a magical trap that reveals a great treasure at its base. A PC inspecting it can discover the following:

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC learns that the eye patch can move but is currently locked in place.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC realizes the statue represents Wotan in one of his more warlike forms.

items.name: {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC unlocks the stone eye patch plate, allowing it to be flipped.

On the reverse side of the stone eye patch is a riddle written in an archaic version of {@language Common|XPHB}. The riddle says: "I have no limits or presence. I fill the gaps between thoughts, words, and even deeds. What am I?" (See handout.) The answer is the word "space" or "nothing."

entries.name: Statue Trap
entries: {@i Nuisance Trap (Levels 11–16)}

entries.name: Trigger:
entries: Someone speaks either answer to the riddle aloud.

entries.name: Duration:
entries: Instantaneous
After someone triggers the trap, all the air in the chamber immediately gets sucked into the statue, and any open doors slam shut. At the same time, the statue rotates in place to face east.

All creatures in the chamber must make a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 4d10} Force damage on a failure, or half that on a success. All creatures in the room also begin suffocating.

entries.name: Detect and Disable
entries: The heroes can overcome this trap in various ways:

items.name: {@dc 20} Strength check:
entries: A PC forces open one of the stone doors, causing air to rush back into the chamber and allowing them to escape.

items: Destroying a door has the same effect as forcing it open. Each door has AC 17, HP 60, {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 10, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Poison and Psychic damage.
Various spells (e.g., {@spell Teleport|XPHB}, {@spell Misty Step|XPHB}) allow one to bypass the door.
{@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB} cast on the statue (against an 8th-level spell) causes it to release the trapped air back into the chamber.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The statue's rotation reveals a hidden compartment below it, which holds the following enchanted items:

items: An {@item Arrow-Catching Shield|XDMG}.
A {@item Giant Slayer Heavy Crossbow|XDMG|Giant Slayer Heavy Crossbow}.
A {@item Portable Hole|XDMG} containing 4 {@item Potion of Superior Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing (Superior)}.

entries.name: North
entries: Door to a trapped walkway (Area 4), then the drake cave (Area 8).

entries.name: East
entries: Door to a trapped hallway (Area 4), then the eastern device room (Area 9).

entries.name: South
entries: Door to the Hall of Fenrikyn (Area 15).

entries.name: West
entries: Door to a hall leading to the northern device room (Area 5) and the einherjar barracks (Area 6).

entries.name: Area 8: Drake Cave
entries: {@i Elevated walkway. Bone-strewn cave. Bitter, cloying scent.}

The elevated walkway crosses over a frozen stream before emptying into a natural cave clawed into the rock. Corroded bones of animals and humanoids are sprinkled over the rough floor. In one corner sits a nest of dried branches and trinkets. The aroma of rotting meat and foul poison clings to the nostrils.
This cave serves as the lair for a monstrous drake. It's also the warmest location in the Den of Fenris.

The PCs may have met the {@creature Deep Drake|ToB1-2023} previously, at the cliff entrance (Area 1). If they haven't encountered it yet, the creature may become aware of their presence only when they trigger the trap on the walkway or make their way under the walkway to travel farther east. If the deep drake has seen them before, it readies its Enervating Breath at the cave mouth before resorting to physical attacks. A truly despicable creature, it refuses to retreat or surrender while in its lair.

entries.name: Walkway
entries: The trapped walkway (Area 4) hangs suspended 5 feet above the stream's frozen surface. The deep drake triggered the trap a couple times in the past and now jumps over the walkway when it needs to get into the tunnel leading to the frozen river cave (Area 3).

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The nest and cave contain:

items: Three rare peach-colored garnets worth 500 GP each.
An old stone tablet containing the spells {@spell Evard's Black Tentacles|XPHB|Black Tentacles}, {@spell Modify Memory|XPHB}, and {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB}.
An {@item Elixir of Health|XDMG} in a bone flask.

entries.name: South
entries: Across the trapped walkway (Area 4) to the eldritch intersection (Area 7).

entries.name: West
entries: Through the tunnel leading to the frozen river cave (Area 3).

entries.name: Area 9: Eastern Device Room
entries: {@i Circular room. Platform above. Swirling frigid air and the stink of ozone.}

Through the double doors is a large circular chamber filled with gusts of cold wind, tortured mist, and freakish sparks of lightning. A set of narrow stairs winds up along the outside of the chamber to a thin stone platform some twenty feet above.
This chamber appears empty except for the elements described above. The room's various features appear in greater detail below:

entries.name: Sisters
entries: A pair of cackling {@creature Ala|ToB1-2023|Alas} inhabit this chamber. {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} placed the ala sisters—named {@creature Morthalyn|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Zythra|NorthlandsSagas}—here to prevent others from using the runic device to open the golden doors into the den (see Area 20). When the PCs enter the chamber, the alas are resting atop the platform near the device but react quickly to any sound, flying down to investigate. These hateful creatures refuse to parley or surrender, insulting the PCs while using flyby attacks to harass them.

entries.name: Stairs
entries: The stairs are too narrow for a Large creature to use; they have no handrail. A PC hit by one of the alas while climbing the stairs must make a {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw, falling off the stairs on a failure and taking appropriate falling damage.

entries.name: Platform
entries: The platform leads to a small rectangular chamber housing a runic device.

entries.name: Runic Device
entries: The device here looks identical to the one in the northern device room (Area 5). The device's dial is set to the second notch. Shifting the dial to the third notch unlocks the eastern lever of the northern grouping in the chamber of levers (Area 16), allowing it to be moved. Moving the dial to any other notch does nothing or locks the corresponding lever back in place. (See Runic Device Shortcut sidebar, above.)

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: Characters can locate a secret door on the south wall of the device chamber with a {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check and open it by pressing a panel in the nearby wall.

entries.name: North
entries: Back through the double doors to the trapped hallway (Area 4), then the eldritch intersection (Area 7).

entries.name: South
entries: Through the secret door and down a long, sloping trapped corridor (Area 4) to the trap controls room (Area 10).

entries.name: Area 10: Trap Controls
entries: {@i Raised flat stones. Delicate square mirrors.}

Four pale gray stone cylinders rise from the floor of this chamber to about waist height, the top of each marked with a dark symbol. The cylinders sit in front of mirrors mounted on the walls. Each mirror reveals a distant image.
The PCs can use this chamber to activate traps in four areas, potentially weakening the forces opposing them; see the Opportunity Traps table.

entries.name: Mirrors
entries: The fragile, magical mirrors see into various areas and radiate powerful Divination magic. PCs looking through one gain a description of its area and any potential threat it may contain. One can shatter the mirrors easily (AC 10, HP 20, {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerable} to Bludgeoning and Thunder damage, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Poison and Psychic damage). They lose their enchantment if removed from the dungeon but are worth 150 GP each if intact.

entries.name: Stones
entries: The top of each stone cylinder bears a symbol. As soon as a PC places a hand on a symbol and stares into its corresponding mirror, the symbol illuminates, and the character can choose to activate a trap in the area displayed. These traps stay active for 1 hour or until triggered by an enemy. The traps match the ones described in Area 4, though the heroes can select which trap takes effect when they activate it.
Each stone's symbol corresponds to a particular area on the Opportunity Traps table.

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: Characters can locate a secret door at the end of a brief hall leading west from this room with a {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check and open it by pressing a panel in the nearby wall.

entries.name: North
entries: Back along the sloping trapped passage (Area 4) to the eastern device room (Area 9).

entries.name: West
entries: Secret door to the chamber of levers (Area 16).

entries.name: Area 11: Awakening Ritual Chamber
entries: {@i Glowing magic circle inlaid in silver.}

Beyond the door lies a frigid room containing a magic circle inscribed into the floor with silver and tiny glittering stones. The circle flutters with a pearly white magical radiance. A stone drum rests in the corner.

This chamber contains a magic circle that characters can use with the proper ritual to awaken the sleeping einherjar in Area 13. This is one of the few places in the dungeon where the group can take a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} safely.

entries.name: Awakening Circle
entries: Runes around the circle read, "Codified in flesh and painted blue / To awaken the einherjar / Speak the words true" (see handout).

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns the circle is a ritual site used to awaken the einherjar, probably using the drum in the corner. Traditionally, the ones speaking the ritual are not harmed by the undead guardians.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC analyzing the runic poem realizes that, to perform the ritual, they should chant the words tattooed on the flesh of the einherjar in Areas 6 and 13.

If a character beats on the drum while they and/or others stand in the center of the circle and recite the parts of incantation in the right order, the einherjar in Area 13 stir from their slumber and begin their patrol. The ritual takes 10 minutes.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The circle contains 1,500 GP worth of silver and 3,000 GP worth of diamond dust. However, removing any silver or diamond dust destroys the circle's functionality.

entries.name: South
entries: Hallway to the looted armory (Area 12).

entries.name: West, then North
entries: Trapped hallway (Area 4) to a door heading back toward the entrance.

entries.name: Area 12: Looted Armory
entries: {@i Demolished room. Looting cultists.}
A small group of cultists is in the process of ransacking this chamber. The square room contains toppled weapon racks, shattered display cases, and an iron-bound wooden chest.
Thyrin's main force has already looted this chamber, taking most of its weapons and armor with them. Little remains, though canny characters can find some treasure here.

entries.name: Looters
entries: 4 mercenaries (use {@creature Bandit Lord|ToB1-2023|Bandit Lords}) hired by Thyrin rifle through what remains of this chamber. They don't take kindly to being disturbed and attack as soon as they see the PCs. The mercenaries aren't particularly challenging opponents; if captured, they happily spill the beans on the rest of Thyrin's forces to stay alive.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: An intact {@item Net|XPHB} and a standard {@item Greatclub|XPHB} lie on the ground. The unlocked chest holds a {@item Chain Shirt|XPHB} and a few scraps of leather, but little else.

items.name: {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC thoroughly searching the wreckage finds a {@item Horn of Blasting|XDMG}.

entries.name: East, then North
entries: Hallway to the awakening ritual chamber (Area 11).

entries.name: West, then South
entries: Trapped hallway (Area 4) to the slumbering einherjar chamber (Area 13).

entries.name: Area 13: Slumbering Einherjar
entries: {@i Cold barracks. Sleeping warriors on cots covered in dust. Chests in corners.}

Silent as a tomb, this large chamber looks like a barracks of some kind, with a pair of side tables and iron-bound wooden chests. A dozen cots hold unstirring warriors, their frames caked in ages-old dust.

This chamber contains 12 {@creature Einherjar|ToB1-2023} defenders, placed in magical slumber by the dungeon's builders. The einherjar here look identical to those found in the einherjar barracks (Area 6). Only a special ritual conducted in the awakening chamber (Area 11) can wake them from their slumber.

entries.name: Einherjar Bodies
entries: The body of each einherjar bears tattooed blue runes in the same pattern (see handout). They look similar to the tattoos on the einherjar in the barracks. This is the first half of the incantation needed to awaken the einherjar; the second is from the barracks.

items.name: {@dc 12} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB} or {@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC reads the runic words: "Herald the words with drums / For the slaying-time comes." The text looks like an incomplete ritual.

entries.name: Dungeon Defenders
entries: When the einherjar awaken, they begin patrolling the dungeon, killing off any creatures they find, other than the PCs (the undead guardians don't harm those who spoke the awakening ritual). The einherjar do not trigger any traps and allow the characters to pass through traps unmolested if they are together.
If no other foes remain, they gather in the den entrance (Area 20). They can't pass beyond the threshold of the golden doors into the den, even if the doors stand open.

entries.name: Chests
entries: The unlocked chests contain 12 sets of archaic noble clothing and 12 brass and ivory drinking horns (worth 25 GP each). Stealing from the chests causes the einherjar present to attack the thieves until they return the stolen items.

entries.name: North
entries: Trapped hallway (Area 4) to the looted armory (Area 12).

entries.name: South
entries: A few steps down a hallway to double doors into the southern device room (Area 14).

entries.name: Area 14: Southern Device Room
entries: {@i Pillared chamber. Short stairs to the east lead up to a shimmering blue and red crystalline device.}

A chill wind whips between the pillars in this chamber, each covered in elaborate runes and glimmering with veins of azure light. The eastern half of the room narrows and ends at a short flight of stairs up to a small landing. A circular runic device fashioned from blue crystal and gold hangs from the far wall.
This is the last room used to activate the levers in the chamber of levers (Area 16). It contains guardians Thyrin left here to prevent others from using the runic device after he activated it.

The chief occupant of this chamber—{@creature Kashagur|NorthlandsSagas}, a blind {@creature Oni|XMM}—has pale green skin and white hair. He wears a red blindfold to cover his damaged eyes. {@creature Kashagur|NorthlandsSagas} has {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} out to 30 feet and waits in front of the runic device. Also in this chamber, 3 {@creature Trollkin Reaver|ToB1-2023|Trollkin Reavers} skulk between the pillars, awaiting the oni's commands.

When {@creature Kashagur|NorthlandsSagas} notices the PCs, he casts {@spell Darkness|XPHB} and orders the trollkin reavers into battle before using his claws and nightmare rays on the party. His {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} makes Kashagur a terrible foe in the dark, though once he's reduced to less than HP 30, he assumes gaseous form and retreats to the chamber of levers (Area 16) by seeping under the secret door, so he can regenerate and resume his attacks.

entries.name: Pillars
entries: Like the pillars in the northern device room (Area 5), the ones here once formed part of a magical trap, now destroyed.

entries.name: Runic Device
entries: This device looks identical to the one in the northern device room (Area 5). The dial is set to the first notch; shifting it to the second notch unlocks the middle northern lever in the chamber of levers. Moving the dial to any other notch does nothing or locks the corresponding lever back in place. (See Runic Device Shortcut sidebar).

entries.name: Secret Door
entries: PCs can locate a secret door in the northeast part of the room with a {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check and open it by pressing a panel in the nearby wall.

entries.name: Northeast
entries: Through a secret passage leading to another secret door ({@dc 20} Intelligence [{@skill Investigation|XPHB}] check to find it); pressing a panel in a nearby wall opens the door into the chamber of levers (Area 16).

entries.name: Northwest
entries: Hallway to the slumbering einherjar chamber (Area 13).

entries.name: Area 15: Hall Of The Fenrikyn
entries: {@i Long rectangular chamber. Ornate walls with scarlet tapestries. Raised dais at the far end and elaborate carvings on the floors. Standing stones along the sides of the room.}

Engravings and murals depicting ancient legends of the Northlands cover the walls of this chamber. Tapestries also hang from the walls, their gold embroidery shaped into howling wolf heads. Twelve standing stones of various sizes and shapes form a path through the center of the chamber, each stone covered with inscriptions and pictographs. At the south end of the room, stairs lead up to a raised dais and a solitary stone door. At the foot of the steps, two wolf-like creatures wearing chains gnaw on the body of a frost giant.

The den's builders designed this enormous chamber as a generator to power the rest of the dungeon by absorbing some of Fenris's potent divine energy and routing it through the standing stones here to the rest of the complex. While the stones here draw power from Fenris, destroying them wouldn't make freeing him any easier, so Thyrin and his followers left them alone.

After Thyrin, Krusgr, and Malfngur entered the chamber of levers (Area 16), Krusgr posted a guard here to prevent others from following them to the den (Area 21). Unfortunately, in a fit of boredom the frost giant posted here attempted to destroy one of the standing stones, which unleashed a powerful trap hidden in the chamber and resulted in his death.

entries.name: Standing Stones
entries: Each stone measures 8 to 12 feet long and roughly 6 feet high. They are decorated with images of wolves and other monsters typical of the Northlands. Some also bear faded, indecipherable script in a language older than humanity.

The standing stones radiate powerful Conjuration and Enchantment magic. They have AC 17, HP 80, {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 10, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistant} to all damage, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Psychic and Poison damage. The stones are also {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to all damaging spells of 3rd level or less.

entries.name: Fangs and Chains
entries: When the characters arrive, 2 {@creature Fenrikyn|NorthlandsWorldbook} sit gnawing on the frost giant's corpse. The two beasts turn from their meal and rush to attack, fighting to the death. Unfortunately, as soon as one dies, another is summoned in a flash of light atop one of the standing stones (randomly chosen). Only two of the creatures can appear in this area at any given time. The only ways to stop them from spawning are to leave the chamber altogether or deactivate the summoning trap by one of the following:

items: Tear down or cover all the tapestries.
Repair the standing stone damaged by the frost giant (the western stone closest to the dais) using a simple {@spell Mending|XPHB} spell.

entries.name: Wolf Tapestries
entries: Each tapestry is 15 feet tall and woven of bright red and gold cloth. The tapestries radiate Conjuration and Enchantment magic, similar to the standing stones. Each time a new fenrikyn appears, the wolf heads on the tapestries briefly animate.

Each tapestry has AC 11, HP 30, {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 3, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistant} to all damage except Fire, to which they are {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerable}, and Psychic and Poison damage, to which they are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune}.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The frost giant's sack contains:

items: A chunk of frozen butter in the shape of a human head.
A {@item Wand of Magic Missiles|XDMG} with a frozen chunk of unidentifiable meat on the end of it.
A stuffed meerkat with a saber-tooth tiger tooth stuck on top of its head like a horn.

entries.name: North
entries: Through the door and into the corridor to the eldritch intersection (Area 7).

entries.name: South
entries: Through the door to the chamber of levers (Area 16).

entries.name: Area 16: Chamber Of Levers
entries: {@i Iron levers jutting from stone pedestals. A rune-covered iron door.}

This large chamber features six smooth granite pedestals arranged in two rows of three. Atop each pedestal sits a shiny iron lever. Deeply inset into the chamber's southern wall stands a burnished iron door. It lacks an obvious handle and bears various engraved runes.
One of the most crucial rooms in the complex, this chamber contains six levers that open both the golden doors in the den entrance (Area 20) and the iron door in this room.

entries.name: Enchanted Iron Door
entries: The iron door is magically locked. It has AC 20, HP 120, {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 15, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistant} to all damage, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to Cold, Poison, and Psychic damage.
The three levers in the southern row unlock the iron door (see below); once unlocked, the door stays that way as long as the characters remain in the dungeon.

items.name: {@dc 25} Strength check:
entries: A PC forces open the door, destroying its hinges in the process.

items.name: {@dc 15} caster check:
entries: A {@spell Knock|XPHB} spell unlocks the door.

entries.name: Northern Row of Levers
entries: When the PCs entered the dungeon, these levers were all locked in place. Only by activating the runic devices in the three device rooms (Areas 5, 9, and 14) can one unlock them easily. Once the characters have unlocked the levers, they can flip them all (in no particular order) to unlock the golden door in Area 20 leading to the den. Afterward, the golden doors remain unlocked for the duration of the adventure. (Thyrin ordered his minions to relock the doors and the levers after he passed through.)

items.name: {@dc 25} Dexterity ({@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC unlocks one of the levers without first activating the corresponding runic device. A character can attempt this check only once per lever.

entries.name: Southern Row of Levers
entries: The characters can manipulate the three levers in the southern row to open the iron door. One can flip the levers in any order to unlock the door, as long as the levers in the northern row have been unlocked already (otherwise, the levers here remain locked as well).

items.name: {@dc 25} Dexterity ({@item Thieves' Tool|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC unlocks one of the levers without having first unlocked the corresponding lever in the northern row. A character can attempt this check only once per lever.

entries.name: Secret Doors
entries: Characters can locate secret doors near the southeast and southwest corners of the room with {@dc 20} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) checks. They can open each one by pressing a panel in the nearby wall.

entries.name: North
entries: Through the door to the hall of fenrikyn (Area 15).

entries.name: East
entries: Through the secret door to the trap controls room (Area 10).

entries.name: South
entries: Through the enchanted iron door to the stairs up (Area 17).

entries.name: West
entries: Through the secret door to the southern device room (Area 14).

entries.name: Area 17: Stairs Up
entries: {@i Steep stairs lead upward from a square chamber.}
The iron door opens into a thirty-foot square chamber with no visible ceiling. A set of carved stone stairs leads upward from this space, hugging the walls as it circles overhead.
This stairwell ascends over 100 feet. The bottom of the chamber lacks all furnishings or guards.

entries.name: Stairs
entries: The stairs measure 5 feet wide and have no railing. The giants with Thyrin could safely ascend thanks to {@item Potion of Diminution|XDMG|Potions of Diminution} they drank in the exterior stairs (Area 2).

entries.name: North
entries: Back through the iron door to the chamber of levers (Area 16).

entries.name: Up
entries: Characters can use either the stairs or flight/levitation magic to access the continuing stairs up (Area 18).

entries.name: Area 18: Stairs Up
entries: These stairs hug the walls clockwise as they continue upward. A 20-foot square void lies in the center of the stairwell. Falling from the stairs here deals at least {@damage 10d6} Bludgeoning damage.

entries.name: Option
entries: If the characters have had too easy a time of things in the dungeon so far, you can place a couple of {@creature Invisible Stalker|XMM|Invisible Stalkers} or similar creatures here to slow them down. Otherwise, the PCs should not face any dangers or difficulties moving up or down the stairs.

entries.name: Up
entries: Continue up the stairs to the guardian cave (Area 19).

entries.name: Down
entries: Back down the stairs to the ground level (Area 17).

entries.name: Locations in the Caverns
entries: Ascending the stairs in Areas 17 and 18 to the higher level of the dungeon brings characters to the natural cavern portion of the Den of Fenris. Formed by ancient volcanic activity, the caverns have the following features (unless otherwise noted).

entries.name: Ceilings
entries: Most corridors are 15 feet high, with ceilings at least 20 feet high.

entries.name: Lightning
entries: The caverns are unlit. A couple areas have incidental illumination (noted in their descriptions).

entries.name: Walls and Floor
entries: Rough, uneven black stone, irregularly shaped.

entries.name: Area 19: Guardian Cave
entries: {@i Natural-looking cavern. Frost blankets the ground.}
The stairs ascend to a large cave with rough, black stone walls. Patches of frost cover the stony floor, and a chill mist hangs in the air. Several figures stand guard, trying to keep warm.
The cavern has few cave formations and feels icy. Creatures without warm clothing or {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistance} to Cold damage suffer exposure to the cold after 10 minutes.

Currently, 8 {@creature Trollkin Reaver|ToB1-2023|Trollkin Reavers} guard this cave, after Thyrin ordered them to stay behind. These savage brutes fiercely defend the way forward. They are all fanatical followers of the cult and refuse to surrender.

entries.name: East
entries: A frozen tunnel heads through the trapped passage (Area 4) to the den entrance (Area 20).

entries.name: Down
entries: A flight of stone steps leads back to the stairwell (Area 18).

entries.name: Area 20: Den Entrance
entries: {@i Huge cave. Frozen cave formations. Large doors of gold.}

The tunnel ends in a large natural cavern containing jagged, rime-coated stalagmites. At the back of the cavern stand massive golden double doors, over twenty feet high. The doors glow with a surreal light and are covered in intricate runes.

This is the final cave before the characters reach the den (Area 21) where Fenris lies bound. Thyrin and {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} posted one last guard here to stop anyone from opening the golden doors.

entries.name: Frosty Foe
entries: A beautiful {@creature Frost Giant|XMM} named {@creature Galnafur|NorthlandsSagas} with flowing white and red hair guards the way forward. Galnafur resembles a normal frost giant but uses a {@item Spear|XPHB} instead of an Axe (increasing her reach to 15 feet) and a shield that gives her AC 17. This plus the following additional special attack (a blessing from Bergelmir) increases her to CR 9.

{@b Bitterfrost Cyclone (1/Day).} As an action, Galnafur whips up a bone-chilling cyclone that swirls around her for up to 10 minutes. The cyclone generates and repositions up to 3 feet of snow in a 15-foot radius that moves with her, creating {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB} for Large and smaller creatures. Additionally, the cyclone protects Galnafur from projectiles. All but the heaviest Ranged weapon attacks targeting her are made at {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. If she takes damage, she makes a {@status Concentration|XPHB} check to maintain the cyclone. Otherwise, the cyclone lasts for the duration, until Galnafur is {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} or spends a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to end the effect.

entries.name: Golden Doors
entries: Powerful divine magic safeguards the golden doors at the north end of the cave; one cannot open them without first activating the correct levers in the chamber of levers (Area 16). Once they are unlocked, the PCs can push the golden doors open with ease.

items.name: {@dc 8} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC hears the muffled sounds of ritual chanting coming from behind the golden doors.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Galnafur's sack contains:

items: A {@item Potion of Diminution|XDMG} in a crystal flask.
A wooden hairbrush with giant boar bristles, sized for a giant.
A platinum and ruby chalice, sized for a human (worth 2,500 GP).
A dirty woolen cape (used as a facecloth).

entries.name: North
entries: Through the golden doors into the den (Area 21).

entries.name: South
entries: Back through the trapped tunnel (Area 4) to the guardian cave (Area 19).

entries.name: Area 21: Den Of Fenris
entries: {@i Massive cavern. Lines of magical blue force and glowing esoteric runes. An enormous, sleeping wolf constrained by golden chains. Sonorous chanting.}

Deep, resonant chanting fills this enormous cavern, which a frozen stream neatly bisects. A magic circle—big enough to enclose a small keep—takes up most of the cavern. The circle's lines and runes of engraved silver glow with a rippling azure light that flows into the air. It coalesces at a point above the cavern's prisoner.

On the far side of the cave lies Fenris, the Great Wolf. He is shackled by thick golden chains leading to black obelisks arrayed about his sleeping form. Creatures surround him at each obelisk, enacting a chanting ritual.

A faint, shimmering wall of blue energy follows the path of the stream and rises to the ceiling. Standing on the near side of the stream are a pair of horse-sized garmrs and four troll hounds. Towering behind them, a fire giant readies his burning sword. On his brow he wears a circlet set with a sapphire that glows with the same hue as the arcane wall.

This, the centerpiece of the adventure, presents a challenging fight for the party—even at full strength. While characters might like to rush forward and stop the ritual by the most expedient means available, they must first take on the creatures on the near side of the cavern.

entries.name: The Cavern
entries: The cavern has the following special features:

items: The 120-foot-high ceiling is dotted with ancient stalactites.
A layer of permafrost covers the hard volcanic stone ground. Burrowing through it is impossible for most creatures.
The cavern's walls, floor, and ceiling have been enchanted to prevent spells like {@spell Stone Shape|XPHB} or {@spell Meld into Stone|XPHB} from affecting them.
The magic circle illuminates the cavern with {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB}.

entries.name: Magic Circle
entries: The magic circle has these special features:

items: The characters cannot damage the magic circle. It resists all attempts to erase or destroy it.

The magic circle prevents creatures from teleporting across the cavern. Teleportation spells like {@spell Dimension Door|XPHB} and {@spell Misty Step|XPHB} fail in this cavern. Spells that transport other creatures, like {@spell Banishment|XPHB}, don't work either.
Creatures attempting to fly over the magic circle are halted by a barrier that runs the length of the stream (see below).

entries.name: Wall of Frozen Force
entries: Overlapping the stream is a wall of frozen force that sparkles faintly in the light.

items: A character approaching the wall can detect it with a {@dc 10} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check.

The barrier functions like a standard {@spell Wall of Force|XPHB}, but a creature that touches the wall must make a {@dc 18} Constitution saving throw, taking 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Cold damage on a failure and freezing in place for 1 minute (as the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB} condition).
A frozen creature can repeat the saving throw at the end of its turn, ending the effect on itself with a success.
{@creature Krusgr Ironcap|NorthlandsSagas|Krusgr} the fire giant wears a circlet (visible just below his helm) that maintains the wall; it breaks if he falls in battle.
Once Krusgr dies, the wall shatters dramatically and collapses in on itself.

entries.name: Ritual
entries: On the far side of the frozen stream, 8 {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics} of Inexorable Ruin gather around Fenris, two at each obelisk. Thyrin (below), wearing a black bearskin cape, and {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} ({@creature Thrudgelmir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thrudgelmir}) stand near Fenris's head, guiding the ritual.
All the cultists seem lost in a trance as they chant the incantation. They take no actions against the PCs until they have completed their summoning (see The Twist).

entries.name: Combat!
entries: Six guards—2 {@creature Garmr|NorthlandsWorldbook|Garmrs} and 4 {@creature Gilitrutt Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Gilitrutt Trolls}—gather around to protect {@creature Krusgr Ironcap|NorthlandsSagas} ({@creature Fire Giant|XMM}). They also try to prevent any creature from reaching the frozen stream. The garmrs and trolls have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on all attack rolls and saving throws while Krusgr lives. When Krusgr dies, refer to The Twist.
Krusgr resembles a normal fire giant with some slightly better ability scores, improving his stat block as follows:

items: AC 20.
{@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} +4 (14).
{@i Melee Attack Roll:} +12, reach 10 ft. {@i Hit:} 22 ({@damage 4d6 + 8}) Slashing damage.
{@i Ranged Attack Roll:} +12, range 60/240 ft. {@i Hit:} 24 ({@damage 3d10 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage.

entries: These updates, plus the following two additional special abilities, increase him to CR 11.

{@b Heated Body.} The heat Krusgr exudes from his body is so intense it provides him with {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistance} to Cold damage. In addition, any creature within 5 feet of him that strikes his heated body with a melee attack takes 7 ({@damage 2d6}) Fire damage.

{@b Angrboda's Tears (Recharge 5–6).} Krusgr can expel a stream of boiling iron from his eyes. {@i Dexterity Saving Throw:} {@dc 18}, each creature in a 30-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}. {@actSaveFail} 27 ({@damage 6d8}) Fire damage, and the creature suffers 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level from the hot metal. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage and negates any further effect.

entries.name: The Twist
entries: Just as the PCs fell Krusgr, Thyrin completes the ritual.

As the magical wall shatters, the chanting reaches its peak, and Thyrin the Black yells, "Come then, oh Norn. We summon thee!" A rapturous, mad expression takes hold of his scarred face; sweaty strands of black hair cling to his skin.
With a soundless explosion of magical energy, an old woman appears in front of Thyrin. "Here I stand," Uror croaks. "Malfngur, are you prepared to pay the price in blood?"

Thyrin looks at the six-headed giant. "Price? What price?" Without warning, the monstrous giant seizes the cult leader and plunges a curved dagger into his back, then drops him screaming to the ground. The other cultists cry out in shock and horror.

"The price is paid in blood and betrayal," Uror intones. "The prize is yours." The crone gestures, and a pair of crude iron shears appears in Malfngur's hands. With four quick snips, the shears cut through Gleipnir—the golden chain binding the Great Wolf to the obelisks—sending glowing links clattering to the ground. Then the shears vanish, to reappear on Uror's belt.

Fenris instantly awakes. Shaking free of the chains with a great howl, he leaps into the air, his terrible claws tearing a hole in reality—and incidentally raking deadly-looking slashes in two of Thyrin's followers. The wolf dives through the rift, followed by the six-headed giant. The rift closes behind them.
Uror shakes her head. "As was foretold. The Wolf is free, the jotuns march, and the siege of Asgard begins." Then she vanishes.
{@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} (below) gets up, battered but not yet defeated, to kill as many PCs as he can alongside his 6 {@creature Cultist Fanatic|XMM|Cultist Fanatics}.

items: Due to Malfngur's attack, Thyrin is {@variantrule Bloodied|XPHB} with only HP 106 remaining.
Adjust the number of cultist fanatics to account for the PCs' current condition

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The defeated foes possess the following treasure:

items: Thyrin's gear.
Four {@item Potion of Diminution|XDMG|Potions of Diminution} in crystal flasks.
The flayed skin of a Large white dragon (a skilled magical crafter can turn it into a suit of white dragon {@item Scale Mail|XPHB}).
A giant-sized drinking horn (made from the horn of a giant goat).

{@item Gleipnir|NorthlandsSagas}. The four pieces of the glowing chain are clearly magical. A {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check allows a PC to sense artifact-level power radiating from them. (GM's Note: It's important to the next adventure that the PCs take this.)

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: Thanks to the Norn, the PCs know that Fenris and the giants are heading to Asgard to attack the home of the gods. The characters should get time to rest and recuperate, but they don't have long before Fenris and {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}—who has been off rallying the jotuns—launch their attack.

entries.name: Further Adventures
entries: The PCs leave the den to find the Valkyrie Sanngrior waiting for them outside in gleaming armor. She says Loki sent her to inform them that Fenris and an army of jotuns and giants march toward Asgard. Loki requires their assistance.

When they are prepared, Sanngrior teleports them to the deck of Kosktup Farleap's magical longship, {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}, back in Thursrike. The vessel's magical figurehead opens a passage to an interplanar waterway called the Everriver...
But that is a story told in {@adventure Ashes of Asgard|NorthlandsSagas|11}, the final adventure in the {@i Northlands Sagas}.

data.name: Ashes of Asgard
entries: {@i Ashes of Asgard} is a third-tier adventure for a party of four to five 12th-level player characters, though you can adjust it to accommodate more or fewer players. This, the climactic adventure of the Northland Sagas, begins in the Jotunheim region and moves to the divine city of Asgard.

At the end of the adventure, the characters should reach 13th level. If this is the first adventure you're playing in the Sagas, refer to the {@adventure Adventure Path Background|NorthlandsSagas|0|Adventure Path Background} in the {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0} for important backstory.

entries.name: Adventure Background
entries: Urged by the influence of Angrboda and Bergelmir, the cruel gods of the giants, the jotun {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} has struck an alliance between his sect, called the Blood Reckoning or Blodgjold, and {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas}, the leader of the Apostles of Inexorable Ruin—a faction of the Cult of Ragnarok. Together these two groups managed to reach the hidden lair where Fenris, the Great Wolf, lay imprisoned.

In a stunning move, the giants betrayed {@creature Thyrin the Black|NorthlandsSagas} to one of the Norns in return for magical shears capable of severing Gleipnir, the only binding able to hold Fenris. Once freed, Fenris and Skymir led a mighty force of giants to attack Asgard itself!

Though the time for Ragnarok has not yet come, the presence of Fenris in Asgard has inflicted mortality upon the gods. Separated and in disarray, the deities struggle to survive while giants ransack their divine city. Without aid, the gods will die, and Ragnarok will actually occur.

But hope is not lost! Under the guidance and patronage of Loki and other allies, a band of adventurers has worked to thwart the Cult of Ragnarok and the Blood Reckoning. With both victories and setbacks behind them, these heroes now rush to the home of the gods aboard a magical longship...

entries.name: Adventure Summary
entries: This adventure has three parts, plus a prelude and epilogue.

items.name: Prelude: Off to War!
entries: The characters arrive in Asgard aboard the magical longship {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}. The vessel's enchanted dragon figurehead has brought the ship to a dock at the edge of the Bifrost Bridge leading to the divine city. There they can see the battle has begun.

items.name: Part 1: Storming the Bifrost
entries: The PCs confront {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas}, the six-headed giant, in a thrilling battle at the gates of the city. Once inside Asgard, they find Fenris running amok and giants rampaging through the streets and burning buildings. When the PCs join some Northern deities struggling to organize a resistance, they learn that four of the gods are missing!

items.name: Part 2: To Rescue the Gods
entries: In sandbox style, the characters venture across the war-torn city to four locations within Asgard. One deity has been driven into Idunn's Farmhouse, while the orchards of immortality apples burn around it. Another came to Volund's Forge, hoping to craft a powerful weapon. The third battles giants among the broken remains of their divine home. The last protects some of the children of the gods in the crumbing ruins of Asgard's Meadery.

items.name: Part 3: Into the Wolf's Jaws
entries: With their divine supporters rescued and walking by their sides, the characters can at last move against {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} and Fenris. This epic confrontation occurs in front of the burning Hall of Valhalla. Careful planning is needed to accomplish two main goals: defeat Skymir and his giants, and use a restored Gleipnir to rechain Fenris before he can destroy the gods.

items.name: Epilogue: Asgard Locations
entries: A description of the various locations in the city of the gods.

entries.name: Factions and Key Players
entries: A few distinct factions and NPCs operate in this adventure:

items.name: Blood Reckoning:
entries: A faction of the giants of Jotunheim led by {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}. They strive to destroy the gods of the North for killing the First Giant. An army of various giants follows their banner.

items.name: Einherjar:
entries: Spirits of renowned warriors who dwell in the Hall of Valhalla, fighting and feasting, while waiting to battle in Ragnarok.

items.name: Gods of the North:
entries: The Aesir and Vanir together form the pantheon of deities worshipped by most in the North. Notable members include Wotan, Thor, Loki, Baldur, Tyr, Freyja, Freyr, Njord, Sif, and Volund. See the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 6: Northlands Pantheons|NorthlandsWorldbook|6}, for more on these and other deities.

items.name: Kosktup Farleap:
entries: A daring and charming ratatosk, captain of the magical longship {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}. One of Loki's agents in the mortal world.

items.name: Loki:
entries: Shapeshifting God of Cunning, Mischief and Malice, Lord of Deception. Father of Fenris, Hel, and Jormungandr. Patron of Thieves. Also the patron of the characters.

items.name: Malfngur:
entries: A dread six-headed giant and loyal minion of {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}.

items.name: Sanngrior:
entries: A hard and unsympathetic Valkyrie.

items.name: Skymir Godkiller:
entries: The jotun leader of the Blood Reckoning.

entries.name: Call to Action
entries: After the events of {@adventure Storming the Den of Fenris|NorthlandsSagas|10}, the characters learned from a Valkyrie named Sanngrior that {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} and Fenris were leading an army of giants to attack Asgard. Thanks to the magical longship of their ally {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas}, the heroes have a way to get to Asgard, so they hasten to aid the gods.

entries.name: Alternate Adventure Hook
entries: If you are not running this as a part of the {@i Northlands Sagas} adventure path, a patron, high priest, or Sanngrior the Valkyrie comes to the characters with a desperate plea for aid. An army of giants attacks the gods' home of Asgard. Worse, they have freed Fenris, the Great Wolf, before the proper time for Ragnarok. Heroes are needed to turn the tide against this great evil and save the gods, before their deaths trigger the end of the world.

entries.name: Prelude: Onward, to War!
entries: {@i Ashes of Asgard} assumes the characters set sail for the home of the gods immediately upon reaching the deck of {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} at the end of the previous adventure. If they instead decide to rest or rearm in a settlement, they can do so. This doesn't adversely affect the events of this adventure, though the GM may wish to emphasize the urgency of a quick departure.

When they set forth, {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}'s magical figurehead instantly transports the entire longship from the mortal world to a tributary of the interplanar waterway called the Everriver. The characters and their longship arrive within view of the city of Asgard...

entries.name: Asgard Under Attack
entries: {@i Void water under keel. Flames rising in the divine city. Roars and screams.}

With a lurch, Stokkvari appears on a stretch of the Everriver's inky black water, suspended in mid-air above a dark void flecked with stars and spectral wisps. At the edges of the tributary, streams spill off into the void, vanishing into the dark. To the north rises the impossible bulk of Yggdrasil, its trunk wider and higher than the eye can see. Two mountainlike branches of the World Tree reach out far to the east and west to form a sheltered valley between them. And there, in that hollow, rests Asgard.

From a distance, the city of the gods shines with divine grandeur, its halls shimmering with gold, silver, and starlight. Grand longhouses and great halls rise from garden-ringed hills, sacred groves, flowered paths, and rivers fed by titanic waterfalls streaming from the World Tree above. The tops of buildings familiar from sagas and songs hove into view: Thor's hall of Bilskirnir, fair Freyja's Sessrumnir, and, of course, the shield-roof of Valhalla. Surrounding the city is its famed wall, built by the giant Hrimthur of massive, rune-marked stones.

Yet, all is not well in Asgard. Flames rise high from several buildings, gaping holes pierce the walls, and the gates hang on shattered hinges. From beyond the walls, the echoing sounds of clashing steel, magical detonations, and roaring war cries herald that the battle for Asgard rages on.

entries.name: {@color From Here...|4d6381}
entries: Go to Part 1: Storming the Bifrost.

entries.name: Falling into the River or Void
entries: During Part 1, a character may fall (or be knocked) off the dock, island, or Bifrost. The rules below can help you manage such a situation.

entries.name: Catch the Edge
entries: Characters can make a last-moment attempt to save themselves from a fall.

items.name: {@dc 15} Dexterity saving throw:
entries: A PC catches themselves on the edge and hangs by their fingertips.

entries.name: Deadly Swim
entries: Anyone falling into the Everriver is in danger of being swept off into the void.

items: A creature that starts its turn in the water moves 20 feet toward the nearest waterfall into the void.
Swimming in the Everriver is considered {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}, even if a creature has a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB}.

entries.name: Into the Void
entries: Falling into the void is usually fatal, but Asgard's magic protects those who fall in near the city.

items: The first creature to fall into the void from the river, dock, or Bifrost is immediately teleported to an unoccupied space within 10 feet of the city gate (south of the gate). Each subsequent creature that falls and is teleported arrives 40 feet farther away from the previous one's arrival spot.
After 10 minutes between teleports, the distance resets.

entries.name: Runestone Upgrades
entries: The upgrade opportunity in this scene is intended to be an "in-game" way to improve the Runestones, as opposed to something hand-waved or done out of character. Hopefully the heroes realize they should allow the Runestones to enter the flames. If they don't, describe how the pull toward the flames grows stronger the farther away they attempt to go. Moving more than 60 feet away ends the pull toward the beacon.
If you are using Runestone cards, give the players each the card for their Patron power.
Should the characters fail to upgrade their stones, don't force the issue. The upgrade can instead take place automatically when they encounter the individual gods whose runes they bear.

entries.name: Bifrost Bridge
entries: {@i Floating island. Dock above endless void. Guarded bridge.}

Ahead, the river tributary ends at a long dock attached to a free-floating island set with a flaming beacon and a dock house. Farther on, another span of stone and wood stretches from the island to the mighty Bifrost. The radiant bridge of the gods seethes with burning fire and light as it traces a luminous path to the shattered gates of the war-torn city.

entries.name: Area 1. Longship
entries: {@creature Kosktup Farleap|NorthlandsSagas|Kosktup} and his crew bring {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas} to a halt alongside the long oak dock. The sounds of battle echo from beyond the towering walls of the city.

items: The {@creature ratatosk|ToB1-2023} tells the PCs he will keep the ship here and protect it from any giants, in case they need a quick exit. (See the {@adventure Appendix|NorthlandsSagas|13} for his NPC description.)
He knows little more than the PCs about the situation; his calls to his patron Loki have gone unanswered.

{@b Important!} Before the characters disembark, they must have with them the pieces of Gleipnir, the chain that once bound Fenris. If they played the previous adventure, {@adventure Storming the Den of Fenris|NorthlandsSagas|10}, they recovered it after the giants freed Fenris. If not, Kosktup gives it to them now.

entries.name: South
entries: To the dock (Area 2).

entries.name: Area 2. Dock
entries: {@i Creaking wood. Distant explosions and clashing steel.}
This long wooden dock seems suspended above a gaping void of stars. A faint outline of glowing runes appears to surround the structure.

entries.name: Spotting Malfngur
entries: The well-hidden six-headed giant lurks in the shadows of the city gates (Area 6). He observed the characters' arrival and plans to ambush them when they cross the walkway from the docking island (Area 3) to the Bifrost.

items.name: {@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}:
entries: A PC actively looking for threats spots the giant in the opening of the city gates.

items: Once the characters start across the walkway to the Bifrost, or upon realizing they've spotted him, {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} immediately begins combat by throwing pieces of rubble at the PCs. See Area 6 for details.

entries.name: North
entries: Back to the longship (Area 1).

entries.name: West
entries: To the docking island (Area 3).

entries.name: Area 3. Docking Island
entries: {@i Scent of burning amber, pine, and tallow. Crackling flame.}

The dock connects to a floating island of grass and flowers. A huge brazier burns with a brilliant fire, throwing up a thick column of black smoke. North of the blaze stands a squat rectangular stone building. Its southwestern corner appears to have been shattered by a massive impact.

entries.name: Blood Trail
entries: A trail of mostly dried blood leads from the building across the wooden walkway to the west.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC spots the blood and can discern that it leads toward the walkway.

entries.name: Runestone Upgrade
entries: When the characters step within 15 feet of the burning beacon, the Runestones they carry begin to glow with a golden nimbus of light. At the same time, the flames in the beacon turn a brilliant golden color. A character holding a Runestone detects a slight pull, as if the stone wants to go to the beacon.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns power unlike anything they've ever sensed radiating from the beacon and the Runestone. It doesn't feel harmful or threatening. The stone seems drawn toward the beacon.

items: If a character lets go of their Runestone, or brings it into contact with the beacon, the stone flies out of their grasp into the flames. It erupts with a brilliant golden light and immediately improves, gaining its Patron power (see this book's {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0}). Then it floats back to its wielder and stops glowing. Once all the Runestones are improved, the color of the flames returns to normal.
When a Runestone improves, the wielder instantly knows the details of the stone's new power.

entries.name: Spotting Malfngur Redux
entries: When the characters enter the western side of this area, they have a greater chance of spotting {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} in the shadows of the city gates (Area 6), as he prepares to ambush them when they cross the walkway from the docking island to the Bifrost.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC actively looking for threats spots the giant in the opening of the city gates.

items: Once the characters start across the walkway to the Bifrost, or upon realizing they've spotted him, {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} immediately begins combat by throwing pieces of rubble at the PCs. See Area 6 for details.

entries.name: North
entries: To the dockmaster's house (Area 4).

entries.name: East
entries: Back to the dock (Area 2).

entries.name: West, then North
entries: Bifrost to the Gates of Asgard (Area 6).

entries.name: West, then South
entries: Bifrost to the lightning barricade (Area 5).

entries.name: Area 4. Dockmaster's House
entries: {@i Crumbled wall. Fresh blood. Alarm mimic.}

This building appears to have been an office and living quarters once, but the southwest wall has been partially destroyed. A wide blood pool stains the floor, and the contents of the room lie strewn all about. In the northwest corner, a wooden chest rests next to a discarded leather satchel spilling out a scattering of gems, coins, and a brass bell.

entries.name: Blood Pool
entries: Someone lost a fight here. The blood spill looks substantial; the smears clearly show someone dragged themselves (or was dragged) to the south.

entries.name: Wooden Chest
entries: The chest in the corner is a {@creature Mimic|XMM}.

items: {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} has trained this mimic to ring the brass bell if any creature other than a giant comes within 10 feet.

{@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} can hear the bell from his hiding spot at the city gates (Area 6). When {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} hears the bell, he begins hurling rocks at the dockmaster's house, any PCs he can see, or the longship.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: 145 GP worth of gems and assorted coins, a brass bell (5 SP).

entries.name: South
entries: Back to the docking island (Area 3).

entries.name: Area 5. Lightning Barricade
entries: {@i Ozone odor. Crackling wall. Runic stones.}
Lighting arcs between two towering menhirs set at the edges of the Bifrost. They form a near-blinding barrier of crackling force.
Created by {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} and the greatest jotun mages, the rune-carved monoliths are powerful enough to keep the Gods of the North from fleeing down the Bifrost.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC realizes they shouldn't go anywhere near this.

items.name: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC discerns the barrier is formed of incredibly powerful Evocation magic. Even {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistance} or {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunity} to traditional Lightning sources would do little to blunt the damage from this wall.

A mortal creature that touches the lightning barricade must make a {@dc 20} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the creature dies; on a success, it takes {@damage 10d10} Lightning damage and {@damage 8d10} Force damage.
The barricade remains in effect while Skymir lives.

entries.name: North
entries: Gates of Asgard (Area 6).

entries.name: North, then East
entries: Bifrost to the walkway leading to the docking island (Area 3).

entries.name: Area 6. Gates of Asgard
entries: {@i Burning tower. Shattered gates. Rubble and danger.}

The incandescent span of the Bifrost ends at a mighty gatehouse piercing the towering walls of the city. Two gate towers show clear signs of recent damage—the western one actively burns with greedy flames. Below, the golden gates lie shattered, hanging from broken hinges.

The immense form of a giant blocks the way forward, his six heads displaying expressions of bloodlust, anger, and determination. He smashes the mauls he holds in each hand together with a deafening clang.
Skymir ordered {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} (a {@creature Thrudgelmir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thrudgelmir}) to hold the gates of the city and prevent the heroes from aiding the gods.

items: The giant gains the following attack option: {@b Rock.} {@atkr r} {@hit 12}  range 60/240 ft., one target. {@h}24 ({@damage 3d10 + 8}) Bludgeoning damage, and the target is pushed up to 15 feet straight away from the giant.
{@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} fights to the death.

entries.name: Blood Trail
entries: A trail of mostly dried blood leads north into the city.

items.name: {@dc 15} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check (with {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} if one of the PCs succeeded on the similar check in Area 3):
entries: A PC spots the blood and can discern that it leads toward the city.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: {@creature Malfngur|NorthlandsSagas} has a sealed clay bottle in his pouch ({@item Oil of Sharpness|XDMG}) and a {@item Belt of Hill Giant Strength|XDMG} looted from an Asgardian.

entries.name: North
entries: Ahead through the gates (Into the City).

entries.name: South, then East
entries: Bifrost to the walkway leading to the docking island (Area 3).

entries.name: South
entries: Bifrost to the lightning barricade (Area 5).

entries.name: Into the City
entries: After the characters step through the gates into Asgard, they meet an ally who will bring them to a place where they can catch their breath and regroup.

Beyond the shattered gates, war has come to Asgard. Screams, sword-song, and the thunderous steps of giants resound in air thick with ash, blood-smoke, and ruin. In every direction, the corpses of the einherjar—the warrior-dead of Valhalla—lie strewn on the perfect flagstones, their bodies crushed and shields broken. Many of the divine longhouses of the gods show damage or are wreathed in flames.

Far ahead, the dim forms of giants fight with more einherjar or smash into the great halls in search of plunder. On the Plain of Idavollr, beyond the northern walls of the city, the titanic bulk of Fenris tramples unseen foes, his howl rising above the clash of steel from hundreds of the warrior-dead who struggle against the wolf.
Splayed out near the gate, at the end of a trail of blood, lies the body of a young man with long blond hair. He wears richly decorated clothing and very fine boots.

entries.name: Body
