entries: This is the body of Meili, God of Travel. Giants injured him in the dockmaster's house (Area 4) when the attack began, but he managed to drag himself here before perishing from his wounds.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Religion|XPHB}) check:
entries: Based on some of the sagas and myths, a PC recognizes the dead man as Meili the God of Travel, a son of Wotan.

items.name: {@dc 10} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|XPHB}) check or {@dc 12} Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) check:
entries: The side of the body appears to have been crushed by a massive impact.

The characters witness this scene to drive home the fact that the gods have been rendered mortal and to increase the stakes and tension. Once they have examined the body, read or paraphrase the following:
"It's you!" a harsh voice croaks out from nearby. "The mortal heroes Loki promised."
A war-stained and weary Valkyrie limps out of the shadow of a ruined longhouse to the northwest. She leans on her bloody spear, her armor marred by many wounds, and gestures urgently.
"Hurry to me. The Queen of the Aesir—Frigg, wife of Wotan—bade me bring you to her."

This is {@creature Sanngrior|NorthlandsSagas}, a {@creature Valkyrie|ToB1-2023} the characters last saw outside the Den of Fenris. She urges them to move swiftly and puts off answering most questions.

entries.name: Meili
entries: If asked about the body, {@creature Sanngrior|NorthlandsSagas} shakes her head sadly and says, "With the Wolf here, our immortality is gone. More of us may end up like poor Meili."

entries.name: Ahead
entries: Go to Speaking with Frigg.

entries.name: South
entries: Gates of Asgard (Area 6).

entries.name: Speaking With Frigg
entries: The Valkyrie brings the PCs to Vingold, the Wine-Hall (see {@adventure Epilogue|NorthlandsSagas|12|Area 2. Vingold, the Wine-Hall} for details). As they approach, the characters can note ranks of einherjar dug into fortified positions around the line of trees surrounding the hall. Occasional boulders crash down on these positions from giants and trolls in the surrounding buildings.

The adventure assumes the characters followed {@creature Sanngrior|NorthlandsSagas}. If they made their own way, Frigg comes to them elsewhere in the city, which may necessitate reworking some of the information below.
When the characters enter Vingold, read or paraphrase the following:

The great hall of Vingold is well fortified with massive timbers reinforced with bands of iron. The gods have repurposed their wine-hall into a hall of war. Comfortable chairs and cushions have been pushed back against the walls to make room for all those gathered in the hall. Everywhere you see warriors resting for the next battle or recovering from wounds. A few smiths repair weapons and armor on the edge of the firepit running down the length of the room.
At the far side of the chamber Frigg stands, still and unshaken amid the turbulent activity of the hall. As you approach, she turns her deep gray eyes upon you.

"Apparently Loki spoke true this time," she says, her voice soft but somehow loud enough for all to hear. "Come. I would have words with you, mortal heroes. Our time grows short, and we have lost too many of us already."

Frigg offers the characters a place to sit, mead to drink, and roasted meat to eat. She also gives them a map of the divine city (see handouts). While they rest, she speaks freely, disclosing the following information:

items: The giants, led by the jotun {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas}, smashed their way into Asgard, thanks to Fenris.
Unprepared for such a direct attack, the gods are scattered and in disarray.
The giants run amok through the city.
The armies of Valhalla battle Fenris on the Plain of Idavollr, but even the einherjar can only delay the Great Wolf for a time.
The einherjar die by the thousands, both on Idavollr and in the city. Though they will arise again tomorrow, Asgard will not last that long.

Most importantly, the presence of Fenris in Asgard has robbed the gods of their immortality. They can be killed in this state. Already they have lost several of their number, such as Wotan's son Meili and the twins Irpa and Gna.

Most of the surviving gods have either gathered here in Vingold or are nearby leading warriors to fight the giants. However, four gods have yet to be found. She names them (see the {@adventure Who Is Missing?|NorthlandsSagas|11|Who Is Missing?} sidebar).
Frigg's divinations and the Vanir scouts have determined the missing gods' locations, but the defenders don't have the resources to devote to rescuing them.
Frigg asks the characters to go into the city and rescue the gods.

She also comments that one of the missing gods is in Volund's Forge—the only place in Asgard where the pieces of Gleipnir the heroes carry can be repaired; she suggests that the four separate pieces, once repaired, could be used to re-shackle Fenris.

entries.name: Who is Missing?
entries: The identity of the missing gods depends on the GM and the decisions made at the beginning of the Sagas campaign. There are 13 possible gods who could be missing; the others are either in Vingold or out fighting the giants. Choose from among these options for the missing gods:

items: {@deity Baldur|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}
{@deity The Bear Maiden|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}
{@deity Freyr and Freyja|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}
{@deity Heimdall|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}
{@deity Loki|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}
{@deity Njord|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}
{@deity Sif|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}
{@deity Thor|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}
{@deity Tyr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}
{@deity Ratatoskr|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}
{@deity Volund|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}
{@deity Wotan|Norse|NorthlandsWorldbook}

entries.name: Matched to Runestones
entries: Ideally, the missing gods match the Runestones held by each PC, so the characters can rescue the deities named in their Runestones' Patron powers (see {@adventure Introduction|NorthlandsSagas|0}).

entries.name: Randomly Chosen
entries: If your group isn't playing {@i Ashes of Asgard} as part of the Sagas adventure path, or isn't using the Runestones, choose four gods at random and place them in the locations noted in Part 2.

entries.name: More than Four Players
entries: If the party consists of more than four players, simply include an extra "missing god" in one of the locations in Part 2.

entries.name: Aid from the Gods
entries: A number of gods in the hall can aid the characters (if convinced to do so) in the form of a Divine Boon. Any of the gods gathered here can aid a PC by granting a boon.

items: A Divine Boon mimics the effect of a potion or spell and is usable three times. For example, a Divine Boon might be that the character can cast the {@spell Darkvision|XPHB} spell or gains the benefits of a {@item Potion of Heroism|XDMG}.
Using a Divine Boon is usually an action unless the spell it mimics has a different type of activation.
The boon given by a god usually plays into that deity's nature, but the exact benefit is up to the GM. For example, a boon from Thor likely would have something to do with lightning or thunder.
Each god can grant only one Divine Boon per day; a PC can only receive one per day.

entries: Additionally, other deities can give other forms of aid instead of Divine Boons. This aid counts as a boon for the purpose of a character's one-per-day limit. Each of the gods below can aid the PCs only once, unless noted otherwise.

entries.name: Bragi
entries: The god of poetry wants to hear one of the PCs perform before giving his aid.

items.name: {@dc 10} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC gains a {@dice d4} Bardic Inspiration die, which must be used in the next 8 hours.

items.name: {@dc 15} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check:
entries: The performing PC gains a {@dice d12} Bardic Inspiration die, which must be used in the next 8 hours.

items.name: {@dc 20}+ Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check:
entries: Each PC gains a {@dice d12} Bardic Inspiration die, which must be used in the next 8 hours.

entries.name: Hel
entries: The god of the underworld isn't particularly fond of her father Loki but will aid the characters nonetheless—if they are hearty enough to endure her touch without flinching. She touches one PC with her cold hand.

items.name: {@dc 10} Constitution saving throw:
entries: The PC automatically succeeds on the next {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} they make in the next 8 hours.

items.name: {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw:
entries: The next successful {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB} the PC makes in the next 8 hours counts as a natural 20.

items.name: {@dc 20}+ Constitution saving throw:
entries: The first time each PC drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, they gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB}s. If they recover and later need to make more {@variantrule Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws}, they don't have this benefit.

entries.name: Idunn
entries: The god of rejuvenation and renewal offers each character an apple. While it won't make them immortal, eating the apple in the presence of Idunn grants a PC the benefit of a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. This gift doesn't count as a Divine Boon.
Idunn says she has enough apples to give one to each PC. But if you, as GM, feel the characters need another rest, she can offer more.

entries.name: Skadi
entries: The god of the hunt asks a character she selects to shoot an arrow at a wooden knot on a ceiling beam at the far side of the hall. To hit the target, the PC must make a ranged weapon attack against AC 15.

items.name: Attack result 15–16:
entries: The PC has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next Melee or Ranged weapon attack they make in the next 8 hours.

items.name: Attack result 17–19:
entries: The PC deals {@damage 1d6} extra damage on all successful Melee or Ranged weapon attacks for 8 hours.

items.name: Attack result 20+:
entries: All the PCs deal {@damage 1d6} extra damage on all successful Melee or Ranged weapon attacks for 8 hours.

entries.name: Vidar
entries: The god of silence scatters dry barley husks across the ground and gestures for one of the characters to walk across them. He places a finger before his lips, indicating they should do so silently.

items.name: {@dc 10} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check:
entries: The PC automatically succeeds on the next Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check they make in the next 8 hours.

items.name: {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check:
entries: The PC gains {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks for the next 8 hours.

items.name: {@dc 20}+ Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check:
entries: All the PCs gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks for the next 8 hours.

entries.name: {@color From Here...|4d6381}
entries: Go to Part 2: To Rescue the Gods.

entries.name: Frigg (Deity)
entries: {@i Quiet and commanding. Tall with long, gold hair bound in an intricate braid. Wears a flowing blue-gray cloak set with a falcon-shaped pin. Her gray eyes see beyond human sight. A ring of silver keys hangs on her belt.}
{@b Background:} God of Prophecy and Motherhood, Queen of the Aesir, Wife of Wotan, Lady of Fensalir.
{@b Personality Traits:} Measured, quiet, and dignified. Wields an arched eyebrow like a blade.
{@b Bonds:} Protective of the other gods, especially her son Baldur and the other female deities.
{@b Flaws:} Refuses to show she is frightened.
{@b Wants:} To repel the attack on Asgard without losing her loved ones.

{@b Talking to Frigg:} The Queen of the Aesir freely relates that the characters can find the missing gods in four locations across Asgard. She doesn't know which god is in which location. Frigg points to a map of the city to show the PCs (see handout):

items: A celestial dwelling east of Njord's Hall. A wounded einherjar scout returned moments ago to report a god is hard-pressed by giants in a building near the home of the sea god in the northwest of Asgard. The scout died before he could relate any further information.
Idunn's Farmhouse. The orchard of immortality burns and poor Idunn's home along with it. Yet, the omens and portents tell me one of us hides there—or will do so soon—with the giants in close pursuit.
Kvasir's Meadery. A force of giants has besieged the Meadery, here in the inner city. So far Kvasir's spirit has warded them off, but he is surely protecting someone.
Volund's Forge. Other giants are busy looting Volund's Forge, but we've word one of the missing gods has taken shelter there.

{@b Reward?} If the characters ask for some manner of reward, Frigg looks at them coldly but agrees to bestow a Supernatural Gift upon each of them, should they return with the missing gods and if they all survive the siege

entries.name: Part 2: To Rescue the Gods
entries: In this part of the adventure, the characters move throughout Asgard; familiarize yourself with the city's map and locations in the {@adventure Epilogue|NorthlandsSagas|12} of this adventure before diving in.

Chaos fills the streets. Giants and their minions smash, burn, and loot, while the einherjar and other divine allies battle the invaders. Using a sandbox-style approach, the characters venture across the war-torn city to four specific locations to rescue the missing gods. They are asked to either deliver the missing gods one by one to the Vingold wine-hall or to return there together with them all.

entries.name: Encounters in the City
entries: This section includes tables of random encounters and rules for when they can occur, as well as tables for what the characters might find in the various buildings in Asgard. The GM should balance the use of the combat encounters carefully, as the PCs also need to conserve resources for the rest of the adventure.

entries.name: Triggers
entries: Every time the characters move into the western or eastern side of the central portion of Asgard (marked on the map by the wide avenue running north and south), cross a bridge, or spend at least 1 hour in any building, roll {@dice 1d12}.

items: On a result of 1, roll {@dice 1d6} and consult the {@table Asgard Random Encounters|NorthlandsSagas} table.
On a result of 10, roll {@dice 1d6} and consult the {@table Asgard Noncombat Encounters|NorthlandsSagas} table.

entries.name: Increasing the Risk
entries: Each time the characters avoid a combat or noncombat encounter they rolled, expand the range of these results by 1. For example, after the PCs avoid a patrol of trolls (see below), on the next trigger a result of 1–2 calls for a combat encounter, and a result of 9–10 dictates a noncombat encounter.
Defeating foes in a combat encounter or overcoming the challenge of a noncombat encounter resets the trigger results to their original state shown above.

entries.name: Using Stealth
entries: Characters can attempt to move stealthily around Asgard. If a majority of them succeed on a {@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) check, it negates the result of a 1 on the {@dice 1d12} roll above.

entries.name: Investigating (and Looting) Buildings
entries: The giants have damaged, set aflame, or looted many buildings in Asgard. Searching a building takes 1 hour. Roll {@dice 1d6} and consult the {@table Asgard Discoveries|NorthlandsSagas} table to learn what the characters find; GMs can add treasures of their own creation.
If the Valkyrie or einherjar discover the PCs looting, they will attack them.

entries.name: Gods and Mortals
entries: Having lost their divine status, the gods rescued in Part 2 avoid battle, keenly aware of their mortality. Should they find themselves in combat after their rescue, the GM can choose how the god should use their action each round:

items: {@action Disengage|XPHB|Withdraw}, {@action Dodge|XPHB}, or {@action Dash|XPHB}.
Bestow a benefit on a nearby character—granting {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attacks, for example, or a bonus equivalent to that of {@spell Bless|XPHB}, {@spell Aid|XPHB}, etc.

entries.name: Seeking the Missing Gods
entries: The four areas the characters need to investigate to find the missing gods lie scattered across Asgard. Three of them—Kvasir's Meadery, Volund's Forge, and Idunn's Farmhouse—have set locations. The fourth, Vanir Longhouse, is described as being east of Njord's Hall, but you can set it anywhere in Asgard you wish.

The specifics of each location are left for you, as GM, to adjust to suit the needs of the PCs and the nature of the missing gods. Location descriptions include suggestions to explain why the giants and the missing god are there. Map key references in the headers correspond to the Asgard map in this adventure's Epilogue. A detail map in this section offers more on each of the four locales, including additional map key areas.
Remember that, if the heroes haven't already upgraded their Runestones, they do so automatically when they meet their aligned god.

entries.name: Idunn's Farmhouse (Area 20)
entries: {@i Thick smoke. Crackling flames. Breaking wood.}

The home of the god of rejuvenation and the keeper of the Apples of Immortality lies beyond the city's western wall. Tucked between two waterways is Idunn's small farmer's longhouse. Her apple orchard is always full of fruit. The apples need Idunn's enchantment to become Apples of Immortality.

Clouds of dark smoke rise into the sky from beyond this small Northern-style farmer's longhouse. Rose vines climb the wood-plank walls. Parts of the structure's eastern wall look fractured and crumbled. Flames rise beyond the farmhouse, where an apple orchard burns.

entries.name: Why Is the Missing God Here?
entries: The god suffers from a life-threatening wound and came to the orchard hoping for healing from an apple. When discovered, the god fled toward the Eldest Tree (detail map, Area 5).

entries.name: Why Are the Giants Here?
entries: Knowing that the Apples of Immortality can nourish and sustain even mortal gods, Skymir ordered 2 {@creature Fire Giant|XMM|Fire Giants} and 3 {@creature Ogre|XMM|Ogres} to burn the orchard. The ogres are demolishing the farmhouse, while the fire giants move toward the Eldest Tree.

entries.name: Development
entries: The fire has infuriated 4 {@creature Malrgotr|NorthlandsWorldbook} in the orchard, which attack anyone they encounter. If the PCs need aid, the Eldest Tree can awaken as a {@creature Treant|XMM}.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Hidden in Idunn's common room (detail map, Area 2) is a {@item Bag of Beans|XDMG}, a {@item Stone of Controlling Earth Elementals|XDMG}, and a crate of apples (ready for Idunn to enchant).

entries.name: Next Locale
entries: Either Kvasir's Meadery, Volund's Forge, or the Vanir Longhouse.

entries.name: If the PCs Found All the Gods
entries: Continue with After the Rescue.

entries.name: Kvasir's Meadery (Area 4)
entries: {@i Heady smell of hops and ale. Crackling flames. Objects break within.}

This factory-like meadery is where brewers create the ales and meads of the gods. Massive tanks of mead and brewing equipment stand everywhere. Kvasir, a divine spirit manifested from the union of the Aesir and Vanir, haunts the meadery. Renowned for his wisdom, he originally created the mead of poetry—which the gods stole to give mortals the gift of song. Kvasir continues to operate the meadery.

Behind a short wall encircling the meadery, flames rise from two massive brewing tanks. Eight more tanks are positioned along the wall. The meadery itself is a series of interconnected wooden buildings engraved with carvings of vines, barley stalks, and frothy mugs of ale. A gaping hole has been smashed into the western side of the structure. The northeastern portion of the building shows damage and is actively burning.

entries.name: Why Is the Missing God Here?
entries: The god brought a number of noncombatants to the meadery, hoping to keep them safe, but got trapped with them in the storage room (detail map, Area 6).

entries.name: Why Are the Giants Here?
entries: The giants seek the mead of poetry, which Wotan stole from them long ago. They suspect it is held in the secure vault (detail map, Area 7).

items: 2 {@creature Glacial Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Glacial Trolls} attempt to bash their way into the storage room, where the god and noncombatants are sheltering.
1 {@creature Frost Giant|XMM} attempts to break into the vault.

4 rounds after combat begins, a patrol of 1 {@creature Stone Giant|XMM} and 2 {@creature Gilitrutt Troll|NorthlandsWorldbook|Gilitrutt Trolls} pass by and automatically investigate any sounds of combat.

entries.name: Kvasir
entries: The divine spirit uses the stats for {@creature Arcane Guardian|ToB1-2023}. He has attempted to subtly mislead and trick the giants with minor illusions. If he decides the characters are here to aid the god in the storage room, he moves to assist them.

entries.name: Development
entries: The secure vault is locked and trapped. It doesn't contain the mead of poetry, but it does have fine vintages of wine and several potions and elixirs (see Treasure). The god in the storage room has the key.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: The vault holds a {@item Potion of Vitality|XDMG}, {@item Potion of Healing|XDMG|Potions of Healing} (2 of each type), a {@item Potion of Cloud Giant Strength|XDMG}, a {@item Potion of Speed|XDMG}, and 150 bottles of divine wines and meads worth a total of 9,000 GP.

entries.name: Next Locale
entries: Either Idunn's Farmhouse, Volund's Forge, or the Vanir Longhouse.

entries.name: If the PCs Found All the Gods
entries: Continue with After the Rescue.

entries.name: Vanir Longhouse (Near Area 21)
entries: {@i Noble home. Broken walls. Thudding sounds and cracking wood.}

This is one of the homes of the gods, located east of Njord's Hall (Area 21). Though a traditional floor plan, the structure is made of the finest materials. Depending on the god who lives here, the dwelling may have additional decorative elements.

This high-roofed longhouse is heavily ornamented, the thick wood of its walls and posts covered with decorative patterns. The southern wall of the home has been smashed in and partially set on fire. From inside comes the sound of hammering fists, breaking wood, and giant voices.

entries.name: Why Is the Missing God Here?
entries: The god knows a {@item Portable Hole|XDMG} containing powerful magic items is hidden here and refuses to let the giants take it. The god is barricaded in the bedroom (detail map, Area 3).

entries.name: Why Are the Giants Here?
entries: One of the giants saw someone flee into the longhouse, so they followed.

items: A {@creature Storm Giant|XMM} attempts to break down the door to the bedchamber (which it accomplishes in 2 rounds).
A {@creature Lightning Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook} smashes things in the northern side of the great hall (detail map, Area 2), while another investigates the kitchen (detail map, Area 4).

entries.name: Development
entries: If the storm giant breaks into the bedroom, the god retrieves the {@item Portable Hole|XDMG} and hides within it. The god tries to keep a corner open to allow in air, but it doesn't work; now the deity has only 6 rounds before they suffocate.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Apart from the god, inside the {@item Portable Hole|XDMG} are 3 {@item Ioun Stone|XDMG|Ioun Stones} ({@item Ioun Stone, Protection|XDMG|Protection}, {@item Ioun Stone, Fortitude|XDMG|Fortitude}, and {@item Ioun Stone, Intellect|XDMG|Intellect}).

entries.name: Next Locale
entries: Either Kvasir's Meadery, Volund's Forge, or Idunn's Farmhouse.

entries.name: If the PCs Found All the Gods
entries: Continue with After the Rescue.

entries.name: Volund's Forge (Area 13)
entries: {@i Sulfur and ash. Heat from molten rock. Broken charcoal-stained stones.}

In Smidaholl, the forge-hall of Volund, the smith-god crafts wonders. A volcano feeds the forge constantly, making the place uncomfortably warm. Usually Volund's disciples operate the forges, but they fled before the giants arrived.

An eighty-foot-high volcano spews a river of molten stone down its eastern side. The magma flows toward a metal longhouse marked with strange protuberances, towers, crenelations, and annexes. The lava falls into a basin at the top of a squat tower, where smoke rises from many chimneys.

entries.name: Why Is the Missing God Here?
entries: The god came to finish crafting the {@item Hammer of Thunderbolts|XDMG} currently in the lava forge (detail map, Area 4). The god has retreated to the southwest corner of the forge to hold off the foes.

entries.name: Why Are the Giants Here?
entries: The giants came to loot the forge. They hope to find magical items, relics, or artifacts.

items: 3 {@creature Thursir Giant|NorthlandsWorldbook|Thursirs} are in the audience hall (detail map, Area 2), having just opened the door.
A {@creature Hill Giant|XMM} searches the residence (detail map, Area 3), while another has moved around the north side of the building; it hurries back if combat begins.
As the encounter begins, 3 giantkin {@creature Berserker|XMM|Berserkers} rush into the residence.

entries.name: Gleipnir
entries: If the PCs don't bring it up, the god senses the presence of Gleipnir and offers help repair it (see below).

entries.name: Treasure
entries: A {@item Hammer of Thunderbolts|XDMG}, a bottle of {@item Sovereign Glue|XDMG}, and a bottle of {@item Universal Solvent|XDMG}.
The god needs only 10 minutes to finish crafting the {@item Hammer of Thunderbolts|XDMG}. If given the time to do so, the deity gives it to the heroes as thanks for the rescue.

entries.name: Repairing the Chain
entries: The god hiding at the forge can attempt to repair the mystical chain Gleipnir but needs the heroes' aid to accomplish it. The god provides the magical power if the characters provide the other skills.

entries.name: Skill Checks
entries: Each PC must succeed on a {@dc 15} ability check using one of their skills, after first justifying to the GM why it would aid in the ritual forging process. No skill can be used twice. Examples of skill use include:

items.name: {@skill Arcana|XPHB}:
entries: Use knowledge of runes to aid the binding process.

items.name: {@skill Religion|XPHB}:
entries: Intone a prayer to the various Northern gods to bless the undertaking.

items.name: {@skill Athletics|XPHB} or {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB}:
entries: Physically repair the severed links, resulting in 4 perfect lengths of chain.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: If more PCs succeed than fail, the repair process works, leaving the characters with 4 mystical lengths of Gleipnir. On a failure or tie, the heroes can attempt it again but must add 1 to each skill's DC.

entries.name: Next Locale
entries: Either Kvasir's Meadery, Idunn's Farmhouse, or the Vanir Longhouse.

entries.name: If the PCs Found All the Gods
entries: Continue with After the Rescue.

entries.name: After the Rescue
entries: When the characters have rescued the missing gods, they should return with them—either one by one or in a group—to Frigg at Vingold (Area 2 on the city map). After they enter the wine-hall, Frigg calls them to her side to discuss the final move against {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Fenris|NorthlandsSagas}.

entries.name: {@color From Here...|4d6381}
entries: Go to Part 3: Into the Wolf's Jaws.

entries.name: Part 3: Into the Wolf's Jaws
entries: In this section, the heroes and their divine allies rush to the Hall of Valhalla to confront {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} and {@creature Fenris|NorthlandsSagas}. Victory here spells the end for the Blood Reckoning—but losing this fight leads to the start of Ragnarok and the end of the world.

entries.name: Preparations
entries: Once they are back in Vingold, Frigg summons the characters and the rescued gods to formulate a plan to deal with Fenris and the giants.

entries.name: The Plan
entries: This is the plan the gods suggest (this adventure assumes the PCs follow it). How to get them to agree to all of this depends on the players and the party makeup.

items: The einherjar and Valkyries will engage the other giants, keeping them out of the courtyard around the Hall of Valhalla (Area 9 on the city map). If any giants slip past, the characters will have to deal with them.
The gods accompanying the heroes will lure Fenris into position in the courtyard between four ceremonial pillars made of primordial stone.
When the wolf is in position, the gods will activate the pillars with their divine power. The pillars can restrain Fenris, but this effect will not last long.
The heroes must use the pieces of Gleipnir to shackle Fenris to the pillars.
The PCs also engage {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} and any of his minions to keep them from disrupting the gods' connection to the pillars.
Everyone will sneak into position and rush the courtyard at the same time.

entries: The GM should allow the characters to formulate whatever plans they wish. Remind them of the bonus they gain from proximity to the gods aligned to their Runestones. See the {@adventure Final Battle|NorthlandsSagas|11|Final Battle} sidebar for some additional advice.

entries.name: Idunn's Aid
entries: If the PCs are really wounded or drained of resources, Idunn can offer more apples that grant {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB|Long Rests} (at the GM's discretion).
When everything is prepared, Frigg orders the gathered gods (other than the four aligned to the characters) to lead the Valkyries and einherjar to engage the giants around Valhalla.

entries.name: {@color From Here...|4d6381}
entries: Go to The Courtyard.

entries.name: The Courtyard
entries: When the heroes and gods reach the courtyard, read or paraphrase the following:

Valhalla burns. Flames lick up from within the building to scorch the golden shields of its roof. The sounds of battle echo from the streets leading toward the hall as the Valkyries and einherjar engage the ranks of giants, trolls, and ogres.

As you rush into the courtyard, the impossibly huge bulk of Fenris stands before the shattered doors, smashing his titanic paws down onto the hall. The equally massive figure of Skymir Godkiller paces back and forth near the Great Wolf, his golden hair stuck to his sweaty face, his bright blue eyes piercing with the look of a fanatic. He calls out orders to the giants fighting in the streets.

entries.name: Luring Fenris
entries: The players are likely to come up with many possible ways to get Fenris to step between the pillars. As GM, allow any reasonable plan to work. Fenris moves toward any prey or threat and steps between the pillars without realizing what they are for.

entries.name: Final Battle
entries: This encounter is quite complicated with many moving parts. The easiest way to run it is for the characters and allies to reach a spot at the edge of the courtyard undetected. The Valkyries and einherjar keep the giants busy.

GMs wishing to make the PCs work for it can have them make {@skill Stealth|XPHB} checks to determine whether any foes spot them. Some of the read-aloud-text will need adjusting if the giants detect the characters on their way to the courtyard or as they get into position.

Directly battling Fenris is a fight no mortal could hope to win. Mechanically, Fenris has a CR off the charts. Thus, the gods should emphasize the importance of following the plan to re-shackle the Great Wolf. Even battling a single jotun may be all—or more than—the PCs can handle.

Once the battle begins, Fenris's struggles against the gods and the magical restraints trigger terrain hazards and environmental effects, as described under {@adventure Fenris Effects|NorthlandsSagas|11|Fenris Effects}.

entries.name: When Skymir Spots the Gods
entries: The jotun laughs and says: "It's the end for you, One-Eye. You and your kind will pay for the murder of Aurgelmir. The time of the Aesir and Vanir is over!"

entries.name: When Fenris Gets in Position
entries: When Fenris moves between the pillars, the gods swiftly activate them. At this point, read or paraphrase the following:

As the gods pour divine energy into the four pillars, golden runes appear on the stone, flowing up and down in complex patterns. Beams of light lance out, catching Fenris between them. The Great Wolf howls in fury and struggles against the radiance holding him in place.

One of the gods calls out to you. "We'll keep Fenris contained while you replace the chains of Glepnir on him. But be swift—we won't be able to restrain him for too long! Oh! And deal with the jotun!"

Skymir grins wickedly. "Look on me, pests, and despair. I am Skymir, son of Aurgelmir, god-slayer and lord of Jotunheim. If you would pray to one of these gods before your death, do it quickly, as they will soon join you."

An all-too-familiar voice rings out as Loki steps out of thin air.{@sup †} "I, for one, accept all prayers, accolades, and sacrifices," he says. The trickster winks at you, drawing a bone-white wand from a belt loop. "It's raining burning debris, so I suppose this counts as a rainy day."
The god points Skirnir's Wand at Skymir, speaks a word, and the sixty-foot-tall jotun is suddenly smaller. Still a giant, but much smaller.
"There," Loki says with a grin. "That seems a bit more fair, doesn't it?"
{@note {@sup †} If Loki was one of the missing gods and is empowering one of the pillars, he does this from his position at the pillar instead.}

{@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} (see below) primarily concentrates on attacking the characters. However, he is very intelligent and can attack a pillar to draw the PCs into range of a Fenris Effect.

entries.name: Fenris Effects
entries: On {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} count 20 (losing ties), Fenris's struggles produce one of the following effects; the same effect can't be used 2 rounds in a row:

items.name: Deadly Howl:
entries: {@actSave con} {@dc 15}, each creature in a 60-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}. {@actSaveFail} 14 ({@damage 4d6}) Thunder damage and creature has the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition until {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} 20 of the next round. {@actSaveSuccess} Half damage and not {@condition Deafened|XPHB}.

items.name: Mesmerizing Tether:
entries: {@actSave wis} {@dc 15}, one creature Fenris can see within 90 feet. {@actSaveFail} Target has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition until {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} 20 on the next round, as it spends its turn mesmerized by the wolf's eyes.

items.name: Paw Slap:
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 15}, one Large or smaller creature within 15 feet of Fenris. {@actSaveFail} The target is pushed 40 feet away from the nearest pillar and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. If the target strikes a solid object, such as a building, it takes {@damage 1d6} Bludgeoning damage for each 5 feet remaining in the 40-foot total movement.

items.name: Void Rip:
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 15}, two creatures Fenris can see. {@actSaveFail} The target is teleported into a space occupied by another creature within 60 feet that Fenris can see. Both creatures in the space take {@damage 3d10} Force damage before falling into the nearest unoccupied spaces and gaining the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. {@actSaveSuccess} The target is teleported to an unoccupied space within 60 feet.

entries.name: Rechaining Fenris
entries: Reconnecting part of Gleipnir to Fenris requires two successful checks for each pillar: one to attach the chain to one of Fenris' limbs and one to lock that attached chain to the nearest pillar. Encourage the players to describe how they use the ability checks listed in this section to attach the chain to the wolf or pillar.
The DCs for the checks in this section increase by 1 for each pillar and chain pair successfully attached.

entries.name: Attaching Chain to Fenris
entries: Success at one of the following checks affixes the chain to Fenris's limb:

items: {@dc 15} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check.
{@dc 18} Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics|XPHB}) check.
{@dc 15} Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) check.
{@dc 20} Wisdom ({@skill Animal Handling|XPHB}) check.
{@dc 20} Charisma ({@skill Persuasion|XPHB}) check.

entries.name: Attaching Chain to Pillar
entries: Success at one of the following checks affixes the chain to a pillar.

items: {@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check.
{@dc 15} Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) check.
{@dc 18} {@item Artisan's Tools|XPHB} check (such as {@item Smith's Tools|XPHB}).
{@dc 18} Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check.
{@dc 20} Charisma ({@skill Performance|XPHB}) check

entries.name: Attacking a God or Pillar
entries: The gods empowering the pillars occupy the same space as the pillars and can't take actions, {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB|Bonus Actions} or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}, though they can speak. A god who takes 50 damage (or more) from any source momentarily loses control of the pillar they empower. This immediately triggers one Fenris Effect (see above).

Pillars have AC 21, HP 200, {@variantrule Damage Threshold|XPHB} 20, and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunity} to Cold, Fire and Lightning damage. A pillar shatters if reduced to HP 0; the act of breaking it renders the god empowering it {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}.
If a pillar breaks, a PC can affix one of the chains to the unconscious god.

items.name: {@dc 18} Intelligence ({@skill Arcana|XPHB}) check:
entries: A PC realizes the unconscious god can be used in place of a pillar to anchor Fenris.

items: If the check fails, one of the other gods can yell out this information.

entries: At the start of a round, if three pillars are broken and the chains from those pillars have not been attached to the wolf, Fenris breaks free and must be slain to win the day. Use the stats for a {@creature Tarrasque|XMM} for a freed {@creature Fenris|NorthlandsSagas}.

entries.name: GM Note:
entries: Give the PCs enough time to attempt to attach chains to the unconscious gods.

entries.name: Development
entries: If the GM wishes, other allies and enemies can enter the area to help or hinder the characters.

items.name: Allies:
entries: {@creature Einherjar|ToB1-2023} (CR 7), {@creature Valkyrie|ToB1-2023} (CR 11).

items.name: Enemies:
entries: {@creature Ettin|XMM} (CR 4), {@creature Hill Giant|XMM} or {@creature Troll|XMM} (CR 5), {@creature Stone Giant|XMM} (CR 7), {@creature Fire Giant|XMM} (CR 8).

entries.name: Victory
entries: Once the group has slain Skymir and attached Fenris to four anchors (pillars or gods), the Great Wolf slumps, his eyes heavy with sleep. He might beg Loki, saying, "Please, Father. Don't make me go back to sleep." Then he falls into slumber.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Gear from Skymir and other foes.

entries.name: Conclusion
entries: When Skymir is dead and Fenris anchored, read or paraphrase the following:

The cheers of the Valkyries and einherjar echo the great victory won this day. Kosktup Farleap picks his way toward you through the battlefield. As he reaches you, Loki appears by your side, grinning widely.
"Well?" he says to the ratatosk.
Kosktup rolls his eyes and hands Loki a single copper piece.

entries.name: A Bet?
entries: If the characters ask, Loki confesses that, while drinking many years ago, he bet Kosktup's grandfather (or was it great-great-grandfather?) that mortals could save Asgard from Fenris. Kosktup's ancestor seemed skeptical anyone could trick the Norns; outmaneuver Angrboda, Bergelmir, and Wotan; somehow get someone to free Fenris; and convince a bunch of mortals to intervene without telling them why they were really doing it. But Loki had faith in mortals.

items: This revelation means that Loki set up everything, from the establishment of the Cult of Ragnarok to today, just to win a bet.
If the PCs don't ask about this, Wotan or Thor will do so.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: Loki and the surviving gods heap rewards upon their mortal saviors. The party receives possession of the magical longship {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}. Kosktup grins at this, assuring the heroes that the ship was always meant for them, should they succeed in their quest. In addition, each PC gains:

items: An {@variantrule Ability Score Improvement|XPHB} (as if they achieved it by gaining a new level).
A {@filter Rare magic item|items|rarity=rare} of their choice.

entries.name: Aftermath
entries: Whichever way the adventure ends—with Asgard saved or in ashes—the world may never be the same again.

entries.name: If the PCs Succeed
entries: The characters' victory in Asgard has the potential to change the face of the Northlands.

items: The defeat of {@creature Skymir Godkiller|NorthlandsSagas} breaks the power of the Blood Reckoning, leading to a decline in raids from Jotunheim until a new giant warlord rises to prominence.

If one (or more) gods took the place of broken pillars, those gods become entombed with the sleeping Great Wolf in the Den of Fenris. Their loss ripples across the mortal world, disrupting the spells and faith of their priests.
How to rescue those gods from this fate is grounds for a new adventure.

entries.name: If They Fail
entries: The results of failing are much more dire for the Northlands.

items: The age-old prophecy of Ragnarok comes to pass with the deaths of Wotan, Thor, and the other gods. Though some mortals and a smattering of gods do survive the cataclysm, the world becomes much different.
Skymir and the other jotuns ascend to become new gods ruling over a restored First World. They begin to spread their domination into other lands.

entries.name: Epilogue: Asgard Locations
entries: This section contains brief descriptions of Asgard's various locations. Refer back to them as needed during Parts 2 and 3 of the adventure. For more on the gods themselves, see the {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 6: Northlands Pantheons|NorthlandsWorldbook|6}.

entries.name: Area 1. Bifrost
entries: The Bifrost is a magical bridge of burning fire and light, glowing with power and purpose. It stretches from the Gates of Asgard to the mortal world—and even to other planes, should the gods desire it. (See also Bifrost Bridge in Part 1.)

entries.name: Area 2. Vingold, the Wine-Hall
entries: This large great hall on the west side of the city is a well-known place of rest and recuperation for the gods of the North. Shielded by a ring of thick trees, the hall is fashioned from massive timbers and reinforced with iron and steel. Garden beds of flowers decorate the grounds around it. To the south, steam rises from rocky hot springs for bathing. (See also Speaking to Frigg in Part 1.)

entries.name: Area 3. Himinborg, Hall of Heimdall
entries: This stern-looking longhouse features a high tower in the middle tall enough to see over the southern wall of the city. If the PCs use the tower as a lookout, they can avoid random encounters in the city for 10 minutes.

entries.name: Area 4. Kvasir's Meadery
entries: Arrayed behind a short wall are a number of large brewing tanks encircling a number of interconnected buildings. At the factory-like Meadery in the southeast portion of the city, brewers craft the ales and meads of the gods. Though slain long ago, the divine spirit of Kvasir continues to operate the meadery. (See also Kvasir's Meadery in Part 2.)

entries.name: Area 5. Gladsheimr, Meeting Hall
entries: Third largest hall in Asgard, Gladsheimr occupies a central location, appropriate for the meeting hall of the gods. The building appears majestic, imposing, and grand.

entries.name: Area 6. Glitnir, Hall of Tyr
entries: The hall of the god Tyr on the eastern side of the city shines in the light of the sun. The walls and roof are sheathed in silver, held up by red-gold pillars. Also called the Judgement House, Glitnir is where the gods go to settle disputes.

entries.name: Area 7. Ridskjol, Hall of the Valkyries
entries: This longhouse and its connected building are made of steel shields and swords hammered together into a whole. Both imposing and near-impenetrable, Ridskjol serves as the home of the Valkyries. They've inscribed records of their victories into the metal of this centrally located hall.

entries.name: Area 8. Halfvegis, Half-Hall of Loki
entries: This longhouse on the city's west side looks half-built, as if the builders stopped construction halfway through and simply closed off the unfinished side. Its state stems from a disagreement between Loki and the dwarf builders. Though the god claims its condition is of no concern, Loki has surrounded the hall with high hedges that hide it from prying eyes.

entries.name: Area 9. Hall of Valhalla
entries: The second largest hall in Asgard, famed Valhalla is an immense longhouse on the north end of the city, with a roof made from golden shields. Here, the honored dead gathered by Wotan and the Valkyries spend their days fighting on the Plain of Idavollr and their nights feasting and drinking. (See also The Courtyard in Part 3.)

entries.name: Area 10. Breidablik, Hall of Baldur
entries: This elegant hall in the northwest corner of the city appears made entirely of shining gold. The structure and the grounds around it remain untouched by the chaos and violence engulfing Asgard. Both look unnaturally clean and amazingly beautiful.

items: Due to the peace-loving nature of Breidablik's patron, no weapon can be used within its grounds, nor can anything evil exist there.
Creatures attempting to fight within the hall must make a {@dc 20} Wisdom saving throw. {@actSaveFail} They do nothing and their action is wasted.
Various noncombatant inhabitants of Asgard—mostly servants—take shelter here from the giants.

entries.name: Area 11. Valaskjalf, Wotan's Hall
entries: A stark and stern longhouse on the city's north side, Valaskjalf is made of gray stone with obsidian runes worked into its surface. A tall tower rises from one corner, its top pierced by windows of green quartz.

A PC attempting to sit on Hildskjalf must make a {@dc 20} Wisdom saving throw. {@actSaveFail} {@damage 8d10} Psychic damage and have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for 1 hour. {@actSaveSuccess} {@damage 4d10} Psychic damage and can see into one location in Asgard of the character's choice for 1 minute.

entries.name: Area 12. Sessrumnir, Hall of Freya
entries: Surrounded by extensive gardens, the beautiful, elegant Hall of Freyja is decorated with the colors of nature and precious metals. Floating golden lights drift between the garden and the hall, which stands on the city's northeast edge.

items: An equal part of the honored dead chosen by Wotan dwell here instead of Valhalla, with no loss of status or reputation.
By day, these einherjar train and battle upon the Field of Folkvangr, and at night they take their rest within Sessrumnir.

entries.name: Area 13. Smidaholl, Forge-Hall of Volund
entries: A pocket volcano northeast of the city wall spews a river of molten stone down its eastern side toward a metal longhouse marked with strange protuberances, towers, crenelations, and annexes—far more than seems traditional. The lava falls into a basin at the top of a squat tower, where smoke rises from many chimneys. In his forge-hall, the smith-god Volund crafts wonders. (See also Volund's Forge in Part 2.)

entries.name: Area 14. Alfholl, Hall of Freyr
entries: Nestled in a wooden glen east of the city wall, this graceful, moss-covered longhouse appears as if it were grown out of the surrounding nature, rather than constructed.

entries.name: Area 15. Bilskirnir, Hall of Thor
entries: Lightning crackles across the slate roof of the largest great hall in Asgard. This massive structure, southeast of the city walls, is held aloft by huge columns and pierced by four massive gates. Far larger inside than even its exterior would suggest, the Hall of Thor boasts over five hundred rooms.

entries.name: Area 16. Murnstal, Thor's Goat Paddock
entries: East of the Hall of Thor lies a huge paddock area set behind 15-foot-high fences. Within it live Thor's two magical goats, Tanngrisnir and Tanngnjostr. Their screams echo off Yggdrasil; several dead giants lying around the pen attest to their might.

entries.name: Area 17. Bari, Grove of Tranquil Paths
entries: This small wood northeast of the forge-hall is tucked into the shadow of a massive branch of Yggdrasil. If offers gentle pathways shaded by tall trees, with stone benches and wells to refresh the gods who stroll through it.

entries.name: Area 18. Tasaeti, Ratatoskr's Tower
entries: Perched high up on top of the titanic branch of Yggdrasil that wraps around the eastern border of Asgard sits a wooden tower with many balconies and ledges. This is the dwelling of Ratatoskr, the divine squirrel, when he comes to the city of the gods. A switch-back trail cut into the wood of the branch leads to the tower from the woods below.

entries.name: Area 19. Byforn, Hall and Hives of the Bear Maiden
entries: Wide fields of grain and rows of huge beehives surround this honey-colored longhouse west of the city wall. Bengta the Bear Maiden owns this hall, but she seldom spends much time in Asgard, preferring to wander the forests of the Northlands. In times of trouble, such as now, she returns to the city to aid in its defense.

entries.name: Area 20. Idunn's Grove
entries: A small farmer's longhouse is tucked between two streams on the far western side of Asgard. Beyond the house grow row upon row of perfect apple trees. Here Idunn cultivates the Apples of Immortality. (See also Idunn's Farmhouse in Part 2.)

entries.name: Area 21. Sjoholl, Hall of Njord
entries: This blue-roofed great hall northwest of the city walls appears to have been fashioned from pieces of ancient longships—some still encrusted with living barnacles and other sea life. It stretches out over the edge of a small lake decorated with a necklace of docks arrayed with boats. When in Asgard, Njord, god of the sea, dwells in Sjoholl. The air around the hall smells of the ocean.

entries.name: Area 22. Fensalir, Hall of Frigg
entries: Isolated by the swamps and wetlands dominating the northwestern edge of Asgard lies the Hall of Frigg. Fensalir sits within the mist cast from the waterfalls streaming from Yggdrasil's higher branches. Covered with a blanket of moss and vine-like roots, the great hall is as enigmatic and mysterious as its owner.

data.name: Appendix
entries: Nonplayer characters, items, and other elements that appear multiple times in the Northlands Sagas are collected in this Appendix.

entries.name: Stat Blocks
entries: Bolgrim first appears in Down the Wolf Barrow and leads the Assault on Hvalfell. Ylsa succeeds him as the characters' main foil with the cult in Wotan's Gauntlet and Attack on Birgkrona.

entries.name: NPC Descriptions
entries: Descriptions of nonplayer characters who show up throughout the Sagas adventures appear in this section, alphabetically. Information they can provide relevant to a particular adventure appears in that adventure.

entries.name: Finulf One-hand (Human Viking)
entries: {@i Early thirties. Blue eyes. Long blond hair, full mustache, and short beard. Blade scar on right cheek. Wears patched leather armor over green tunic, black pants. A cloak with a white fur trim. Sword and dagger on his belt. Missing left hand capped with metal cuff.}
{@b Found Initially In:} {@adventure Down the Wolf Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1}. Also appears in {@adventure Attack on Birgkrona|NorthlandsSagas|9}.
{@b Background:} Leader of the Fangs of Vanagandr, a mercenary company.
{@b Personality Traits:} Direct, never gives up, has a hundred stories that start "This reminds me of the time..."
{@b Bonds:} Members of the Fangs. Fighting the good fight.
{@b Flaws:} Is a bit "glass-half-empty," cheerfully points out problems in gory detail.
{@b Wants:} When they first meet, to keep the stolen {@item Uror's Shears|NorthlandsSagas} from the hands of the Cult of Ragnarok. Later, to defeat the cult once and for all.

entries.name: Hekja No-Curl (Werekin Warrior Veteran)
entries: {@i Lanky sailor with a surprising bald head. Yellow eyes and lupine features. Always scowling. Hide armor. Handaxe and seax dagger on her belt.}
{@b Found Initially In:} {@adventure Ogre's Run|NorthlandsSagas|2}. Also appears in {@adventure The Redspear Trail|NorthlandsSagas|7}.
{@b Background:} First mate on Sly Raven; later second in command of the longship {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}.
{@b Personality Traits:} Grim and brooding, dark sense of humor.
{@b Bonds:} Owes a life-bond to Kosktup for saving her life.
{@b Flaws:} She is a descriptive pessimist, providing "helpful" worst-case-possibilities.
{@b Wants:} To save her captain and support him in his crazy adventures.

entries.name: Kosktup Farleap (Ratatosk Merchant Captain)
entries: {@i Small squirrelfolk. Red-brown fur. Eyes the color of acorns. Cocky grin. Plain but serviceable leather armor over a teal shirt. Gold earrings in one tufted ear. Matching rapier and dagger hanging from his belt.}
{@b Found Initially In:} {@adventure Ogre's Run|NorthlandsSagas|2}. Also appears in {@adventure Among the Norns|NorthlandsSagas|3}, {@adventure The Redspear Trail|NorthlandsSagas|7}, and others.
{@b Background:} Courageous swashbuckler, longship captain, squirrelfolk.
{@b Personality Traits:} Daring, cocky, and charming in equal measure.
{@b Bonds:} This longship dream—oh, and stopping the Cult of Ragnarok.
{@b Flaws:} Hides his idealism and dedication behind vanity and playful indifference.

{@b Wants:} To fulfill his dream of building and owning the greatest longship in the North, but when they first meet him, he'd settle for getting away from the ogres and perhaps a nice bath. Ultimately, he wants to keep his ship and crew alive and whole, which means stopping the end of the world.

entries.name: Loki (Deity)
entries: {@i Sly smile and an overwhelming presence. Fiery red hair. Handsome with an indeterminate gender. Wears an embroidered silk tunic and a coat the hue of ochre. A dagger and a net hang from their belt.}

{@b Found Initially In:} {@adventure Down the Wolf Barrow|NorthlandsSagas|1}. Also appears in {@adventure Among the Norns|NorthlandsSagas|3}, {@adventure Ashes of Asgard|NorthlandsSagas|11}, and others.
{@b Background:} Shape-shifting God of Cunning, Lord of Deception, Patron of Thieves, solver of the gods' problems—but also sometimes the instigator of the gods' problems.
{@b Personality Traits:} Dramatic and perhaps a trifle smug.
{@b Bonds:} Looks out for themself, which means not perishing in the fires of Ragnarok.
{@b Flaws:} Misunderstood by the dim witted. Keeps secrets.
{@b Wants:} The heroes to work for them to oppose the Cult of Ragnarok; to win a bet.

entries.name: Ship
entries: Kosktup Farleap's longship, {@vehicle Stokkvari|NorthlandsSagas}, is an impressive specimen of its type. Its stat block appears below. See "{@variantrule Ships and Sea Combat|NorthlandsWorldbook}" in {@book Northlands Worldbook|NorthlandsWorldbook}, {@book Chapter 7: Running a Northlands Campaign|NorthlandsWorldbook|7} for ship rules.
